lead: Thousands of photos from around the world flow into our picture archives every day. From horrifying current events to serene landscapes, from breaking news to seemingly small moments. What do you choose when everything happens at once? Where do you put the emphasis and which images stay with you? Every month the NRC photo desk selects the photos that made the greatest impression.

title: Calm and fairly cold weekend, first official ground frost of autumn
lead: The first official frost of autumn has now become a fact. In De Bilt the mercury dropped to -1.4 degrees. The rest of the weekend will be calm, with regional differences in the amount of sun and cloud.

title: Three injured after ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian capital
lead: In the night from Saturday to Sunday, Russia fired at least six ballistic missiles at Kyiv. Three people, including a child, were injured. The Kyiv Post reports this. A two-storey building on the grounds of a nursery school was destroyed in a missile attack. Follow all developments in the war in Ukraine in our liveblog.

title: 'Spiral of distrust' due to increasing police monitoring of demonstrators
lead: The Dutch government collects information on demonstration participants too often, while in many cases this is not proportionate. That is the conclusion of the <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> in its annual report on demonstrating. As a result, citizens and the government are sinking ever deeper into a spiral of mutual distrust, argues chair <entity id="person:rick-lawson">Rick Lawson</entity>. "People with good intentions are now taking to the streets wearing masks."

title: Student protest in Serbia is already bearing fruit: several police officers arrested for torture
lead: In Serbia, nine police officers still on active duty and one former officer were arrested on Wednesday on suspicion of using excessive force and torture against demonstrators. The ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> announced this.

lead: Anyone who has to leave the house early next week had better get out their gloves, winter coat and ice scraper. After a sunny Monday, we are in for significant night frost. As a result, it will be quite cold in the mornings.

lead: The KNVB and Vitesse will try, "under the supervision of an independent third party", to permanently resolve the club's long-running licence case. The football association and the club from Arnhem announced this on Tuesday through their own channels.

title: Netherlands invests heavily in protecting tropical forests

lead: Political reporter Mats Akkerman (32) is the winner of the autumn season of De slimste mens 2026. In a nerve-wracking finale, the political journalist on Friday evening outdid journalist Jeroen Gortworst and cabaret performer Claudia de Breij. The fresh winner thus follows in the footsteps of WNL colleague Frank van Leeuwen, who won the title this spring.

title: Arrest in Argentina over death threat against pope, church leader calls on people to marry and have children during trip through South America
lead: On the eve of Pope Leo XIV's visit on Sunday, a person has been arrested in Argentina for death threats against the church leader. The Argentine intelligence service SIDE reported this on Saturday.

title: Government wants to strengthen parents' educational knowledge
lead: This week minister <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Mirjam Sterk</entity> for Long-term Care and Sport and state secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> of Education and Emancipation launched the initiative 'Team Ouders'. lead: The Jetten cabinet is wobbling after just nine months in office. The VVD feels completely ambushed by the deal between D66 and CDA with PRO and Volt. The VVD cannot live with it and now wants the coalition partners to turn against that agreement after all. They refuse. The crucial vote is tomorrow, but things look bad for the survival of this cabinet.

lead: Chelsea has warned staff to be careful with the virtual football game Fantasy Premier League, the BBC and The Athletic report. The club is doing so after an injury to João Pedro, which may have been leaked by participating Chelsea staff members.

title: Commissioner of the King: 'Municipalities must house more status holders, otherwise the province will step in'
lead: Municipalities must house status holders more quickly. That is the call from the Commissioner of the King in <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity>, <entity id="person:wouter-kolff">Wouter Kolff</entity>. Municipalities have a legal duty when it comes to designating housing for status holders. Provinces supervise and can ultimately intervene themselves. "Make sure you tackle it as a municipality. Otherwise the province will step in. Nobody should want that."

lead: <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Koning Willem-Alexander</entity> opened the new headquarters of Robin Radar. The company also sees plenty of growth opportunities after an end to the war in Ukraine, such as protecting events with anti-drone systems.

lead: Ajax have finally suffered damage after weeks of escapes against FC Twente. After an early goal, it was all hands on deck in the Amsterdam camp. And that while coach Míchel Sánchez wants to blow opponents away. Two painful figures make clear how far his team still is from that after the 2-2 in Enschede.

title: Immediate nationwide mandatory housing of poultry after three bird flu outbreaks
lead: Poultry farmers must keep their chickens indoors immediately to limit the spread of bird flu as much as possible, the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> announced on Wednesday. lead: The enormous success of the Democrats in the US midterm elections continues: in the southern state of Mississippi, Democratic candidate Scott Colom (43) narrowly defeated sitting Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith (67).

title: Videoland may take over Viaplay: 'For subscribers, nothing changes at this moment'

The Authority for Consumers & Markets (<entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity>) has granted permission to the streamer, which is part of DPG Media. The ACM does not expect any adverse consequences of the takeover for viewers, the purchase of sports rights or the sale of advertising space, the ACM announced.

title: Trump still determines what the Republican future looks like without him
lead: The American voter has made clear to the Republicans that they must decide what their party will look like after Donald Trump. That is not simple, because he is not going anywhere for now. The bear has been wounded, but still has sharp claws.

title: Construction seeks 73,000 workers, competes with Defence
lead: The Dutch construction sector needs some 73,000 new employees over the next three years. That is what the Economic Institute for Construction (EIB) calculates. The construction industry has been struggling with staff shortages for years, while the Netherlands wants to build many homes, expand the power grid, renovate infrastructure and make it more sustainable.

lead: For the first time, the Netherlands is represented in boxing at the Youth Olympic Games. The 17-year-old Liz Thijssen will try to win a gold medal there. She herself has no doubt that she will bring home the prize.

lead: At least eight flights to and from Prague were affected by bomb threats on Friday. These include a KLM flight to the Netherlands. Hungarian fighter jets had to escort three aircraft. No explosives have been found yet.

title: Investigation places blame for building supervision problems mainly on BKapp
lead: Building technical supervision has improved, particularly for construction projects in smaller municipalities, since the introduction of the Wet kwaliteitsborging voor het bouwen (Wkb). That is the conclusion of the Economisch Instituut voor de Bouw (EIB) in a study after two years of the Wkb. "It does open people's eyes."

title: Protest after rainbow flags vandalised in Arnhem: 'I find it heartbreaking'
lead: People are gathering in Arnhem after several rainbow flags were vandalised. This happened at the artwork Blauwe Golven. The flags have since been set up again and the municipality is going to file a report.

title: French schoolchildren's protest grows into a broader popular movement: 'This gives hope'
lead: "I am here to demonstrate and to stand up for my rights and those of my friends", says Adam Boucherca, second-year law student at the Paris-Panthéon-Assas university. For almost a month, demonstrators have been taking to the streets across France. Massive protests are also underway again today. At 5:30 a.m., Boucherca had arranged with friends to meet near the Paris university to set up a blockade. There they were met by a group of far-right youths armed with glass bottles, he says, while showing footage of it on his phone. "As we walked forward, they started throwing the bottles. I was hit on my elbow, and a friend of mine was injured." Discontent over rising costs. With a march to the official residence of Prime Minister Lecornu, demonstrators continue their action today. Along the way, students and teachers from other faculties join them. According to Boucherca, the protest has long been about more than problems in education. This is also evident from the presence of politicians from the radical left La France Insoumise (LFI) at the university blockade. "All polls show that Rassemblement National (RN) has a chance of winning the presidential elections next year", says Boucherca. That makes him afraid, he says. "This protest gives hope. It shows that French people are mobilising against it." What began as a schoolchildren's protest, and then gained support from students, has now grown into a broader popular movement. Many French people are dissatisfied with high fuel prices, rising housing costs and the policy of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> in general. Demands submitted. The Franco-Dutch Suzanne Nijdam is chair of one of the largest French student unions. Together with other trade unions, she has submitted ten demands to the Ministry of Education, including extra investment. But the ministry has so far not responded to them. "It cannot be that so many students have to take to the streets again. Things must change, and it is up to the ministry to ensure that." Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg also joined a protest at a secondary school in Saint-Denis, a suburb of Paris, today. A recent Ipsos survey shows how divided France is over the protests of recent weeks: 54 percent of respondents support the demonstrations, 40 percent are against. The older the respondents, the smaller the support. Politics in France is also divided over the protest movement. For example, supporters of La France Insoumise (LFI) and the alliance Socialist Party-Place Publique are most enthusiastic; supporters of Rassemblement National (RN), on the other hand, think there should be an end to the movement and the violence that comes with it. Got out of hand. That is also visible on the streets. At Paris-Panthéon-Assas university, among others, LFI parliamentarian Rodrigo Arenas is present. "All LFI parliamentarians are on the side of the students", he says. "We are here simply to ensure everything goes well and to monitor the conduct of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>." According to Arenas, the way the police have intervened at the protests has recently got out of hand. In his view, they have regularly overstepped the limits of what is allowed. More than 7,000 people have now been arrested, most of them minors. At Place Vauban, three kilometres further on, there were violent clashes with riot police: LFI parliamentarian Manon Aubry is also at the demonstration at the university to support the students. "That pupils taking part in demonstrations have been maimed for life should not happen in a democratic country where young people only stand up for their rights." Ange Lacour, himself a student, supports the demands of the demonstrators, but not the way they take action. "I have difficulty with the blockades that are set up without it always being clear what the demonstrators actually want to achieve." According to him, this is because the protest movement has no clear leader. Yellow vests. Meanwhile, more than half of French people think the protests will continue for a while. That is a setback for the government, which is trying to calm tempers by making promises, for example by calling up 3,000 substitute teachers. Trade unions have announced large-scale protests for Saturday, focusing on the widespread discontent in France. On social media, calls from the gilets jaunes to join the demonstrations are circulating. The well-known yellow vest movement paralysed large parts of France for months in 2018.

title: Empty shelves in no time: Albert Heijn outage shows how vulnerable the food chain is
lead: Not so much the production but mainly the distribution of products is a vulnerable point in the food security of the Netherlands. That is what experts say about the cyber incident at Albert Heijn , which halted operations and left supermarkets with empty shelves yesterday. According to Pieter Zwaan of research institute Clingendael, supermarkets and suppliers work so efficiently that there are almost no stocks to fall back on in case of incidents or disruptions. Zwaan investigated the vulnerabilities of the current food system on commission from the Ministry of Agriculture together with others. "In a situation like this, other supermarkets can offer relief for those who specifically want fresh products such as cauliflower or broccoli", says Zwaan. But in his view it is not unthinkable that if the outage at Albert Heijn had lasted longer, shortages would eventually have arisen at other supermarket chains such as Jumbo or Lidl as well. Eight days of home supplies Supermarkets and distribution centres together have a stock for about six days, says Zwaan, with a continuous supply of new products. He sees that supermarkets rely heavily on IT systems for the distribution of products, in order to get new stock exactly on time. These IT systems themselves are vulnerable to disruptions, as the cyber incident at Albert Heijn shows, but also because of their dependence on the power supply. In the report that the researchers of Clingendael and Erasmus University published last month, they concluded that the Dutch should therefore build an emergency food supply for eight days, not for three. One of the scenarios that was examined showed that in the case of a serious weather event, such as prolonged heavy rain, combined with a major power and IT outage, it could take as long as two weeks before the distribution chain is fully back up and running. Storage in city centres The researchers also write in the report that supermarkets must maintain an emergency stock with a minimum quantity of products for households so that they can keep a supply for eight days. Right now supermarkets do not have such a buffer at all, he says. Bart de Steenhuijsen Piters of Wageningen University & Research agrees. "Supermarkets have no stocks, and all their deliveries have to come from a central distribution centre", says the researcher, who specialises in food systems. "And that has a direct effect on what is on the supermarket shelves." Because food security is in the public interest, the government must think about how this vulnerability can be limited and what role stocks play in that, says Zwaan. "But the question is how that should happen. It is a political question of who will bear the responsibility." "It is also the question where those stocks should be kept, especially in places like city centres where space is limited", says Zwaan. Besides that, it is a cost issue, he says. "Because who has to pay for it: the supermarket or the government that wants them to hold extra stock?" De Steenhuijsen Piters explains that supermarkets are focused on efficiency, with the aim of keeping prices low for consumers and profit margins as high as possible for the company. According to him this has come at the expense of resilience, continuity and supply security. Yet stocks may also be sensible in these uncertain times from the perspective of supermarkets' profit margins, says Zwaan. "If you see how much turnover Albert Heijn is now missing, then it may be smart from a business economics perspective to keep a somewhat larger stock." Redistributing food In the event of a future major national shock, certain groups will be hit disproportionately hard, says De Steenhuijsen Piters. "According to the FAO (UN agriculture organisation, ed.) there are now 1.6 million people in the Netherlands who are food-poor and therefore have difficulty with their food supply and certainly with access to healthy food." To support this group, the government would then have to adopt a protocol to redistribute food. But such a national protocol does not yet exist. "And while shocks to the food system such as climate change, international conflicts and hybrid attacks are only increasing." Work on this is under way. This summer <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity>, who has Food Security in his portfolio, informed the House of Representatives in a letter that the government is working on plans to increase food security. "We know that our food system is uncertain, but we are not sufficiently prepared for it", says De Steenhuijsen Piters. He acknowledges that measures may come at the expense of profit margins, so investment in resilience will have to take place across the board. In his view, the realisation that they must work together on this is slowly sinking in. "We are at the start of that process."

title: Groningen comes to the aid of Ter Apel and offers a hundred temporary reception places
lead: The municipality of Groningen will temporarily take in extra asylum seekers from tomorrow. It makes a hundred beds available at an existing emergency reception location on the Europaweg for families with young children. This is intended to relieve the pressure on the registration centre in Ter Apel. The extra reception has been arranged by the municipality of Groningen at the request of the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. Earlier today Minister Van den Brink wrote a letter to the House of Representatives in which he spoke of an "unsustainable" situation in Ter Apel. He asked all Dutch municipalities to "urgently create extra reception places". The situation in Ter Apel is again pressing. Last week twenty asylum seekers had to sleep outside in the grass in the rain, because there were too few reception places. Dispersal Act According to Groningen alderman Jalt de Haan, the situation is still acute and the pressure on the registration centre in Ter Apel is "unchanged and great". "The municipality of Groningen stands for humane reception of refugees and we do not want people to have to sleep outside out of necessity." Groningen already complies with the Dispersal Act, which regulates that municipalities take in asylum seekers in proportion to their size, and believes that other municipalities must also take their responsibility. "It is up to the national government to come up with a structural solution," says De Haan. Minister Van den Brink is pleased with the extra Groningen places and hopes that other municipalities will follow the example of the municipality. "They already do a lot there," he says in a response to news agency ANP. He also expresses his appreciation that Groningen is making room for families. "That is a vulnerable group." Three weeks The reception is initially intended for three weeks. What happens after that is not yet clear. According to De Haan's spokesperson, the situation will be reviewed if there are still insufficient reception places in Ter Apel in three weeks, or if no alternatives are available in other municipalities. Residents and businesses in the immediate vicinity have been informed by the municipality about the arrival of the families. Until recently, 150 asylum seekers were housed on the Europaweg. Most of them have since moved to another reception location. Currently forty unaccompanied minor asylum seekers are still staying at the Europaweg.

title: Penalty payments for asylum seekers disappear: large majority in Senate approves
lead: The Senate has in large majority agreed to two asylum measures that were earlier defeated. As a result, the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst</entity> (IND) will no longer have to pay penalty payments to asylum seekers who have to wait too long for a decision on their stay in the Netherlands. Furthermore, it becomes easier to declare criminal asylum seekers 'undesirable' and deport them. That can now be done if they commit offences that carry a prison sentence of at least two years. Laws of Faber Both measures were part of the asylum emergency measures act of former asylum minister Faber (PVV). That law was voted down in the senate in April, because it also stated that illegal residence in the Netherlands would become punishable. Helping, for example, rejected asylum seekers would also be punishable. Asylum minister Van den Brink has nevertheless now achieved two other measures, the penalty payments and the expansion of the declaration of undesirability, via a detour. He linked them to another law, which was voted on today: the Return and Immigration Detention Act. That must regulate that more force can be used when deporting rejected asylum seekers. But also that their stay in detention centres becomes more humane. Nearly 100 million euro in penalty payments That last point is the reason that, for example, Pro, the largest party in the Senate, also voted for the law. Senator Thijssen finds the current detention regime for rejected asylum seekers far too harsh. That has even repeatedly led to suicide, she recalled, such as with Russian activist Dolmatov in 2013. Still, Pro is not in favour of abolishing the penalty payments, because they also act as an incentive for the IND to decide faster. A majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> does want to get rid of them, because the amounts the IND pays out are rising sharply. Last year it concerned 79 million euro, while in the first half of this year the IND already paid out nearly 100 million euro. After the defeat of the asylum emergency measures act, Van den Brink promised to still get its content through parliament. That partly succeeded already with the introduction of the European Migration Pact, a few months later. Last week he came with the plan to make refusing to return to the country of origin punishable.

title: Prison and TBS for series of offences ending in rape of 87-year-old woman
lead: A man from Ede must go to prison for eight years for a series of offences, including attempted manslaughter and the rape of an 87-year-old woman. The court also imposed a TBS order on the man, who is 27. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded thirteen years and TBS. The offences took place between August and October last year. The man first sexually assaulted a woman (34) in a forest near Bennekom. Two days later he sexually abused a 16-year-old girl. She was assaulted on a park bench. The man also committed several thefts afterwards. In early October the man broke into the home of the 87-year-old woman. She caught him inside the house at night. The man then lost control: he pulled her down the stairs and repeatedly threw her "like a doll" onto the floor, the verdict states. While she lay on the floor, he raped her several times. He then searched the house for items to take. He left the woman for dead. The woman was found the next morning by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. They had been alerted by a concerned neighbour and family. The victim still suffers every day from the rape and the violence. Mental disorders The man has largely confessed to the offences. Research by the Pieter Baan Centrum shows that he has several mental disorders. According to experts, the man was severely diminished in criminal responsibility at the time of the offences. They therefore advised imposing TBS with compulsory treatment. The judge followed this advice. The TBS can be extended repeatedly, for as long as the risk of reoffending has not been sufficiently reduced. The TBS treatment begins once the man has served his prison sentence. He must also pay damages: 45,000 euros to the older woman and 2,000 euros to the 34-year-old woman he sexually assaulted.

title: Strike in regional transport, impact differs by region
lead: Regional transport is on strike today. Travellers should expect delays and cancelled services. The impact differs by region. Due to the strike, no Arriva trains are running in Limburg. In other parts of the country, Arriva trains are running according to the timetable. For example, all trains between Zwolle and Emmen, between Almelo and Hardenberg, and between Zutphen and Oldenzaal are running. There are also no cancellations on the regional lines in Groningen and Friesland. In bus transport, the effects of the strike are greatest in North Brabant, where about 10 percent of buses are running, according to Omroep Brabant. At the central bus station in Tilburg, some people who were unaware of the strike stood there this morning. In Twente and Limburg, about 70 percent of buses are running. In the Achterhoek, there are no cancellations at all. Collective agreement negotiations The strike was prompted by the failure of collective agreement negotiations. Drivers and conductors at operators such as Arriva, Keolis, Qbuzz, Transdev and EBS have been called on by the unions to lay down their work. Office staff are also joining the strike. Urban transport in Amsterdam (GVB) and The Hague (HTM) does not fall under regional transport. Buses, trams and metros are therefore running as normal there. In Rotterdam, no buses are running, but trams and metros are. In Utrecht, about a quarter of buses appear to be running. There are also fewer tram services. What is running and what is not? Operators find it difficult to indicate which buses and trains are running and which are not. For example, Keolis says on its own website: "We only know shortly in advance which buses/trains will be running". Transdev also simply says it does not yet know what will be achieved. Like other operators, Arriva advises travellers to check the journey planner shortly before departure. Trade unions CNV and FNV called for the nationwide strike last week. They believe that the operators' collective agreement proposals amount to a deterioration. The operators, for their part, say that their financial scope is limited and that public transport must remain affordable. The unions themselves demand, among other things, 9.5 percent additional salary over a period of two years and better working conditions for older staff. If the employers do not give in, the unions say strikes will take place on a different day each week from now on.

title: Wake-up call 14/10: Bus strikes across the country • Nord Stream bombing trial begins
lead: Good morning! Bus passengers, take note: due to strikes, fewer buses are running throughout the country today. And in Germany, the trial over the 2022 Nord Stream bombing begins today. First, the weather: it is dry, and especially this morning the sun is regularly visible. Now and then high cirrus clouds drift over. This afternoon cumulus clouds also appear. With a weak to moderate southwesterly wind, it will be 16 to 18 degrees. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The man found guilty of the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in the US must go to prison for 40 years. A judge yesterday set the sentence for Duane Davis (63). In August a jury already found it proven that Davis had planned the murder of Shakur. For decades all kinds of theories circulated about the murder of Shakur. Until Davis, a former gang member, spoke about his role in the shooting in interviews and in his 2019 memoir. Three years ago he was arrested. Davis is appealing. Other news from the night: And then just this: It was no longer really exciting after the 8-0 win on Saturday, but the Dutch women's footballers have now definitively qualified for the final round of the World Cup play-offs, next year. In Tilburg Hungary was again beaten: 3-0. In the last qualifying round Oranje plays two matches against Slovenia. The international break runs from 26 November up to and including 5 December, so by Sinterklaas evening at the latest Oranje will know whether the tickets to the World Cup can be booked. Missed goals? Watch our summary: Have a nice day!

title: Trial over Nord Stream attack starts today: 6 questions about 'sabotage of the century'
lead: The criminal trial against Ukrainian national Serhii K. begins today in Hamburg. He is charged with blowing up the Nord Stream pipelines between Russia and Germany in 2022. K. is alleged to have coordinated the sabotage of the most controversial energy project in Europe, on behalf of Ukraine. Because of its scale and impact, it is sometimes called "the sabotage of the century". Not everything about the background has been clarified yet. Was this, for example, an act of terrorism? Or were the pipelines a legitimate military target? And what role did the Ukrainian government play? Six questions and answers about the Nord Stream trial. How did K. go about it? In late summer 2022, the group around Ukrainian soldier Serhii K. rented an inconspicuous German sailing boat, the Andromeda, for several weeks, without a GPS tracker on board. From the port of Rostock, the ship then disappeared over the horizon for almost three weeks. During those days, in mid-September, divers from the group are alleged to have placed powerful explosives at several locations. A complicated job, at depths of tens of meters. "Professionals", according to the prosecutors. Before the explosives detonated, the group returned the yacht and left Germany. Shortly after 02.00 on the night of Monday 26 September 2022, powerful explosions were measured in the Baltic Sea. Gas bubbles became visible near the Danish island of Bornholm. The operation had succeeded: the explosions rendered three of the four pipes unusable. Nord Stream The Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany have been controversial since the start of the project in 2005. Poland and Ukraine lost revenue from gas transport. Germany benefited from cheap Russian gas, but became dependent on the whims of Moscow. This became clear after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. In response to EU sanctions, Russia stopped the gas supply via Nord Stream 1. Nord Stream 2 had not yet been put into use. The German government has since ruled out restoration and commissioning. What evidence is there? Images of the white van in which the saboteurs drove to and from the port eventually led investigators to K. At border checks, it turned out he had been checked using a forged but traceable passport. He did not, however, feel he was in danger. K. travelled to the Italian city of Rimini in 2025 and could thus be arrested. In the Italian cell, K. himself provided the most incriminating evidence. In a telephone conversation with his wife, he reportedly spoke, according to the prosecutors, about admitting the sabotage operation as an "official military operation". That was supposed to prevent his extradition to Germany. This conversation was intercepted and now serves as the basis of the charges. Beyond that, there are more indications than hard evidence. For example, K. had two different passports, a sign that there was something to hide. His internet behaviour is said to show that K. searched extensively for information about critical infrastructure, specifically in the area around the Nord Stream pipelines. His smartwatch was switched off around the time of the sabotage. What is K.'s defence? K.'s German lawyers reject all accusations. Regardless of whether K. was involved in the operation, his defence argues that the German court lacks jurisdiction. The sabotage is probably the work of a state, and therefore an individual cannot be held responsible, K.'s lawyer Ilona Menaker told NOS earlier. The lawyers want the court to also rule on whether the pipelines were allowed to be in operation at all or were a legitimate military target. K. is the only person on trial. One of the divers, Volodymyr Z., was previously arrested in Poland but not extradited. This summer he was arrested again, this time in Croatia, where he is said to have attended the filming of a Hollywood film about the Nord Stream sabotage. What role does the Ukrainian state play? The German prosecutors state that there are "sufficient suspicions" that the sabotage was carried out on the orders of the Ukrainian state. What evidence exists for this is not known. According to Der Spiegel, the operation was approved by then commander-in-chief Zaluzhnyi. The plans reportedly were drawn up by a group of former commandos of the Ukrainian army. President Zelensky reportedly was not informed, while the Dutch military intelligence service <entity id="org:militaire-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">MIVD</entity> reportedly was. The Netherlands had therefore already warned Germany and the US about the plans earlier, according to research by Nieuwsuur. Why is this case being heard in Germany? While Sweden and Denmark quickly discontinued their investigations, the German public prosecutor's office pressed on. Germany is treating the case very seriously, as the largest act of sabotage against German infrastructure since the Second World War. The pipelines were partly owned by German companies, and the operation was carried out from the German coast. The case causes a certain unease in political Berlin. Germany is Ukraine's most important ally. If involvement from Kyiv is proven, that would at the very least be painful for relations between the two countries. Pro-Russian parties such as the AfD and BSW want to stop supporting Ukraine, partly because of this issue. What sentence hangs over K.? Serhii K. is suspected of war crimes, causing explosions and damaging critical infrastructure, carrying a maximum sentence of fifteen years in prison. Hearing days are scheduled through February.

title: No cabinet plan yet on compensation for healthcare costs, uncertainty for chronically ill people
lead: What will happen with compensation for people with high healthcare costs? Today there is a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> on the healthcare budget, but it is still unclear how the cabinet wants to help chronically ill and disabled people. Because the first healthcare cut is due to be voted on at the end of this year, concern in this group is growing. "I find the uncertainty very annoying", says Bo Rijvers, who uses a wheelchair. "I know that blows will fall, but not yet how I am supposed to absorb them." Mainly uncertainty about the tax deduction It is mainly unclear how the tax deduction for healthcare costs will proceed. Under this scheme, people can claim costs for things like orthotic insoles, car adaptations and prostheses as a deduction and pay less tax. "For me that is 2000 to 3000 euros per year", says Rijvers. In the coalition agreement the cabinet agreed to scrap this scheme from 2028, because it is too complex and the money does not always actually reach chronically ill and disabled people. To compensate the low-income group for the healthcare cuts, 350 million euros has been reserved. But a concrete plan for how that money will be distributed still does not exist, while the Tweede Kamer has to vote on the budgets in a few weeks. "We are still studying it", says <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscal Affairs). A large majority of the Tweede Kamer asked the cabinet last month to examine whether the deduction for healthcare costs could be retained, but only for people who are truly chronically ill or disabled. Parties are mainly worried about the accumulation of cuts coming for this group in the coming years. For example, the cabinet plans to introduce a personal contribution for district nursing, to raise the own risk and to abolish domestic help under the Social Support Act (Wmo). Some people will as a result lose hundreds of euros per month, Nibud calculated earlier . Other consequences are also still unclear. Stopping the deduction could, for example, mean that chronically ill and disabled people receive less allowance. "You of course have to look at how we pay for the rising healthcare costs", says ChristenUnie-<entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">fractieleider Bikker</entity>, who submitted a motion on it. "But it cannot be that a group of people who already have it harder disproportionately pays the bill." Pro thinks the uncertainty is lasting too long. "People know their healthcare bill is going up, but not yet whether they will be compensated for it", says Kamerlid Julian Bushoff. Various political parties have little confidence that 350 million is enough for the new scheme, but staatssecretaris Eerenberg thinks it is. He says there are still many people using the schemes, while financially that does not need to be the case. He wants the money to be used only for chronically ill people who really need it. The target group will thereby become smaller, "so we think we should be able to get by with that amount." 'Kept me awake' Rijvers finds it mainly annoying that there has been so much uncertainty since the presentation of the coalition agreement. "At first it really kept me awake", he says. "But now that they don't know it themselves either, I think: why all this panic? I can't follow it." Eerenberg has let it be known that he will come up with a plan for the healthcare cost deduction within a month. The question is whether the Tweede Kamer can agree to it then. Several parties hinted that they could otherwise remove that measure from the Tax Plan, so that there is no vote on it at all this year. In that case the current deduction would certainly remain in place up to and including 2028.

title: Good third quarter for ASML, further growth expected
lead: Dutch chip machine maker ASML has a successful third quarter behind it. Moreover, the company says it is already seeing interest from customers in ordering chip machines for the coming few years. "Many conversations with customers are now about the period after 2027," says CEO Christophe Fouquet at the presentation of the quarterly figures. ASML is benefiting enormously from investments in artificial intelligence and other technology that requires chips. ASML customers expect that they themselves cannot meet demand for chips until at least 2028, says Fouquet. "For us, that means more demand in the short term." According to its own account, ASML has already received many orders for 2028. "But there is also great interest in placing orders now for 2029 and sometimes even 2030." This means ASML has to work hard to meet demand for its chip machines. Three months ago the company said it must increase its capacity for EUV machines. ASML is the only company in the world that can make chip machines with this technology, which works with extreme ultraviolet light. The company earlier expressed the ambition to have 30 percent more capacity for these machines in 2027 than this year. In 2028 another 30 percent should be added on top of that. "But to be honest, it is becoming increasingly clear that 30 percent in 2027 and 30 percent in 2028 will not ensure that we can meet the demand from our customers," says Fouquet now. Sharp rise in profit. The sales of EUV machines are the biggest driver of the higher revenue and profit that ASML is booking. Over the past three months the company sold for 11.6 billion euros, partly through sales of new machines and upgrades of existing machines. Profit in the last quarter came to almost 5 billion euros. That is considerably more than in the same period in recent years: then the profit in the third quarter was consistently around 2 billion euros. "All in all, I would say it was a very, very strong quarter," Fouquet said. So far in 2026 ASML has made over 10.6 billion euros in profit. The company expects to ship 65 machines to customers this year, 50 percent more than last year. The company is also working on upgrades to its machines, so that customers can make more chips in the same period. ASML's customers include chipmakers TSMC, Samsung and Intel. ASML is one of the largest companies in the world and is of considerable importance to the Dutch economy. The Dutch chip industry has grown enormously in recent years, partly thanks to ASML, and provides tens of thousands of jobs. American bill. Alongside the challenge of meeting demand from the chip industry, ASML still faces an American bill that could practically halt the company's business in China. Supporters of the bill want to prevent ASML from supplying or maintaining its chip machines for China. ASML's financial chief Roger Dassen hopes that the American Congress will realise after the midterm elections in November that the proposal is not a good idea, reports ANP. In June, <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">minister Sjoerdsma</entity> of Foreign Trade already travelled to the US to discuss his concerns. He says the law will precisely ensure that China copies Western technology faster. China is expected this year to account for around 20 percent of ASML's business, the company says today.

title: Body 'forgotten' Frenchman has been lying in morgue in Toulouse for 14 years
lead: At the university hospital of Toulouse, a body has been found that had been lying in the morgue for about fourteen years. The regional newspaper La Dépêche discovered this. The man died in 2012 in his house in the village of Castelnau-d'Auzan. He was 58 years old. "We received a phone call on 1 October", says the mayor of Castelnau-d'Auzan to La Dépêche. "I thought it was a joke." After the autopsy in 2013, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had already ordered that the body be released so that a funeral could be arranged. But the Frenchman's body never left the morgue. No family had reported itself. Therefore, it was the municipality's task to finish the matter. The municipality says it had received no response from the morgue at that point. Another scandal The body was found at the beginning of this month during an inspection of the cold rooms at the Hôpital Rangueil. That inspection of the morgue took place as part of an investigation by the Public Prosecution Service. According to the newspaper Sud Ouest, this was because of the discovery, at the end of last month, of the remains of two newborn babies and two foetuses. These lay in a container with medical waste from the morgue. Lonely The Frenchman is described as a lonely man. He was divorced, had no children and died a natural death. One of his neighbours raised the alarm at the time, when the man had not been seen for some time. A search has nevertheless been started to find relatives of the man.

title: Eighteen Ajax supporters arrested in Croatia, 'they had weapons on them'
lead: In the Croatian city of Split, eighteen Ajax supporters were arrested yesterday, Croatian media report. Photos and videos of the arrests are circulating on social media. The Amsterdam club plays an away match against Hajduk Split in the Conference League tomorrow. Footage from news site Tportal, among others, shows the supporters being arrested on a terrace in the centre of Split, after which they are taken away in police vans. Bladed weapons were reportedly found on the fans. Stone blocks can be seen on the terrace tables. According to Croatian media, it was a preventive action and the aim was to prevent the Ajax supporters from clashing with supporters of the home club, NH Nieuws reports. Physically attacked: The Ajax supporters' association reports that fans were attacked by supporters of Hajduk Split. Ajax also writes that it has received multiple reports this morning of "Ajax supporters who have been intimidated or physically attacked in Split". Taxi drivers reportedly passed on to Hajduk's hardcore group that they were transporting Ajax supporters, after which they are waiting for them when they get out. "In some cases their luggage has been searched for club symbols", the club writes. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is said to be aware and to be present in greater numbers at the airport and in the city. "Please stay alert for your own safety", the club advises. Ajax had already warned its own fans in advance about safety risks. "Supporters of Hajduk Split are known for their fanatical following and may react to visible Ajax symbols or recognisable groups of Ajax supporters", the club said earlier. The match between Ajax and Hajduk Split will be played tomorrow at 18:45.

title: Tree of the year is red beech in Middelstum
lead: The red beech by the entrance of the Sint-Hippolytuskerk in Middelstum (<entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>) won the public vote for Tree of the Year. The tree, more than 150 years old, received nearly 3000 more votes than the number two, which stands in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>. The election is organised by the SBNL Natuurfonds. With the prize, the fund wants to draw attention to beautiful, special or monumental trees, or trees that are significant for their surroundings and community. Last year the mammoth tree in the Abraham Ledeboerpark in <entity id="org:gemeente-enschede">Enschede</entity> was named Tree of the Year. The beech was already chosen in a preliminary round as the most beautiful tree in the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>. In the national final, the tree received 6721 votes, RTV Noord reports. Hoping for offspring: member of the local church committee Mark van Dijken views the prize with mixed feelings: "Our red beech is having a pretty hard time. Just look at how many beechnuts are lying around. It is producing extra many, in the hope of offspring." According to Miriam van der Waart, green manager at Groninger Kerken, the beeches in the churchyard of Middelstum are suffering from prolonged drought and changing climate conditions. "That is exactly why this recognition is so special. It shows how much this tree means to Middelstum, but also how vulnerable our green heritage is", says Van der Waart.

title: Dolfinarium must work towards an end to dolphins in captivity
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> considers keeping dolphins in pools such as those at the Dolfinarium in Harderwijk untenable. But for now there is no decision to close the Dolfinarium. However, a formal breeding ban will come in two years, and dolphins may still be imported to a limited extent. That is stated in a letter from <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. An immediate ban on keeping dolphins in captivity is not desirable, says Erkens. It would mean that the 22 bottlenose dolphins in the Dolfinarium would have to be killed because they cannot survive in the wild. Erkens does not consider that an option. But in the long term, an end must come to this practice, he says. "Dolphins are intelligent animals that must be continually challenged and have a natural need to dive deep and swim long distances," says Erkens. "That cannot be offered in captivity. Living in chlorinated pools can also cause health problems." No new dolphins Erkens is working towards what he calls "phasing out the keeping of dolphins in captivity". This means that no new dolphins may be born in the Netherlands. Dolphins from outside the Netherlands may be imported, but this must not lead to "a population that rejuvenates itself permanently". The ultimate goal is that at some point no dolphins will be kept in captivity in the Netherlands. Erkens says this policy is not aimed against the Dolfinarium, but is related to the public debate about dolphins that must live in pools. The Dolfinarium disagrees with the cabinet decision and wants to talk with Erkens. "In practice, it means keeping males and females separate or giving animals long-term contraception," says a statement. "That may affect their social life and natural behaviour, and long-term contraception can carry health risks."

title: Again one-way traffic for shipping on the IJssel due to low water level
lead: Since this morning, shipping on the IJssel between IJsselkop and Zutphen may again only sail in one direction. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> has reinstated the measure due to the low water level. As a result, ships must again make a detour of around 300 kilometres. On Monday, the one-way traffic was still lifted, because the minimum measured depth on the Boven-IJssel had reached the required 1.45 metres. Because less rain has fallen than expected, the water level has dropped below that threshold again, reports Rijkswaterstaat. Inland shipping may now only sail upstream. Ships wanting to enter the IJssel from Germany therefore cannot sail towards Zutphen at Arnhem. They must make a detour via Amsterdam and the IJsselmeer. The one-way traffic also affects inland shipping towards the Twente Canal, writes RTV Oost. Skippers can no longer sail directly to the canal from either direction and must therefore make a detour. Water level continues to fall. Rijkswaterstaat expects the water level to fall further over the next five days. That depends, among other things, on the amount of water entering the Netherlands via the Rhine at Lobith. Rain in Germany and Switzerland may cause water levels to rise again. Water levels are therefore being closely monitored. If they change, the measures for shipping may also be adjusted.

title: Former mayor Schuiling convicted again for masturbating, gets fine
lead: Former <entity id="pos:burgemeester-groningen">burgemeester van Groningen</entity> Koen Schuiling must pay 250 euros for what is officially called schennispleging. The court of appeal in <entity id="org:gemeente-zwolle">Zwolle</entity> finds it proven that he masturbated in his car in March 2024. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded a fine of 250 euros. That is the same amount Schuiling was ordered to pay by the district court last year. The former mayor has always maintained that he was not masturbating. That is why he appealed. Schuiling was mayor of Groningen between 2019 and 2024. He stepped down before the end of his term after what he called an "extremely intensive period". Dagblad van het Noorden wrote that minister Uitermark of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> put pressure on Schuiling because of the matter. If he did not announce his departure, the ministry would suspend him. The mayor would then have decided to stop. The ministry tells NOS that Schuiling did not leave under pressure. Driver's statement The case against Schuiling started after a statement from a lorry driver. He had stated that from his cab he could see the mayor masturbating in his car, while the interior light was on. The two vehicles, according to the lorry driver, were near each other for some time. The OM considered the driver's statement reliable, and so did the court. In this regard the court points out that the driver had a good view of Schuiling's car and that the man always gave a detailed and consistent statement. Also, according to the court, there is no reason to assume the driver wanted to set Schuiling up. Stomach pain 'not credible' Schuiling has always firmly denied that he was masturbating. He argued that since 2022 he has suffered from sudden, severe stomach pain and that he had it at that moment. For that reason he would have undone his belt and rubbed his stomach. The court does not believe that. According to the court, Schuiling has not always given the same statement. He initially stated that he had his trousers open because he needed to pee, later Schuiling said he had a lot of stomach pain. In principle the statement of one witness is not enough for a conviction, but the court finds so-called corroborating evidence in an audio recording of the lorry driver. On it can be heard that the driver angrily confronts Schuiling at the exit. Schuiling then responds that he had to pee. Furthermore, the court points out that the former mayor did state that he was in the car and that the interior light was on. Together that makes the evidence sufficient, the court holds.

title: Three more arrests for fatal shooting incident at the Four Days Marches festivities in Nijmegen
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has made three new arrests in the investigation into the fatal shooting incident during the Four Days Marches festivities in Nijmegen. They concern an 18-year-old man from Zwaag, a minor boy from Hoorn and a 19-year-old man from Avenhorn. On Monday the police announced that they had arrested a 19-year-old Amsterdammer and a 21-year-old man from Hoorn in connection with the shooting. The suspects remain in custody, Omroep Gelderland writes . On Tuesday 21 July, around 22.00 hours, an 18-year-old man from Rotterdam was shot dead on the Graafseweg. That happened not far from the Four Days Marches festivities, which were under way in the city at that time. That same evening an 18-year-old fellow townsperson was arrested. He was released again a day later and is no longer a suspect. The motive for the shooting is still being investigated. The police therefore no longer provide information about exactly what the suspects are suspected of.

title: Arrests and raid at Turkish opposition channel Halk TV: 'Black day for Turkey'
lead: Turkish authorities raided the headquarters of opposition broadcaster Halk TV in Istanbul this morning. This is one of the most popular channels among the opposition. Critics therefore say the raid is politically motivated. According to the channel, hundreds of police officers entered the building around 06:30 local time. Images circulating on social media show staff filming the officers. Access to the premises has been closed off and live broadcasts have been stopped. A repeat is being aired. Turkish authorities have appointed a trustee to run the channel. 'Unfounded' The Turkish Public Prosecutor's Office suspects the channel's chairman, Cafer Mahiroglu, of bribery, money laundering and fraud. Mahiroglu lives in the United Kingdom and has not been arrested. As part of the investigation into him, Turkish authorities have issued arrest warrants against seventeen other people. According to Mahiroglu, these include some of his family members. Eleven suspects have since been arrested. In a video message on X, Mahiroglu condemns the raid. He calls it politically motivated and speaks of a "black day for Turkey". Mahiroglu denies the accusations, which he calls "unfounded". According to him, the raid shows how the judiciary in Turkey is being misused for political gain. It is the fifth time in twenty months that Turkish police have raided a television channel and a new trustee has taken over the channel. This also happened to Flash TV, EKOTÜRK, Habertürk and Tele1. The reasons Turkish authorities gave for these differ. Press freedom organisations and critics have long feared that independent journalism in Turkey is coming under ever greater pressure. Turkish opposition leader Özgür Özel reacted sharply to the raid. The leader of the Yeni Parti (New Party) calls the authorities' actions "weak and cowardly" and says they go against democratic principles. The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGS) also strongly condemns the action. The association calls the decision "arbitrary" and states that journalists in Turkey must be able to do their work freely, without government censorship. Gezi protests Halk TV was founded in 2004. For a long time the channel was closely tied to the largest Turkish opposition party, CHP. Due to a split within the opposition, the channel is now associated with Özgür Özel's New Party. The channel gained nationwide fame during the Gezi Park protests in 2013. While many major Turkish channels, including CNN Türk, paid hardly any attention to the mass demonstrations, Halk TV kept reporting. As a result, the channel grew into an important platform and mouthpiece for the Turkish opposition. Since then Halk TV has regularly been fined by the Turkish media watchdog. The reasons included, among other things, critical remarks about the government made by guests on the channel. In Reporters Without Borders' annual World Press Freedom Index, Turkey dropped from 159th to 163rd place out of 180 countries this year. Turkey thus belongs to the countries with the worst scores for press freedom. Muzzling Opposition in Turkey has also been under enormous pressure for a year and a half. A large corruption investigation is underway into hundreds of people with ties to the opposition. Several mayors, officials and prominent members are in custody. The removed mayor of Istanbul, Ekrem Imamoglu, is also still in custody. Last July, several more CHP mayors were arrested. The government says the judiciary operates independently. The opposition sees things very differently. It believes the investigation and police actions are being used to silence them and eliminate political opponents.

title: Family of Ivana Smit receives no compensation, and no new investigation in Malaysia
lead: The authorities of Malaysia do not have to pay compensation after all to the parents of Ivana Smit, who died in 2017. Last year a court ruled that serious mistakes were made in the investigation into the death of the 18-year-old Dutch model. That ruling has now been overturned on appeal. The news has hit Smit's relatives hard. "There have been serious shortcomings established in the police investigation into her death, but the government nevertheless manages to escape liability," lawyer Sébas Diekstra says on behalf of the family in a statement. "For them this is once again a particularly painful blow in a struggle that has been going on far too long." Suspicious circumstances The ruling on appeal is the latest twist in the case, which has now been going on for almost nine years. The 18-year-old died under suspicious circumstances in the capital Kuala Lumpur after she went home with an American couple. Initially Smit's mysterious death was treated as an accident. Almost two years later the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> nevertheless opened a murder investigation , but it never led to a conviction. Dismissal The family filed a lawsuit against the authorities in 2020. Last year the victim's mother was ruled in the right. The judge ruled that damages of the equivalent of almost a quarter million euros had to be paid. At the same time the judge ordered the police to dismiss the officer in charge of the investigation into Smit's death and to reopen the investigation. But the Court of Appeal has now ruled that judgment unlawful. Supervision of police investigations is reserved for the executive branch and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the court said. "The court must respect the separation of powers." 'Corruption' Lawyer Diekstra calls this turn of events scandalous. "This is exactly the kind of ruling that a corrupt or incompetent government can make very good use of." According to him the ruling on appeal sends the message that the police can get away with serious mistakes. According to Diekstra the family does not yet intend to give up the legal fight. It is possible to challenge the court's ruling at the highest court in the country, but first permission must be requested from this Federal Court. This option is currently being considered.

title: Five years in prison for drunk man who ran over 4-year-old child in Maastricht
lead: A 30-year-old man from Maastricht has been sentenced to five years in prison for causing a fatal traffic accident in which a 4-year-old boy died. He drove more than 60 kilometres per hour over the limit within the built-up area and had more than 3.5 times the alcohol in his blood that is permitted. The sentence imposed by the <entity id="org:rechtbank-limburg">rechtbank Limburg</entity> is equal to the demand of the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM). The court rules that reckless driving is the cause of the fatal accident. On 27 March, the convicted man, the 30-year-old Janus K. from Maastricht, drove 112 kilometres per hour within the built-up area, where 50 kilometres per hour was permitted. Around 19:10 a mother and her 4-year-old son Djorginyo got out of a bus. The woman put her child in a pushchair and wanted to cross the Dorpstraat. Before they reached the other side, they were hit by K., who was driving with a passenger in a borrowed black Mazda. The boy died a day later from his injuries. The mother was seriously injured. She suffered, among other things, a concussion, a broken neck vertebra and multiple fractures in her pelvis and right lower leg. She has permanent injuries. Without reason: Before the ride, K. said he had drunk seven glasses of beer with a friend in a café. While drinking, K. and his friend decided without reason to "go for a drive". The court finds this very difficult to understand, the verdict states. "What is especially worrying is that he stated that he himself thought he was not driving too fast." Blood tests after the accident showed that K. had 1.8 per mille alcohol in his blood, while the legal limit is 0.5 per mille. That corresponds to roughly eight glasses of beer. The man previously struggled with alcohol problems. He was in treatment for that, but stopped a detox programme a few months before the accident. He had not previously come into contact with the justice system for this type of offence. Living with a lifelong emptiness: The moving victim statements during the hearing show how irreparable the grief of the next of kin is. "When I woke up from the coma, I heard that my child was dead," said the mother. "I have to live on with physical limitations because of the accident, but these visible consequences pale next to the scar on my heart and the loss of my child. Since that night I have to live with a lifelong emptiness." The father stated that he cannot comprehend that his little son will never come home again. "A part of me died with him. He was my best little friend. People say that life goes on, but not for me." According to forensic research, K. could have prevented the collision if he had kept to the maximum speed. He could then still have stopped in time. The court therefore fully attributes the accident to him.

title: House of Representatives wants to curb experiments with small schools
lead: The law that makes it easier to set up a new school will be tightened again within five years, because too many small schools are being added. An example is the Renaissanceschool in Almere, which started this year with only four pupils. The school is closely linked to the political party Forum voor Democratie (FVD). <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> had already written to the House of Representatives that she wants to do something about the growth. "It is no longer sustainable to keep so many small schools running", she said. In a debate today she promised to take another close look at the market research that new schools must carry out in advance to gauge parents' interest in the neighbourhood. The coalition parties (D66, VVD and CDA) and several opposition parties have serious doubts about that market research, which would actually be no more than an online survey. The people filling it in often would not know exactly what kind of school it is. In part this is how the so-called FVD school, which opened its doors in August, was able to get approval. Beforehand it was measured that around 350 people were positive about its arrival, and that number counted for a large part in the approval of the school. Tielen wants to "look at whether we should tighten that part of the law or remove it entirely". She admitted that she too was surprised when only four children turned up at the new school in Almere. Innovative educational ideas The More Room for New Schools Act, an initiative of the VVD, came into effect in 2021. The law is meant to make it easier to start a school with government subsidy based on innovative educational ideas or a life or religious conviction. FVD voted against the law at the time. Since its introduction, more schools are founded every year, a large part of them Islamic. Political parties may also set up a new school under this law, provided there is sufficient interest and the educational requirements are met. According to a large part of the House of Representatives, there is a lot to criticise about the Renaissanceschool on that last point. It assumes, for example, that boys and girls need a different form of education. "Why I am so angry about this", said D66 MP Rooderkerk, "is that we are talking about 4-year-old children who may be indoctrinated by the FVD. Our education is meant to teach children to read and write and arithmetic, and to learn to form their own opinions. It must not be an experiment by a political party." 'Future ruined' Pro, for example, is also angry about the number of schools that are added too easily. That leads to segregation, competition and poor quality, says MP Moorman. She said there is not so much a need for more schools as for good schools. She also believes that children must not be used for experiments "who are now attending schools that will completely ruin their future and school career". Tielen said she sympathises with the concerns in the House, but so far sees no reason to intervene at the Renaissanceschool. She pointed out that at the start of the fourth school year the school must have at least 139 pupils, and otherwise must close at the end of that school year. "That will be quite a challenge", according to her. During the debate, VVD MP Kisteman announced a further private member's bill to allow earlier intervention at schools that underperform. In his view, such schools should be able to be closed much sooner if they perform poorly. News programme Nieuwsuur made this report about the Renaissanceschool in Almere on the first school day:

title: Police and Public Prosecution Service invite Ahold to file a report about 'cybersecurity incident'
lead: The police and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> say they have invited parent company Ahold to file a report about the hacking attack, or attempted attack, at Albert Heijn. Such a call is not often made publicly. A police press release states that there is currently no criminal investigation into the attack on the supermarket chain. The police write that there has been contact with Ahold, but that did not lead to a report. The company, which itself still speaks of a "cybersecurity incident", says in a written response that it is "cooperating with all relevant authorities". No explanation is given for why a report has not been filed so far. Ahold says it cannot make any further statements at this time. As soon as possible The police and the Public Prosecution Service emphasise the importance of a report in the press release. "To be able to investigate and prosecute successfully, it is crucial to always receive information from victims as quickly as possible", the press release states. The National Unit for Investigation and Interventions of the police says it has nothing to add to the appeal at this time. The Public Prosecution Service says it is waiting to see what happens. Ahold did report the incident to the National Cyber Security Centre, as the law requires. A criminal investigation can also be started without a report, in which case it is 'ex officio'. That is how the police and the Public Prosecution Service began a criminal investigation after a data leak at a laboratory in Rijswijk without a report having been filed.

title: Serious sexual violence against women in internment camps after WWII
lead: Thousands of Dutch women who were interned in camps after the Second World War were raped, tortured and humiliated by their guards. This is shown by witness statements that ended up in a drawer and have only now been examined by the NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies. The images of Dutch girls and women who were shaved bald after the Second World War because they were supposed to have associated with Germans during the occupation, had a relationship with them or collaborated, are burned into the minds of many. They were called 'moffenmeiden' instead of collaborators. Interrogations from 1950 That thousands of them were locked up in camps after the war and faced serious sexual violence there hardly features in the standard works on the war. Studies have been made of the shaving of the women's heads, but only for about fifteen years have historians known the testimonies about the camps. That is remarkable, because the interrogation reports of women held in this kind of internment camp have existed since 1950. Some of them were interrogated that year by former police inspector Johanna van Schilfgaarde of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> as part of the parliamentary inquiry into Dutch government policy in the war years. Historian and journalist Ewoud Kieft carried out research for the NIOD into these witness reports. He came across the statements while working on a series of background articles on the special legal procedure, the special legal system in the Netherlands after the Second World War. In his article published today he describes how women were raped and humiliated on a large scale, among others by the camp guards. The prisoners were penetrated with objects and their vaginas were roughly examined without medical necessity. The historian also describes testimonies in which women state that guards made them false promises of acquittal, reduced sentences or food in exchange for sex. Because prisoners were suffering from malnutrition, this was quite a means of pressure. Those promises usually turned out to be worthless. Yet the chief investigator of this commission, Arnaud Marie baron van Tuyl van Serooskerken, did not mention these testimonies at all in his final report from 1950. He even made it seem as if no witnesses willing to speak had been found, because the women would have been too afraid. "There is no evidence that women were raped", he wrote in his report. "Nevertheless, it cannot be ruled out that it did happen, because victims may not wish to make a statement about it." Because the report says nothing about the testimonies, which do indeed exist, the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> never accounted for them. Negligent "I have not yet been able to establish whether the chief investigator deliberately left out the testimonies", Kieft tells the NOS. "But he was very negligent. This was not simply careless, it was irresponsible. He did not do his job", the historian says. Police inspector Van Schilfgaarde then brought her remaining documents to The Hague, where they were stored in various depots of the Ministry of Justice. There they remained untouched until they were transferred to the <entity id="org:nationaal-archief">Nationaal Archief</entity>. Other journalists and historians consulted the documents now and then since then, but no structural attention was paid to the sexual abuses in the camps. Victims not safe Kieft writes in his article that shortly after the war the Netherlands did not have a well-functioning legal system. "The Dutch government had been absent during the war and the police had worked for the Nazi regime", the historian explains. "So few people remained who could enforce the law and administer justice. There was popular rage about what had happened during the war, and a group of people wanted to assert themselves after the liberation." Kieft speaks of "wild arrests", in which women were picked up after gossip that they had a relationship with a German soldier. "Those women must have felt so alone." Victims did not dare to raise the sexual violence done to them in court, for fear of not being believed, he says. "They ran a great risk, it was not safe." The testimonies he has examined so far are "the tip of the iceberg", he says. In total there were more than 200 such camps. Kieft therefore also wants to do further research to map out the violence against women in internment camps. Second World War newsletter Interested in the Second World War?
