Asylum minister <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> said earlier that he aims for this, but could not make firm commitments. Today, those did not come either. According to Eerdmans, the cabinet does not want to "budge" on this. If that remains the case, according to Eerdmans it will be over, and in his view "they must" "go over to the left". The cabinet, by contrast, says it keeps aiming for broad support from both left-wing and right-wing parties. Other parties too, including BBB and SGP, are linking their support for the tax plan to other demands. What <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> thinks of this he made clear when he today called on parties to let the negotiations on the tax plan "really be about that plan". According to Jetten, the cabinet has many plans that "are better for people and businesses", and hopes the opposition will mainly want to look at those. This weekend it became known that the cabinet has agreed internally on how it wants to meet the opposition halfway. It announced it would again sit down at the table with seven parties: Pro, JA21, BBB, SGP, ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Volt: BBB earlier repeated that, without "significant adjustments" to the nitrogen plans, the party cannot give support to the tax plan. According to BBB-<entity id="person:hendrik-vermeer">fractievoorzitter Vermeer</entity>, small adjustments are not sufficient. "Making a bad plan a little less bad" is not something you can agree to, says Vermeer. BBB and JA21 both feel the cabinet still is not making clear choices. Vermeer calls the amount of 350 million that the cabinet now wants to set aside to soften the planned tax increases a "drop in the ocean". Time is pressing. The tax plan is important for the cabinet, because it sets out how taxes will be arranged in the coming years. This year, for example, the cabinet plans to extend the reduction of the excise duty on petrol and diesel by 1 year, to the end of 2027. It also wants to implement a reduction of the starter's deduction for entrepreneurs. Time is pressing. Because the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> needs time to implement these measures, the tax plan cannot be postponed for too long. The aim is for it to be voted on on 12 November. Tomorrow, talks with, among others, 50Plus, BBB and PRO and Volt are on the agenda. The cabinet also warned today that if the Tax Plan is voted down, matters such as the excise cut on petrol will also be off the table. Box 3. There is also still no solution for the wealth tax (box 3). The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> majority agrees with the plan that <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> has for this, but it remains unclear how it is to be paid for. A plan to have 'smaller' savers and investors pay for it was withdrawn by the cabinet after criticism. D66, VVD and CDA are reportedly in agreement on new funding, but a majority in both the Eerste and Tweede Kamer still needs to be found for that too.

title: Romania: sabotage network directed by Russian secret service uncovered
lead: Romania's intelligence service says it has uncovered a sabotage network coordinated by Russia. According to the service, the group set a fire in September close to a Romanian state-owned company that produces weapons. The Romanian news site Digi24 writes that the intelligence services believe the network was directly controlled by the Russian secret service. That service had given the group a list of targets. These included state-owned and private companies producing weapons, and other targets "of military and industrial importance", according to the intelligence service. Those targets were not only in Romania but also in other EU countries. Which EU countries has not been disclosed. A Ukrainian and two Belarusians are linked to the network and are being prosecuted for attempted sabotage. Two of them were arrested in Germany, where, according to the Romanian public prosecutor, they were engaged in similar actions. The third was arrested in Poland. The Romanian authorities will request the transfer of the suspects. Hybrid actions Last month the security services of Estonia announced that, in their view, Russia was behind an arson attack at a defence company in the capital Tallinn. That company supplies weapons to Ukraine. Intelligence services across Europe, including the Netherlands, have been warning for some time that the threat of Russian hybrid activities has increased. For example, the services suspect that Russia is responsible for, among other things, arson, disrupting air traffic with drones and damaging undersea cables. In hybrid warfare a country tries to weaken an opponent without starting a war. The aim is to cause unrest, undermine trust in governments and thus sow division. Russia consistently denies accusations of sabotage in Europe.

title: After persistent protests, France announces measures for better education
lead: The French government is announcing measures to improve education. For example, 5 billion euros is being set aside for the renovation of school buildings and universities, say education ministers Geffray and Baptiste. The measures follow persistent mass protests. Pupils are taking action against problems in education, such as dilapidated school buildings, overcrowded classes, a shortage of teachers and high workloads. Earlier today President Macron said that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> would meet the 'legitimate demands' of the demonstrators. The money for renovating school buildings will be made available to local governments. It mainly concerns loans. Furthermore, ministers Geffray and Baptiste promise to make 15,000 extra places available in higher education. This should give more pupils the chance to study. The French Parcoursup system for admission to higher education is also being adjusted. Students criticise unclear selection criteria and unequal opportunities. They say that as a result they cannot follow their desired studies. The education ministers promise that the system will become more transparent and will be replaced in 2028. For secondary schools, a maximum of 28 pupils per class in la Seconde will be introduced. That is the first year of the upper school of secondary education, which corresponds to the fourth year in the Netherlands. In cities, more than 35 pupils often sit in a class in la Seconde now. To make smaller classes possible, 500 extra teachers will be hired. Pupils continue to demonstrate. Geffray and Baptiste met this afternoon with Prime Minister Lecornu and representatives of secondary schools and universities. Pupils' trade unions then announced that they are pleased with the announced measures, but feel they are not enough. "Not everything has been solved yet." They therefore call on pupils to demonstrate again this coming Saturday. Protests have been going on in France for weeks. The persistent actions by pupils for improvements in education have grown into a broader protest with trade unions, farmers and the opposition movement of the yellow vests. Last weekend hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across the country. The protests often start peacefully, but troublemakers and looters change the atmosphere. On 17 October, demonstrations in several cities escalated into riots, looting and arson. Hundreds of millions of euros in damage was caused. More than 2300 people were arrested. To prevent new violence, last week the right to demonstrate was considerably restricted. For example, a curfew applies in various places in the country. Also, 70,000 officers were deployed at this weekend's protests. According to Minister Nuñez of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, new looting has been prevented by police action. 'Saturday will be a risky day' Earlier today President Macron warned that Saturday will again be a 'risky day', just like 5 November. On that day the trade unions have planned a nationwide action. Macron says demonstrators should again not come into city centres then. It cannot be ruled out that a state of emergency will be declared, Macron says. If that happens, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> can carry out preventive searches and demonstrators can be ordered to stay at home. The education ministers hope that the announced measures will calm things down and stress that the plans will actually be carried out. "They are not empty promises."

title: Court of Audit: Rent in Rotterdam remains too high despite municipality's efforts
lead: Many private landlords in Rotterdam still ask far too high rent, despite the municipality's efforts to do something about it. That is the conclusion of the Rotterdam Court of Audit, which examined the municipality's approach since the introduction of the Affordable Rent Act. To protect people from excessive rent, the Affordable Rent Act has existed since July 2024. A points system now determines how much the homeowner may ask for a house or room. As a result, the rent is in many cases lower than what the landlord wants to charge. With the introduction of the law, the municipality has gained more options to tackle excessive rent prices. The municipality can give a landlord who asks too much a warning and ultimately also fine them. But before the municipality can intervene, tenants must first report to the municipality that they are paying too much. Few reports from tenants. In Rotterdam there are about 213,000 rental homes. Nearly 7 in 10 of these are owned by housing associations. The rest belong to private owners. The municipality tried to persuade tenants through a campaign and home visits to report if they pay too much rent. The Court of Audit's research shows that only a few tenants have done so. Until March this year, only 212 reports came in. Of those reports, few have led to rent reductions: in total, the rent of only 34 homes has been lowered. Disappointing results. The Court of Audit finds the results disappointing. Relative to the results, the approach is labour-intensive and expensive, according to the Court of Audit: "Every euro of rent reduction costs the municipality 95 euros." A majority of tenants still cannot find the municipality's reporting point. The Court of Audit's survey shows that only 30 percent of tenants have some idea where to go if they pay too much rent. There is also another reason why few reports are made. "The worse the behaviour of the landlord, the lower the willingness of tenants to report. These are precisely the tenants who must be protected by the law," says director Sjoerd Keulen. "We see that reports fail to come in, often because of fear of the consequences, little trust in the government, or intimidation by the landlord." 'Cautious approach' As long as no report is made, a landlord who does not comply with the law remains out of reach, the Court of Audit says. "While the municipality informally knows which landlords systematically break the law." For example, Rotterdam suspects that in the Carnisse district, where many migrant workers live, at least 60 percent of tenants pay too much rent or live in terrible conditions. If a violation is found, the municipality chooses a cautious approach, according to the Court of Audit. While the research was ongoing, the municipality did not take over any homes from landlords. No fines have been imposed either. "Because of this approach, it pays for a landlord not to comply with the Affordable Rent Act." Court of Audit wants a stricter approach. The Court of Audit recommends actively tackling systematic offenders. Moreover, heavier measures should be applied more quickly in the case of violations. Attention should also be paid to tenants who get into trouble after making a report, the Court of Audit advises. The city administration almost fully adopts the recommendations. For example, enforcement was tightened just before the summer, the responsible alderman Kockelkoren told regional broadcaster Rijnmond. "Everyone in Rotterdam deserves a safe and affordable place to live," she says. "Yet there are still tenants who pay too much or face discrimination and intimidation. That is unacceptable."

title: Flávio Bolsonaro says he may not leave Brazil: 'It is an attempt at intimidation'
lead: Brazilian senator and former presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro says the federal police have ordered him to hand in his passports. The son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro speaks of an 'atrocity' intended to intimidate him. Bolsonaro junior says he was approached by the police after visiting his father, who is under house arrest. "I was ordered to hand in my passports. I was also forbidden to leave the country," Bolsonaro says in a video on social media. This reportedly happened on the orders of a judge of the Supreme Federal Court following statements by Flávio's brother. Eduardo Bolsonaro said last week that Flávio could do better to leave the country if he lost the presidential election, but Flávio says he will not do that. "I have never considered leaving the country. I will hand in my passports and defend myself against this atrocity." Refuses to accept defeat. On Sunday it became known that the far-right Bolsonaro had lost the presidential election. The victory went to the left-wing incumbent president Lula, who received almost 52 percent of the votes. Bolsonaro refuses to accept his defeat and wants the result declared invalid. In a short speech after the result was announced, Bolsonaro pointed to the decision of the Supreme Federal Court to keep the polling stations open for two hours longer. Bolsonaro calls that "unacceptable", which is remarkable. He had himself asked for a longer voting period because some voters had difficulty reaching the polling station due to heavy rain. On Monday Bolsonaro again criticised keeping the polling stations open longer. "What happened in those two hours must be clarified. Nobody knows exactly what the consequences are," he said. Brazilian media report that around 34,000 votes were cast in those two hours. That seems to have made little difference to the result. Lula received over 4 million more votes than Bolsonaro. Lula's Army: The elections were a neck-and-neck race. The first round was won by Bolsonaro. Afterwards, supporters of Lula, mainly many young people, began to mobilise. In groups they took to the streets to win over the undecided voter. Online campaigning on social media was also in full swing. Via WhatsApp nearly 11 million people were mobilised under the name "Lula's Army". They were asked to help Lula with his campaign. After the first round, Lula's team concluded that their messages were hard to find on Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. Parent company Meta attributes the problems to technical glitches. Lula went to the electoral court, which ruled that Meta had to ensure that Lula and Bolsonaro were treated equally with immediate effect. According to analysts, his online campaign partly ensured that Lula, despite his deficit in the first round, won the second round. It is the first time since 1989 that a candidate has succeeded in doing so. Lula is said to owe this mainly to the more than 14 million people who did not vote in the first round or who chose one of the other candidates. Three quarters of those people are now said to have chosen Lula. Lula is expected to take office on 5 January for his fourth term. Governing will not be easy for him, partly because of the increased power of the Bolsonaro family. Members of the family are represented in both the House of Representatives and in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. 'Strange elections' US President Trump has also reacted to the election result. He says it seems that the elections were "manipulated", without providing any evidence. "The longer voting period was very strange. It looks corrupt," said Trump. The US president is trying to exert his influence in the region as much as possible. He prefers to do business with right-wing governments that are ideologically close to him, but says he "likes" Lula and gets along well with him.

title: Survey: considerable group of Dutch people feel disadvantaged
lead: Most Dutch people do not feel disadvantaged. But a "considerable minority" does feel that people like themselves are being disadvantaged and that other groups are unfairly benefiting, according to new research by the <entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau</entity> (SCP). This is particularly the case for two topics that also rank high on other research's list of social concerns. On housing, 30 percent of the population experiences disadvantage; on political representation, 28 percent. That is quite a lot, but a broad majority of Dutch people still does not feel that disadvantage. From conversations the SCP held, it emerged that especially Dutch people with a secondary vocational education (mbo) are deeply outraged, for example, about the priority that status holders still receive in many municipalities when housing association homes are allocated. They consider it self-evident that in times of scarcity the government should help 'their own people' first with housing. In their eyes, the opposite is now happening: politicians give excessive attention and tax money to newcomers and are not there for their own population. Sinterklaas 'taken away' That impression exists among both mbo-educated people with and without a migration background. On some other points, those two groups feel disadvantaged compared to each other. The SCP spoke with white Dutch people with an mbo background who are convinced that judges disadvantage them compared to people of color, whereas the latter group says the exact opposite is happening. A similar pattern is visible with cultural traditions such as Sinterklaas and Zwarte Piet. On one hand there is the fear that these kinds of holidays are being 'taken away' in favor of Suikerfeest or Eid al-Fitr. Mbo-educated people with a migration background, on the other hand, feel that Eid al-Fitr is indeed embraced in a city like <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, but much less so in smaller places across the country. Fighting for political attention The planbureau's research centers on perceived disadvantage, but the researchers point out that there is also actual disadvantage for both people with a migration background and people with an education up to and including mbo-2. "Dutch people who feel they are getting the short end of the stick are more often in a less favorable position on the housing or labor market, for example," the report reads. "They also more often face other disadvantages, such as a lower income, a weaker network or poorer health." According to the SCP, mbo-educated people more often see society as a battlefield where one must fight for scarce resources, political attention and social recognition. In contrast are people with a university education, who seem to live "in a different reality". They see cultural diversity as more of an enrichment than a threat, trust fair justice, and feel well represented by politics. People who feel advantaged too This kind of difference also shows in voting behavior: the group that feels it is in second place tends to vote above average for PVV or Forum voor Democratie, or does not vote. Meanwhile, people who feel advantaged - on a topic like housing, 20 percent - more often end up with parties such as D66, Pro, VVD and CDA. Incidentally, most Dutch people take a middle position: they feel neither disadvantaged nor advantaged. The research The Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau bases this research primarily on a survey of 1239 Dutch people aged 18 and over, which is representative by gender, age and education. In addition, there were four more in-depth conversations with a total of 31 people in four focus groups, including two focus groups with only people with a migration background.

title: Israel goes to the polls: will Netanyahu stay in power?
lead: Most polling stations have opened for the Israeli parliamentary elections. It is the first parliamentary election since the Hamas terror attack of 7 October 2023. That makes security the most important issue for many Israelis. On the day of the terror attack, Hamas fired thousands of rockets at Israel, and in the early morning thousands of Hamas militants crossed the border at dozens of points. 1200 Israeli soldiers and civilians were killed and more than 250 people were abducted. At the Nova music festival in the Negev desert, 378 people were killed. The war that followed saw Israel destroy a large part of Gaza, and tens of thousands of Palestinians were killed. Although Israelis do not vote for individuals in the election but for parties, the election is also seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu, the longest-serving prime minister the country has ever had. One party never gets a majority. The Knesset, the Israeli parliament, has 120 seats. A majority or a majority government requires at least 61 seats. As in the Netherlands, it has never happened that one party won an absolute majority in a parliamentary election. This means that parties in the Knesset always have to form a coalition in order to govern or need support from outside the government. Netanyahu's party became the largest in the previous election in 2022, but according to the latest polls it is slightly behind the Yashar party, a new party led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. Because neither party is expected to win a majority in parliament, they will have to work with other parties. Broadly speaking, there are two major blocs: Netanyahu's Likud party together with the parties that favour cooperation with the prime minister, and a coalition of parties that do not want to work with the current prime minister, including the Yashar party. Correspondent Lennard Swolfs is following the elections in Israel: One of the themes central to this election is what preceded the terror attacks of 7 October. According to several media outlets, Netanyahu had been warned in advance of an imminent attack but ignored those signals. Eisenkot's party wants an independent investigation into this, while Netanyahu is mainly campaigning on the military successes he says have been achieved in the war in the Gaza Strip and in the fight against Iran. The election also concerns the Israeli rule of law. Netanyahu pushed through controversial reforms, including a law that gives the Israeli government influence over the appointment of judges and limits the power of the Supreme Court. Eisenkot wants to reverse those reforms. Military conscription, as in every Israeli election, is also an important issue. Although the Supreme Court has ruled that ultra-Orthodox Jews should not be exempt from conscription, they themselves still believe they do not have to serve. The opposition wants conscription to apply to everyone and for it to be enforced. Netanyahu needs the support of ultra-Orthodox parties and is therefore less firm on the matter. The suffering of the Palestinians is barely part of the election. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot oppose a two-state solution and see no point in peace plans as long as Hamas is in power in the Gaza Strip. Uncertain Neither bloc is expected to win a majority according to the polls, which makes it highly uncertain what will happen after the results. If there is a deadlock, new elections could follow. That would not be unusual: between April 2019 and November 2022 no fewer than five parliamentary elections were held. Twice it proved impossible to form a coalition, and twice <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> fell relatively quickly. The current coalition came to power at the last election. Polling stations are open until 22.00 local time (21.00 Dutch time). Exit polls on Israeli television channels will follow immediately afterwards, providing a first indication of the result.

title: Wake-up service 27/10: Israel goes to the polls • Ruling on explosion at Schammenkamp
lead: Good morning! Israel goes to the polls to elect a new parliament and in <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> the court rules on the explosion in 2024 in a business premises on the Rotterdam Schammenkamp. First the weather: the day starts dry with some sun, later showers. With 15 to 19 degrees it is quite warm for the time of year. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: Jean-Louis van der Velde is, according to the Quote 500, the new richest Dutchman. He is dethroning Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken, who has led the list since 2012. His fortune, estimated at 26 billion euros, Van der Velde earned with cryptocurrencies. The list shows that the 500 richest Dutch people became even richer over the past year and that the Netherlands has more billionaires. The total wealth of the 500 richest Dutch people amounts to 300 billion euros, comparable to a quarter of the total Dutch economy. Other news from the night: And finally: A resident of <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> has made an app that is handy for the fellow residents of his apartment complex, but it has already cost the municipality 50,000 euros. Have a nice day!

title: Quote 500 shaken up by AI entrepreneurs and new richest Dutch person
lead: The 500 richest Dutch people became even richer last year, the Netherlands has more billionaires, and the richest Dutch person this year is no longer Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken but a newcomer: Jean-Louis van der Velde, who earned his money with cryptocurrencies. That is what emerges from the annual list of the 500 Dutch people with the most wealth from business magazine Quote. The five richest Dutch people and their estimated wealth: The total wealth of the 500 richest Dutch people amounts to 300 billion euros. For comparison, that is a quarter of the total size of the Dutch economy. The wealth of the 500 richest has moreover risen by more than 10 percent compared with last year. Last year their total wealth was 273 billion euros. The number of billionaires has also increased, from 52 to 56. Quote's list is an estimate based on annual reports, the <entity id="org:zbo-dienst-voor-het-kadaster-en-de-openbare-registers">Kadaster</entity> and other public sources. For a long time it was unclear whether Van der Velde actually has a Dutch passport. That is why he was not included in the list. "He left for Asia in the 1980s, but we have been able to confirm that he has a Dutch passport," says deputy editor-in-chief Jeroen Molenaar. What stands out about the list is that more AI entrepreneurs have also been added. "That can now happen very quickly," says Molenaar. "Within a year, entrepreneurs in this sector can enter the list. That speed is really new." Exemplary of this is Pim de Witte, who founded an AI company last year and, at 31, enters the list as the youngest Dutch billionaire ever. And there are many more examples of people who are now on the list as AI entrepreneurs. "If the Quote 500 is the annual X-ray of the economy, then AI is the most discussed break with the past," the magazine writes. That X-ray still paints a fairly one-sided picture. 44 of the 500 are women, "dismally low," says Molenaar. "You quickly get the idea that such a list is really just a list of rich older white men. Largely, that is indeed the case." According to Molenaar, how these women came by their wealth is very diverse. Some women have taken over a company from the family but have developed it and made it big themselves, he says. The number of women on the list has stalled for years. On the list of the hundred richest Dutch people under 40, there are only four women. Molenaar does have high hopes that this will change. "The new intake is largely in retail, but more and more women are also coming through in other sectors," Molenaar said. "Fortunately, more and more women are starting businesses, although it takes time before you see that reflected in the list." To appear in the current edition, a fortune of over 140 million euros is needed. The youngest person on the list remains Max Verstappen (29 years old). <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> figures. Today Statistics Netherlands also released new figures on the number of millionaires in the country. On the reference date of 1 January 2025 there were 547,000 households with wealth of at least 1 million euros. That is 81,000 more households than a year earlier. A person's wealth consists of several aspects, such as stakes in businesses and the value of one's own home. According to the CBS, the rise in wealth is mainly due to higher house prices. The highest number of millionaires in the Netherlands lives in <entity id="org:gemeente-bloemendaal">Bloemendaal</entity> and Laren. The fewest millionaire households are found in the provinces of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity>, Limburg and <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>.

title: Pro and CDA: dangerous driving to be fined more heavily, minor offences more leniently
lead: The system of traffic fines must be overhauled, according to MPs Abdi (Pro) and Straatman (CDA). In an initiative memorandum they write that harder action should be taken against "asphalt aces who endanger others" and less harsh action against people who commit relatively minor offences. According to the two MPs, the balance is currently skewed. "The more serious the offence, the more lenient the policy. And the more vulnerable the offender, the harsher the system turns out." They want higher fines for dangerous driving behaviour such as serious speeding, driving under the influence and holding a phone while driving. The chance of being caught for these drivers should also be increased, including by deploying better speed cameras. For repeat offenders, a person-focused approach should be introduced. Harsh criticism The initiators also want the increases for unpaid fines to be reduced: from 50 to 25 percent for the first time and from 100 to 50 percent for the second. They also believe there should be more room for payment arrangements and the possibility of waiving debts for people who cannot pay their fines. In their memorandum, the two give a calculation example: "Where a minor traffic offence led to a traffic fine of (converted) 68.06 euros in 1990, that same person would have to pay 490 euros for it in 2026." If the fine is not paid, the amount can now rise to 1470 euros, which is unaffordable for a group of "vulnerable people". "It cannot be that someone who cannot pay their traffic fine ends up having to pay three times as much", says CDA MP Straatman. "A government that profits from the debts of its own citizens. That is the world turned upside down", Abdi of Pro adds. The MPs are presenting their proposal after harsh criticism of the plan of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to raise traffic fines next year in line with inflation, which amounts to an increase of another 2.7 percent. For example, running a red light would become ten euros more expensive, bringing the bill to 330 euros. 'Milk cow' Abdi and Straatman state that the government is using traffic fines as a milk cow. Scrapping the plan would cause the state treasury to lose 46 million euros. Their plan to fill that gap has a good chance of success. The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> already asked the cabinet last month to abandon the intention, because fines would already barely be proportionate to the seriousness of the offences. The <entity id="org:centraal-justitieel-incassobureau">Centraal Justitieel Incassobureau</entity> also criticises the level of traffic fines, which are "increasingly out of step with fines in criminal law".

title: Bird flu at Groningen poultry farm, 45,000 animals culled
lead: Bird flu has been confirmed at a farm in the Groningen village of Lutjegast (<entity id="org:gemeente-westerkwartier">gemeente Westerkwartier</entity>). The 45,000 animals on the site will be culled. It is the first bird flu outbreak since July, the Ministry of Agriculture reports. According to regional broadcaster RTV NOF, it concerns a farm with laying hens. To prevent further spread, a transport ban applies with immediate effect within a radius of ten kilometres around the affected farm. No birds, eggs, manure or used litter may be transported. Within the zone, which lies partly in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> and partly in <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>, there are 21 other agricultural farms. No housing requirement. According to the ministry, the outbreak does not yet give cause for a national or regional housing requirement. That requirement still applied earlier this year, but was lifted in June. The ministry says it is keeping a close eye on the situation.

title: Trump administration makes third attempt to prosecute former FBI director Comey
lead: The US Justice Department is making a third attempt to prosecute former FBI director James Comey. "There they go again," Comey responds drily to the new charges. "It would almost be funny if it weren't such disgusting abuse of power by the Justice Department." The new case revolves around an article from The New York Times from 2016 , in which an anonymous government source is quoted. According to the prosecutors, Comey was behind that leak and is therefore guilty of passing on secret information. The article revolved around a secret court order that instructed provider Yahoo to scan emails for references to terrorism. Comey rejects the accusations. "Nothing has changed for me, I am still innocent. I am not afraid of the people and I believe in our independent judges." Strained relationship Comey, appointed by Obama as head of the federal police, has a strained relationship with Donald Trump. Trump held it against him that Comey's FBI investigated Russian interference in his election victory. Comey claimed the president fired him after he refused to swear personal loyalty to him. Justice has already charged Comey twice under Trump. Due to a procedural error, the judge dismissed the first charge, concerning leaking information and lying to Congress. A second charge, for threatening, is still pending. That case revolves around a photo Comey posted on Instagram last year with the message "86 47" in seashells. "86" stands for eliminate in English, and Trump is the 47th president of the US. The president therefore took it as a death threat. The case is still before the judge. Comey's lawyers say the case about the article is now time-barred. The New York Times piece dates from early October 2016, so the 10 years the Justice Department had to start a case have expired. Comey's lawyer also points out that the case has not been weighed by a grand jury as required, and so officially there is still no indictment. Two earlier investigations into the leak were closed without charges. A Justice Department spokesperson does not want to comment on ongoing cases. President Trump told journalists "I know little about the case, I have only just heard about it", an evasive answer that he often gives when asked about controversial subjects. He did call Comey "a dirty cop ", a crooked cop. Trump has in the past repeatedly pressed the Justice Department to prosecute people he considers opponents. For example, he once asked in a public post why Attorney General Bondi had not yet prosecuted, among others, prominent Democrats and the prosecutor who successfully prosecuted him for fraud. Earlier this month there was also a raid on a Democratic congressman, highly unusual so shortly before the elections. Daughter's dismissal unlawful A judge ruled yesterday that Trump's Justice Department had wrongly dismissed Comey's daughter as a prosecutor in the state of New York. Maurene Comey argued that she was dismissed only because the president has a feud with her father. In the ruling, the judge found that Maurene Comey had indeed done excellent work for 10 years, "with praise from both managers and direct colleagues". Letting the White House decide who may stay in service, according to the judge, "goes against two centuries of case law" and "disturbs the balance of our constitutional system". Maurene Comey's request was granted to change her dismissal date retroactively from July 2025 to December that year, so that she is entitled to back pay. She has meanwhile found new work at a law firm.

title: Regulator refuses takeover of Unox by Zwanenberg, fears sausage monopoly
lead: The takeover of Unox by Zwanenberg may not go ahead, according to the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">Autoriteit Consument en Markt</entity> (ACM). The regulator has refused permission for the takeover after follow-up investigation of the proposed purchase. Through the takeover, Zwanenberg would become roughly the only major supplier of smoked and knackwurst sausages in Dutch supermarkets. It would also gain a monopoly in the field of shelf-stable soups, the ACM says. More expensive A major reason the ACM says no to the takeover is that consumers could end up paying more as a result. Zwanenberg already has a large market share. According to the regulator, there is a risk that it could use this position to charge supermarkets higher prices, as there would then be few alternatives. "That is undesirable, especially at a time when there are already concerns about higher food prices", says <entity id="person:martijn-snoep">Martijn Snoep</entity>, chair of the ACM's board. The ACM investigated the consequences of this takeover. Several supermarkets stated in this investigation that they were concerned about the risk of price increases. Disappointed Zwanenberg, which produces sausages, meals and soups on a European level, says it is considering appealing the decision. It says, among other things, that the market for these products is much broader than the ACM interprets. Unox also says it is disappointed with the ACM's decision. The company, which falls under Unilever, says it will use the coming period to "determine our next steps".

title: 12 years in prison and TBS sought against man for kicking girlfriend to death in Vlijmen
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has sought twelve years in prison and TBS with compulsory psychiatric care against Coen K. (36) from Uden. He is suspected of the violent death of his girlfriend. Jessica Brants (38) was killed in July last year in her own home in Vlijmen, in the presence of her then 2-year-old daughter. Coen K. is said to have lost control during an argument and to have delivered hard kicks. K.'s shoe tread was found on the woman's head. In total, 21 injuries were found on her body, 16 of them on the head and neck. The man himself denies that he kicked his girlfriend while she was lying on the ground. The woman died in hospital in Tilburg. Alcohol and drugs K. had used alcohol and drugs and suffers from several disorders, such as borderline personality disorder. He drank six to twelve cans of beer daily and used strong medication such as oxazepam, which he bought himself online. He also suffered from fear of abandonment. According to experts, he was therefore not fully criminally responsible during the manslaughter. Several relatives of the 38-year-old woman left the courtroom this morning when K.'s lawyer took the floor, writes Omroep Brabant. The lawyer said, among other things, that K. did not intend to kill his girlfriend. Right to speak Yesterday the woman's relatives made use of their right to speak. "We no longer recognised our daughter after you had abused her. We are upset, angry, furious. What you did is beastly. Why do you keep going at such a beautiful, sweet girl? Do you realise that these young children must go on without their mother? And we without our daughter?" said Brants' mother. The woman's eldest daughter said, among other things, that she could not say goodbye because her mother's body was no longer viewable. "I have little concentration at school. I try my best. Sometimes I get panic attacks," she said, among other things. The relatives are claiming around four hundred thousand euros in compensation. The court will give its ruling on 20 November.

title: Charles's controversial visit to the Caribbean: calls for an apology for the slave trade
lead: The British King Charles leaves today for a royal tour of the Caribbean. It is a sensitive visit, because in this region the calls for apologies and reparations for the historical slave trade are growing ever louder. King Charles will visit the Bahamas, Guyana and then Antigua and Barbuda, where he will attend the Commonwealth conference. Charles is, in addition to king of the UK, head of state in 14 other countries and the symbolic head of the Commonwealth, which consists of 56 countries. But the question is how long all of this will remain so. His son and heir to the throne, Prince William, and his wife, Princess Kate, also made a trip to the Caribbean a few years ago, where in Jamaica they were greeted with protest signs. Awkward photo Their royal visit led to uncomfortable questions about Britain's colonial past, about slavery and the role of the monarchy within the Commonwealth. An awkward photo, in which the royal couple shook hands with children through a fence, went around the world and was portrayed by critics as a symbol of the colonial relations that still persist. After that trip, Prince William hinted that he would not automatically follow in the footsteps of his father Charles and his grandmother Queen Elizabeth as head of the Commonwealth. King Charles is therefore possibly the last British monarch to fulfil this role. King Charles is prepared for the risks and controversies surrounding his trip to the Caribbean. He takes into account protests and discussions about apologies and reparations, topics that are not new to him. In Antigua and Barbuda and in the Bahamas, where Charles is king and head of state, there is also discussion about whether it is time to abolish the monarchy and become a republic. Reparations The Bahamas National Reparations Committee even warned the king with the message: "Do not come empty-handed". Meanwhile, Jamaica, another country in the Caribbean, is trying through a legal procedure to get clarity about Britain's responsibility for slavery. The country recently submitted a petition to King Charles and his advisory body, with questions about the legality of British slavery and whether Britain is obliged to make reparations. But such steps will be absent during this trip. King Charles follows the British government's advice not to offer official apologies for Britain's role in the trans-Atlantic slave trade. At the same time, he will not shy away from the history of slavery. In 2022 he spoke as Prince of Wales of "the darkest period in our history" and his "personal sorrow is for the suffering of so many". He also acknowledged that "this is a conversation whose time has come". Enormous scale In the United Kingdom, people have looked closely at the Netherlands when <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> commissioned a large-scale investigation into the ties between the House of Orange-Nassau and slavery. In addition, in 2023 he apologised to Suriname for the Dutch history of slavery and asked forgiveness for the fact that his ancestors had not intervened against these crimes. The United Kingdom is more reserved about this. British colonial history is of enormous scale: at its height the British Empire covered almost a quarter of the global land surface and included about a quarter of the world population. The Caribbean was crucial to the British trans-Atlantic slave trade. Between 1624 and 1807, an estimated 2.3 million enslaved Africans were brought to the British colonies in the Caribbean. The scale of Britain's colonial past, with a history of slavery, plunder, oppression and exploitation, makes the discussion about apologies and redress very complex. Importance of the Commonwealth An attempt to put a price tag on reparations was made a few years ago by the Brattle Group, an economic consultancy. The total damage of trans-Atlantic slavery by Western countries was put at about 100 trillion dollars. The United Kingdom, second after America, stood at 18 trillion. That is about seven times the total annual GDP of the UK. Despite the discussions that Charles may face during this trip, he also emphasises the importance of the Commonwealth: a partnership of 56 independent countries that took its current form in 1949. According to him, it is also a group of countries that together can tackle the great challenges of this time, such as climate change and biodiversity and better education for young people. During a visit to Samoa in 2024 the king said: "None of us can change the past. But we can devote ourselves with heart and soul to learning from it and finding ways to put right lasting inequality."

title: Acquittal in case over fatal explosion at Schammenkamp apartment building Rotterdam
lead: The man suspected of involvement in the fatal explosion at Schammenkamp in Rotterdam two years ago has been acquitted. The public prosecution service had demanded seven years in prison against the 37-year-old suspect Jalal O., but according to the court in Rotterdam there is no evidence that he is responsible for the explosion. In the explosion in a garage unit in January 2024, three people lost their lives. Above the garage unit were apartments. Several residents were injured and people also lost their homes. O. had for years been the main tenant of the garage unit. Earlier it was investigated whether there was a drug lab in the building. The court found no evidence for this. Traces of cocaine were found, but these could not be linked to a lab or to the suspect. Procaine The court does consider it proven that the explosion is linked to the processing of procaine, a cutting agent for cocaine. This appears from, among other things, objects that were found and images found on a phone belonging to one of the deceased victims. According to the court, it is therefore plausible that procaine was being processed in the building, at least on the day before the explosion. Processing procaine involves heating the flammable substance acetone. According to the court, the most likely cause is that an explosive acetone-air mixture exploded. How the acetone exploded, and how that mixture could cause such a devastating explosion, is not known. The suspect has always denied it The explosion was in the rear part of the garage unit. O. stated that he had rented that part to someone. He denies knowing what was being done in that part. According to the court, there is no evidence that O. lied about this. There are no camera images or witnesses who saw him going inside. The use of a police informant and the tapping of telephone conversations also produced no evidence. Shortly before the explosion, O. was still in the front part of the building, the court says. He then left for Belgium and returned a few hours after the explosion, the court says. He afterwards helped search for victims under the rubble. One of the fatal victims was his 22-year-old nephew.

title: Foundation problems? Then you may get a lower mortgage
lead: Future homeowners of a property with foundation problems may in future be able to get a lower mortgage if they take it out with the Nationale Hypotheekgarantie (NHG). NHG says it wants to prevent buyers from being faced with high repair costs they cannot pay. Think of fixing cracks in walls, damp problems or a tilting structure. From 1 January 2027, lenders such as banks must therefore take expected repair costs into account when setting the maximum mortgage amount for such an NHG mortgage. "By weighing these costs in advance, we create more clarity and responsible financing", says NHG director Roald van der Linde. What is NHG? NHG stands for Nationale Hypotheekgarantie, and is a kind of insurance for the affordability of a home. It protects buyers against financial risks. For example, if homeowners are forced to sell their home, for instance due to a divorce, the NHG takes over the residual debt. Whether repair costs count toward the amount of the NHG mortgage depends on the risk assessment in the valuation report and possibly additional investigation. This assessment has been mandatory since 1 April this year and is included in the valuation report of a home, including for people without an NHG mortgage. The valuation produces a rating for the foundation. That scale runs from A through E. A score of D or E means a higher risk that the foundation has problems. If a home falls into these risk classes, NHG requires a foundation investigation. If that then shows that the home has a high foundation risk, the lender must take the expected repair costs into account when setting the mortgage amount. Climate damage The Netherlands has a major foundation problem. This is worsened by, among other things, drought and fluctuating groundwater levels as a result of climate change. It is expected that in the short term around 425,000 buildings will face foundation damage. The Kennis Centrum Aanpak Funderingsproblematiek (KCAF) expects that, due to climate change, this number will have risen to around 687,000 properties over roughly thirty years. High costs Foundation damage is unaffordable for many homeowners, according to research earlier this year by the <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">Autoriteit Financiële Markten</entity> (AFM). The regulator found that around 120,000 homeowners have foundation problems that need to be fixed. But the majority cannot pay for this directly. Calculation example Suppose you want to buy a home for 500,000 euros in 2027 with an NHG mortgage. Research then shows that the home has a high foundation risk. The valuation report states, for example, an average of 50,000 euros in estimated repair costs. Those costs are then included in the assessment of the financing. That means you can borrow that amount less as a mortgage. (Source: NVB) Nevertheless, the Dutch Banking Association (NVB) writes that many owners can finance this through their bank, for example by increasing their mortgage. The Fonds Duurzaam Funderingsherstel may also offer a solution. "At the same time, we must be honest", the NVB writes. "For some homeowners, foundation repair remains a disruptive and costly undertaking." The association refers homeowners with questions to the national foundation helpdesk. 'Not a pleasant message' According to NHG, it is "not a pleasant message" that buyers with foundation damage may now not be able to borrow the maximum amount. But the thinking behind it is protection: the bank wants to prevent people from borrowing so much that there is no money left for repairs. "By borrowing just a little less now, buyers keep financial room to later, when the foundation indeed needs to be built, borrow responsibly through a second mortgage, or pay from their own savings", a spokesperson says. Timing Precisely because of the cost, NHG's decision is a sensible one, according to Vereniging Eigen Huis. However, the interest organisation is critical of the moment at which foundation risks are disclosed in the purchase process. Currently this happens after an offer has been made. "But a buyer must know beforehand what they are buying and not be confronted with a possible foundation problem only at the valuation", a spokesperson says. They therefore advise sellers to share available information and relevant investigations with potential buyers in advance, and buyers to request this information. NHG limit In 2027, mortgages up to 500,000 euros may fall under NHG, if the conditions are met. For mortgages without NHG, this approach does not apply automatically. Banks may choose to weigh the foundation risk in a similar way, the NVB writes.

title: Highest turnout in decades at 'most important elections ever' in Israel
lead: Turnout in Israel's elections today has not been this high in decades. Halfway through election day, turnout stood at 44.9 percent, according to the Central Elections Committee. Turnout has not been this high since 1973. The committee announces a turnout figure roughly every hour. Figures from earlier today also pointed to strong eagerness to vote. The Israeli army, which reports turnout figures among soldiers, paints a similar picture. Long queues form at many polling stations. Local media report that 70,000 eligible voters traveled to Israel from abroad to cast their vote. Voting from abroad is not possible in Israel. According to experts, people are so motivated to vote because of the big question surrounding these elections: will Prime Minister Netanyahu remain in power? Security is a major theme after the Hamas terror attack on 7 October 2023, as is the democratic rule of law, in which Prime Minister Netanyahu carried out a number of controversial reforms. People on the street therefore see the elections as the "most important elections ever", they tell NOS. Torn ballots Meanwhile, incidents are also being reported on election day, with accompanying accusations of interference from both sides. At least six parties complained about irregularities at polling stations. For example, ballots were allegedly deliberately defaced or torn, rendering them invalid. According to Yashar, the party of Netanyahu's main challenger Gadi Eisenkot, there were so many that they cannot have been isolated mistakes. The Election Committee has not yet found evidence of this. The Arab party Ra'am is accused of involvement in bribing citizens to vote for it. Envelopes with money were found during house searches, the Election Committee confirms to The Jerusalem Post. Three people have been arrested and are being questioned. Long queues and considerable delays are mainly reported at polling stations in Arab communities. Some voters have to wait there for hours, partly because polling station staff take a very long time to check identities and ask all sorts of unnecessary questions, Haaretz reports. Polling stations also reportedly suddenly closed their doors for "a meeting" or for "changing ballots". Man with knife In Tel Aviv a man has been arrested who approached Yair Golan, leader of the Democratic Party. When he was stopped by security guards, a large knife fell out from under his clothing. Israelis can vote until 21.00 Dutch time tonight. When polling stations close, an exit poll follows immediately. The latest polls predicted a neck-and-neck race between sitting Prime Minister Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot. Neither of their parties will win an absolute majority, so a coalition will have to be formed. In recent years that has often failed, leading to new elections.

title: Belgian former dentist (72) sentenced to seven years in prison for years of abuse of patients
lead: A former dentist from Belgium has been sentenced to seven years in prison for sexually assaulting and raping female patients over many years. The court in Antwerp ruled that the man abused his position for 25 years to act on his sexual fantasies. The 72-year-old man from Wilrijk, south of Antwerp, among other things carried out treatments he called "keelontsmettingen" (throat disinfections), a treatment that does not exist at all. During that "throat disinfection" the man masturbated while filming the patients. He scheduled appointments at times when no other people were present in the dental practice. The dentist was arrested in April 2025 after his actions came to light at the end of 2024. A patient had been left with a strange feeling after the treatment and filed a complaint. Further reports followed. In total, 73 victims have come forward. The first complaint dates back to 1995. Patients humiliated. During the trial in September 2025, several victims described their experiences. One victim stated that the dentist pushed his fingers deep into her throat until she had to gag and vomit. Others said the dentist stroked them in various places on the body, under the pretext that this was necessary for the treatment. Victims also remain with questions about what happened during treatments under anaesthesia and how the abuse could continue for so long. During the investigation, police found large amounts of footage of treatments in the dental practice and the man's home. Sexually charged acts were reportedly visible on it during dental treatments. Images of sexual abuse of minors were also found on his computer. Higher sentence. The Belgian Public Prosecution Service had initially requested a prison sentence of five years. The court found that sentence insufficient given the long period over which the offences took place, the large number of victims and the traumatic consequences. In addition to rape, the dentist was also convicted of forgery of documents, fraud and unlawfully practising his profession.

title: Minimum tax brings the treasury almost half a billion in one year
lead: Multinationals paid 449 million euros in minimum tax over the year 2024, when the Netherlands introduced that new tax. That is stated in an answer from <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> to parliamentary questions. When the minimum tax was introduced, the expectation was that it would ultimately yield the Netherlands around 466 million per year. More than 140 countries worldwide agreed a few years ago that if multinationals in a certain country pay less than 15 percent tax on their profits, that country may levy extra tax to reach that 15 percent. In this way they want to ensure that large companies can avoid less tax. If a company has, for example, a parent company in the Netherlands and a subsidiary in the Bahamas and pays only 10 percent profit tax there, the Netherlands may still collect that 5 percent. The rule applies only to large companies with a worldwide turnover of 750 million euros or more. Amount may still change So far about 200 multinationals in the Netherlands have paid 449 million in total in minimum tax for 2024. In principle, companies had until the end of August this year to file and pay. But due to technical problems at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> this has been extended to the end of this month. The amount may therefore still rise. On the other hand, companies can also file objections, so the amount may fall again. According to staatssecretaris Eerenberg, some objections have already been filed. How much companies must pay for 2025 is still unclear, because they have a long time for that, until the end of May 2027. Also 'too little' in the Netherlands Notably, about 129 million of the 449 million euros had to be paid because companies in the Netherlands themselves paid 'too little' profit tax. The Netherlands has a profit tax of 19 percent on the first 200,000 euros and 25.8 percent on everything above that. That is higher than the minimum of 15 percent. But there are special schemes that allow companies to still fall below 15 percent, such as the so-called innovation box. For all profit a company makes from innovative activities it pays only 9 percent profit tax. The company must then receive a 'stamp' from the government stating that the activity is genuinely innovative. And for sea shipping there is the so-called tonnage scheme. Shipping companies then pay no tax on their actual profit, but on the net loading capacity of their ships. This too can bring profit tax below 15 percent. According to staatssecretaris Eerenberg, that domestic top-up tax is "only applicable to a very limited number of taxpayers, and the top-ups are generally limited in size". More countries follow How the revenues from the minimum tax will develop in the coming years remains to be seen. In 2024 some countries that intended to apply the floor had not yet introduced these rules. Therefore the Netherlands could often collect money, because in other countries at least 15 percent was not yet being collected. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> therefore expects the yield to become lower over time, because in some countries the minimum tax only takes effect from 2025 or later. On the other hand, companies are expected to book their profits more often in the Netherlands, because the tax advantage from artificially shifting profit to a low-tax country becomes smaller for companies. As a result, the amount of ordinary profit tax in the Netherlands may rise. Exception US Then there are the United States. Under pressure from President Trump an exception has been made for multinationals with a headquarters in the US. As a result, it becomes harder for other countries to impose an extra minimum tax on them from 2026. For 2024 the Netherlands still collected 120 million euros from multinationals with an American parent company. How much of that will remain because of the exception for the US still needs to be seen. All in all, it is still difficult to say how much the Dutch treasury will benefit from the minimum tax in the coming years. But this tax is not only about companies in the Netherlands paying more tax, but also about them doing so worldwide, and countries thus also competing less with each other on low taxes. According to the latest estimates, the minimum tax will yield between 70 and 98 billion euros per year worldwide.

title: House majority wants investigation into legal limit on private donations by sperm donors
lead: Minister <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> of Public Health must again look into whether and how <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> can intervene with sperm donors who try to father as many children as possible. Predecessors of the minister considered this legally unfeasible in recent years, but <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> wants Hermans to look at this again. "We want the interests of donor children to be given more priority in the discussion about mass donors," says House member André Poortman (CDA). Together with coalition partners VVD and D66 he submitted the motion that calls on Minister Hermans to investigate whether a legal limit can be set on mass donation in the private sphere. The motion was adopted today with broad support in the House. Only the SGP did not vote in favour. Last summer Nieuwsuur reported on a Dutch mass donor, Simon , who says he has fathered almost two hundred children by offering himself as a donor in the private sphere and through clinics. He came to light when several mothers involved found each other and thus discovered that Simon had lied about how many children he has. He told the women that he was absolutely against mass donation. The ministry of Public Health (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">VWS</entity>) had known for years that Simon was a mass donor, but did nothing more with that information. Last month Hermans wrote in a letter to the House that she regrets that parents have been in ignorance and uncertainty for almost ten years. Private donation Since 1 April last year, data of intended mothers and sperm donors from all clinics have been linked in the national register. Donors may be used for up to twelve families via a clinic. But what sperm donors do outside the clinic, for example by offering themselves as private donors via internet forums, is unknown. It is not the first time the House has demanded action from the minister to counter mass donation. In 2023 a similar motion by then House member Corinne Ellemeet (GroenLinks) already received broad support. But according to then minister Pia Dijkstra (D66), setting a maximum would "be a form of birth restriction that deeply intrudes on the personal sphere of those involved." Moreover, how do you check such a ban, and can the government actually enforce it? Until recently Minister Hermans also saw little in a legal maximum for private donations. Intended parents would mainly be responsible themselves for good agreements with the sperm donor. "Donations in the private sphere fall outside the scope of the law and outside the view of the government and clinics," Hermans said at the end of September in a letter to the House. Even so, Hermans indicated she wants to look again at what can be done, she said two weeks ago during a debate on mass donors. But she also tempered expectations. "I also want to tell the honest story, namely that it is difficult to intervene in that private sphere." Time for action For House member <entity id="person:lisa-vliegenthart">Lisa Vliegenthart</entity> (Pro), the call for an investigation by the minister does not go far enough. "Every time a new mass donor comes to light, the House says: 'never again'. Instead of yet another investigation now, it is really time for action," says Vliegenthart. She wants the minister to come directly with a bill that takes into account the so-called "reproductive freedom" and privacy of intended parents. CDA member Poortman admits that he too would prefer to go further. "Investigation is a first step. I don't want to ask the impossible of the minister by expecting a law right away. But it is clear that it cannot stop at investigation." As for which options he does see, Poortman does not want to say too much yet. "I don't want to pin the minister down on anything. But you could think of registration of sperm donation in the private sphere. That gives intended parents in a vulnerable position more tools. Their interests, and especially those of donor children, must weigh more heavily than the privacy of donors." Fixed contact point There is also a House majority for a motion calling for a "national support route" for donor children and parents to be set up. This should include, among other things, a fixed contact point for those involved and "appropriate psychosocial support".

title: Belongings of missing kitesurfer (18) found, search called off
lead: In the search for a kitesurfer who has been missing since Sunday, belongings were found off the Scheveningen coast. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports that these are a kiteboard and the kite. The search for the 18-year-old man was called off around midday. The police say the chance that the kitesurfer is still alive is very small, writes Omroep West. This morning the man was searched for at the Zuidelijk Havenhoofd. Because of the weather conditions the police are not searching further. The coast will still be monitored, says a spokesperson. Family The family is not giving up hope, but is "strongly taking the worst into account," says a spokesperson for Namens de Familie. "They are grateful for everyone's support," says the spokesperson. They are also "extremely grateful" to the emergency services. The spokesperson says it is terrible for the family that the man has not been found. Storm and high waves The kitesurfer was reported missing on Sunday at around 14.00 hours. In the past days, searches have been carried out from land, at sea and from the air. Boats of the Koninklijke Nederlandse Redding Maatschappij (KNRM) and a helicopter of the coast guard were deployed. The weather was stormy in the search area, with gusts up to 80 kilometers per hour. The storm and high waves hampered the search.

title: Skating fans can once again take the train straight to Thialf this winter
lead: Skating enthusiasts can once again take the train to Thialf this winter. During four major skating events, the sprinter train stops between <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-zwolle">Zwolle</entity> every half hour at <entity id="org:gemeente-heerenveen">Heerenveen</entity> IJsstadion station. The extra stop applies during the World Cup, the NK Allround and Sprint, the EK Allround and Sprint and the NK Afstanden. The four events take place in December and January. This coming weekend, at the World Cup qualifying tournament, the train will still pass the station. Extended due to success It is the second time since 2015 that the train has stopped at Thialf specifically for skating events. During a trial last spring, about 12 percent of visitors travelled by train. That result tasted like more, so the province of <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>, the municipality of Heerenveen and the NS continued the trial. On event days the trains stop at Thialf in both directions, from one to two hours before the start until one to two hours after the end. The stations Wolvega and Steenwijk also remain served as usual this time. Olympic Winter Games The province hopes that even more visitors will find their way to the train. The experiences are also useful with a view to 2030, when Thialf will host the Olympic speed skating tournament during the Winter Games. "We are going to talk with the parties involved about how the train stop can be secured and financed in the longer term", says the Frisian administration. The costs are currently paid by the region.

title: The king and queen lunch with 'standouts' like Suzan & Freek and Connie Palmen
lead: Singing duo Suzan & Freek and writer Connie Palmen were today among the guests of the so-called standouts lunch of <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima. At the lunch, 27 people were put in the spotlight at Noordeinde Palace in The Hague for having achieved an exceptional accomplishment in the arts, the media, science, sport or business. For example, Palmen won the Constantijn Huygens Prize and Suzan & Freek won a 3FM Award. Presenters Merel Westrik and Jeroen Kramer attended on behalf of Het Sinterklaasjournaal , the NTR programme that won the 2025 Machiavelli Prize. Track cyclist Hetty van de Wouw also joined, for her achievements at last year's track cycling World Championships. The royal couple invites people to such a lunch a few times a year. Today was the 42nd time.

title: Redrawing electoral districts does not seem to help Republicans in elections
lead: The Republican party of US President Trump tried in the run-up to the midterm elections to change the boundaries of the electoral districts in order to keep its majority in the House of Representatives. With one week still to go until the midterm elections, this gerrymandering, as redrawing electoral districts for political advantage is called, appears to be failing. Through a redrawing of 15 electoral districts in Texas, Florida and a handful of other states, the Republicans tried to steer the congressional elections to their advantage. Even so, there is a good chance that the seats in ten of those districts will fall to their opponents, the Democrats. Analysts say this is based on the most recent polls . Expected voting behaviour If that prediction comes true on 3 November, it will go down as a fiasco for Trump. He already began pushing last summer for a redrawing of the electoral districts where progressive voters were in the majority. By dividing those progressive districts and merging them with adjacent, more conservative areas, new electoral districts emerged where the Republicans would have the advantage. This method is called "gerrymandering". Look here to see how this works: In the newly drawn electoral districts, the Republicans appeared assured of gains in the midterm elections next week. The party based this on voting behaviour during the 2024 presidential election. In theory, Trump would win most of the new gerrymandered electoral districts by a margin of 10 percent of the votes. So the idea was: if Trump wins there, the Republican congressional candidates should also win. Popularity plummeted But then a few things happened that tilted the picture. First, Trump's popularity plummeted after March this year when he introduced new trade tariffs, cut deeper into government subsidies for Americans on lower incomes and began the war with Iran. Another factor is that a counter-movement arose after the Republican gerrymandering. For example, the Democratic governor of California created new electoral districts in his state with an overwhelming progressive majority. That cancelled out part of the possible advantage for the Republicans in the coming midterms. In addition, the Democratic party expects to draw many potential voters to the polls with the argument that the Republicans are acting undemocratically and manipulatively. Millions for campaign ads The Republicans and their donors are clearly not at ease about the outcome. In the hard-fought districts formed through gerrymandering, they are spending unprecedented sums to buy more and more political ads. In district 1 of North Carolina, where the Republicans at the beginning of this year still expected an easy victory, they have since September bought 20 million dollars' worth of ads in the hope of winning the seat after all. In the 15 districts they redrew themselves, they have hastily spent 150 million dollars in advertising money to rescue their faltering strategy. It is not the case that the Democrats are assured of winning the House of Representatives. Even if the gerrymandering pushed through by Trump fails, it is still possible that the Republicans will pull a stunt in other districts. And in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> the race is anything but a foregone conclusion . Polls simply do not tell everything. Erosion of norms Gerrymandering is not new, and certainly not exclusively a method of one of the parties. Already in the 19th century Republicans and Democrats used it. Still, a few things have changed in recent years. One of them is the timing. Normally it always happened right after a census. In the US there is a census every ten years, and the results become available soon after the start of the new decade. This matters for Congress, because the number of residents of a state determines the number of seats in the House of Representatives. What Trump has now done is demand a redrawing of electoral districts at a very different moment, in the middle of a decade. That gives more the impression of manipulation and of a clear attempt to retain power. That impression is reinforced by the fact that in April this year the Supreme Court weakened an important civil rights law , so that voters can no longer legally challenge gerrymandering if they believe they are disadvantaged on the basis of skin colour.

title: Restructuring at shipbuilder Damen, 225 jobs cut in the Netherlands
lead: Shipbuilder Damen is going to cut around 225 of its 4000 jobs in the Netherlands. The company wants to make its organisation "simpler and more efficient" with this. The jobs will disappear over the next twelve to eighteen months at the various Damen companies in the Netherlands. This happens both in offices and at the shipyards. It concerns positions at all levels and in all fields, a spokesperson says. The company from Gorinchem, with shipyards all over the world, expects that "a large part" of the restructuring can be absorbed through natural attrition, but does not rule out forced dismissals. 'It hits hard' According to union CNV, the news hits employees hard. "Everyone here is working incredibly hard to keep Damen on course despite changing circumstances. So it hits hard to hear that you may become a victim of an efficiency drive yourself", the union tells news agency ANP. At the end of June, the shipbuilder lost an important order. The German minister of Defence cancelled the order for six frigates, which Damen says was completely unexpected. A spokesperson for the shipbuilder says the restructuring in the Netherlands has nothing to do with this setback. Damen says it has invited the unions to talk about a social plan for the employees who lose their jobs.

title: Prosecutors demand heavy sentences against staff of illegal medicine website
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> demands 10 and 6,5 years against two suspects behind Slaappillen.net. The webshop sold, among other things, a counterfeit version of the strong painkiller oxycodone, which in reality contained the highly dangerous substance nitazenes. At least three people appear to have died from it. In total, nitazenes have now been found in the blood in thirteen deaths in the Netherlands. PostNL employee handled the shipping. The two residents of Breda who appeared in The Hague today were not the main persons responsible for Slaappillen.net. One is said to have packed the orders and managed the huge stock of, among other things, 400.000 pills, 6000 XTC tablets and large quantities of amphetamines. The oxycodone alone present in the house of his mother, where he lived and worked, had a value of 135.000 euros according to the OM. The other, a PostNL employee, is said to have ensured that the packages entered that company's shipping system. In addition, the OM suspects him of importing and trading large quantities of cocaine. That is why the demand against him is the highest. 'Multi-million business' Both say they had no idea they were contributing to the supply of contaminated pills to customers. The lawyer of one of them described his client as no more than "a glorified assembly-line worker", who acted solely on the orders of others. Both are not directly held responsible by justice for the deaths of the women, but according to the lawyer the OM, with the "exorbitantly high" demands, acts as if that is the case. The public prosecutor countered that both men were precisely "crucial links" in the "professionally run multi-million business" that Slaappillen.net was. The webshop made the threshold for customers as low as possible, among other things by offering payment with iDeal. Also shipments to other countries "Those customers were drawn into a trade," said the prosecutor, "in which only one thing mattered: making money. Vulnerable people were regarded as a goose that lays the golden eggs." They thought they were ordering painkillers, but got a deadly agent into their home that had ten to a hundred times the effect of oxycodone and in dozens of cases poisoned them or even cost them their lives. At the hearing this afternoon it emerged that the packages were not only sent to Dutch addresses, but also to at least Spain, Denmark and Belgium. Of the total of 5000 orders at Slaappillen.net that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was able to bring to light via the laptop of one of the suspects, 550 cases involved oxycodone. Main players now arrested. Further investigation will need to show in the coming time whether more deaths from nitazenes can be linked to Slaappillen.net. Last week the police arrested three men suspected of being the main persons responsible for this website, plus dozens of other websites on which illegal medicines and drugs were sold. The Hague District Court will rule on 17 November.

title: Two Britons charged over 'plot' at RAF air base
lead: Two Britons have been charged at a court in London in connection with the events of 27 September at the RAF air base in Fairford. The 24-year-old Mohmed A. has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, presumably from Iran. The equally 24-year-old Nouman E. is accused of entering a prohibited area "for a purpose harmful to the United Kingdom". On 27 September, five Britons were arrested at night at or near the base.
