Shortly before, they had left three minibuses with barrels of petrol at the edge of the site. The five were initially suspected of preparing a terrorist offence. Prime Minister Burnham said two weeks later that the five were "almost certainly" directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard in Iran. That suspicion still stands. Ali Mohmed A. was not part of the group of five. He was only arrested last week. According to the British prosecution service, he was the link between the five and someone called "Ali", who gave the orders. This Ali is said to be staying abroad. After the five had left the minibuses and petrol at the base, they were, according to the prosecution service, called by Ali. He reportedly said there was "a bomb in the cars". One of the five then called the police, the prosecutor said today. This mobilised a large police force, after which the five could quickly be arrested. In addition, the police had been alerted by a farmer's wife living nearby. She and her husband were returning from a party and suddenly saw men in balaclavas scattering in all directions in the glare of their headlights. They did not trust it and called the police. Reconnaissance The 24-year-old Nouman E. was charged today with entering the air base, but not on 27 September; rather on 22 August. He was reportedly conducting reconnaissance there at the time and made video recordings. Mohmed A. has been released on bail. Nouman E. had previously been released on bail, but was arrested again last week. He will remain in custody until the next hearing on 20 November, where Mohmed A. must also appear again. Six other suspects may await the case at liberty, after paying a bail sum. No bomb What the purpose of the minibuses and barrels of petrol was remains unclear. They may have been intended for an attack on the American bombers that carried out bombings on Iran from this base. But the bomb Ali was said to have talked about has never been found. The bombers were removed from there on 5 October, according to American media because new threats from Iran reportedly came in.

title: No clear winner in Israel, Arab parties larger than ever
lead: The parliamentary elections in Israel do not appear to have produced a clear winner. According to the first exit polls, the Likud party of Prime Minister Netanyahu wins 24 seats and thus remains the largest party. That would be a loss of 8 seats. The anti-Netanyahu bloc of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot would have grown larger than the pro-Netanyahu bloc: 52 to 50 seats, according to the exit polls. Neither is enough for a majority in parliament. Netanyahu relied on a coalition of five parties that together held 64 seats in parliament. On X, Eisenkot is already drawing the far-reaching conclusion that this first assessment of the result indicates "a total lack of confidence in Netanyahu and his <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>". Arab parties The two blocs with Arab parties have together won 18 seats according to the exit polls, a record. As a result, they could play an important role in forming a government without Prime Minister Netanyahu, although Jewish opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. Such cooperation has been especially sensitive since the terrorist attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023. Voting was possible until 21.00 Dutch time this evening. The exit polls are a first assessment of the result. The first official results come in overnight, so a clearer picture will probably emerge tomorrow. The official result follows later. One party never wins a majority The Knesset has 120 seats. A majority government therefore requires 61 seats. It has never happened that one party has won an absolute majority. This means parties must always form a coalition to govern or secure support from outside the government. In recent years, forming a coalition has often failed, which has forced new elections. Referendum on Netanyahu These are the first parliamentary elections since the terrorist attack by Hamas in 2023. As a result, security is the most important issue for many Israelis. Although Israelis do not vote for individuals in the election but for parties, the election is also seen as a referendum on Netanyahu. He is the longest-serving prime minister the country has ever had. Turnout today was very high: by 22.00, the time when polling stations closed, more than 77 percent of eligible voters had voted, the Central Elections Committee reports. That is the highest turnout in decades. Local media report that 70,000 eligible voters traveled to Israel from abroad to cast their vote. Voting from abroad is not possible in Israel.

title: CBS: number of homes allocated to status holders remains the same
lead: The number of housing association homes allocated to status holders barely rose in 2024, according to figures from Statistics Netherlands (CBS). Just over 8 percent of all housing association homes that became vacant in 2024 were allocated to households with one or more status holders. That concerns just over 13,000 homes, roughly the same as a year earlier. Among starters, the share of status holders is considerably higher. In 2024, 21 percent of the starters who moved into a vacated housing association home were status holders. "That share has been constant for a few years," says CBS demographer Ruben van Gaalen. "But compared with longer ago, an increase is visible. In 2018, for example, the percentage was 9, a lot lower." The figures for 2024 are the most recent data. The umbrella organisation of housing associations, Aedes, has more recent figures, but those are estimates. More status holders among starters. The CBS examined both the total group of status holders and the group of status holders among starters. "Those are people who are getting a home in the Netherlands for the first time," says Van Gaalen. "In addition, there are also status holders who move on, from one home to another. They usually leave behind a home that someone else can live in." That group of starters has grown in recent years. In 2024, 67 percent of households with a status holder were starters on the housing market. In 2023 that was 64 percent. How many homes really go to status holders? In politics, there has been regular debate in recent years about how many social rental homes go to status holders. Some political parties cited the CBS figures, while other parties mentioned much higher percentages. That debate about figures mainly revolves around whether you look at all social rental homes that go to status holders or only at 'starter homes'. In this study, the CBS looked at all social rental homes. That there are more status holders among starters on the housing market is, according to Van Gaalen, because backlogs are still being worked through. "In 2015 and 2016 the influx of asylum seekers in the Netherlands was very high. As a result, many status holders had to wait a long time for a home." While waiting, they stayed in a temporary reception location. When they were later allocated a home, they therefore did not leave a home behind. This is also reflected in the CBS figures. For 16 percent of households with a status holder, a home became vacant after their move. For households without status holders, that was just over half. In addition, almost one in five households with a status holder moved out of a home in which other residents remained. Regional differences Most housing association homes in 2024 went to single-person households. Status holders who move into a housing association home also more often live alone. How many housing association homes were allocated to status holders differs by region. In <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> the share was highest at 12 percent. In the Gooi en Vechtstreek region and in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> too, relatively many housing association homes went to status holders. Whether that also means the waiting list for a housing association home was longer there than in other places, the CBS cannot say. "You cannot calculate exactly how much longer people have to wait with the national figures," says Van Gaalen. "That also depends, for example, on how many housing association homes and home seekers there are in a municipality and to what extent people move on." Too few homes When refugees are granted residence status in the Netherlands, they are also entitled to housing. Municipalities are responsible for arranging those homes. According to professor of the housing market Peter Boelhouwer, they regularly make agreements about this with housing associations. In consultation with the municipality, some housing associations allocate a part of their homes to so-called urgent cases, who then get a home with priority. These are, for example, people who cannot remain in their current home due to illness or people whose home is being demolished. Or status holders, for example. "In recent years, more and more groups have fallen under the urgency category," says Boelhouwer. "Housing associations want at the same time to prevent the priority group from becoming so large that regular home seekers have to wait very long. As a result, municipalities increasingly have to look for housing for status holders themselves." Due to the tight housing market, that does not always succeed, according to Boelhouwer. This means that many people with an official residence status still live in temporary reception locations in the Netherlands. "That increases the pressure on those locations, which are actually meant for people who do not yet have a residence status," says Boelhouwer.

title: Wake-up call 28/10: House debates infrastructure • Court case over desecration of graves in Utrecht
lead: Good morning! The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> is debating spending on bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure, and in Utrecht women are appearing in court for holding a seance at children's graves. First, the weather: today there is plenty of sun but also occasional cloud. It stays dry in most places, with highs of 14 or 15 degrees and a moderate south-westerly wind. This evening more cloud, and with the exception of the south, there is a local chance of some rain. The coming days bring quiet autumn weather with sun, clouds and sometimes mist. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a speech on election night, called for a "strong, national, right-wing" <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. According to him, the exit polls show that the right wing has won a "large majority" among Israel's "Zionist voters". Nearly 42 percent of all votes have been counted. The pro-Netanyahu bloc, with 57 seats for now, has ten seats more than the bloc of former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. Other news from the night: And finally: a nipple tattoo is often the last step for women after a major period, such as a mastectomy or breast cancer treatment. Mariska de Jong is a medical tattoo artist and may call herself the best in the world. Have a nice day!

title: PvdD makes a new attempt to ban slaughter without stunning
lead: The Party for the Animals is once again trying to ban slaughter without stunning. The party wants animals always to be stunned beforehand, including in ritual slaughter. The bill, which goes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> today, contains further measures. "The purpose of the law is to limit animal suffering during slaughter as much as possible," says MP Ouwehand. If it is up to the Party for the Animals, CO2 stunning of pigs and the use of an electric water bath for chickens, ducks and turkeys must also stop. The party also wants highly pregnant animals no longer to be transported to the slaughterhouse. Furthermore, an end must come to tipping ducks, chickens and turkeys out of crates onto a moving conveyor belt without stunning. The party also considers it important not to look only at slaughter. Ouwehand has therefore previously submitted another law, which is meant to ensure that the way animals are treated in intensive livestock farming changes significantly. "With our bills we are making a shift towards animal-friendly livestock farming," she says. Stunning in ritual slaughter too: fifteen years ago the Party for the Animals also tried to ban slaughter without stunning. That bill failed in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>, partly because of the freedom of religion of Jews and Muslims in this case. But the Party for the Animals believes animal suffering weighs more heavily. The <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> recently ruled that there is now also more room to choose that, since a ban already applies in other countries and thinking about animal welfare has changed. Not all ritual slaughter takes place without stunning. <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> (Agriculture) said earlier this year that two thirds of the animals during the Feast of Sacrifice are already stunned before being slaughtered with a neck cut. Erkens said this month that they are "personally" in favour of a ban on slaughter without stunning. There is in principle also a majority in the House. However, this subject is sensitive, so parties still want to look carefully at the bill text. It is therefore not yet possible to say in advance whether the law will succeed this time.

title: Minor boy shot dead in Belgrade after attack on Israeli embassy
lead: A minor boy was shot dead shortly after midnight in the Serbian capital Belgrade after he attacked a member of a special police unit with two knives. The officer was guarding the Israeli embassy. Serbian Minister Dacic of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> speaks of a terrorist attack. The terror threat in the country has been raised to the highest level. There is more police presence at important locations in Serbia. The boy was shot dead by the security guard himself after his knife attack. According to the minister, the security guard acted in self-defence and was slightly injured in the face in the process. He has been taken to hospital. Serbian media report that he will probably be allowed home today. According to Dacic, the young attacker came from the city of Sabac, west of Belgrade. He was on the radar of the national security services and a supporter of Islamic State, the minister said. During the attack he reportedly shouted "Allahoe akbar" and images with IS symbols reportedly appeared on his Instagram account.

title: President Zelensky in The Hague today, visits Jetten and the king
lead: The Ukrainian president Zelensky comes to The Hague today for, among other things, a visit to <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity>. Zelensky will be received at Paleis Huis ten Bosch early in the evening, the <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> says. Beforehand he will hold talks with <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, Minister Yesilgöz of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> and <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. The Ukrainian president also speaks with leading figures from the Dutch and Ukrainian business communities. The visit comes on the day that the Netherlands has announced a support package for Ukraine. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> makes 1,2 billion euros in total available in non-military support for the coming three years. <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Minister Sjoerdsma</entity> is in Kyiv. Minister Sjoerdsma of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-bho">Buitenlandse Handel en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking</entity> announced that this morning during a visit to Kyiv. He is in the Ukrainian capital to talk with representatives of the Ukrainian government and with Dutch companies that are active in Ukraine. Sjoerdsma points to the harsh winter the country is facing. "It is also of great importance for the safety of us all that we keep supporting the Ukrainians so that they can sustain the fight. That is why the cabinet is now taking an extra step." For this year alone, 40 million euros will therefore be transferred to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund, a fund set up by the European Commission and the Ukrainian Ministry of Energy to repair the heavily damaged energy infrastructure in the country. This infrastructure is under heavy fire due to ongoing Russian air attacks. The Ukrainian capital Kyiv is being bombarded with missiles practically day and night, so the power already often goes out even though winter has not even really begun yet. Money for reconstruction The cabinet also makes 55 million euros available so that Ukraine can order parts from Dutch companies that are needed to keep the energy infrastructure running. Furthermore, 136 million goes to companies that want to help with the reconstruction of Ukraine. The cabinet also helps companies that want to export to Ukraine to limit their financial risks. Coen van Oostrom of employers' organisation VNO-NCW, who is travelling with the minister, says the task in Ukraine is enormous. "Dutch companies can play an important role in that. But then we must work closely with the Ukrainian government and remove the obstacles for companies." The support package does not mean that extra money is being set aside for Ukraine. Of the 1,2 billion euros, 878 million euros comes from the coalition agreement, and the 327 million extra was announced on Prinsjesdag. Norway and Finland call Putin The visit by Zelensky to The Hague comes on the eve of possible negotiations to end the war. These are expected to take place somewhere early next month. An exact date for talks between Russian, American and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi has not yet been set. Europe is not at the table, for now. The Finnish president Stubb and the Norwegian prime minister Støre called the Russian president Putin on their own initiative yesterday. They had coordinated this with Ukraine beforehand, but Denmark was not happy about it. The Danish prime minister Frederiksen warns that "solo actions" could put Europe's unity under pressure. In response, Zelensky expressed his support for the action by Norway and Finland. Zelensky may discuss Europe's role with Jetten today as well, along with the role of the International Criminal Court (ICC). After the war, the ICC would have to examine war crimes committed against Ukraine. That Russia is held responsible for this war is an important point for Ukraine, as are security guarantees. Zelensky's visit live on NOS The visit of President Zelensky to Prime Minister Jetten can be watched live on NOS this afternoon. Join live from 13.45 hours, with the press conference at 15.30 hours. You can follow the visit via the livestream in the NOS app and on NOS.nl.

title: New cold case investigation method is successful and will be used more often
lead: There is a new investigative method for solving serious cold cases. A pilot by the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> and the <entity id="org:nederlands-forensisch-instituut">Nederlands Forensisch Instituut</entity>, which uses private DNA databases, has been successfully completed. This method will therefore be used in more cases. The method makes it possible to compare DNA from the scene of a crime with DNA profiles from databases that have given permission for this. In this way it becomes easier to trace a suspect through (distant) relatives. The method can also help establish the identity of unknown victims. "I am confident that thanks to this method we will solve cases in the future," says Mirjam Warnaar, national public prosecutor for forensic investigation. Only in serious cases The OM currently decides when the new method may be used precisely. This will in any case only happen in murder cases and other serious criminal cases, says Warnaar. "Such as an investigation into a serial rapist." Another condition is that there are no leads left. Permission will also be requested from the investigating judge for each case. Heuvelmoord lead The new method has been used since 2023 in six cases, including the so-called Heuvelmoord case. In two cases new leads were found. The Heuvelmoord case revolves around the death of 68-year-old Sjef Leukel in Berg en Terblijt. An unknown man entered the home of Leukel and his wife in 2004 and attacked them. Sjef Leukel died and his wife was seriously injured. During the pilot, two possible relatives of the perpetrator were found in DNA databases, who live in the United States. To investigate that lead further, a request for legal assistance to the US is now underway.

title: Olympic athlete and former politician Mieke Sterk dies aged 80
lead: Former athlete and former politician Mieke Sterk has died at the age of 80. The Haarlem native was part of the quartet that ran a world record of 43.4 seconds in the heats of the 4x100 metres at the 1968 Olympic Games in Mexico City. In the final the quartet finished fourth. Sterk's time, together with Wilma van den Berg, Truus Hennipman-Cruiming and Corrie Bakker, remained the Dutch record for 44 years. It was only equalled during the 2011 World Athletics Championships in Daegu, South Korea, and a year later the record fell. Sterk was a sprinter, hurdler and multi-event athlete. During her career she won twenty national titles in individual and relay events. Outside the track she also stood out for her (in those years) unconventional behaviour. For example, just before the opening ceremony of the 1968 Summer Games she cut off her skirt, because in her view the garment was "te truttig" (too prim). During her career Sterk was politically engaged. For instance, in 1969 she refused to take part in the European Championships in Athens, in protest against the dictatorial regime that was in power in Greece. After her athletics career Sterk became a politician. At the request of Felix Rottenberg she sat for the Labour Party from 1994 to 1998 in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. She was given a portfolio including sport and care for people with disabilities. Criticism of the PvdA's policy brought an early end to her political career in 1997. After harsh words directed at the party executive, Sterk was placed in an unelectable position, after which she was not re-elected.

title: Explosives from WWII found at Eindhoven Airport
lead: Two explosives have been found at Eindhoven Airport. They are explosives left over from the Second World War. According to a spokesperson for the Royal Marechaussee, one is a mortar shell and the other is a provisionally unidentified object. The Explosive Ordnance Disposal Service of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> will render the bombs harmless. Air traffic at Eindhoven Airport is not affected by the find. The explosives were discovered during groundwork. This is related to the major renovation of the airport, which begins early next year. WWII newsletter Interested in the Second World War? Then subscribe to our newsletter here.

title: Feminist Aletta Jacobs to get a statue in central The Hague
lead: Aletta Jacobs (1854-1929) will get a statue in the centre of The Hague. The statue of the feminist must be unveiled by the end of 2028 at the latest at the Wijnhaven, close to the The Hague campus of the University of <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>. Already in 2017, former House Speaker and then PvdA municipal councillor Jeltje van Nieuwenhoven proposed the plan to put a woman on a pedestal in The Hague for once. And although Jacobs was born in the Groningen village of Sappemeer, as a champion of women's suffrage and the first female doctor in the Netherlands she was, according to the municipality of The Hague, extremely suitable to get a likeness in the city. Hundredth death anniversary. Originally the plan was to unveil a statue for the celebration of one hundred years of women's suffrage in 2019, but that did not succeed. Now the municipality is trying to place the likeness well before the commemoration of the hundredth death anniversary of Jacobs on 10 August 2029. Meanwhile the intended location has also changed, writes regional broadcaster West. First the statue was to come at the Hofvijver, but according to alderman Van Basten Batenburg that spot is not suitable. "The scale and appearance of the intended statue do not relate well to the green character and the other statues along the Hofvijver", writes the alderman. The newly chosen place close to the campus she does find a "fitting location". First feminist wave. Jacobs was born in 1854 as the eighth of eleven children in a Jewish family. As the first woman in the Netherlands she obtained her university degree and became a doctor. After graduating from the State University of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> she went to London, where she specialised in paediatrics and as a women's doctor. She became an important figure in the first feminist wave. For example, Jacobs fought for women's suffrage and equality in marriage. She became co-founder and chair of the Vereeniging voor Vrouwenkiesrecht. In September 1919, partly through her efforts, women's suffrage was introduced. At the State University of Groningen a statue of Jacobs already stands. She is also included in the Canon of the Netherlands, the list of the most important themes from the nation's history.

title: 'Cutting civil servants is a nice plan, but it has never worked'
lead: The cabinet's plan to make deep cuts in the number of central government civil servants has the support of almost the entire <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity>. At the same time, almost everyone is convinced that it will not succeed. Within nine years, 25,000 of the 160,000 civil servants must have been cut, state secretary <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> for Slagvaardige Overheid announced. That would yield an annual saving of 3.5 billion euros. Money that is badly needed to balance the budget. But recent history offers little hope: of the last ten cabinets, eight argued for fewer central government civil servants. None of those eight cabinets ultimately managed it. In fact, in recent years the number of civil servants at ministries rose from 110,000 to 160,000. "It has exploded," says former senior civil servant Roel Bekker. According to him, that is mainly because the number of parliamentary motions is higher than ever. This calendar year there were already well over 4,700. It is a monstrous task for civil servants to examine and answer all of them. Arjan Noorlander: 'Plan is a castle in the air' "This goes down well with voters and MPs, but it is not feasible. It is precisely those MPs who burden civil servants with endless questions and regulations that they have endless work on. The Tweede Kamer currently has a record number of seventeen factions. They all want to arrange something for their own constituency through motions and parliamentary questions. Saying that you are going to shrink the ministries is, according to the <entity id="org:centraal-planbureau">Centraal Planbureau</entity> and the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Rekenkamer</entity>, a false promise. You simply won't achieve it. Don't do it, they say to the current <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>, once again. Certainly if you have no concrete plan for where the civil servants are supposed to go. And what does the cabinet do? Exactly that: name an amount of 3.5 billion, but no concrete plan. So for now this cabinet is building castles in the air." Bekker also finds it remarkable that the cabinet already links a concrete amount of 3.5 billion to the cut, without it being clear which departments must cut how many jobs. What is clear is that <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and defence remain untouched. Implementing agencies such as the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> are not excluded in advance. Those organisations are already under considerable pressure and in fact need more staff rather than less. Bekker worked in 2007 at the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> when he was given the task of shrinking the government by 12,800 fte. With great difficulty he managed, by his own account, to bring about a "dip" in the development of the number of civil servants. But in the years after, tens of thousands of jobs were added again. "Politicians quickly forgot the intention and came up with all sorts of things that cost enormous amounts of staff. More police on the streets, expanding prisons. You then have to box against that." Crises and the whim of the day The number of motions has been rising for years. According to Bekker, that is partly because "the whim of the day" rules. He also sees that parliamentarians increasingly insist on tailor-made solutions and devise complicated regulations. Implementing those places a heavy burden on civil servants. Crises such as corona, the childcare benefits affair and gas extraction in Groningen also led to extra civil servants. "The mood in cabinets was: put more people on it. But somehow it is difficult to put an end to it." MPs themselves also find the number of motions far too high. CDA member Harmen Krul calls it "too bizarre for words" that the figure of 5,000 is likely to be reached this year. "Crazy," says Gidi Markuszower. "A great many motions are not adopted, so why submit them?" BBB MP Caroline van der Plas also thinks parliament should be self-critical, but at the same time she understands that the number of motions is rising. "There are a lot of new MPs. They want to make their point and be seen. Because they want to stand higher on the list at the next elections." It is a trend that worries former civil servant Bekker. He therefore pleads for "strong ministers" who simply do not answer parliamentary questions. "If you say: 'At this moment I do not have the capacity', then I may hope that the House sees that this is a very reasonable answer." The Hague negotiations continue The proposed civil service cut is an important part of the budget, on which the minority Jetten cabinet is again talking with the opposition this week. It mainly concerns the tax plan. The road to a deal with the opposition still seems long. Meanwhile the deadline is approaching. Today ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker visits <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>.

title: Judge sides with Booking, staff must be required to come to the office more often
lead: Booking.com may require staff to spend 40 percent of their working time at the office. If someone works five days, that means two days at the office. The works council of the hotel booking site did not want to agree to that requirement, so the company took the matter to the court in Amsterdam. And the judge now sides with Booking. The judge agrees with Booking that "meeting each other at the office can contribute to promoting mutual connection, training and development and effective cooperation between teams and team members." Amsterdam is the base location. The judge also finds the requirement acceptable because encouraging employees to come to the office in Amsterdam more often did not work. At present only 27 percent of employees are at the office at least 40 percent of their working time. The judge also says that the hotel booking site never claimed to be a company where you never have to come to the office. "Employees were hired with Amsterdam as their base location. They themselves have influenced their commuting time through their choice of place of residence, and they can also change that." A transition period of six months will now apply before the requirement takes effect. Exceptions can also still be made for individual employees who run into problems because of the new policy. Lost time and extra costs The works council of Booking opposed the plan because more office work means, according to the council, a worsening for part of the employees. Nearly half of the 6000 employees filled in a survey by the works council. 87 percent said they were satisfied with the current rules. According to the council, many people said they will suffer from lost time and extra costs due to commuting. They also expected to be less able to work with focus. Corona During the corona pandemic, companies with office staff switched en masse to working from home. Many employees liked that, and it became here to stay. But in recent years some companies want employees to come to the office more often again.

title: Dead animal delivered again at Oldebroek town hall
lead: A package containing a dead animal was delivered at the town hall in Oldebroek yesterday afternoon. An enclosed letter states that the council is not doing enough about the wolf. <entity id="person:tanja-haseloop-amsing">Burgemeester Haseloop-Amsing</entity> of the Veluwe municipality rejects the action and wants security cameras installed as soon as possible. During a committee meeting last night the mayor made the incident public, reports Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> . She said counter staff found the package suspicious and called in the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. She did not say which animal it was. Intimidation is not the way. The mayor understands there are great concerns about the wolf, but finds this goes too far. "Although we understand the despair very well, we are doing what we can." According to Haseloop-Amsing, the options for measures against the wolf are limited, because the province and <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> are largely responsible for that. "And intimidation is not the way to get something done." Earlier dead animals. It is not the first time the municipality has had to deal with dead animals. A week and a half ago, unknown persons placed about six sheep that had been killed by wolves along a road in protest. Mid-July a dead sheep was left in front of the town hall. Slightly earlier, a cart with about ten mauled sheep was driven through the village. Investigation. It is still unknown who delivered the package. The police are conducting neighborhood inquiries around the town hall. It is also not known whether a report has been filed.

title: Growing criticism of headstrong conduct by minister Heinen
lead: Criticism is growing among D66 and the CDA of minister Eelco Heinen of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. Behind the scenes it can be heard that he works too much on his own and speaks out of turn. This morning, after a meeting with the ChristenUnie about support for the Tax Plan, the VVD minister again caused irritation among coalition partners. Heinen suggested that he has a solution for the adjustments to box 3, which will cost the state treasury many billions in the coming years. "I think I have put together a puzzle that can count on broad support," he said. But inquiries with the other coalition parties show that it is not yet that far: there is no deal within the coalition, there is no funding proposal. "He is not speaking on behalf of the whole <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>," is what can be heard. Yet the rule is that a minister always speaks on behalf of the whole cabinet; this is called unity of cabinet policy. ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker, who came out right after Heinen, said that at least she has not been presented with funding and that therefore he cannot simply count on her support. Moreover, she is worried that the problem still has not been solved. Markuszower Notably, Heinen held a conversation on his own initiative yesterday with parliamentary group leader Gidi Markuszower. Other coalition parties and cabinet members were not informed of that. However, according to the ministry of Finance, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> had been informed about it in advance. The former PVV member has seven seats in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, but has not been invited by the cabinet to budget talks. Even so, he was at the ministry of Finance on Tuesday morning to talk about possible support for the Tax Plan. Afterwards Markuszower was enthusiastic. He says he makes few demands. "I had a good conversation with <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> and I hope it leads to a package that is better." Markuszower considers support for the Tax Plan important because otherwise he fears elections. "Nobody is waiting for Jesse Klaver as prime minister." Minister Heinen does not think it strange that he arranged with Markuszower independently. That is necessary, he says, in his search for as much support as possible. "Let's speak openly with everyone in parliament. See whether we can accommodate wishes and work toward broad support." Not the first time Criticism of Heinen's headstrong conduct has been heard from the CDA and D66 for some time. At the end of August the cabinet even briefly wobbled because of it. The minister of Finance had that month spoken with the financial spokespersons of several opposition parties about support for the budget and the tax plan. That was separate from the talks the top of the cabinet was having at the same time with the parliamentary group leaders of those same parties. Heinen soon came out with the announcement that "the puzzle" had been laid with the opposition parties, while according to D66 and the CDA that was not at all the case. There was no agreement. 'Inflexible' The minister of Finance drew up a draft budget which he said could count on a majority in the House of Representatives, but D66 premier Jetten and CDA deputy premier Van den Brink, among others, found the story far too right-wing. This would close the door to Pro, the largest opposition party in both the House and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. Early October Heinen also had to admit that his first plan for funding the box 3 gap put too much on the plate of relatively small savers. He had underestimated that from his hyperfocus on a solution, he said in the House of Representatives. Also among several opposition parties who are sitting at the table with him these days, it can be heard that the minister of Finance is 'little constructive' in talks, 'inflexible' when it comes to their proposals, and lives in his 'own financial reality'. Time is running out meanwhile. CDA <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">leider Bontenbal</entity> wants quick clarity about the outcome of the negotiations. "What I find very important is that we come to an outcome this week. It is taking far too long, I had wanted a deal already in the summer." Opposition parties are increasing the pressure. "Before you know it we'll have to go back to the voters and I want to prevent that," said Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> last night.

title: Tens of thousands of seniors' emergency buttons to fail when 2G network stops
lead: Tens of thousands of seniors with an emergency alarm button risk ending up in life-threatening situations. That is what EenVandaag reports, based on its own research. The 2G network these buttons are connected to will be shut down soon. The alarm systems can be pressed by vulnerable seniors, for example after a fall at home, when they suddenly feel unwell, or in an unsafe situation, such as unknown people at the door. By pressing the button, an alarm signal is sent to pre-set contact persons. These can be family members or, for example, the district nursing service. The research by EenVandaag shows that some 30,000 to 80,000 mobile alarm systems function on 2G networks. These include, for example, senior phones, emergency buttons and alarm watches. Moreover, many of these systems are still for sale. And buyers are not warned that the systems will soon stop working. Sellers Bol, Thuiszorgwinkel.nl and LifeWatcher have, after being asked, said they will adjust the advertisements on their sites or are willing to exchange products, EenVandaag writes. Outdated networks The senior association ANBO-PCOB heard a few weeks ago about the problems when it was approached by EenVandaag . The association had earlier received a report from a woman from Zeist. She reported that the device with which she could normally call for help did not work. That also ran on 2G. After EenVandaag's questions, the association ran into problems and also decided to place a warning on its site . Telecom providers are stopping the 2G and 3G networks because they are outdated. Odido already shut down its network in 2023. KPN will do so at the end of 2027. Provider KPN has already placed an article on its website to warn people . "We communicate to our customers that we are stopping the service", a KPN spokesperson says. But it becomes complicated when those parties provide a service to their customers via the network again, such as with alarm buttons. The provider has no view of that. However, people can use a help line to check whether their system is connected via 2G or 3G. He does warn that this only works for KPN customers. If the systems run via the network of another provider, that cannot be checked with that number. 'Life-threatening' It has been known for some time that the networks are being shut down, explains the spokesperson for ANBO-PCOB. But this is only known to a very small audience. For example, the Authority for Consumers & Markets already issued a warning about the consequences of this at the end of 2023. "But many people do not know this." ANBO-PCOB warns of life-threatening situations if the systems suddenly stop working. If someone, for example, falls in the bathroom and lives alone, but the button to call for help does not work, the spokesperson explains. "That can sometimes lead to death." The senior association therefore urges people to check their device and, if it is unclear, to contact the supplier. It also advises that, if necessary, the children of the elderly keep an eye on things. The senior association also hopes that the government will take on a role, for example through a campaign. That would have to reach as large an audience as possible. "Nobody of course wants an elderly person to be unable to call for help after a fall. I understand that the seniors' association is worried about this", responds a spokesperson on behalf of the Minister for Long-Term Care, <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Mirjam Sterk</entity>. She emphasises that the shutdown of the 2G network is primarily the responsibility of the telecom providers and of the care providers to ensure that the assistive devices they use work properly. The Ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> supports the care providers in this.

title: Gas price keeps rising, above 100 euros per megawatt hour
lead: The European gas price has today risen above the 100 euro per megawatt hour mark. That is the highest level since the gas crisis of 2022, when Russia invaded Ukraine. In February, before America and Israel began the war against Iran, the price on the wholesale market was still below 30 euros per megawatt hour. Since then, important refineries and liquefied natural gas (lng) pipelines in the Middle East have been hit, so less is being exported from there. Dynamic contract For people with a dynamic contract, a higher gas price means they will also pay more right away. Their energy supplier sets a new price every day based on the wholesale price. Around 8 percent of all households have such a dynamic contract. To illustrate: today a customer of one of the larger providers of dynamic contracts pays 1.95 euros per cubic metre of natural gas, including tax. Exactly one year ago that was still only 1.13 euros. According to the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity>, households use an average of around 790 cubic metres of gas per year. Based on the price from a year ago, that comes to around 893 euros per year, and based on today's price it is around 1540 euros. For people with a variable contract (around 37 percent of households), the gas price usually changes every three months or half a year. They therefore notice the higher gas price with some delay. More than half of households (54 percent) have a fixed energy contract. During the term of their contract, the price they pay for gas does not change. But when their contract expires and they have to sign a new one, they may be confronted with a higher price.

title: Community service demanded for séance at children's graves in Amersfoort cemetery
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has demanded community service of up to 200 hours against four women suspected of desecrating graves at the Rusthof cemetery in Amersfoort. The women held a spiritual session there in 2021, without the knowledge of relatives. Six women had received permission from the then director to hold a gathering after closing time at the cemetery about spiritual phenomena. Accompanied by an employee of the cemetery, they tried to make contact with the spirits of the dead. For this they used a device that measures electric fields, which according to the women would react to the energy of the deceased. The women also tried to make paranormal contact with deceased children at the cemetery. The gathering only came to light a few weeks later, when a father of a deceased child found a camera with footage of the séance. In the end, 57 relatives jointly filed a complaint, and some people did so individually. When the matter came to light, the director was placed on leave. A new director was subsequently appointed. Unusual case According to the OM, graves were touched and contact was sought with the deceased. "It is a very uncomfortable feeling that this kind of act takes place at the cemetery where your loved one lies", RTV Utrecht quotes the public prosecutor. The prosecutor spoke of an unusual case in the courtroom. The case is also unique, according to the prosecutor, because the court must answer the question of whether paranormal investigation is a form of grave desecration, for which the women must be prosecuted and punished. Questions Only one of the suspects was present in court today. For her, the lowest community service of 40 hours, of which 20 suspended, was demanded. Several relatives of children buried at the cemetery were also present. "We live not only with the loss, but also with questions about what exactly happened", said one of the mothers. "We left our child there, because we thought it was safe there." The lawyers for the suspects argue that nothing was damaged or destroyed and that there is therefore no question of grave desecration. The court will rule soon.

title: Minister: high-speed train in Spain ran through red signal on instruction from traffic control
lead: The high-speed train that ran into a stationary train in Spain had continued on with the permission of the train traffic control despite a red signal. That is what Transport Minister Puente said at a press conference. At least 68 people have died in the disaster. 107 people were injured. According to Puente, there was a computer fault before the accident and the collision may be related to it. The control system at Urda station failed around 08.30 hours, he said, so the safety system stopped working on a 63-kilometre stretch. As a result, all trains on that stretch came to a standstill. Permission to proceed The high-speed train of the national railway company Renfe was then nevertheless given permission by the train traffic control to continue, despite the signals being red. Normally the protocol is that a train maintains a speed of up to 40 kilometres per hour so that drivers can drive by sight and still have enough time to intervene. Here, however, the driver was given permission to continue the journey at a higher speed. According to Puente, that decision was taken "under inexplicable circumstances". 147 passengers The train then collided with a stationary high-speed train of operator Iryo carrying 147 passengers. Most of the fatal victims were in the stationary train. At least 40 people in that train lost their lives. Survivors speak of a very hard impact. "I was in the aisle and was thrown four or five seats further", says a man who was in the stationary train, speaking to radio station Onda Cero. He saw dead people lying in the carriage after the collision, he says. Prime Minister Sánchez went to the command centre in Toledo, which is near the disaster site. "Today all of Spain is in mourning", he told the massed press. He speaks of an event "that is unacceptable for a country like Spain". He expressed his sympathy with the victims and their families. He announced three days of national mourning starting tomorrow. A brief reconstruction of what went wrong this morning: The prime minister says the first priority is support for the victims. "Our second goal is to clarify what happened." An independent commission is investigating the disaster, and the ministries of Transport and of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> are also conducting investigations. Sánchez: "We will get to the bottom of what happened. And if there has been negligence, it will come to light." It is the second train disaster in Spain this year with many deaths. On 18 January two high-speed trains derailed in Adamuz, in the southern province of Córdoba. More than forty people died. Other major train accidents also occurred this year. The Spanish train drivers' union had earlier called for better rail safety and had already planned a strike for tomorrow before the accident. That will go ahead, union Semaf announced. "Semaf maintains the strike called in defence of rail safety, as well as adherence to the commitments to bring about structural change in safety", the union writes in a statement.

title: Utrecht will keep banning public nuisance makers from the station area for another two years
lead: For the fourth time in a row, the municipality of Utrecht is extending a so-called area ban around Utrecht Centraal station. Until 1 November 2028, officers and enforcers can keep people who cause nuisance out of parts of the Utrecht city centre and Lombok-Oost. For years the municipality has struggled with aggressive behaviour, intimidation, theft and violent incidents in the station area. The nuisance is caused by addicts, homeless people, criminals and young people. Therefore, in September 2022 the municipality designated areas where persons causing nuisance may temporarily not enter. This measure was already extended three times before, and the areas have also already been expanded. Slight decline in incidents According to the city council, this is an important measure to tackle nuisance. Even so, the number of incidents has hardly decreased in recent years, RTV Utrecht writes. Police data show that it rose from 4959 incidents in 2023 and 5125 in 2025, and slightly fell to 4278 in 2026. According to the municipality, a slight decrease is visible in pickpocketing, shoplifting, nuisance from vagrants and nuisance related to alcohol and drug use. Serious incidents such as assault, threats, public violence and brawls occurred in the city centre in 2026 just as often as in previous years. This year, up to and including August, a total of 744 persons have received an area ban. That is roughly comparable to previous years. In some places such a ban has been imposed slightly less often. The municipality thinks this is because people know that public nuisance makers can receive an area ban there and that the measure's familiarity works preventively. Long-term matter The measure would expire in November. Mayor <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity> considers that irresponsible. According to her, the number of times the measure has been taken indicates how urgent the problem is. "The nuisance is there and you want to be able to act effectively against it," she explains to RTV Utrecht. Extending this measure is part of a set of measures. Because, the mayor argues, some people who cause nuisance also need care. If it is up to the mayor, the municipality may be caring on the one hand, but on the other hand sometimes has to act firmly. It is not all happening overnight. "It is a long-term matter," says Dijksma.

title: Woman, 93, breaks back after being robbed on the street in Amsterdam
lead: A woman of 93 was attacked on the street in Amsterdam-Slotervaart yesterday afternoon and robbed of her handbag. The very elderly woman fell hard and broke her back. That is reported by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The robbery took place around 14.00 hours at a flat on Comeniusstraat. The woman was on her way at that moment to a friend for a game of Rummikub, her son tells AT5. The suspect then ran off with her handbag. The 93-year-old woman is still in hospital. Screaming Residents heard screaming and rushed to help the woman, they tell the city broadcaster. "I thought: those are children playing outside. My wife ran downstairs, and shortly after I went down too, and there lay our 93-year-old neighbour on the street," says Ed Krauss. "She was extremely confused. It is so sad." The police are looking for more people who saw something. The suspect is a man of around 40 with a light complexion and light brown hair. He wore a dark winter coat and carried a large weekend bag. A police spokesperson tells AT5 of an "incomprehensible, cowardly deed".

title: 'Winter Support Package' for Ukraine: Netherlands provides 500 million for air defence
lead: The Netherlands is giving Ukraine 500 million euros in military support. This 'winter support package' is intended for air defence and drones. That is what <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> said at a press conference after his meeting with Ukrainian President Zelensky at the Catshuis in The Hague. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> had already reserved this money for Ukraine. Zelensky expressed his gratitude for all the support he receives from the Netherlands, and from other allies as well. His country needs it badly, he says, referring to the fact that Russia has recently stepped up attacks on, among other things, energy plants, bridges and roads. This is how the new support package was announced: Jetten repeatedly stressed that Dutch support is "rock solid". "Ukraine has been defending itself against barbaric Russian aggression for years. Not only for itself, but also for us in Europe. You are not alone: your struggle is our struggle." He also called on other European countries to keep supporting Ukraine. After the meeting with Jetten, Zelensky held a conversation in which Minister Yesilgöz of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> and <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> also took part. This evening he will also visit <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> at Paleis Huis ten Bosch. 1,2 miljard in drie jaar, or 1,2 billion over three years. Meanwhile, <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">minister Sjoerdsma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-bho">Buitenlandse Handel en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking</entity> is in Kyiv today. There he announced that the Netherlands will make 1,2 billion euros available over the coming three years for non-military support to Ukraine. This money was already reserved: 878 million euros from the coalition agreement, and 327 million extra was announced on Prinsjesdag. That money is intended for "the most urgent needs", explained premier Jetten, such as humanitarian aid, drinking water, energy, reconstruction and demining. Jetten also pointed to cooperation with the business sector. "We must deploy Dutch expertise where it is most needed." A substantial part of the promised millions will go to Dutch companies helping Ukraine with reconstruction. 40 million euros is already being transferred this year to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund, intended for restoring energy infrastructure. These millions are coming sooner than previously agreed, to help Ukraine get through the winter. Peace negotiations in November When asked, Zelensky also addressed the talks between his country, Russia and the United States that are on the agenda, possibly in Abu Dhabi. There is no date yet. Zelensky expects that after the American midterm elections, between 6 and 10 November, talks about ending the war will resume. For the time being, there is no European representation involved. Zelensky keeps calling for this. According to him, it would help if Europe projected a bit more unity so that someone can be brought to the table.

title: Podcast De Monarchie: how the royal house and defence embrace each other
lead: Princess Amalia was promoted to a higher rank at the Royal Netherlands Navy last week. She has been promoted from corporal to sergeant. It is part of her study and work track at the Defensity College. Amalia's choice for defence fits in with the line of her family. "There has been a long history between the Oranges and the armed forces. It began already during the Eighty Years' War," military historian Erwin van Loo says in the podcast De Monarchie. "That bond has remained, and it really comes from two sides: the armed forces are Orange-minded and the royal family embraces that." Want to listen? You can hear more about this story in the new episode of the NOS podcast De Monarchie via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. "The bond between the royal house and defence begins already with William of Orange. First the stadtholders and later the king held supreme command over the army," Van Loo says. This lasted until the 19th century. The last king who actively took part in combat was King Willem II during the Battle of Waterloo. After 1848 the power of the royal house was restricted, and so the role of the king in defence became more symbolic, but according to Van Loo the bond is still very close. He noticed that himself when he was deployed to Mali as a reserve officer. "I was there during King's Day, and at such a military camp far from home, you see how strong that bond with the Royal House is. It is celebrated with a special roll call and then orange bitters is also handed out, non-alcoholic of course, because you are on deployment." After Willem III there were no male heirs to the throne, and because women were only welcome in defence after the Second World War, Wilhelmina and Juliana, for example, could not take an active part themselves. Van Loo: "Still, they held a warm heart towards the army. Wilhelmina in particular always felt a very warm bond with the armed forces. During the First and Second World Wars Wilhelmina played an important role morally in supporting soldiers. She was not called the soldiers' queen for nothing." <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Willem-Alexander</entity> to Sarajevo After his secondary school, Willem-Alexander completed his conscription with the navy and then stayed in service. "What is not so well known is that Willem-Alexander actually flew over Sarajevo when the city was under siege. He very much wanted to experience that himself, but it was certainly not without risk," the military historian says. Willem-Alexander remained in service until he was sworn in as king in 2013. As a member of the government, the king may not serve in defence, so he had to lay down his duties. He received an honourable discharge. 'Amalia effect' Amalia is now the first princess of Orange to be active in defence, and it seems to be a trend, because in Spain, Norway and Belgium the crown princesses also followed military training. It proved good for their popularity. And the reverse also holds: through Amalia's participation the number of applications to Defensity College increased, and after Máxima was trained as a reservist, the number of visitors to the Defence vacancy site rose. Whether Amalia will end up in an active combat situation after her training seems unlikely to military historian Erwin van Loo: "If you look at history, that was always avoided, so I think that would be the case for Amalia too. In any case, only a small part of the military ends up at the front. There are also supporting roles through which you can contribute in another way."

title: House of Representatives support for the budget for roads, locks and bridges
lead: In the House of Representatives a majority is taking shape to vote for the budget of the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity>. That emerged during the budget debate. Besides the coalition parties, opposition parties JA21, SGP and CU can also give their approval, even though there is too little money for everything that needs to be done. These parties have a majority in the House of Representatives. JA21 can live with the money going mainly to making existing roads and bridges safe again. The SGP also regrets that certain new construction projects have been put on ice, but understands that maintaining existing infrastructure is more important for now. The ChristenUnie, like the other parties, believes it must never come to the point where so much infrastructure has a maintenance backlog. And in the future more money must also go to making new housing estates accessible. But the party is not "going to topple the budget" for now. BBB has fought hard for regional projects such as the Nedersaksenlijn to go ahead, and is broadly satisfied. But the party does not yet want to say out loud that it will vote in favour. With BBB on board there is a majority in both the House of Representatives and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. Outdated bridges and roads <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Minister Karremans</entity> (VVD) and <entity id="person:annet-bertram">staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> (CDA) received compliments for their approach and for the attention they have paid to the wishes from the opposition. Various factions also expressed understanding for the financial choices. Maintenance of outdated bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure takes priority for them. In the coming years 18 billion euros will go to that. A large part of that amount is taken from planned new projects for which money had already been reserved. Those projects are therefore put on the long finger. In the debate on the budget, parties are still trying to get some adjustments through. For example, coalition party D66 wants a new tram line to be put 'on the list' for a housing estate to be built near Utrecht. And the VVD advocates extending the metro and Randstadrail around Rotterdam and The Hague anyway. But there is no money for that in the budget. Karremans has already said that parties themselves must find majorities for small changes, and that they must then also agree on where this tax money should come from. The various factions will still make attempts to do so in the coming weeks. Pro said in the debate that the party wants to cooperate on an overall deal covering all ministry budgets, but that Infrastructure needs more money before the party will vote in favour. Mileage charge In the debate there was also a brief discussion about road pricing or a mileage charge. D66, VVD and CDA have agreed among themselves to examine a reform of car tax. The condition is that motorists must not be worse off. In the debate the VVD did not rule out that the study could lead to some form of mileage charge, and that the VVD would then not be opposed in advance. That could also be pay-per-use via toll roads. But the chance that anything happens within this cabinet term is practically nil. Support for more budgets There are several budgets from ministers that can expect the support of a majority in the House of Representatives and almost certainly in the Eerste Kamer. These are Education under <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">minister Letschert</entity> (D66), Public Health under <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">minister Hermans</entity> (VVD) and Social Affairs under <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">minister Vijlbrief</entity> (D66). The latter ministry is covered by Pro's pledge after the cut to social security was scrapped. The biggest hurdle for the minority cabinet, however, is the 2027 Tax Plan of <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> Heinen (VVD). A large part of the factions are still struggling to negotiate on it.

title: Nationwide housing order for poultry with immediate effect due to bird flu
lead: A nationwide housing order for poultry takes effect immediately. According to <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> (Agriculture), this is necessary because three bird flu outbreaks have occurred in a short time. The virus has been confirmed in recent days in Lutjegast (Groningen), Middelie (North Holland) and Grootegast (Groningen). Wild birds recently found in the Netherlands and other European countries also had the disease. People who keep birds as a hobby do not have to comply with the housing order, but must shield their birds. This can be done, for example, by keeping them in an aviary. 'Preventing new outbreaks' Erkens says he is aware that poultry farmers are hit hard. "Still, it is important to limit contact between kept birds and possibly infected wild birds as much as possible," he says in a response. "This way we are doing everything we can to prevent new outbreaks." A number of other measures will also apply again. For example, there will again be a ban on visitors to places with birds, meaning people may only enter in necessary cases. Also, birds that pose a risk may no longer be exhibited. Bird flu has also been confirmed in Denmark, Germany and the United Kingdom, among others. Because bird migration is now getting underway, the risk of the virus spreading increases further. Last year a nationwide housing order was also introduced, which was lifted in June this year. The number of infections had then dropped sharply, although the ministry already called the virus "unpredictable" at the time. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is working on a plan to vaccinate laying hens compulsorily.

title: Restaurants in Sardinia ban phones at the table: 'Encouraging parent-child conversation'
lead: A group of fifteen restaurants on the Italian island of Sardinia is temporarily banning the use of phones and other screens at the table. The Italian regional newspaper L'Unione Sarda reports this. The initiative is meant as a trial to curb, among other things, screen use by children and to encourage conversation at the table. The children's ombudsman of the Italian island leads the project, called A tavola senza schermi, or 'At the table without screens'. The participating restaurants signed up voluntarily, and the newspaper writes that the businesses had no doubts about taking part. "Restaurants play an essential role in promoting the intimacy that families rediscover when they go out to eat," says Emanuele Frongia to the British newspaper The Guardian. Frongia is chair of a hospitality and tourism association on the island and is involved in the project. "We increasingly see that during these moments the lively chatter gives way to periods of silence, because people are looking at their devices. Often a child is handed one to keep them quiet." Risks of the digital age. When guests eat at one of the fifteen restaurants, they must put away or hand in their phones and other screens. The table party then receives a package with games or colouring sheets. The package was designed by the Italian federation of paediatricians and is meant to help children under 18 start a conversation with their parents, for example by sharing stories about their day. The package also contains a brochure describing the risks of spending too much time online. The leaflet also includes tips to limit social media use. According to the paediatricians, problems stem not only from the time spent on technology but also from the type of content children watch. The paediatricians state that problems such as insomnia, social isolation and self-harm are occurring more and more often. Protection. The children's ombudsman, Anna Cau, says minors must be protected against misuse of electronic devices and inappropriate content. She also believes parents should be more aware of the risks, but also of the possibilities of the digital age. The trial starts next week and lasts one month. <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">De ombudsman</entity> hopes that more restaurants will join.

title: Police find vapes worth half a million euros in Tilburg property
lead: The police seized thousands of vapes in a property in Tilburg this week. According to the police, the illegal vapes have a combined value of nearly half a million euros. Officers entered the property on the night of Monday to Tuesday after a tip. The property contained three pallets with boxes holding more than 5100 THC vapes and 17.120 flavoured e-cigarettes. A 28-year-old man has been arrested. THC vapes contain a psychoactive substance from the cannabis plant. Legally, THC vapes fall under hard drugs. The man is therefore suspected of possession of hard drugs. Regular weed and hashish fall under soft drugs in the Netherlands. Contents unclear. Flavoured vapes have been banned in the Netherlands since 2024, but are still popular among young people. According to the police, the THC vapes can be especially harmful. Initial police analyses show that they contain highly concentrated hemp oil or synthetic cannabis. The exact contents of a vape are not always clear, the police say. The police are further investigating the find in Tilburg and the suspect. Omroep Brabant writes that the police also seized two jammers. These are devices that can, among other things, disrupt GPS signals and phone traffic.

title: New prison sentence for Iranian filmmaker and dissident Jafar Panahi
lead: Filmmaker Jafar Panahi has been sentenced in Iran to five years and one month in prison. His lawyer reports this to Iranian media. It is unclear exactly what he is accused of. It is not clear whether the Iranian director is in Iran or abroad. In addition to the prison sentence, all of Panahi's possessions are being seized. He receives a two-year travel ban and may not use social media for two years. Panahi and his lawyer were both absent from the verdict. They only found out when the filmmaker discovered that his bank accounts had been blocked. The lawyer then made inquiries with the judiciary, which informed him of the sentence. 'Propaganda' The 66-year-old director is one of the best-known Iranian dissidents. He has been arrested countless times and has been convicted several times by Iranian courts for "propaganda against the regime". In 2010 he was sentenced to six years in prison, though he never served that sentence. In 2022 he served a prison sentence in the notorious Evin prison. He was released on bail after six months. In 2025 he was sentenced in absentia to one year in prison. Panhi was abroad at the time, but he reportedly returned to Iran early this year, when the United States and Israel attacked the country. He may have left the country again since then. The court's 2010 ruling also stated that Panahi could not make films for twenty years, but Panahi did not abide by that ban. In secret and with simple means he managed to release six more films. Sometimes these had to be smuggled out of the country on a USB stick. Golden Palm and Oscar nomination Panahi's work addresses social issues within Iran, such as the position of women or the actions of the Iranian regime. In the country almost all of his films are banned. Abroad his work has won many prizes. His latest film, It was just an accident, is about a former prisoner who wants to take revenge on the guard who tortured him in prison. With it he won the Golden Palm at the Cannes Film Festival last year. He was also nominated for an Oscar and two Golden Globes.

title: Man arrested for flying drone over Eemshaven
lead: The police have arrested a man who allegedly flew a drone over the Eemshaven. That is what the mayor of the municipality of <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity> announced this evening during the council meeting, RTV Noord reports. The police were able to take over control of the drone and seize the drone. The man was arrested last Tuesday, according to the mayor. The suspect is a man from Belgium. His identity will not be disclosed further. The man has been questioned and released, but remains a suspect. Flying over the Eemshaven is prohibited, among other reasons because of the presence of a large industrial port and critical infrastructure such as power cables and a helicopter port. Defence also has a fixed location there. Other drones The police do not assume there is a connection between this drone and other unknown drones that have recently been seen in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>. This happened in Meeden, Scheemda and Zuidbroek, among other places.

title: Frustration among the left-wing opposition over D66's U-turn on tax assessment for the Oranjes
lead: That Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> does not intend to have members of the Royal House pay tax is causing frustration among the left-wing opposition. They point out that D66 itself submitted a similar plan two years ago. That motion by D66 MP Joost Sneller received a broad majority in 2024, but then-prime minister <entity id="person:mark-rutte">Mark Rutte</entity> and his successor Dick Schoof set the motion aside. D66 leader Jetten is now doing the same with a similar motion by Pro MP <entity id="person:laura-bromet">Laura Bromet</entity>. The same applies to an adopted motion by SP MP Sandra Beckerman to make the royal house more transparent about its spending. Jetten calls that plan "in effect unworkable". Pro and SP do not understand the prime minister's position at all. "D66 was angry every year that the motions were not carried out. Now the party has the unique opportunity to think about the future of the royal house," says Beckerman. "You would think you would seize that opportunity, wouldn't you?" 'Barren dynamic' In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, the tax exemptions of the Oranjes have been debated for more than ten years. In 2024 there was, for the first time in parliamentary history, a two-thirds majority for the D66 plan to make the king pay tax on his income. That majority is needed because it involves a constitutional amendment. But Jetten is no longer willing to go along with this plan. He calls the annually recurring discussion a "barren dynamic", because each time "the familiar positions come up again". The prime minister is therefore focusing on broader research into "a future-proof royal house". He agreed with Pro MP Bromet that they would then come up with concrete proposals. King of the reserve bench Several parties praise the role of the royal house during the budget debate. "It is not cheap, but at the same time of incalculable value to our country," says JA21 parliamentary group leader Joost Eerdmans, for example. "The king brings connection, neutrality and stability and is of direct value to trade interests." CDA MP Tijs van den Brink also says there is "every reason to be happy with the royal house". He received a commitment from Prime Minister Jetten that the proposals will not lead to a ceremonial monarchy. A large number of parties, by contrast, see a bigger role for the king in the future. Since 2017 the king has sat in the gallery during formations, but VVD, CDA, BBB, ChristenUnie and SGP want to reverse that. That would mean the king appoints the first informateur again after elections. The recent formations went far from smoothly, and the parties hope to break through that with this step. "In politics in recent years there has been fragmentation and division," says VVD MP <entity id="person:renate-den-hollander">Renate den Hollander</entity>. "Continuity lies in the king as head of state, who stands above the parties and positions himself between the people." It is still unclear whether there is a majority for this plan. That will be voted on later. Podcast De Monarchie More about the Oranjes can be heard in the new episode of the NOS podcast De Monarchie via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps.

title: American central bank leaves interest rate unchanged despite high inflation
lead: The American central bank, the Federal Reserve, is keeping the interest rate unchanged. Nevertheless, chair Kevin Warsh does not rule out that, because of high inflation, the interest rate could soon be raised further. Last month Warsh raised the rate for the first time in more than three years. The rate was then raised from 3.5 to 3.75 percent to 3.75 to 4 percent to curb inflation in the United States. Because of high oil prices, inflation now keeps fluctuating around 4 percent. Although that decision to raise the rate did not come as a complete surprise, President Trump had hoped that it would lower the rate. And Trump hoped for that now too. Midterms The interest rate decision comes less than a week before the midterms, the mid-term elections. At stake is a majority in the two chambers of Congress: the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. The Republicans are doing everything they can to keep their majorities. Last month Trump called the central bank's board "very hostile" after the announced increase. "They are very political. They are doing the wrong thing. They are a bunch of politicians," he said while campaigning in North Carolina. "They are raising rates to make Trump perform as badly as possible." Clash This is not the first time Trump has lashed out hard at the Fed. He clashed several times with Warsh's predecessor, Jerome Powell. Trump believes American borrowing costs should be the lowest in the world. This year he regularly lashed out publicly at the Fed. He called Powell a "loser", threatened to fire him and even accused him of fraud. Trump chose Warsh as the new Fed chair this spring after Warsh had regularly spoken out in favour of lower rates. "If Kevin is in his seat, then the rate will go down," Trump said. In Warsh's explanation of the new rate decision, he says that politics played no role.

title: D66 council member (38) from Boxtel arrested on suspicion of electoral fraud
lead: D66 council member in Boxtel and employee of the Public Prosecution Service, Sohib H. (38), was arrested yesterday on suspicion of, among other things, electoral fraud and official corruption.
