When they lost that, their lawyer filed a second summary injunction, but the Surinamese authorities did not wait for it and went ahead with deportation this weekend. The Mennonites are a current within the Anabaptists, also called 'rebaptizers', and originally followed the 16th-century priest and church reformer Menno Simons from Friesland. Living apart. Because Simons and his community were persecuted in the Netherlands, they moved to Germany. His followers spread over various places in the world in the following centuries, including Latin America. There, Mennonite colonies were founded in nine countries. Among other places in Bolivia and Peru they practise large-scale agriculture, such as soy cultivation. They prefer to live as isolated as possible. They separate themselves from the outside world and mix as little as possible with residents of the countries where they settle, in order to continue their traditional way of life. In their households they use no telephone, electricity or television. Watch this report by Nina Jurna from last year for Nieuwsuur about Mennonites in Latin America: According to international environmental organizations such as WWF and Greenpeace, the growing presence and expansion of Mennonite colonies in Latin America is one of the increasing causes of deforestation of the Amazon. Their presence also poses a threat to indigenous communities. Pilot project under the <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>-Santokhi. Since 2022 Mennonites from Bolivia, Belize and Mexico have been focusing their attention on Suriname, in a search for more land and space to found colonies. Their affairs are handled by local parties and private intermediaries, including a number of Dutch entrepreneurs in Suriname. Under the Santokhi government (2020-2025), fifty Mennonite families were given permission to come to Suriname for three years for a pilot project on about 35,000 hectares of land. The plans to clear large tracts of land in the interior for large-scale agriculture leaked out and seemed to have been made outside parliament. This caused great public outrage, particularly among environmental organizations, indigenous groups and maroon communities. They feared large-scale deforestation and loss of their habitats. After public pressure and a lawsuit against the state and the Mennonites' representatives, Santokhi ultimately pulled the plug on the pilot project. Some of the Mennonites were already in Suriname by then. Tougher action. The Surinamese government of President Jennifer Simons is taking a stricter approach to illegal logging and the lack of permits. The president has indicated that land in the coastal plain is available for large-scale agricultural development. No tropical forest needs to be destroyed for this. It is estimated that several hundred Mennonites are still in Suriname, even after the expulsion of the group of 63. Their status is unclear. Surinamese environmental organizations, such as Probios, are continuously working to trace Mennonite colonies and draw attention to deforestation of Suriname's interior.

title: 800-year-old churches in Groningen crack under summer drought
lead: Besides earthquake damage, medieval churches in Groningen may also be suffering from drought damage. That is what climate and soil experts state in an exploratory study commissioned by the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity> and the Stichting Oude Groninger Kerken. They examined the influence of drought on the wierden (mounds) on which churches stand in Oostum and Den Ham, northwest of the city of Groningen. The reason for the study is damage to the church in Oostum. It was discovered in 2018, while suspected earthquake damage had been repaired just two years earlier. Since then there have been no major earthquakes there, but the damage still appears to be increasing. The researchers therefore think soil movements caused by drought play a role. They warn that more heritage faces this problem. The nave of the small church in Oostum has stood for 800 years, say caretakers Hesther le Grand and Niels Smit Duyzentkunst. They love their church. Le Grand: "I always think it sounds a bit corny, but it does something to the energy that it is already so old. Somehow you feel it." Age That long history is easy to see for a trained eye. "It was a barrel-vaulted church, but after two centuries they were fed up with it and put a beamed ceiling in," says Smit Duyzentkunst, pointing at the roof. "Two centuries later the pulpit came in, and the family pews. The whole history can be seen here." It makes for a lovely picture of the times, but in recent years more and more cracks have appeared in the walls. Where there are cracks, water seeps in and age takes hold of the centuries-old house of God, which as a result is falling into decay. The cracks in the building are clearly visible: "It is not a given that the church will still be standing here in 800 years, because the aging is now going very fast," says lecturer in climate adaptation Floris Boogaard of the Hanze University of Applied Sciences. "Groningen pride," he calls this kind of small church, of which, according to him, more than the two buildings studied struggle with this problem. "We have looked at the movement of the building and also at the wierden. You can see that the church in Oostum is moving," he explains. The research runs for two years, and longer-term research is needed before definitive conclusions can be drawn. Boogaard is already certain that the ground under the church is sensitive to shrinking and swelling. That can have far-reaching effects during prolonged drought. Longer dry periods "You can see the groundwater levels dropping," says Boogaard, who mapped the soil. "Peat is known to oxidise and can become more compact. And then there is clay. We sampled that in the laboratory and it turns out to be 'shrink-swell clay'. That means it swells when water is added, and that the ground sinks during drought." The scientist stresses that all kinds of factors play a role in crack formation in churches; besides drought, for example, heavier traffic, changes in the surroundings and earthquakes. Apart from the drought, none of these factors has changed significantly in this region in recent years, while the cracks have become much worse. Boogaard: "The climate is changing. The drought periods are significantly longer: in 2018 it was dry for two months, and that simply has a real effect." This year also saw exceptionally long dry periods. "The intensity can be seen in the structural condition of this building." Digging pits Solutions are still being investigated, but what the researchers consider necessary in any case is a stable water management system at the old churches. At Oostum, for example, some pits could be dug around the church so that water collects there and slowly sinks into the ground. Such measures could offer relief in more places, they think. The caretakers in Oostum are pleased with the study. "I think it is wonderful that people are now looking into what it is and what we can do about it," says Smit Duyzentkunst. "For the whole community it would be lovely if places like this could continue to exist." Le Grand: "Even in 800 years' time."

title: Dutch foundation tries to prevent Swedish wolf hunt
lead: Stichting Wolven Belangen has lodged an appeal in Sweden against the shooting of 72 wolves. The Dutch foundation also demands that, pending a ruling by the court, no wolves are hunted. This year five Swedish district boards decided to shoot 72 wolves jointly in 2027. That number is higher than in other years, because the Swedish government has decided that the wolf population must decrease from 355 to 220 animals. Stichting Wolven Belangen lodged appeals in those five districts. The reason for this was "the exceptional scale of the Swedish hunting decisions", the foundation writes in a press release. Protected status The animal welfare organisation asks for a careful assessment of the consequences of the planned culling for the wolf population. The wolf has a protected status under European nature conservation rules. According to Stichting Wolven Belangen, the justification for the Swedish hunting decisions and the consequences for the conservation of the wolf must be critically assessed. The administrative court in Luleå will handle the appeal, but first that court will consider whether a Dutch organisation can start a legal case in Sweden on this matter and whether the demand to suspend the wolf hunt will be granted.

title: Fair elections? American voters fear most what comes after
lead: Requesting voter data, collecting ballots, redrawing electoral districts and filing lawsuits. These are just a few of the actions President Trump has taken in the run-up to the midterm elections. He also added last week that he would only accept the outcome of the elections "if they are fair". On Tuesday American voters will vote for Congress, their parliament. The elections will determine how much support Trump can count on in the last two years of his term in the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. For months the president has been trying to sow doubt about the fairness of the results. Listen to our podcasts about the midterms in the US In the run-up to the midterms on 3 November, our correspondents in Washington are making new episodes of the podcast Amerika Kiest. Listen to them via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister or via another audio platform A president is actually not supposed to meddle in elections. "The organisation of elections in the US lies primarily with the states", explains Lou Errens, an expert on American law affiliated with the UvA. "The president cannot independently decide how elections are organised. That is established in the American constitution." That does not mean the Trump administration abides by it. "They are simply pulling out all the stops to see whether they can get something done anywhere", says Errens. Invalid blockades For example, Trump tried to have 20,000 votes of registered voters in California declared invalid. He claimed that these were people who are not American citizens. Trump also wanted to block the results in Alaska in advance, should the sitting Republican senator lose. A judge rejected both actions. As recently as Thursday, the US Department of Justice sent letters to election officials in all fifty states, threatening a prison sentence of up to one year and a fine of a thousand dollars if they do not preserve election documents. In response, a judge prohibited the Department of Justice from threatening or pressuring election staff. Election officials trained The fact that these actions have little legal chance of success does not mean they have no consequences. "We have never before witnessed such a large degree of interference", says Kim Wehle, an American legal scholar and expert on democracy. Across the country, election officials are being prepared and trained in various scenarios. They learn what to do when immigration agents show up at a polling station and what federal observers may and may not do on election day. The threats could lead officials to no longer dare to do their work, says Wehle, because they fear prosecution. "There is a hundred percent chance the government will try something", she expects. Most Americans appear to share Wehle's concerns: seven in ten have no confidence that Trump will accept the election results if the Republicans lose; half of them even have "no confidence at all", according to a poll by ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos. Despite Trump's actions, most Americans do have confidence in the results themselves. What could Trump do? What will happen should the Republicans lose will become clear next week. "I think we can at least expect a lot more chaos", says Errens. The problems may not be limited to election day. For example, The New Republic sketches a scenario for afterwards, if the Democrats have won in the House of Representatives. House Speaker Mike Johnson could replace the clerk in January, when the new members of the House are sworn in. He could appoint a partisan clerk who does not carry through the installation of the Democratic candidates. Ultimately that situation could end up with the Supreme Court, some of whose justices were appointed by Trump. In an interview with Time magazine, the American president also left open the possibility of declaring a national emergency. "I rule nothing out or in", he said. "We will see." Some people think these scenarios go too far, but Wehle does not. "In 2020 we saw more than sixty lawsuits in which Trump tried to overturn the election results. When that failed, we saw the storming of the Capitol on 6 January. Those are scenarios that are more likely than the quiet elections we used to have."

title: UN withdraws peacekeeping mission from Western Sahara, conflict not yet over
lead: There will be an end to the Minurso peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara. That is what the United Nations has announced. The UN troops and equipment will return in the coming weeks to the countries that took part in the mission. On Friday Russia vetoed an American proposal to extend the mandate of Minurso. As a result, after 35 years the peacekeeping operation will end, without the conflict having been resolved. The struggle over Western Sahara is one of the longest-running and most complex conflicts in the world. The area on the Atlantic Ocean is six times the size of the Netherlands and is rich in the valuable raw material phosphate. Morocco says it has always belonged to the kingdom, long before the former Spanish colonizer incorporated the area in 1884. Struggle since 1975 On the other side is the independence movement Polisario, which fights for an independent state. The diplomatic and sometimes armed struggle over the area has been raging since 1975. Morocco controls most of Western Sahara. Polisario, supported by neighbouring Algeria, controls areas east of the Moroccan military sand wall. In 1991 the United Nations set up the Minurso peacekeeping mission. It was to oversee the ceasefire between Morocco and Polisario and pave the way for a referendum on the future of Western Sahara. But since 2020 the ceasefire has broken down and there are small-scale clashes. Minurso reported these incidents to the UN, but with the mission's departure the independent observer also disappears. Referendum In the planned referendum the population could vote for their own state or for continuing as part of Morocco, but it never happened. Morocco and Polisario did not agree, among other things, on who would be allowed to vote. Later Morocco turned against a referendum in which independence was one of the options. End of the ceasefire In November 2020 the ceasefire between Morocco and the independence movement Polisario ended after 30 years. The trigger was a Moroccan military operation at the Guerguerat border crossing. Polisario supporters blocked the passage for weeks, until the Moroccan army intervened. Polisario considered that a violation of the 1991 ceasefire and announced it would resume the armed struggle. Since then there have again been armed clashes, although there is no large-scale war. On 10 December 2020 an important diplomatic development followed: the American president Trump recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara. This happened after Morocco had agreed to normalise relations with Israel. It was a breakthrough for Morocco, but Polisario condemned the decision. In 2007 Morocco presented an alternative plan for resolving the conflict. The area would receive self-government in a number of fields, but would definitively become part of Moroccan territory. Since 2020 more and more Western countries, such as the United States, France and Spain, have backed this autonomy plan. Different role for UN On Friday, at a session of the UN Security Council where the extension of the Minurso mandate was voted on, the American UN ambassador Mike Waltz presented a new resolution. It provided for a different role for the UN mission. The reference to the referendum - the R - would also disappear from the name; the mission would from then on be called Minuso. In response the Russian delegation submitted a counterproposal to leave the mission's name unchanged and keep the referendum plan on the negotiating table. The Security Council voted that down. When announcing the withdrawal of the UN troops, Secretary-General António Guterres made clear that peace negotiations would continue. The special envoy for Western Sahara, Staffan de Mistura, remains in place as leader of the negotiations between Polisario and Morocco. Concerns about rising violence Guterres has also called on both parties to keep to the ceasefire. The UN chief fears that violence in the area will flare up again once the UN troops are gone. <entity id="pos:minister-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Minister van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> Nasser Bourita promised that Morocco will support the UN troops in their withdrawal. He also said Morocco continues to abide by the ceasefire. Morocco remains willing to hold peace negotiations, but on condition that the Moroccan autonomy plan is the only basis for talks about the future of the area. Polisario says in a response that it is very concerned about the possible consequences of the withdrawal of the UN troops. The movement thanks Russia for vetoing the American proposal and for its support for the self-determination right of the Sahrawi population.

title: After the elections and a bewildering week in Brazil, what now?
lead: A week after the tense elections in Brazil, which were surprisingly won by incumbent president Lula da Silva, the spectacular events are following one another at breakneck speed. Brazilians are left bewildered, as if they had ended up in a soap opera. Flávio Bolsonaro, of the radical right PL party, fled to the United States and called himself the elected president, even though he had just lost the elections. His party was not happy with the claim. Some of his supporters find it understandable that Bolsonaro fled the country. "He would have been arrested in Brazil and locked up, just like his father. I do understand that he left. The justice system here is not impartial, they would hunt him down," says Uber driver Henrique Santos Silva a few days after Bolsonaro's departure. 'I hope he comes back' A colleague who also voted for Bolsonaro would have preferred to see Flávio stay in Brazil. "If he has nothing to hide, he doesn't need to flee. I believe he is innocent, I hope he comes back," says driver Diogo Neto. The justice system already expected that Bolsonaro might try to flee the country. Several judicial investigations are underway against him, including for corruption and money laundering. After the Brazilian election result, he initially refused to accept his defeat and made accusations of fraud. America involved? His party, the Partido Liberal (PL), on the other hand, did recognise the victory of President Lula da Silva. The party was not aware of his plans to flee the country. Bolsonaro left in secret and without a passport. The Brazilian justice system had given him 24 hours after the election result to hand in his passport. After his flight, on a private plane via Argentina and Ecuador, Flávio Bolsonaro landed in Miami, where he received a visa from US President Trump. The American minister Rubio of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> denied this weekend that the US was directly involved in Flávio Bolsonaro's flight from Brazil. Nevertheless, according to various media, the Trump administration played an important role behind the scenes. More Bolsonaros in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> In Brazil, sixty million Brazilians voted for Bolsonaro. His party has grown strongly in the National Congress, and several members of the Bolsonaro family were elected to the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies and the Senate. Two younger brothers have won seats in the Senate, as has his father's wife Michelle. The party now has to regroup, with Flávio Bolsonaro in the US and father Jair Bolsonaro serving a prison sentence at home. He received 27 years for an attempted coup. In a letter Flávio published from the US last week, he calls himself the "true and rightful president of Brazil". In a second version he changed this to "leader of Brazil". The letter has not gone down well with his party. PL chairman Costa Neto rejects the descriptions. "I found that nothing," says the chairman of the Partido Liberal. It is still unclear who will take over the actual leadership of the party in Brazil. Bolsonaro has announced that he wants to run for the presidency again in 2030. 'We have been woken up' Meanwhile, supporters of President Lula da Silva are still euphoric about the surprising election victory. In the first round they had still lost to Bolsonaro. "The idea that Bolsonarism would have so much power, with gains in Congress and also a president, has woken us up," says student Lucas Correa (20), who campaigned hard together with many other students. But Lula's Workers' Party PT also has to reflect on the future. Lula is 81 and begins his fourth and final term in January. So a successor will have to emerge. Moreover, governing will not be easy, because the president faces a strong bloc of right-wing parties in the National Congress, including, of course, Bolsonaro's party.

title: Pro wants ban on addictive algorithms that keep you scrolling
lead: There must be a ban on tricks that make you keep scrolling endlessly on online media or, for example, make you quickly make a purchase when you did not intend to. That is what Pro MP Kathmann wants, who is submitting a bill today to tackle harmful algorithms. "As consumers we deserve better protection," she says. "This law must ensure that all manipulative tricks that make us addicted, that make us spend money and spend far too much time online, are removed in the Netherlands." Kathmann wants manipulative gimmicks in the design of online platforms to be regarded from now on as 'unfair trading practices', which are prohibited by law. Just like unsafe toys. So far the law only concerns physical products, but "online platforms have now become the new shopping street or marketplace", says the House of Representatives member. "If a toy doll is unsafe, we take it off the market." As far as she is concerned, this should also apply to digital products. "If social media platforms are unsafe, they must go back to the drawing board and be adjusted." Games and dating apps too. Her proposal is not only about social media, but also about games, dating apps and chatbots. According to her, all these digital products have built-in tricks "that make us addicted and tempt us to spend money, so that a handful of tech billionaires earn a lot". Kathmann actually wants the harmful algorithms to be tackled at European level, "but that takes too long". She hopes that 'Brussels' will take action following the Dutch proposal, as happened earlier when an age limit for social media was proposed in France. Kathmann is working with parliamentarians in, among others, Germany, France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Italy and Portugal, who also want to regulate this by law. The Pro MP points out that last year it succeeded in getting an algorithm-free option on Instagram and Facebook in the Netherlands.

title: Wake-up call 2/11: Wielergala Awards are presented • Deceased commemorated on All Souls' Day
lead: Good morning! Warnings for thunderstorms, ice, rain or other potentially dangerous weather will from now on be issued locally instead of per province. And in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> the cyclist and female cyclist of the year will be announced. First the weather: this morning a rain area is moving away from the south. In Limburg it stays grey for a long time. Elsewhere clouds, sun and scattered showers alternate. It will be 10 to 13 degrees. From tomorrow the wind turns to the east and dry air is brought in. As a result it is often sunny. Temperatures will then drop to around 10 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? Kimi Antonelli won his first Formula 1 world title in Mexico. The 20-year-old Italian did so by finishing third in the race that Max Verstappen won after an intense battle. Antonelli is the youngest Formula 1 world champion ever. He takes the record from Sebastian Vettel, who won his first world title in 2010 at the age of 23. Antonelli let his tears flow freely after the win. "Thank you so much, we pulled it off!" is all he could manage to say. Just before he went up on the podium, he had found more words. In this article you can read what those were. Other news from the night: And then just this: Since last night the NOS Journaal of 20 o'clock has a new look. The new studio will from now on also be used for the NOS Journaal of 18 o'clock, the NOS Jeugdjournaal, Nieuwsuur and the new programme NOS Weer. Watch the studio renovation in one and a half minutes here: Have a nice day!

title: KNMI warnings overhauled: end to code yellow, orange or red per province
lead: When it used to be slippery in the northern tip of <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">Noord-Holland</entity>, the KNMI issued a code yellow, orange or red for the entire province. Large parts of the country also received a warning when thunderstorms and storms were threatening, even though meteorologists knew that was unnecessary. From today that is over, the KNMI promises. The weather institute will issue more local warnings for storm, fog, heat, slipperiness, thunderstorms and other dangerous weather. That should help organisations prepare more precisely for weather risks. The weather institute also hopes that people will less often receive a weather alarm that does not match what they see around them. More precise maps "That means we can warn people better," says <entity id="person:maarten-van-aalst">Maarten van Aalst</entity>, director-general of the KNMI. "But it also means that trust in the warnings can remain better." Meteorologists will soon be able to draw an area on the map where a weather alarm applies. They do not have to take into account the boundaries of provinces or municipalities. The maps can be viewed online and in the KNMI app. People can zoom in or search by their place of residence. Organisations can also download the data to create their own maps or applications. Working more efficiently The safety regions hope that with this change they can work more efficiently, says Remmy van Lieshout, director of Crisis Management at the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Amstelland Safety Region. As an example she mentions a storm that hits <entity id="org:gemeente-den-helder">Den Helder</entity>. In that case the safety region must brace itself there for fallen trees and accidents. "But we are also doing that right now in Amsterdam, because we do not know whether it will happen in Amsterdam," says Van Lieshout. "If all goes well, from November we will hear: 'It is in Den Helder and not in Amsterdam'." A change in the law was first needed to make the local warnings possible. Since 20 May the KNMI may issue warnings that are smaller in scale than provinces. The weather institute then spent months preparing to be able to do it technically as well. Alerts for thunderstorms Earlier, the KNMI app received a feature that gives a notification when you are within a maximum of 15 minutes of a threatening thunderstorm. That option was launched in August. So far it has been used at least once around Middelburg, in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>, which was struck by a thunderstorm on 28 August. Commercial providers of weather information claimed last year that the KNMI competes unfairly with them. The institute is paid with tax money and offers a free app. The court ruled against them and the KNMI may keep offering its app. As for weather alarms, firm limits have been agreed for each type for a code yellow or orange. A code red is issued, in consultation with other organisations, when it is clear that the impact of the weather will be very great. This year the KNMI issued a code red for heat for the first time. The Caribbean islands have their own warning system, for example for hurricanes. That is coordinated with islands in the area.

title: 68 wild ducks with broken wings and gunshot wounds dumped in Belgium
lead: In the Belgian province of Antwerp, dozens of dead wild ducks with broken wings and gunshot wounds have been illegally dumped in nature. Initially it was thought the birds had died from a disease. The report was made on 6 October, but Vogelopvangcentrum Brasschaat/Kapellen is only now announcing the news so as not to hinder the investigation. It is not known who left the 68 animals in nature. That is still being investigated. The rescue centre has taken three ducks for further examination. "At the first external examination we quickly noted things that did not seem to fit the picture of natural death or disease", the animal shelter says on Facebook. Broken wings Among the animals taken in, three broken wings and a broken neck were found. The animal centre also saw entry wounds from gunshots in the three birds and made X-rays to be sure. "Sadly, these confirmed what we already feared: all three ducks had several pellets in their bodies. The fractures we found were also confirmed on the images", according to VOC Brasschaat/Kapellen. The animal centre says it is disappointed and shocked by the find. "This is not a situation we can simply accept." Wild ducks, like in the Netherlands, are protected native species. Hunting the animals is permitted under certain conditions.

title: 'Distressing situations' due to unclarity about survivors' pensions, says AFM
lead: The death of a partner or parent is tragic enough, but if as a survivor you only discover afterwards that you are not entitled to the pension, that leads to "distressing situations". The supervisor Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) therefore wants pension providers to inform participants more actively about survivors' pensions. The AFM notes that "there are a number of situations in which participants, without being aware of it, are not covered for survivors' pensions upon death". As a result, survivors discover too late that they are entitled to nothing. A survivors' pension is a benefit that survivors receive to prevent their income from dropping sharply after the death of a partner or parent. Not every survivor is sufficiently aware of this. According to the AFM, this is because pension providers fall short in providing information about the pension. Complex and hard to find As a result, it can turn out after a death that certain matters are not properly arranged. For example, a pension provider may require that a partner be registered for the death. If that does not happen, a survivor is not entitled to a survivors' pension. It may also turn out afterwards that the coverage is insufficient to compensate for the lost income. "There is not necessarily too little information", says Anne de Groot, head of pensions at the AFM. "The problem is mainly that the information is very complex and difficult for participants to find. People encounter it at a time in their lives when they are very vulnerable." Active outreach The AFM believes that pension providers should therefore regularly ask their participants actively whether everything is properly arranged. In addition, they must inform survivors clearly and fully. For example, about the amount they receive, when the benefit starts and how the pension will develop in the future. Some pension providers choose to assign a survivor a guide. "But even then it often remains difficult to find out exactly what your partner has built up", says De Groot. By making the information clearer and actively informing participants and survivors, according to the AFM much hardship can be prevented. "Participants have to make choices at different moments in their lives", says De Groot. "For example, you have to name a partner yourself with your pension provider. That requires action, you have to arrange it yourself." New rules The AFM's warning coincides with the transition to the new pension system. The rules for survivors' pensions also change as part of this. "In the past, during your working life you built up a pot that remained after your retirement", says De Groot. "That is now changing. It becomes a kind of insurance. When you leave employment, the pot lapses and your survivors are no longer entitled to that part of your pension. You can choose to keep the accrued amount, but you do have to take action for that. Many people don't know that." It also becomes possible to register people you live with but are not married to as your partner.

title: Tip money for Bolle Jos raised to record amount of 2 million euros
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is raising the reward for the tip that leads to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, better known as Bolle Jos, to 2 million euros. That is the highest tip money ever offered in the Netherlands. Our country has been intensively hunting Bolle Jos for years; he is staying in Sierra Leone. There he reportedly has close ties with people in high positions, including the president. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the OM hope that with the increase they will tempt citizens of Sierra Leone and other countries in West Africa to provide information about his travel and residence details. Golden tip "We want to make the temptation greater for the golden tip", says <entity id="person:david-van-weel">minister Van Weel</entity> of Justice in an explanation. He mainly says he hopes people from the criminal's environment will be prompted by this. But it really has to be a tip that leads to the arrest of Leijdekkers, Van Weel adds. The hope is, for example, that a tip comes in when Bolle Jos is in a country other than Sierra Leone. That makes it easier to arrest him. Sierra Leone has so far not shown willingness to cooperate in the arrest or extradition of the drug criminal. Cocaine trade Leijdekkers is called the most wanted criminal of the Low Countries. In the Netherlands he was sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted murder; in Belgium he has received more than a hundred years of imprisonment in various cases combined. The reward for tips about Jos Leijdekkers had so far been 200,000 euros. The highest reward justice previously offered to catch a wanted criminal was for Ridouan Taghi. That concerned 100,000 euros.

title: Another hack at supermarket chains, cooling systems in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden thrown into disarray
lead: Freezers and refrigerators of several supermarket chains in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden have been hacked. Belgian supermarket chain Delhaize confirms reports on this in Belgian media. A spokesperson says that "dozens of stores" have been affected in both Flanders and Wallonia. Supermarket Carrefour Belgium also reports that fifteen stores were hit this morning. In addition, supermarket chains in Sweden have been affected. HLN writes that the temperatures of cooling installations have risen to 70 degrees, but Delhaize cannot yet confirm that. The sister chain of Albert Heijn speaks of an "IT incident". Delhaize stores in Luxembourg have also been hit, says the company's spokesperson. It is not known how many branches are involved. Delhaize also reports that the cooling systems in the stores have been directly disconnected from the internet. "Swift action was taken so that the stores can remain operational", the spokesperson said. Delhaize cannot yet say whether the hack of the cooling systems is related to the cyberattack on Ahold Delhaize last month: "That is now being investigated." Warning by text message Managers of the supermarkets received a text message from Delhaize around 04.00 this morning warning them of the sudden temperature rise, writes the Belgian news site RTL Info. Some stores have deployed refrigerated trucks to save their stock. Belgian butcher De Laet & Van Haver also reports that the temperatures of cooling installations in its branches suddenly shot up. "Around 03.00 hours last night a few settings of the coolers were changed from outside", says team leader operations Werner Muylle to the NOS. "Those are settings of a system that prevents the coolers from freezing. Normally, now and then a little warm air gets into the coolers against ice formation. After that the system should actually start cooling again. That did not happen this time. Only warm air kept flowing into the coolers." XWeb and Danfoss The hack was quickly discovered, after which the butcher shut down the equipment. As a result, heating stopped. Part of the products could be saved because there was enough cold air present to keep them well. The rest has been thrown away, says Muylle. The coolers at De Laet & Van Haver run on systems from XWeb, says Muylle. "In other branches we have coolers that work with Danfoss, but so far nothing seems to be wrong there. To be safe, we have also disconnected those coolers from the system." Two large chains in Sweden also say that their freezers and refrigerators have been hacked. At supermarket Ica, freezers reportedly were set to 50 degrees, the company told daily Dagens Nyheter . Some Coop supermarkets have also reportedly been affected. French supermarkets Three weeks ago, supermarket chains in France were also hit by a cyberattack. In that attack, hackers disrupted the cooling systems. Some systems were set to 50 degrees. Hundreds of stores of, among others, Intermarché, E.Leclerc, Netto and Coopérative U were involved. At that time it appeared to be mainly cooling installations from the Danish manufacturer Danfoss. Albert Heijn Last month, the services of Albert Heijn were brought down. Customers could, among other things, not order groceries. Because of the cyberattack, parent company Ahold preventively took systems offline. The company's website and app were therefore unreachable. The same applied to other Ahold brands such as Etos and Gall & Gall. Following a call from the police and the Public Prosecution Service, Ahold has filed a report of the cyberattack.

title: Car on its side in Velp, driver arrested
lead: A car overturned in a traffic accident in Velp last night. The driver of the car has been arrested, reports Omroep Gelderland . The report of the accident came in at 19.22 hours at the control room. Footage from after the accident shows the vehicle lying on its side, on a narrow road between terraced houses and a green strip. The accident led to a lot of commotion in the residential area, a 112 reporter tells Omroep Gelderland. A fight is even said to have broken out during the accident. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was called in to restore calm. Officers have cordoned off part of the street. It is not yet known why the car ended up on its side. It is also unclear whether anyone was injured.

title: Council of State scathing about haste with Box 3, budget talks under further pressure
lead: The Council of State has issued a scathing verdict on the cabinet's plan to introduce a new capital gains tax via Box 3. The adviser to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> advises against pursuing the plan because it is too fast and not carefully done. Its implementation would also suffer as a result, according to the Council of State, with all the consequences that entails for the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> and banks. The Council of State is not opposed to the content of the plans but to the way they are being pursued. The Council also refers to a not yet published implementation test by the Belastingdienst, which shows that introduction by 2028 would not be feasible. The cabinet can set aside advice from the Council of State. Should the cabinet wish to proceed with the plans, the Council says it is better not to do so before 2030. <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> was aiming for 2028 until now. The Council wants the cabinet to come up with a well-founded bill. Box 3 has become a headache dossier in The Hague. What is the discussion about? And what is Box 3 actually? We explain it in the video below: Almost all political parties want to change the way wealthy people are taxed. In the new system, wealthy people would only pay tax on their savings, home or investments when they actually sell or cash them in. Currently tax is paid each year on a fictitious return. That new system would cost the government many billions in the first years. Politics has long debated where the money should come from, and there is still no agreement on the funding. Besides, banks have already indicated they have little time to adapt their IT systems. It was a VVD wish to introduce the changes quickly. Whether the minority cabinet pushes through the plans should become clear in the coming days during negotiations on the tax plan. Because of this advice, the talks will come under even more pressure.

title: Erasmus's own portrait wall of female professors: 'Role models urgently needed'
lead: At Erasmus University Rotterdam, a portrait gallery of professors has recently been expanded with portraits of female professors. According to Renske Keizer, who is also a professor herself, female role models are still urgently needed. "It is not only a profession for men." In the main building of the university, a collection of portraits of mainly male professors hangs on the walls next to the stairs. Since this summer, 48 new portraits of female professors have been added. The aim of this gallery: better visibility of women in academic top positions. Role models, then. "It is a recognition of what we as women have also contributed to the development of the university", says professor of Family Sociology Renske Keizer (43) to the regional broadcaster Rijnmond. Her photo is also a recent addition to the portrait series. Equality. Although slightly more than half of the students are women and slightly less than half of the PhD students are too, that percentage becomes smaller the higher the position. From the latest figures of the Rathenau Institute, which advises <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>, it appears that nationally one in three professors is a woman. Keizer: "That has nothing to do with what women are actually capable of, but with how we look at men and women and how we judge male and female behaviour, but also how tasks are divided between men and women." Keizer gives an example. "Recently I was at a speech by a colleague in Delft. We were asked to stand up, and it was said that I should stand next to a male professor because women should be accompanied by men. I thought: surely you can't mean this? But he said it very seriously." According to Keizer, it turned out afterwards to be a misplaced joke. "But it does say something about how in some places women, and here specifically female professors, are still thought of." Parenthood also plays a major role, according to Keizer. She is a full-time professor and mother of three children. "Although care tasks are being divided much more equally between men and women than before, you still see that it is very often the woman who runs family life in the background. This 'mental load', a largely invisible task, takes up a lot of time", Keizer says. She experiences this herself too. "I too am largely responsible at home for managing the household. And that while my husband is a successful manager in working life. Unfortunately it has crept in", she laughs. "But that household and family life in many cases are still largely seen as the responsibility of women contributes to the combination of a leadership role and a family still being challenging for women." Role model. Keizer therefore also tries to be a role model for young scientists, showing that a busy private life can be combined in a healthy way with a successful academic career. "Work as a lecturer or scientist is never finished, after all; you can always keep working. And I feel a responsibility towards the younger generations to be sharp about that." Although Keizer thinks the photo gallery is a good initiative, she does have a critical note. "When you look at the photos, they are mainly white women. I think that in a world city like Rotterdam we could and should be a better reflection of society, including among professors."

title: Another report against Philip Morris: 'Heated tobacco product a new wave of deception'
lead: The Youth Smoking Prevention Foundation is going to file a report against tobacco producer Philip Morris for deception and prohibited advertising. According to the foundation, the producer claims in its advertising that its electronic cigarette is less harmful than regular smoking, and consumers are thereby deceived. For the report, the foundation has engaged lawyer Bénédicte Ficq. It is not the first time the Youth Smoking Prevention Foundation has teamed up with Ficq against Philip Morris. In 2016 they also filed a report against the tobacco producer, then for, among other things, attempted manslaughter and attempted assault. This did not lead to criminal prosecution of Philip Morris at the time. In the new report the foundation focuses on the system developed by Philip Morris in which tobacco is not burned but heated. According to the tobacco producer, this so-called IQOS system is less harmful to health because the lower combustion temperature releases lower concentrations of toxic substances. 'Disease-causing deception' The Youth Smoking Prevention Foundation states that smoking via this tobacco heater is just as addictive as smoking a regular cigarette. The smoke released contains just as many carcinogenic substances and, because real tobacco is used, it can just as well cause damage to the lungs and airways. Also according to the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> (RIVM), it is not a safe alternative to smoking. For this reason, Philip Morris's claim that smoking via IQOS is less harmful to health is questionable, according to lawyer Ficq. "We are filing a report against disease-causing deception. It fits a pattern of deception and fraud of nearly 100 years. In the past the cigarette was already presented as good for asthma and respiratory infections," she says. "Governments have let themselves be lobbied and misled, resulting in regulations that are very convenient and workable for the industry itself." The report is therefore not only against Philip Morris but also against the company's executives and the scientists who support its health claims, according to Ficq. "The heated tobacco product is a new wave of deception. It is a new way to keep the business model of the tobacco industry afloat." Report supported by KWF The report the foundation will file in mid-November with the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) is supported by the Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Netherlands Cancer Institute, Lung Cancer Netherlands Foundation, the Dutch Journal of Medicine, the Dutch Heart Foundation, the Longfonds and KWF. According to Ficq, the report has a better chance of success than the case brought in 2016. At that time the focus was on the so-called sjoemelsigaret (cheat cigarette), a cigarette through which the smoker takes in, via ventilation holes in the filter, more harmful substances than permitted and which is also stated on the packaging. The judge then ruled, however, that regulation of the tobacco industry should happen through politics, not through a criminal case. Ficq: "The cheat cigarette was already plugged by the legislator. Now there is something new on the market. We believe we have a strong criminal case because we have already mapped out the violations."

title: Price up again: stamp to cost 1,52 euro
lead: Stamps will become more expensive again from 1 January 2027. A single stamp will cost 1,52 euro. That is 12 eurocent more than a stamp currently costs. Right now a stamp costs 1,40 euro. The price is rising because fewer and fewer cards and letters are expected to be sent. Postal delivery costs are also rising, and inflation is playing a role too. This summer it became known that PostNL may raise its rates next year, and the Autoriteit Consument & Markt (<entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity>) allowed this. The director of PostNL, Maurice Unck, says the increase stays within the so-called tariff room set by regulator ACM. PostNL has been designated by the government as the operator of the Dutch postal service, where no market forces apply. ACM supervises the working methods of the postal company. Condolence mail and priority letters: A card or letter with a standard stamp is delivered within two delivery days. PostNL recently implemented this change; previously this mail was delivered within one day. The company wants to extend that period even further. Stamps for priority letters or condolence mail will cost the same next year as this year, respectively 3,95 euro and 3,25 euro. That mail lands on the doormat within one delivery day, is the promise.

title: Witness became suspect in investigation into death of Hajar after images were found on phone
lead: The 23-year-old man suspected of killing Hajar last month was named a suspect after footage was found on his phone. That is what the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> reports in a press release. The OM does not want to explain what kind of footage it is, but says upon request that the discovery of the footage led to the man, who had previously been heard as a witness, subsequently being suspected of killing the 29-year-old woman from <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. The pre-trial chamber decided today that the suspect, a man without a fixed residence, will remain in custody for 90 days longer. Missing and found in a suitcase Hajar was last seen on 4 October at the RAI in Amsterdam, when she cycled with a man, who later turned out to be the suspect, in the direction of the Buitenveldert district. A family member then reported her missing. On 16 October Hajar's body was found in a suitcase in the water at the Amsteldijk, after which the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> started an investigation into her death. Before that investigation began, the police were already working on her disappearance. Several people were heard as witnesses and the police had examined camera footage, which showed that she had been seen with the 23-year-old man. Other witnesses then stated that she had been with a different man, which according to the OM would mean that the 23-year-old was not the person she was last seen with. Phone seized For that reason the 23-year-old was also treated as a witness and an investigation was carried out into the other person Hajar was said to have been seen with, the OM says. As part of the investigation into her death, the 23-year-old's phone was seized. There the police found footage that led to him being named a suspect rather than a witness. Later investigation showed that the witnesses who were supposed to have seen Hajar probably saw a different woman, not her. It is also possible that they did see Hajar, but at a different time. Suspected of murder or manslaughter The 23-year-old, who came to the Netherlands from Somalia at the age of six, is suspected of murder or manslaughter of Hajar and of attempted murder or manslaughter of a man. This probably concerns his foster father, whom he attacked in <entity id="org:gemeente-koggenland">Koggenland</entity>, after which he was arrested for Hajar's death. He is also suspected of threatening a woman in the North Holland municipality of Koggenland and of disposing of Hajar's body. As of today he is no longer under restrictions, which means he is no longer limited to contact with his lawyer only. The OM tells NOS that he is invoking his right to remain silent and therefore does not wish to say anything.

title: Following Spanish example, House of Representatives calls for media code on femicide
lead: Dutch media could do better to think about their reporting on femicide and gender-based violence, a majority of the House of Representatives believes. D66, VVD, PRO, SP, JA21 and BBB want <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">minister Letschert</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-onderwijs-cultuur-en-wetenschap">Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap</entity> to enter into discussion with media organisations about a voluntary media code on femicide, as already exists in Spain. The request was submitted by Hanneke van der Werf (D66). Last month she, together with other parliamentarians, visited Spain. There, policy to combat gender-based violence has been pursued since 2004. "In Spain, active work is being done in many different domains to combat femicide," says Van der Werf. "And the media play an active role there, especially in raising awareness of the subject." <entity id="org:regering">De regering</entity> cannot impose anything on media organisations, but can enter into discussion with them. "For example, it is important to talk about language use. That you are as clear as possible about who the victim is and who the perpetrator is. Labels such as family drama do not do justice to what happens in a relationship behind closed doors", states the House of Representatives member. She is also considering providing more context in the form of a referral for more information, as is currently done for 113 suicide prevention. How it works in Spain. In Spain there is no official guideline that journalists must follow. However, two laws mention the responsibility of the media. Based on those laws and the experiences of specialised journalists, media have drawn up their own rules. Laura De Grado Alonso works for the Spanish news agency EFE and is one of the journalists there who specialise in the subject. In general she is satisfied with the Spanish approach. De Grado describes how it began in Spain, with the story of Ana Orantes. For forty years she was together with José Parejo. Throughout their entire marriage he abused her. Domestic violence was not taken seriously by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. In 1996 she was finally able to divorce him. A year later, on 4 December 1997, she told her story on television. That was unprecedented at the time. Less than two weeks later she was murdered by her ex-husband. "This was a major event because the case received enormous media attention. Until then, violence against women was often regarded as a private matter, a family issue or simply the problem of an individual. But this case changed everything", says De Grado. In Spain awareness grew that change was needed to curb violence against women. A few years later, in 2004, under the socialist government of Prime Minister Zapatero, the first step was taken toward a law against gender violence. In the following years Spanish media developed their own frameworks for their reporting. Agreements on paper. EFE also has agreements on paper, says De Grado. "First, we never present gender-related violence as a standalone incident or a conflict between two individuals. In our reporting we explain the broader context of gender inequality and violence against women. To make clear that this is a societal problem". This starting point also meant media adjusted their language. "If femicide is involved, we explicitly name it. Where possible we avoid euphemistic terms such as deceased", says De Grado. In addition, they avoid phrasing that places responsibility on the victim. They also try not to reduce victims to numbers, but to give each victim a face. In Spain figures on femicide and gender violence have been kept nationally since 2003. Since 2022 a distinction has also been made between the different types of murders. In the Netherlands that does not happen. De Grado considers the figures certainly important: "We always state how many women were murdered that year and how many since the start of counting in 2003". But in her view it should not stop there. As a final important point she mentions that journalists must be aware of their role. For example, by not only reporting when it is too late and someone has been murdered. But also more often reporting on gender violence in itself. Whether Dutch media are open to discussing similar agreements remains to be seen. D66 member of the House of Representatives Van der Werf does hope to have taken a first step. "Hopefully society can become more aware of the warning signs in advance. And that people more quickly recognise the signals".

title: Prison sentence sought against Eindhoven man who 'went hunting' for cats with a crossbow
lead: Nine months in prison has been demanded against a 26-year-old resident of Eindhoven, because he shot cats with a crossbow. One of the five cats attacked was hit in its eye and did not survive. The shootings caused a lot of unrest in the neighbourhood, according to the Public Prosecution Service. Between November 2025 and May of this year, four cats were hit by an arrow. The suspect "really went hunting for cats in the neighbourhood in a targeted way. He did not take into account the impact that had on the owners and other people in the neighbourhood," says the public prosecutor. Suspect Yihui L. initially denied that he had shot at cats. Later he admitted it and L. stated that he had been angry, partly because a cat had scratched him. Stepped in cat poop The man said that on the street he had tried to take a cat home for his girlfriend. He tried to lure the animals with cat food. He eventually got scratched by a cat he had tried to pick up. His anger was further fuelled after he stepped in cat poop in the forest. A disorder within the autism spectrum has been identified in the suspect. At the time of the shootings, according to experts, he had diminished criminal responsibility. L. expressed regret for his actions during the interrogations and hearings. According to the OM, L. has now almost entirely repaid the veterinary costs that cat owners incurred for their injured animals. With the help of doorbell cameras, the police tried to track down the shooter. The suspect was eventually caught by neighbourhood residents on 19 May and handed over to officers. L. has been in custody since then. To China The OM finds it worrying that the man "shot at cats with a crossbow for such a minor reason". An unconditional prison sentence has been demanded, because the suspect indicated that he will return to China after serving his sentence. L. is of Chinese descent and studied and worked in Eindhoven. The court will give its ruling in two weeks.

title: Over one million euros collected for restoration of burned Limoges town hall
lead: For the restoration of the town hall of Limoges in France, more than 9,000 donors have collected over 1 million euros in less than two weeks. The historic building partly went up in flames during the night of 17 to 18 October after masked rioters entered the town hall and set it on fire. Images of the collapsed building went around the world and led to outraged reactions from French politicians. The fundraising campaign comes from the French heritage foundation Fondation du patrimoine. The town hall had been in use since 1883 and has been on the French list of monuments since 1975. Images of the fire: The town hall has great historical value for the Limousin region and is regarded as one of the symbols of Limoges, a medium-sized city at the foot of the Massif Central. During the Second World War, the town hall served as a refuge for Belgian parliamentarians in exile, after Belgium had surrendered to Nazi Germany. Under the supervision of the regional heritage service, work has now begun to protect and secure the parts of the building that were not destroyed. The restoration itself is due to begin in 2028 and, according to a provisional forecast by the Ministry of Culture, should be completed between 2030 and 2031. How much the full restoration will cost has not been announced. The aim of the fundraising is to raise at least 2 million euros. Tax deduction The fire started on 17 October during large-scale riots across France. The roof and bell tower of the town hall largely collapsed. A few days later, a 34-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson. According to the French news agency AFP, the suspect has ties to extreme left-wing circles and is known to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, because he previously used violence against officers. Prime Minister Lecornu came to Limoges after the fire and promised that the town hall would be rebuilt 'identically'. The French government also decided to extend the monument status of the building, so that the restoration can receive extra financial support, on top of the money from public and private financiers. To encourage donations for the restoration, the French <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> agreed at the end of October to a budget amendment for 2027. As a result, donations to the reconstruction now receive an increased tax deduction of 75 percent, up to a maximum of 1,000 euros. The social unrest in France of recent weeks is not over for now. Today, after a short holiday, pupils have resumed their protests at secondary schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes, broadcaster BFMTV reports. Although things remained relatively quiet today, student organisations have announced that they will step up the actions in the coming days. New blockades and demonstrations are planned for tomorrow, a general strike day follows on Thursday, and on Friday and Saturday the yellow vests are also expected to join the protests again.

title: Breda pub crawl during Elfde van de Elfde cancelled due to expected crowds
lead: The pub crawl in Breda during the kickoff of the carnival season on 11 November will not go ahead. The municipality fears it will become too busy in the city centre. "An organised pub crawl conflicts with the measures aimed at controlling and spreading visitor flows", is the statement. So next Wednesday at exactly 18:11 there will be no crowd at the Breda Nachthoreca Kroegentocht. Officially, the municipality could not ban it: no permit had been applied for, so it could not be refused either. But after a conversation with the organisation, the organisation itself decided to cancel the event. The pub crawl has existed since 2022, and since then dozens of cafés have taken part each year. This year was going to be the same, but although the programme for the next edition was already finalised before it was called off, the organisation says. Stamp cards had been printed, flyers handed out and posters hung up around the city. "That makes it disappointing, because we have been organising this for years." The municipality says it contacted the organisation directly as soon as the plans became known via social media. 'Really an event' Despite the disappointment, the organisation does understand the municipality's request. Just like carnival itself, the celebration of the Elfde van de Elfde is also attracting ever larger crowds. "In recent years we have seen that it has really become an event", says a spokesperson for Breda speaking to Omroep Brabant. "With activities, stages and many visitors." The municipality is taking measures to better spread the crowds across the city. For example, the Grote Markt will have two stages this year instead of one. The municipality is also doing crowd control. With measures such as closing streets, softer music or diversions, the municipality wants to ensure that the flow of revellers runs smoothly. Busier and busier: 11 November is the traditional start of the carnival season, and it is celebrated on a grand scale mainly in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> and Limburg. The season is kicked off at 11:11 sharp. Two years ago the Elfde van de Elfde was celebrated in Brabant and Limburg in this way. Carnival itself begins next year on Sunday 7 February. That event is also well attended every year. In recent years, according to NS figures, 200,000 people travelled by train to carnival cities south of the big rivers on Saturday and Sunday. Last year the <entity id="org:gemeente-breda">gemeente Breda</entity> called on revellers not to come to the city centre because of the crowds. This prompted the municipality of Den Bosch to decide this summer to abolish carnival Thursday. The festivities drew too many visitors, which led to nuisance. The Thursday before carnival is officially not a carnival day, but in Oeteldonk, the name the city takes on during carnival, celebrations normally already take place on that day. Up in the air: In <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity> the entire future of the festivities on 11 November is up in the air. Local hospitality businesses and the municipality of Tilburg clash over whether minors are always welcome on that day. The municipality considers it a party for everyone, including minors, and wants the hospitality sector to sign a contract stating that everyone is welcome on the party squares. The hospitality sector calls teenagers a vulnerable group. Entrepreneurs want to keep the option to refuse them if it is too busy or if they are drunk. So far the municipality and Tilburg hospitality have not reached a solution. This week they will sit down together again.

title: '2 million for golden tip Bolle Jos' is buzzing in Sierra Leone, will he be betrayed?
lead: He reportedly earns tens of millions of euros a month from drug trafficking, has been sentenced in several court cases in the Netherlands and Belgium to a total of 103 years in prison, and reportedly stays in Sierra Leone. After earlier attempts to arrest Jos Leijdekkers, alias Bolle Jos, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) today took a new step in the hunt for the drug criminal. The OM announced that the reward for the tip that leads to his arrest is being increased tenfold, from 200,000 euros to two million euros. Moreover, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is launching a social media campaign in Sierra Leone and neighbouring countries. In it, people who know something about Leijdekkers' whereabouts or travel details are called on to come forward. Justice Minister Van Weel says that "we want to make the temptation greater for the golden tip". It is an open question whether Leijdekkers, who is known to spend part of his fortune on a high-tech team that protects him, is impressed by this. Disbelief over the amount. It is certain that two million euros is a lot of money in Sierra Leone. For comparison: a teacher earns sixty leones per day, which comes to 2.30 euros. And for residents of the poverty-stricken country, such a teacher's salary is already a high amount that many of them do not even earn. Today the news that the million-euro sum has been offered for the golden tip about Bolle Jos was already buzzing among residents of Sierra Leone. Sources at the NOS reacted with disbelief to the news. They can hardly imagine the amount, and in theory it could therefore lead to tips from Sierra Leoneans about the travel or residence details of the convicted drug criminal. Enormous risk. However, it must be noted that very few people have this kind of information about Leijdekkers: even people at high levels do not know where he is and how he moves. For those who do know, such as a pilot of a plane or a captain of a ship he travels on, sharing that information is an enormous risk. If they did, and that tip leads to Leijdekkers' arrest, the tipster risks having Leijdekkers' vast criminal network after them. He or she would then have to leave home and hearth behind, because going unnoticed with two million euros is a challenge in West Africa. NOS op 3 made this video about Sierra Leone in October: That Leijdekkers still walks free has everything to do with the high circles he moves in. The convicted drug criminal reportedly associates with President Bio of Sierra Leone, is said to be married to his daughter, and has ties with the head of the country's immigration service and the head of the anti-drug brigade. Van Weel hopes that people from the criminal's close circle will be stimulated by the increased tip amount. But it is a question whether this is interesting for these people; his circle is not large and those who deal closely with Leijdekkers have become wealthy thanks to him. And they too run an enormous risk if they snitch (klikken). In October the European Commission suspended payments of budget support to Sierra Leone, to put the country under pressure. But for the ordinary Sierra Leonean, who is affected by such measures, it is dangerous to rise up, and all the more so to say anything about Leijdekkers. Earlier, criminal law professor Sven Brinkhoff told the NOS that offering a high reward for a tip can create so much unrest around a suspect that it leads to evidence. It is clear that pressure around Leijdekkers is being increased, especially in combination with intercepted shipments linked to him. Now that more attention is being drawn to him partly because of the increased tip money, it becomes harder to work with him. That is why the question is how comfortable Leijdekkers feels in the country and whether he can still trust the people around him.

title: Coalition parties agree among themselves on tax plan and box 3, extra Council of Ministers this morning
lead: The coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA have reached agreement on adjusting the tax plan for next year and introducing a capital gains tax in box 3. According to insiders, the new form of wealth tax will be postponed by one year. Furthermore, the coalition parties are not choosing between the left-wing or right-wing opposition to achieve a majority. This morning <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will meet in an additional Council of Ministers meeting, after which the proposals will be sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. On Wednesday evening there is a debate on the tax plan. On Monday the top of the coalition discussed the matter for hours. Until now the minority cabinet tried to secure a majority in advance by seeking an agreement with opposition parties. But over the weekend, talks with both left-wing and right-wing parties again did not lead to a breakthrough. The left-wing bloc of Pro and Volt wants investors to pay more tax and workers less. But the VVD did not want that. The right-wing bloc of JA21, SGP and BBB wants to abolish the obligation for municipalities to accommodate asylum seekers and wants changes in the area of nitrogen and the liberal abortion practice. And those demands went too far for D66 in particular. Offers In the letter with adjustments that goes to the Chamber tomorrow, the cabinet will make offers to the opposition. That mainly concerns some extra tax relief for citizens. But that does not mean a choice is made for left or right. The coalition is charting its own course. With that, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, unlike he initially wanted, is letting it come to the debate on Wednesday. In the dynamics of that debate, a package could still emerge that can gather approval from a majority. Parties can also propose amendments during the debate itself. The government parties might embrace those. But entering the debate without prospects of a majority is risky for the cabinet. If the tax plan is voted down, that has major consequences for both taxpaying citizens and the treasury of the Kingdom. Haste Today finding a majority became even harder due to an advice from the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. It judges harshly the haste the cabinet has in introducing the tax on gains from wealth in box 3. That change would be introduced in 2028, but according to the Raad van State that is not feasible. More than 250 extra civil servants are needed for that at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, and the banks are also not yet able to supply the data on their clients' wealth gains to the tax authorities. Therefore the Raad van State calls on the cabinet to postpone the plans until at least 2030. But the cabinet therefore does not want to go beyond a one-year postponement for now.

title: Two arrests for violent robbery of 93-year-old woman in Amsterdam
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested a 16-year-old boy and a 30-year-old man on suspicion of robbing a very elderly woman in Amsterdam last week. The 93-year-old woman broke her back in the process, but is doing as well as can be expected under the circumstances. On Tuesday last, the woman was walking with her rollator under the gallery of a flat on Comeniusstraat in the West district when a man suddenly struck her. She was hit so hard that she fell to the ground and broke her back. He then robbed her of her bag, which hung from the handlebar of the rollator. Neighbours rushed to help as soon as they heard the woman screaming. "She was extremely confused," a neighbourhood resident said after the incident to city broadcaster AT5. "It's so sad." A police spokesperson spoke of an "incomprehensible, cowardly act". Rummikub game The woman was on her way to a friend to play a game of Rummikub, regional broadcaster NH reports. After her fall she was taken to hospital. The victim's family calls the robbery incomprehensible. "We can barely comprehend that anyone is capable of such a cowardly act," says her son. "The eventual loot: three tenners and a box of Rummikub tiles." He lets it be known that his family is "extremely grateful" to the neighbours who came to help. Investigating judge The 16-year-old boy who was arrested remains a suspect in the case, but is no longer in custody. The 30-year-old man is. Tomorrow the investigating judge will decide whether he remains in custody.

title: Dead and seriously injured in shooting in car in residential area of Rotterdam-Oost
lead: A driver of a vehicle died tonight in a shooting in a car in a residential area in Rotterdam-Oost. In a press release, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports that the deceased is a 36-year-old man from Dordrecht. Another man was seriously injured in the shooting, the police write on X. The shooting took place shortly after 20.00 hours on the Evenaar in the Oosterflank neighborhood. Because it is not yet clear how this could happen, the other three occupants have been named as suspects and arrested. The seriously injured man is one of the arrestees. He has been taken to hospital. Footage shows that several ambulances are present: A trauma helicopter was also called out. Investigators worked at the scene of the shooting for a long time.

title: Gelderland partly locked for new grid connections: 'Bitter pill'
lead: Some municipalities in Gelderland are being locked for new connections to the electricity grid. That is what the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-economische-zaken-en-klimaat">Economische Zaken en Klimaat</entity> (EZK) announced this evening. New applications will have to wait from next year until capacity becomes available. The municipalities concerned are sixteen, writes Omroep Gelderland, including <entity id="org:gemeente-doetinchem">Doetinchem</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-lochem">Lochem</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-zutphen">Zutphen</entity>. "This is a bitter pill for the region," says deputy Ans Mol-van de Camp. Because new applications have to wait for a connection, "important social tasks" will be put on hold for the time being, she says. "Housing construction, economic development and sustainability require speed and cannot afford delay." Applications with social priority, such as a school or a hospital, will still be approved. Applications for housing construction that have already been submitted also have room. New homes or plans for them will have to wait. The connection stop applies in any case until 1 July 2027, the regional broadcaster reports. In the course of that year it will be assessed whether the measures are sufficiently effective to start granting applications again. Pressing In February, grid operators sounded the alarm because the situation in <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity>, Gelderland and <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> was pressing, and much more serious than assumed. In part of Gelderland the grid is now indeed full. For the rest of the province, "unremitting effort" is needed to prevent a complete connection stop, the province says. Gelderland is not the first province to take its own measures due to overloading of the electricity grid. In part of Utrecht, a complete stop on new or heavier connections was announced in April. The shortage of space there has decreased, but is not yet sufficient for new connections. Housing construction can continue. Since 1 July of this year, national priority rules have applied to the grid. All applications for power supplies go to grid operators, who decide who gets priority. These include basic facilities such as hospitals and projects that spare the grid (such as companies that store energy), as well as, for example, someone who wants to install a charging point. Since summer, unused space on the grid is no longer reserved for households either. Across almost the whole country there is a waiting list for new or heavier connections. The waiting time differs by region. Last month it became clear that the number of companies and organisations waiting for a connection to use (more) electricity has increased further. According to Netbeheer Nederland, the cooperative organisation of grid operators, there were about 15,500 people waiting in the first half of the year. The problems with the overfull grid are causing companies to postpone investments and sustainability efforts.

title: Hotel in Amsterdam evacuated due to major fire
lead: During a major fire at a hotel in Amsterdam, 140 guests were evacuated overnight. The fire possibly started because of an appliance that caught fire. The fire brigade quickly had the fire under control. Several hotel guests were checked by ambulance personnel. Two of them had to go to hospital for a check-up because they had inhaled smoke. The fire at the hotel on Johan Cruijff Boulevard broke out at 23:45 on Monday evening. Because many calls came in to the emergency services and because of the smoke, the fire brigade escalated to 'major fire'. Since there were around 140 hotel guests present, the fire brigade searched the building several times to make sure all people were out of the hotel in time. The evacuated hotel guests were initially taken in at the concourse of Bijlmer Arena station. Later in the night they were housed in hotels nearby.

title: Two million retirees, including former civil servants, can expect a significantly higher pension
lead: For some 2 million retired Dutch people, 2027 looks set to start off financially very well. This is shown by a calculation by pension adviser Aon at the request of NOS.
