(34), who is under a less serious suspicion and who according to the OM was not present at the attack, concluded. He addressed the next of kin and victims in the courtroom. "My words have no value. I can only offer the truth."

title: Problems at Eindhoven air traffic quickly resolved, but Transavia cancels remaining flights
lead: Air traffic at Eindhoven Airport will continue as normal this evening. Earlier, Omroep Brabant reported that no air traffic would be possible at the airport from 19:45, due to staffing problems at the military radar air traffic control at Schiphol-Oost. However, the staffing problem has now been resolved, a spokesperson for Eindhoven Airport told the NOS. Cancelled after all Because airlines must act quickly as soon as it becomes clear that no air traffic is possible, Transavia has cancelled the remaining flights from Eindhoven Airport today. "Although air traffic can now resume, it is not feasible for our operation to still operate these flights", says a Transavia spokesperson. These concern three return flights to Alicante, Valencia and Barcelona. The aircraft were due to return to Eindhoven from those cities this evening. These return flights have also been cancelled. "Enough aircraft will be ready tomorrow morning, so passengers will not experience any further inconvenience", the spokesperson adds. Schiphol-Oost The problem arose at the staffing at Schiphol-Oost. From there, aircraft are guided that are still further away from Eindhoven Airport. Only when the aircraft approach Eindhoven are they handed over to the air traffic control of Eindhoven air base. Eindhoven Airport is a commercial airport and makes use of various facilities of the military air base.

title: Young terrorism suspects were looking for weapons just before their arrest
lead: The four teenagers arrested this summer for plotting a terrorist attack were looking for weapons and talked among themselves about shooting. The Public Prosecution Service (OM) said today at the first hearing in the case that the suspects are strongly under the influence of violent jihadist ideology. All of them will remain in custody for longer. Three of the boys, aged 16 to 19, from Rotterdam, Eindhoven and De Rijp (North Holland), were taken from their beds by heavily armed police teams at the end of July. They were arrested in an ongoing terrorism investigation. Two of them were minors at the time. It later turned out that all of them had previously been arrested in other terrorism cases. The boy from Eindhoven and the boy from De Rijp have also been convicted for those. The case of the 17-year-old boy from Rotterdam is still ongoing. Early in August, a fourth suspect, aged 18, was also arrested in Kesteren. For him, it is the first time he has come into contact with the justice system. The OM suspects the four of preparing a terrorist attack and of wanting to be part of the terrorist organization IS. Contact with an extremist. At the hearing it emerged that the suspects admire the notorious English Islamist Mohammed Mizanur Rahman, who is known as Abu Baraa. The OM considers it worrying that they look up to him so much. The two youngest suspects reportedly asked Rahman for advice. Rahman was convicted in 2016, at the time when IS was powerful, in the United Kingdom for, among other things, jihadist recruitment practices. Today he is active on TikTok and has published several books. In them, he writes, among other things, that women must ask their husband's permission if they want to leave the house. Right-hand man of hate preacher. In the past, Rahman was the right-hand man of hate preacher Anjem Choudary. According to the OM, Choudary is "the biggest IS recruiter in Europe". Choudary was also the face of an organization responsible for several terrorist attacks, such as the one on London Bridge in 2017, in which eight people died. In the United Kingdom, Choudary was sentenced to life imprisonment. Searching for weapons. The suspects who were arrested this summer were, at the end of July, trying through various channels to get hold of weapons. Via the messaging platform Signal, one of the boys asked about automatic weapons and pistols. He asked ChatGPT what is meant by a converted weapon. The suspect also had contact with a weapons dealer via WhatsApp. He forwarded the contact details of that weapons dealer via Snapchat to the 19-year-old suspect from Eindhoven: "Hit up this Pakistani. He can probably sort it out". The Eindhoven man responds: "Bro, are you dumb or what". According to the OM, the suspect sent this to make clear that this should not be communicated via Snapchat. The suspect's lawyer disputes this and says he sent it precisely because he wanted nothing to do with it. A martyrdom video was also found on one of the suspects' phones, according to the OM. It shows, among other things, jihadist propaganda. Four photos also hang in the background, two of which show two of the suspects. 'If you miss, you're the jerk'. The last suspect from Kesteren only came into view later, after he made an appointment with one of the minor suspects. During that meeting they discussed how automatic firearms work. "If we start spraying", they say to each other, presumably referring to shooting randomly. "Only if you miss, then you're the jerk. After that you have no bullets left." What the four planned to do with the weapons, and where they might have wanted to carry out an attack, does not come up during the hearing. The police investigation has also not yet been fully completed. This is partly because one of the suspects does not want to give the access code to his phone. The expectation is that the case will be heard on its substance in the first part of next year. All four suspects will remain in custody for the time being.

title: From red to blue wave: which voters in the US made the difference?
lead: The midterm elections in the United States have led to a striking shift from Republican red to Democratic blue. Republicans lost power in states where they had held the senate seat for decades. According to the explanation, many turned their backs on President Trump out of dissatisfaction with his policies. Who are these people? Preliminary analyses show that voters of every age, ethnicity, gender and education level switched from the Republican party to the Democratic party. The biggest changes are visible among young voters, male voters, Latino voters and people whose highest education level is secondary school. These are all groups that two years ago, during the presidential elections, voted massively for Trump. Below you can see how the vote of different voter groups for the House of Representatives changed: In the presidential elections at the end of 2024, more than half of young men voted for Trump. He won the group over by campaigning as a 'businessman', hammering on improving the economy and presenting a certain image of masculinity. American men this week shifted more toward the Democrats compared with the last presidential elections than female voters did, by 18 percentage points versus 13 percentage points. The biggest distinction was made by young voters, aged 18 to 30, according to a preliminary analysis by The New York Times. Of young men, 38 percentage points made the switch to the Democrats this week; among young women, the shift was 28 percentage points. In a recent poll, it turned out that seven in ten young men now think Trump is not doing a good job. They mainly find the cost of living and diesel prices too high and are dissatisfied with the war in Iran. Latinos switched en masse. One of the biggest shifts took place among Latino voters. In the last presidential elections, Trump managed to win as many as half of all Latino votes, partly through his promises to improve the economy and tackle inflation. That was an important issue for Latinos, four in five of whom are part of the working class. The president's popularity among Latinos has nevertheless dropped sharply: at the start of Trump's presidential term, 93 percent were still positive about his performance. That percentage is now only 57 percent. "We feel betrayed", a Latino voter told the NOS recently. Not only did the cost of living rise, Trump's immigration policy also frightened many Latino voters. A study by the Pew Research Center showed that about half of Latinos in the US were worried that they or someone in their close circle could be deported by Trump's erratic immigration service ICE. What are ICE agents allowed to do? Nieuwsuur looked into this earlier this year: in a state such as Texas, where more than 40 percent of voters have Latino ancestry, this was clearly visible. Latinos switched to the Democrats by 42 percentage points. Nationally, the shift was also clearly visible among young Latino men, who moved 47 percentage points toward the Democrats compared with the previous elections. No further education. Another important group of voters for the Republican party and President Trump is white voters without further education. In agricultural states such as Kansas and Ohio, that group makes up the majority of <entity id="org:kiesgerechtigden-nederland">het electoraat</entity>. This group also made a striking swing toward the Democrats. Among other things, farmers in those agricultural states were dissatisfied with import tariffs and high diesel prices, for which they hold Trump responsible. Because fertilizer is more expensive and their agricultural machines run largely on diesel, these voters feel Trump's policy regarding Iran, for example, directly in their wallets. Democrats more motivated. Although exact turnout figures are not yet available, turnout in midterm elections is usually lower than in presidential elections. At the end of 2024, around 154 million people voted for a new president, while during the previous midterms there were 112 million. Preliminary analyses show that Democrats were more motivated to go to the polls in these elections. Some former Trump voters will have stayed at home. Although the shifts are large, this does not mean that all former Trump voters switched to the Democratic party. The party is even very unpopular: only 28 percent of voters say they are satisfied with the Democrats. For many, these midterm elections were mainly a vote against President Trump. The question now is whether the Democrats can turn that sentiment into lasting political support.

title: The Passion not free for the first time: 'Limited space in Ootmarsum'
lead: For the first time, visitors to The Passion will have to pay for a ticket. The popular musical Easter tradition will move to the Twente town of Ootmarsum next year. A ticket for the event on 25 March will cost 7.50 euros, RTV Oost writes. According to organiser KRO-NCRV, space in the historic town centre is limited. "With tickets we can take the number of visitors into account in advance and ensure the event runs safely and pleasantly", the organising broadcaster writes on its website. The organisation does not yet want to say how many tickets are for sale. It concerns a "limited number". Residents of Ootmarsum will get priority in ticket sales, the organisation promises. It is not yet known when sales will start. Big cities The Passion has been organised since 2011 and in its first years took place in larger cities such as Groningen, Rotterdam and Roermond. This year the event was for the first time in a village, in Dwingeloo in Drenthe, a place with about 4000 inhabitants. About 4500 people live in Ootmarsum. The organisation describes the town as very suitable for the event, chairman of the board Arie Koornneef said earlier. "Some places seem made for The Passion and Ootmarsum is such a place. A town where centuries-old Easter traditions are still thriving and where connection is a natural part of life." The Passion is taking place in Overijssel for the second time. In 2015 the event was held in Enschede.

title: Parliamentary leaders of D66, VVD and CDA talk one-on-one with opposition over tax plan
lead: The parliamentary leaders of D66, VVD and CDA are seeking contact separately with opposition parties in the coming days to find a solution to the problems surrounding the tax plan for 2027. Every morning Paternotte (D66), Brekelmans (VVD) and Bontenbal (CDA) will have contact about the progress of those talks. This morning was the first consultation. The three parliamentary leaders hope that by early next week they will have an idea of how there can still be sufficient support for the tax plan in the Lower House, but preferably also in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. This parliamentary support for the tax plan, which contains all kinds of tax measures for 2027, does not yet exist. There is urgency, because next Tuesday the debate on the tax plan continues and on Thursday the final votes take place. This time pressure exists because the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> needs time to introduce new rules into the system. Wishes incorporated The minority cabinet-Jetten has in recent weeks made all kinds of attempts to win over opposition parties from left to right for support. Those attempts failed. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> then presented a tax plan earlier this week that incorporated wishes from various opposition parties. But the necessary support was not secured with this, and it was then up to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> itself to see whether a solution could be found for the complex problem. Wealth tax Yesterday was the first part of a plenary debate on the tax plan, but no solution emerged. Opposition parties Pro and Volt made an 'ultimate' offer for the desired support: the parties want to shift 1.5 billion euros from the tax on labour to the tax on wealth. But that goes too far for coalition party VVD, because the party is strongly opposed to raising the tax on wealth. The two other coalition parties, D66 and CDA, have fewer reservations about the proposal of Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity>. In the debate it again became clear that the three coalition parties are divided among themselves over raising the wealth tax. The VVD considers it contrary to the coalition agreement and bad for the Dutch investment climate. The party fears that Dutch companies will leave for abroad. You can read the live blog about the debate on the tax plan here: In the coming days the three parliamentary leaders will therefore try to keep searching for a solution. The three will not jointly invite opposition leaders for a conversation, but will keep to the one-on-one talks. It is not known which parliamentary leader has which opposition leader on their list. Shifting demands The outcome of these talks is currently uncertain. Pro leader Klaver showed last evening no inclination to weaken his proposal further. According to him the party has "gone deep" with the proposal. JA21, BBB and the SGP are acting together as a bloc and have also set additional demands regarding asylum policy, surrogacy, abortion and nitrogen policy. The cabinet does not want to meet those. The ChristenUnie, 50Plus and group-Markuszower do want to vote for the tax plan, but then there is still no majority in the Eerste Kamer. Open marriage It is also possible that the three coalition parties split their votes at the last moment, next Thursday. This form of an 'open marriage' is unusual in The Hague. Governing parties have after all set a certain course for the coming years in a coalition agreement with fixed agreements. It is then not intended that one coalition party votes for important plans while another votes against them.

title: KLM cuts thousands of jobs, is that enough to survive in the aviation market?
lead: Airline KLM is cutting 5,000 jobs. That is necessary because its "survival is not a given", writes KLM president-director Marjan Rintel in a press release. It is an ominous message. Is the situation really that urgent? For aviation experts, it is no surprise that KLM is opting for a reorganisation now. "Profitability has not been anything to write home about for years," says aviation economist Rogier Lieshout. Trade union De Unie, one of the largest unions among KLM employees, also says it understands the company's choice. Investors on the stock exchange also reacted very positively to the news of the reorganisation. The Air France-KLM share rose 12.5 percent at the opening. "We are doing everything to secure KLM's future, while maintaining 160 destinations and a new fleet," says president-director Rintel. "If you have no money to invest, then we can buy fewer aircraft or offer fewer destinations, and we want to prevent that at all costs." High pilot salaries KLM cites high flight tax and airport charges at Schiphol as important cost items that weigh on profits. According to Floris de Haan, aviation economist at Erasmus University, other costs also play a role. "For example, personnel costs. Those are high compared with direct competitors British Airways and Lufthansa." "A few years ago KLM could still grow out of its costs by flying more, but the number of permitted flights at Schiphol is now capped," says De Haan. "KLM therefore can no longer apply this strategy." How does that compare with competitors in the aviation sector? "Profitability is declining at almost all airlines, but KLM is doing somewhat worse than its direct competitors," Lieshout says. Future scenarios In September KLM itself published a report with four scenarios for the future. Today's decision seems mainly in line with two of those four scenarios: a stronger position for KLM as part of Air France-KLM, and now intervening by cutting jobs and thereby lowering costs. But the airline is also moving 2,000 jobs to parent company Air France-KLM. In addition, it will outsource part of baggage handling to other companies. If that is not enough, KLM says it is not unthinkable that the other two scenarios will have to be set in motion. One of these has the ominous name 'Brace for Impact'. In those scenarios, KLM becomes a smaller independent part within Air France-KLM and more work is outsourced to other airlines within the group. If KLM waits too long and keeps postponing difficult decisions, then a reorganisation and a smaller fleet are, according to KLM, unavoidable. It is a future the company would rather avoid. According to Lieshout, the question is whether KLM is already postponing those 'difficult decisions'. "Salaries are a major cost item for KLM. Little is being done about that with this decision." Becoming more profitable For a long time KLM accounted for most of the profit that the Air France-KLM aviation group made. After the merger in 2004 this kept some balance between the two airlines. Air France had a larger fleet and more employees, KLM earned more. That changed a few years ago. Operating profit, the profit before taxes, for example, was more than twice as high at the French arm last year as at KLM. Air France-KLM chief executive Benjamin Smith says KLM needs to become more profitable than it is now. Otherwise, the chief executive says, other measures will follow.

title: Bomb threat on KLM flight, what happens in the air and on the ground?
lead: A series of European flights faced a bomb threat this week. No explosives were found, but air traffic was disrupted nonetheless. A KLM aircraft, which was heading to Tel Aviv on Thursday, was also faced with a threat. The Boeing made a scheduled stopover in Bucharest, where it still remains this morning due to a defect. Airlines and authorities reveal little about the precise security procedures for bomb threats. However, it is broadly known what happens in the cockpit and at the airport in the rare case that a bomb threat comes in during a flight. Threat emails: It can begin with an email, as on Tuesday in Bulgaria. It warned of an explosive on board an aircraft that had departed from the Italian city of Bergamo bound for Sofia. The same email mentioned a second threat, against a flight from Dublin that also had the Bulgarian capital Sofia as its destination. Such a threat can reach the airline or the authorities. Someone on board can also report one. The International Air Transport Association (IATA) will not say how the credibility and seriousness of such a message is assessed. However, on behalf of the airlines it says that they take all threats seriously. The organisation calls on European authorities to trace the origin of this week's false threats. Checklist in the cockpit: If a bomb threat reaches the cockpit, pilots have fixed procedures and a checklist they go through, a spokesperson for the Vereniging Nederlandse Verkeersvliegers (VNV) tells the NOS. Pilots train for this. "At KLM, all pilots practised this scenario in the simulator again in the past six months," says the VNV spokesperson. "That checklist sets out exactly how to deal with such a bomb threat. For example, the cabin can be searched for the bomb," a Dutch pilot told Een Vandaag a few years ago. Which measures are needed depends on the circumstances and the information available. VNV says little about the security procedures, only that the crew, the airline, air traffic control and the emergency services work together on this. It can be decided not to land at a busy airport. This did not happen with the two flights to Sofia, but it did with an aircraft that was travelling from Dublin to Rome today. That aircraft made an intermediate landing at a French military base. Sometimes the military also comes to the rescue in the air. For example, a Finnair aircraft travelling from Helsinki to Rome received an escort from the Italian air force. Remote location at the airport: If an aircraft with a possible bomb on board is on the ground, the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee takes over in the Netherlands. According to Marco Chan, a former pilot who is now senior lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University London, such an aircraft is usually guided to a remote spot at the airport. Bomb experts then get to work there, he told the British broadcaster BBC. At Sofia airport, the two aircraft, the passengers, the crew and the luggage were inspected on Tuesday by officers from a special anti-terrorism unit and the border police. Four police dogs were deployed on the last aircraft. Nothing was found. Passengers are not always told immediately what is going on. A passenger who was on a flight from Manchester to Murcia in Spain on Tuesday told the BBC that she only learned of the bomb threat after she was taken to the arrivals hall under police escort and without her suitcase.

title: Cabinet wants to give working status holders years more time for civic integration
lead: The cabinet wants to give a group of status holders more time for their civic integration. That is what <entity id="person:thierry-aartsen">minister Aartsen</entity> of Work and Participation writes in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The status holders who qualify must work, or have worked, at least 28 hours a week. Working status holders may, depending on their situation, take up to three years longer to complete their civic integration. They must have been in continuous employment for at least three months. The same applies to status holders who are yet to start work. The rules take effect next year, Aartsen writes. How does civic integration work? If someone's application for a temporary residence permit has been assessed positively, that person becomes a status holder and the civic integration period begins. Status holders are obliged to acquaint themselves with the Dutch language, rules and culture. The municipality helps status holders with that process. In principle a status holder has three years to complete civic integration. That Minister Aartsen wants to give some status holders more time for civic integration therefore deviates from that norm. If a status holder fails to show up for lessons, fines may be imposed. If someone does not complete their civic integration within three years, no permanent residence permit is granted. You also can only obtain a Dutch passport once you have completed civic integration. Many status holders find it difficult to combine the current civic integration obligation with a (full-time) job. Slow asylum procedures and housing also take up time. A large share of status holders therefore do not work and receive social assistance benefits. 'Your colleagues are your dictionary' But the cabinet wants work to become the norm during civic integration, and therefore introduces the new rules. The cabinet hopes that in four years' time 75,000 more status holders will be in work than now. The rules must be evaluated in the second half of 2027. "At work you are in contact with the Dutch language and customs all day long. Your colleagues are your dictionary," says Minister Aartsen. "Moreover, the sooner people who come here find work, the greater the support for taking them in within our society." Status holders who care for young children may also take up to one year longer over their civic integration if no childcare is available for their children. This rule applies mainly to female status holders. Reducing the teacher shortage The new rule is part of a cabinet plan that also includes other plans intended to ease the integration of status holders. For example, there are plans to reduce the shortage of teachers who can teach Dutch to non-native speakers.

title: Governor of California commutes death sentences of over 500 condemned prisoners to life imprisonment
lead: The governor of the American state of California, Gavin Newsom, is going to commute the death sentences of 548 prisoners to life imprisonment without the possibility of early release. The decision comes at a time when the Democrat must step down in January, after two terms as governor. The measure is largely symbolic: the last time a prisoner was executed in the state was in 2006. At that time, the Republican Arnold Schwarzenegger was still governor. In 2019, Newsom temporarily suspended executions through a decree. As a result, executions were temporarily halted, but the condemned remained imprisoned, because their death sentences were still legally in force. "I am making this decision because I am convinced that executions are not consistent with California's values, undermine the foundations of our justice system and harm us as a society", said Newsom. Of the prisoners, 529 are men and 19 are women. According to the governor, the death penalty inflicts indescribable suffering on "victims, their families, communities and our state as a whole". The prisoners will "die in prison, but not by our hand" as a result of the decision. The governor cannot independently commute the death sentences of these prisoners to life imprisonment. According to the California constitution, approval from the state Supreme Court is required for this. This applies to anyone who has been convicted more than once of a serious crime. The court can therefore still reverse the decision. According to The Washington Post, about 70 percent of those condemned to death in California have, in addition to a murder conviction, other convictions for various serious crimes. Thirteen executions Newsom says this decision was one of the most difficult choices of his career, because it may also evoke painful memories among the families of the victims of the crimes the prisoners committed. Since voters in California reintroduced the death penalty through a referendum in 1978, only thirteen prisoners have been executed. In 2012 and 2016, voters in the traditionally Democratic state rejected a proposal to abolish or replace the death penalty. 'Inhumane punishment' The American civil rights organization American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) has responded positively to the news. The organization is involved in an ongoing legal case against the legislation on the death penalty in California, and believes that imposing the penalty is racist, discriminatory and unconstitutional in nature. "These sentence reductions reflect what justice requires: an end to a racist, error-prone and inhumane punishment that has burdened California for far too long." Newsom has said in the past that it is wrong for the government to kill its own citizens. He also says that in practice the death penalty discriminates against people with a mental illness and against people of color. Multiple executions Newsom will be succeeded in January by Xavier Becerra, who was Secretary of Health and Human Services under President Biden (2021-2025). He was previously attorney general of the state of California and therefore the successor to Kamala Harris. Newsom is mentioned as a possible candidate for the Democrats in the 2028 presidential election. According to American media, the commutation of the death sentences could earn him more support among liberal Democrats. The news from California coincides with three executions scheduled today in the states of Florida, Alabama and Indiana. In Florida and Alabama, two men who killed elderly people during home invasions will be executed. In Indiana, a third man, Jeffrey Weisheit, has already been executed by lethal injection. Recently, the failed execution of Christa Pike in the state of Tennessee received a lot of news coverage. She was sentenced to death in 1996 for the torture and brutal murder of a classmate of hers. Last month, Pike received two injections with a heavy medical anesthetic and sedative, but the IV line got stuck and she fell into a coma. She recently said she still constantly experiences both physical and mental pain. Executions suspended Following the failed execution, her lawyers are campaigning to have her death sentence converted into life imprisonment without the possibility of early release. They point, among other things, to the consequences of the failed execution for her health. Critics also believe that Tennessee should refrain from a new attempt to execute her. The state has suspended executions until at least the end of the year.

title: Baby dies of measles in US, first fatality in Wisconsin in 36 years
lead: A baby has died of measles in the American state of Wisconsin. It is the first time since 1990 that someone in the state has died from the contagious infectious disease. The head of the health agency CDC sympathises with the bereaved. "The death of a child is always a tragedy, but it is especially heartbreaking because measles can be prevented with a vaccination." In Wisconsin there are now 431 people who have measles. Only three of the infected people were vaccinated. Nine patients have been admitted to hospital because of the disease. The state in the north of the US has a relatively large Amish community. The conservative, Christian Protestant community is critical of vaccination. Earlier this week a child also died of measles in the state of New York. That was also the first measles death in more than thirty years. At the beginning of the month a state of emergency was declared in New York because more than a hundred people became infected within a week. Serious nationwide outbreak According to the American health institute, the US is experiencing the worst measles outbreak since 1991 nationally. At the end of October there were 5000 cases of people with measles. For comparison: in all of 2025 there were 2289 cases of measles in the US. In the US the spread of the contagious infectious disease stopped around 2000 due to the high vaccination rate. That has declined in recent years. To keep the disease under control, at least 95 percent of the population must be vaccinated. The vaccination rate is now below that. The governor of New York blames the rising infections in New York on the policy of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>-Trump, which according to her has undermined trust in vaccinations. Health minister Robert Kennedy Jr. has also been under fire for some time because he has repeatedly expressed doubts about the usefulness of vaccinations. MMR vaccination Measles is one of the most contagious infectious diseases in the world. A measles infection is usually mild, but serious complications can occur and the patient can die from it. The virus is in the throat of someone who is infected. When someone with measles coughs or sneezes, tiny droplets of the virus enter the air. The infection most often occurs in babies under twelve months old. In the Netherlands children receive the MMR vaccination at 14 months and 3 years. The vaccination protects against measles, mumps and rubella. Since the introduction of the measles vaccination in 1976, a few dozen cases of measles are reported in the Netherlands each year. According to the reports, a total of eleven deaths from measles have been known since 1981.

title: Mountaineer (21) leaves 17-year-old behind on mountain, Austrian police investigate
lead: The highest mountain in Germany is where a 21-year-old man left a 17-year-old girl behind. The two made a night trek to the top of the Zugspitze, on the border of Germany and Austria. They wanted to watch the sunrise there. When they could go no further because of harsh conditions, the man left the girl alone on the mountain. He himself started the descent. Why the two separated and whether that was a joint decision is not clear. The girl raised the alarm and was eventually taken to hospital severely hypothermic. She was quickly allowed home. The police in Austria, where the two had started their trek, have started an investigation into the man's conduct. He is suspected of physically endangering a minor. For that he can receive a maximum of three months in prison. The young Germans left Ehrwald in Austria at around 01.30 on Sunday night. At around 2500 metres altitude, a few hundred metres below the top of the Zugspitze, they ran into trouble. It was snowing heavily and it was -12 degrees. They were knee-deep in snow, the police say. Because of the bad weather a rescue by helicopter was initially not possible. Later they still managed to evacuate her by police helicopter. Meanwhile the man had arrived alone in the valley, Der Spiegel reports. Fatal climbing accident The story recalls a fatal climbing accident that the court dealt with at the beginning of this year. A 37-year-old man had the year before left his 33-year-old girlfriend, deep in the night, just below the top of the highest mountain in Austria. When they got into trouble, the man decided after several hours to leave his girlfriend behind in order to get help himself. Only in the morning could rescuers reach her, but the woman had by then already died. The man was convicted by the court of death through negligence. He received a suspended prison sentence of five months and had to pay a fine of more than 9000 euros.

title: German supermarket worker cashes in 2 ton with thousands of fake deposit vouchers
lead: A former employee of a supermarket in Germany is suspected of forging deposit vouchers for years. He is said to have made some 230,000 euros from it, German media report. The case came to light when the supermarket in Waldshut-Tiengen in southern Germany carried out its annual stocktake. The 37-year-old man is said to have submitted 2299 fake deposit vouchers to the return machine. For each voucher he is said to have collected 90 to 100 hundred euros, sometimes in quick succession. Depending on the type of bottle, between 360 and 1200 deposit bottles per voucher would have had to be returned. The suspect started as an intern and eventually became a manager at the supermarket, where he was responsible for the return machines. He admits in court that he stole money, but disputes the amount. According to him, he cashed in no more than 45,000 euros in deposit vouchers. Acknowledgement of debt: The supermarket initially did not want to make a case of it and had the suspect sign an acknowledgement of debt. It was agreed with him that he would repay the stolen amount in instalments. The matter nevertheless went to court when the suspect became unemployed and stopped paying. In court the man stated that he had only signed the acknowledgement of debt because his superiors put pressure on him. Expensive watches and football matches: His former employer stated in court that the suspect's lifestyle did not match his salary. For example, he is said to have bought expensive watches and a new car, and he often attended football matches. Because of the fraud, a maximum of 5 euros in deposit bottles can now be returned at the supermarket.

title: A32 in Friesland closed due to dangerous lamps
lead: The A32 near Grou has been closed since last evening because glass lamp covers could fall onto the road. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> is taking no chances and has all traffic diverted. The closure may last the entire weekend, a spokesperson for the road authority tells Omrop Fryslân. The culprits are the glass panels of the lighting in the Aquaduct Midden-Friesland. The A32 runs under the Prinses Margrietkanaal there. That they could come loose became clear yesterday during inspections. Specialists are now checking whether only the glass panels need to be removed, or whether the lamps must go entirely. The motorway will remain closed until everything is safe again. How long that will take is not yet clear. The A32 is an important traffic artery in the North of the Netherlands. The road connects Leeuwarden, Heerenveen and Meppel. Traffic between Heerenveen and Leeuwarden is being diverted via Drachten, over the A7 and the N31.

title: D66 and Pro want a ban on stacking political positions
lead: D66 and Pro want a ban on holding multiple positions in politics. The largest governing party and the largest opposition party have jointly drawn up a plan to that end. CDA-<entity id="person:pieter-heerma">minister Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> sees some merit in it. Politicians can currently combine several political positions and sometimes do. For example, they are a member of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> and of the municipal council of their place of residence, or an alderman and at the same time a Provincial Council member in the province their municipality belongs to. They receive a payment for each position. Conflict of interest There are parties that prohibit such constructions in their own rules. D66 and Pro want to amend the law so that no politician may hold a dual position. One of their objections is that stacking political positions can lead to conflicts of interest, or the appearance of them, says D66 MP Renilde Huizenga: "I have been a Provincial Council member, and then you deal with, for example, an environmental vision in a province. It would be strange if you were also an alderman in that same province. Then you decide at different levels on the same area." According to her Pro colleague Mohammed Mohandis, there is a risk that an alderman who is also a Provincial Council member will be tempted to favour his own municipality if, for example, a decision is made about building a new residential district. "That chance exists. And that appearance of conflict of interest must be prevented at all times." Dozens of extra hours a week Time also plays a role, Huizenga and Mohandis say. In their view, political positions require so much time and commitment that a combination is simply impossible in practice. "The work of an MP really requires more than forty hours a week," says Huizenga. "It can never be the case that you can also do another position well." Mohandis speaks from experience; he was previously a council member in Gouda. That position cost him about thirty hours a week. That is absolutely impossible to combine with being an MP, he says. "It is electoral deception if you pretend you can do both at the same time." It is mainly politicians from the PVV and Forum voor Democratie who stack positions. For example, Forum MP Gideon van Meijeren was until two years ago also a Provincial Council member in <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity> and a member of The Hague municipal council. His parliamentary group colleague Ralf Dekker is also a Provincial Council member in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">Noord-Holland</entity>. PVV MP <entity id="person:jeremy-mooiman">Jeremy Mooiman</entity> combines his membership of the House of Representatives with that of <entity id="org:provinciale-staten-zuid-holland">Provinciale Staten van Zuid-Holland</entity>. Senator Alexander van <entity id="org:gemeente-hattem">Hattem</entity> (PVV) is also a council member in Den Bosch and a Provincial Council member in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity>. And JA21 MP Annabel Nanninga was, before joining the House of Representatives, simultaneously a senator, a council member in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> and a Provincial Council member in Noord-Holland. There are more examples. 'Almost offended' Forum voor Democratie MP <entity id="person:milan-schenk">Milan Schenk</entity> said this week that his party will certainly not support the proposal from D66 and Pro. "It is up to the voter to judge that," he said in a debate where this came up. Schenk is also a council member in the South Holland <entity id="org:gemeente-teylingen">gemeente Teylingen</entity>. He feels "almost offended" by the proposal, because it would suggest that he is not doing his work properly, while he says he works 100 hours a week to perform both roles well. Heerma positive CDA minister Heerma, who is responsible for the functioning of the democratic constitutional state, responded positively yesterday to the proposal from D66 and Pro. "I recognise the importance of proper relations in our democratic governance, and that includes a balanced distribution of power, especially across the different tiers of government." Therefore he thinks it is good to "once again critically examine the phenomenon of dual mandates". The proposal from D66 and Pro still needs to be worked out and formally submitted. Given the size of the parties and the sympathy for their plan from the minister, this proposal could well receive support from a majority in the House.

title: Gold-glittering Oval Office declared national monument by Trump
lead: U.S. President Donald Trump has declared two rooms in the White House a national monument. He thereby wants to prevent his successors from undoing the changes he has made. His decision can, however, be reversed. Trump has added gold decorations in the Oval Office, his work room. There is also a gilded bronze eagle sculpture there. In the Cabinet Room, the meeting room of the American government, Trump had portraits of former presidents hung last year, such as those of George Washington, Abraham Lincoln and Franklin D. Roosevelt. He also had chandeliers installed in the room because of the "very poor lighting". "It will not be touched by anyone, destroyed or brought down by stupid people, just to build something with a different shape in its place," said Trump. Although the president spoke in grand words, his decision can be reversed by future presidents. He himself has previously undone monument statuses.

title: Trump meets Russian envoy at White House
lead: President Trump held a conversation at the White House with an envoy of Russian President Putin. He did not meet with the Ukrainian representatives who were also at the White House. Envoy Kirill Dmitriev is a confidant of Putin and conducts talks and negotiations for him on the war in Ukraine. Dmitriev is therefore the counterpart of the well-known American envoy Steve Witkoff, who in turn has been received by Putin more often. Dmitriev was in Washington for a conversation with Ukrainian negotiators and Trump's wife Melania. She contributed to a temporary ceasefire in the Ukrainian front city of Olesjky. That expired last week. Trump himself therefore also made time for a conversation with Dmitriev. What it was about has not been shared. Trump only announced "a great deal", which would concern not only Ukraine but "all of Europe". The president did not say what he meant by that and did not name a timeline either. Trump has been wrongly optimistic more often about a quick end to the war. Next week there will be negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the United States in the United Arab Emirates. Ahead of those talks there is again more diplomatic contact between those countries. The talks are due to begin Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. Also in Brussels yesterday there was discussion about a possible end to the war in Ukraine. Representatives of the US, NATO, Ukraine and European countries were present. According to Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, who is involved, the "productive talks" concerned, among other things, possible security guarantees for Ukraine and a "broader European security architecture". Letters for Putin and Zelensky. The reason for Dmitriev's visit to the White House was therefore a meeting with Melania Trump. On behalf of Ukraine, the parliamentary group leader of President Zelensky's party and <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">de ombudsman</entity> were present. They asked the first lady to keep working for peace in Ukraine. Both sides brought gifts for Melania. She handed the delegations letters for Putin and Zelensky.

title: Older people also prove vulnerable to RS virus, doctors call for vaccinations
lead: Not only for babies, but also for older people with chronic lung conditions such as COPD and severe asthma, the RS virus can be life-threatening. According to pulmonologists, they should receive a vaccine just like babies, but it is questionable whether a shot suitable for older people will also be reimbursed. In medical circles there is unanimous agreement that vulnerable older people with a lung condition should get the shot. Pulmonologists often see these patients arrive very ill at the emergency department in winter and have to admit them. That increase in admissions in winter was long attributed to the weaker health of older people combined with the many viruses circulating in this period. That the RS virus in particular is the culprit among these patients as well was not immediately clear. It was thought that only babies were at risk. In past winters they ended up in children's ICUs because of it. More than 1000 hospital days. "We know better now", says lung specialist Chantal Kroesse of the Ikazia Ziekenhuis Rotterdam. "During the coronavirus pandemic a rapid test became available with which we could test for flu, corona and RS at the same time. And then you immediately saw the impact of this virus." About 80 of her patients with a chronic lung condition had to visit the emergency department every winter as a result of the RS virus. "And you see that 75 percent of them had to be admitted for longer", said Kroesse. "Such a disruption and worsening of a lung condition can be very dangerous." Over the past three years, people with a chronic lung condition spent 1093 days in the Ikazia Ziekenhuis, 91 of them in the ICU. Preventing admissions. Susanne Huijts, member of the infectious diseases section of the professional association of lung specialists (NVALT), recognises this picture from Rotterdam. Across the rest of the country it is no different. "Regularly I see lung patients lose a lot of function after going through a respiratory infection. For example, they can no longer do their own shopping, or they temporarily or long-term need more care." Vaccines are now available. "And those turn out to be very effective", Huijts states. From her review of scientific studies it appears that the vaccines offer a high level of protection to all people aged 60 and over. Samples in the United States showed that the vaccines prevented more than 80 percent of hospital admissions. Other countries do reimburse. In neighbouring countries such as the United Kingdom, Germany and Belgium, the vaccine is fully or partly reimbursed for vulnerable older people or all people aged 75 and over. There they see a sharp decrease in the number of hospital admissions during winter. But the <entity id="org:zbo-zorginstituut-nederland">Zorginstituut Nederland</entity>, an important advisory body for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, last year still did not want to recommend reimbursement for the vaccine for vulnerable older people. The drug turned out to be effective for older people in general, the institute reasoned, but there have not yet been large studies on the effectiveness of the vaccines for vulnerable older people. "That is why there is still insufficient scientific evidence", said the spokesperson. "And that needs to be the case, as it is legally regulated." Getting vaccinated ourselves. Nevertheless, the Long Alliantie Nederland is already calling for vaccination now. Given the successes abroad, they see the question of whether the vaccine also works for vulnerable older people as outdated. Lung specialist Kroesse, together with her hospital, managed to convince the health insurer to reimburse the vaccines for her severe lung patients. "Then we'll just do it ourselves. Prevention is so important." The hospital vaccinated hundreds of patients last year. "You can already see a positive effect", says Kroesse. In 2025 there were 95 people admitted because of RS. After vaccination, the number of admissions has so far been limited to 34 people, a decrease of nearly two thirds. "Do the math", says Kroesse. "A vaccine costs about 200 euros, an admission quickly costs thousands of euros." New advice on the way. The Zorginstituut Nederland says in a response that new advice for three vaccines intended for people at increased risk of serious illness from the RS virus will come in early 2027. "Compared with last year there is new evidence, including data on hospital admissions of medical risk groups that are prevented after vaccination", says the spokesperson. "In this assessment we also look at evidence on the prevention of hospital admissions after vaccination among people who belong to a medical risk group."

title: Morning briefing 6/11: Pope Leo on a working visit to South America • Kenyan cult leader hears sentence
lead: Good morning! Pope Leo XIV departs today on a working visit to South America, shortly after his cancer surgery. And a Kenyan cult leader suspected of murdering dozens of children is hearing his sentence. First the weather: The sun is shining fully today. With a weak to moderate east wind, the temperature rises to 8 to 10 degrees. In the course of the afternoon, cloud cover increases from the southwest. In the coming days there is a mix of sun and clouds, with highs around 9 degrees. The forecast for the coming days; watch the NOS Weather from Thursday evening again here: Are you going out today? Here you can find an overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? D66 and Pro want a ban on dual positions in politics. The largest governing party and the largest opposition party want a new law to prohibit, for example, being both a member of the House of Representatives and a member of a Provincial Council. Such combinations can lead to conflicts of interest and cost too much time, they argue. <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Minister Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> is positive about it. A majority in the House also appears possible. Other news from the night: And then also this: For the first time, visitors to The Passion must pay for a ticket. The popular musical Easter tradition moves next year to the Twente town of Ootmarsum. A ticket for the event on 25 March will cost 7.50 euros. Organiser KRO-NCRV says the decision to charge admission is related to the limited space in the historic town centre. The organisation does not yet want to say how many tickets are for sale. It concerns a "limited number". About 4500 people live in Ootmarsum. They will get priority in ticket sales. Have a nice day!

title: Pope Leo XIV after surgery on trip to South America and his second homeland Peru
lead: Barely a month after his diagnosis of lung cancer, Leo XIV boards a plane for an eleven-day trip that takes him to three countries in South America. After a lower lung lobe was surgically removed, the pope has been declared completely cancer-free by his doctors. This is to the great relief of the inhabitants of Uruguay, Argentina and especially Peru, who are looking forward to welcoming Leo. The pope has a packed programme with twelve flights, many masses and celebrations, almost forty speeches and a visit to a city high in the Andes mountains. Rise of evangelical churches Leo arrives in South America at a time when the Roman Catholic Church is steadily losing ground to evangelical Christian movements. This religious shift is one of the most far-reaching social and political developments in the region in recent decades. Especially in Brazil and Colombia, but also in Argentina and Peru, the conservative faith movement is growing. This papal visit is therefore strategically important for strengthening the Catholic identity in the region. First of all in Uruguay, which is considered the most secularised country in South America. Only a third of the population is Catholic. The second country Leo visits is Argentina, the birthplace of Leo's predecessor Francis. He postponed a visit for years because of his difficult relationship with his compatriots. Between President Milei and Francis things did not go well at all in the beginning, but later the president completely changed his tune. Now Milei is awaiting Leo with open arms, despite strong disagreements about, for example, the regulation of AI. Francis did visit other countries in South America. In 2015 he acknowledged that the Roman Catholic Church had played a very controversial and active role during the colonial conquest, the oppression of indigenous peoples and the trans-Atlantic slavery. He asked forgiveness for the "many grave sins against the indigenous peoples committed in the name of God". Leo is expected to follow the line of Francis, but he will also try to be as little polarising as possible. Undoubtedly he too will speak out on themes such as social injustice, poverty, protection of the environment and of life, and care for the weak and minorities. He will certainly also address social and economic themes. From Chicago to Chiclayo The big highlight of this apostolic journey, however, is Peru. Many Peruvians see Robert Francis Prevost, as the pope is actually called, an American born in Chicago, as one of their own because he worked in their country for more than twenty years as a missionary and bishop. He also took on Peruvian nationality and speaks fluent Spanish. His deep bond with Peru became clear on the day of his election as pope. First Leo addressed the crowd from the balcony of Saint Peter's in Italian, but right after that he greeted the people of his former diocese of Chiclayo in Spanish. Not a word of English passed his lips. Expectations for the visit are therefore high and preparations are in full swing. President Keiko Fujimori calls the trip of great national importance and all kinds of religious and cultural events are being organised. The programme includes a visit to four cities, including the capital Lima and of course Chiclayo. It will be a true homecoming for the pope. A gigantic open-air mass will be held, where more than a million believers are expected. Because of the enormous influx of people, the government has asked residents whether they are willing to open their homes to pilgrims, as there are too few hotels in the city. Papacopter Pope Leo will also travel by Papacopter, a special papal helicopter, to Cuzco, the historic Inca city at over 3,400 metres altitude in the Andes. He will also go to Pucallpa, deep in the Peruvian Amazon region, where a meeting takes place with indigenous communities and missionaries and where thousands of pilgrims are expected. After the South American-born Francis, now the adopted South American Leo is visiting the continent on what many already call a historic journey. From the Polish pope John Paul II, who linked Western and Eastern Europe, through the Argentine pope Francis, who sought out the periphery of the world, it is now Leo's turn to connect North and South America with each other. He seems the right man for this difficult task.

title: Belgian ambulances will soon also be allowed into Dutch emergency departments
lead: Ambulances from Belgium will soon gain access to Dutch hospitals. In an emergency in the border region, the Belgian control room will then look at which hospital is closest, without taking the border into account. The current rules do not allow Belgian ambulances to take patients to a Dutch hospital, even if it is closer than a Belgian hospital or the medical care offered is more suitable. This will change before the end of the year, according to <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">minister Hermans</entity> of Public Health. She says changes to the rules are in the "final phase". Maastricht Ambulances from the southern neighbours may now only drive to Maastricht UMC+, L1 Nieuws writes. That Limburg hospital has been recognised by Belgium for emergency care. Soon all Dutch hospitals will be. "Cross-border cooperation is mainly prepared for urgent large-scale crises", writes minister Hermans. "For long-term crises, no structural agreements with neighbouring countries have yet been made." The only stumbling block is the difference in reimbursement for the journeys and medical care, the minister says. Belgium and the Netherlands use different systems. The Ministry of Public Health and the Belgian federal public health service are holding talks to find a solution. Dutch ambulances are already allowed to take patients to a Belgian hospital.

title: Power outages in seven Ukrainian regions after Russian attacks
lead: Due to Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, power has gone out in parts of seven Ukrainian regions. The Ukrainian Ministry of Energy reports this. The regions concerned are Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv and Chernihiv. These regions are spread across Ukraine, so they are not only areas close to the front. Considerable damage is said to have occurred. Repair work is under way in the affected areas. In a statement on Telegram, the ministry writes that the situation is "the most critical" in the region around the capital Kyiv. According to the Ministry of Energy, technicians are working day and night to restore the power supply. Ukraine is facing a harsh winter because of the ongoing Russian attacks on infrastructure. A report by the United Nations Human Rights Council classified these attacks as a war crime at the end of October. Russia: Ukrainian drones shot down Russia says it shot down 142 Ukrainian drones overnight over various regions, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. According to Russian authorities, a fire broke out at a company in the southern region of Krasnodar due to debris from a drone. The independent Russian medium Astra reports that the Afipsky oil refinery near Krasnodar was probably the target of the attack. This is one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia. Ukraine has not yet commented on any involvement in the attack. Negotiations Russian and Ukrainian representatives were at the White House yesterday. US President Trump then spoke separately with the Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev. New negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are scheduled next week in Abu Dhabi. Death toll from attack on aid post rises Also, the death toll from the Russian attack on an aid post in the Ukrainian town of Komyshuvakha on Monday has risen to 53. The acting governor of the Zaporizhzhia region reports this on Telegram. Search and rescue operations have been under way at the site of the attack for five days. In that attack, a former school where aid goods were being distributed was bombed. The building was also being used as a shelter. Earlier, 26 deaths had been reported.

title: Two dead in bus crash with schoolchildren in France, several injured
lead: In France, two people have died in an accident involving a bus. Local authorities report that sixteen others were also injured, four of them seriously. The two dead are a 7-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man. The four seriously injured are between 18 and 45 years old. The accident happened near the village of Lent, in eastern France near the Swiss border. Local newspaper La Voix de l'Ain reports that the bus was a regional transport bus on its way to Bourg-en-Bresse. Minister of Transport Philippe Tabarot is at the scene of the accident. "As a father of young children, one of whom has just come back from a school trip by bus, I am deeply moved by what has happened", he says. According to Tabarot, about fifteen children were on the bus. He reported that there were 49 people on board the bus, not 43 as initially reported by the authorities. Mayor Yves Cristin of Lent told French media that the bus left the road and crashed into a tree in the verge. "The road was a little wet this morning, but we don't understand why the bus veered from its lane, crossed the road and ended up in the verge on the other side", Cristin said. "Unfortunately there was a tree in the way, and it was that tree that made the accident so tragic." The accident happened around 07.00 hours in the morning on a regional road. Emergency services and police are on site. The fire brigade asks road users to give priority to the emergency services. A spokesperson for civil protection says helicopters have been sent to the scene of the accident. "Their task is to quickly evacuate the victims and take them to a trauma centre or a specialised hospital for the seriously injured", he added. A reception centre has also been set up for relatives of those involved. Investigation into the bus driver: The public prosecution service of Bourg-en-Bresse says the bus driver is in hospital and "could not yet be questioned". The prosecution service reports that a "preliminary investigation into causing death by dangerous driving and serious injury by a road traffic accident" has been started by police in Lyon. A representative of the National Federation of Passenger Transport tells BFMTV that the driver is 26 years old and has one and a half years of experience as a bus driver.

title: Parking in Dokkum free for now, power grid too full for payment machines
lead: The introduction of paid parking at several parking spaces in Dokkum has been delayed again. The parking machines cannot be connected to the power grid because there is no room. It concerns four parking spaces on the edge of the Frisian town, with a combined capacity of about 600 parking bays. Originally, the park-and-ride spaces should already have been paid since the beginning of this year. The municipality had counted on 580,000 euros in parking revenue for this year. Planning too optimistic The project soon fell behind schedule because it required more preparation than initially thought. "This involves, among other things, technical setup, the necessary connections and carefully going through the participation process," the municipality said about this last spring. The executive board acknowledged that the planning had in hindsight been too optimistic. The deadline was postponed to 1 October, but even then people could still park for free. Grid operator Liander has no room on the power grid. "Due to busyness and waiting times at Liander, the work cannot yet be carried out," the municipality said. It is still unclear how Dokkum will fill the financial gap, writes Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity> . Power grid Because the power grid is full, nationwide priority rules have applied since 1 July this year. All requests for power connections go to grid operators, who decide who gets priority. Basic facilities such as hospitals get priority over, for example, someone who wants to install a charging point. Since the summer, no unused capacity on the power grid has been reserved for households either. In almost the whole country there is a waiting list for new or heavier connections. The waiting time varies by region. Last month it became clear that the number of businesses and organisations waiting for a connection to use (more) power has increased further .

title: Turkish former minister Kaya arrested in major stock market scandal
lead: In an investigation into share price manipulation in Turkey, former minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya has been arrested. She was for many years minister of Family Affairs. Almost ten years ago Kaya was declared 'unwanted alien' in the Netherlands and was led out of the country by agents. This led to a major diplomatic row between The Hague and Ankara. Kaya has been arrested on suspicion of violating the capital markets law and membership of a criminal organisation. Her husband Ilyas Kaya has been released under judicial supervision and has a travel ban. The interrogations lasted nine hours in total. The couple says they are innocent. 38 million euro In September a spokesperson for the opposition party accused the couple of dubiously earning some 38 million million euro through the sale of shares. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> now reports that Kaya had access to non-public information that could affect the value of these investments. She is said to have bought the shares in April and transferred them on 16 September. That is one day before the decision of the Turkish regulator to dissolve the investment funds in question. Turkey was shaken earlier that month by a major stock market scandal. The Turkish regulator SPK decided to dissolve 131 funds managed by seven asset managers. Some money managers were unable to repay investors. 455,000 Turkish savers were involved. Many lost their savings, while others made tens of millions of dollars in profit. Many people had invested in investment funds because the Turkish lira had lost value in recent years and prices rose rapidly. They hoped in this way to preserve the value of their money. In the media the scandal is compared to a pyramid scheme, an illegal method in which new money is used to pay earlier investors. Vice chair of Erdogan's party Kaya was vice chair of the ruling AK Party, the party of Turkish president Erdogan. Because of the scandal she stepped down in September. On the return flight from his visit to South Korea, Erdogan said: "People you would never expect have become involved in this case." He added that the necessary measures have been taken by the judiciary. The scandal led to fierce criticism from the opposition. Opposition leader of the New Party Özgür Özel said earlier that this is not only about fraudsters, but also about political connections and failing oversight. But there was also criticism from within the AK Party's own ranks. For affected investors a scheme has been set up under which investments under 1 million Turkish lira, around 18,000 euro, are repaid. For larger amounts a maximum of 1 million Turkish lira is paid out for the time being. The Netherlands knows Kaya from 2017. At the time she was minister of Family Affairs and wanted to give a speech in Rotterdam about a constitutional referendum in Turkey. She did not receive permission from the Dutch authorities and her car was stopped by agents. Kaya initially refused to leave. Eventually a crane truck was deployed to tow her car away. The minister stepped out, ranting, and was taken away in another car. Near the consulate in Rotterdam the ME riot police clashed with demonstrators. The Turkish authorities reacted furiously to both the treatment of Kaya and the conduct of the Dutch <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>.

title: Riot police deployed to clear occupied construction site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam
lead: The police are clearing the site in Amsterdam where a Microsoft data centre is to be built. Dozens, and according to themselves even hundreds, of pro-Palestinian activists had entered the site in the Sloterdijk district around midday. Part of the demonstrators have left the site voluntarily. The riot police are intervening to remove dozens of other protesters. Groups of protesters have been surrounded and loose demonstrators are being brought out one by one, a NOS cameraman on site sees. The demonstrators who do not leave voluntarily are being arrested, the police say. A protest by Fossielvrij NL was due to begin at the construction site at 12:00, but another group of activists broke through the fences. According to the police, there were demonstrators on their way to the location of the protest carrying, among other things, an angle grinder and climbing equipment. Despite repeated calls, they did not hand over these items, which led to confrontations. After these items were eventually handed in, they nevertheless went to the protest site, the police say. They then climbed onto a crane on the site and onto the roof of the data centre under construction. In doing so a fence was cut open and demonstrators entered the site from the back. Geef Tegengas says in a press release that the occupation succeeded. According to the organisation, several hundred demonstrators got onto the construction site. One demonstrator has been arrested for "obstructing and hindering the performance of the work", the police say. "The police tried to prevent this and to arrest demonstrators, but were unable to prevent it, and force was used in doing so", the police say in a statement. During the protest one officer was slightly injured. Even before the protest began there were activists at the data centre site, including activists from the organisation Geef Tegengas. They walked around with banners reading "Microsoft is genocide". On the link between Microsoft and the Gaza war, one demonstrator says that the Israeli army is a customer of Microsoft. Images of the confrontation: NOS reporter Danny Simons is at the site and saw the activists tie balloons to the fences. They also hung up Palestinian flags and were skipping rope. Protests across Europe: outside the site there was a demonstration by Fossielvrij NL. They oppose the arrival of data centres because some of them run on gas. Microsoft has informed the NOS that it is aware of the demonstration that got out of hand. "We understand that this project stirs up a lot and we respect people's right to express their opinion peacefully. However, we do not approve of actions that violate the law or endanger people's safety."

title: 2026 almost certain to exceed 1,5 degrees of warming after record-warm October
lead: Last month was the warmest October ever measured worldwide, and it is now almost certain that 2026 will exceed the 1,5 degrees of warming. This is according to the latest data from the European Earth observation programme Copernicus. This means 2026 looks set to be the second calendar year in which the symbolically important 1,5 degrees is exceeded. The previous time was in 2024. Although the long-term average is not yet above 1,5 degrees, the United Nations now do assume that this has become unavoidable. The UN argues for keeping the overshoot of 1,5 degrees as short as possible: Last month the worldwide average was 15,35 degrees Celsius. That is 1,75 degrees above the October average for the period 1850-1900. That was when humanity began burning fossil fuels on a large scale, releasing many greenhouse gases into the atmosphere that warm the Earth. Although it was the warmest October ever measured worldwide, for Europe it was the second warmest. October 2022 was warmer here. In Western and Central Europe temperatures last month were above average, but the real outliers were in Eastern Europe and Scandinavia. Warm seas Once again, exceptionally high sea surface temperatures were measured worldwide, as is to be expected in an El Niño year. Outside the polar regions that temperature averaged 20,95 degrees, which is a record. "October has continued the pattern of extraordinary global warming, with record-high global and sea surface temperatures," says Samantha Burgess of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). "An exceptionally strong El Niño further warms a climate that has already been warmed by human activities." At sea it was not only extremely warm in the Pacific Ocean, where the hand of El Niño is clearly visible. Along Europe's Atlantic coast and in the western Mediterranean it was also record warm, which also contributed to the high temperatures on land. Low river levels Last month the European Earth observation programme also saw exceptional drought in Central and Eastern Europe. Copernicus points in particular to the low river levels of the Rhine and the Danube. Conversely, the eastern part of the Iberian Peninsula, the United Kingdom, large parts of France and Germany, and Greece experienced a wetter period. Among others, the UK, Spain, Greece and Turkey had heavy rainfall and even flooding last month. Why 1,5 degrees? In 2009, at the climate summit in Copenhagen, a group of Pacific island states launched the goal of keeping global warming below 1,5 degrees Celsius. Strong sea-level rise threatens the survival of these low-lying countries, and they therefore wanted more action against climate change. The Copenhagen summit was a failure, but six years later nearly all countries in Paris nonetheless agreed to keep warming well below 2 degrees Celsius and preferably below 1,5 degrees. Doubts about feasibility were also voiced at the time. The Paris summit asked for research into the difference in impacts between 1,5 and 2 degrees of warming. Three years later the climate panel IPCC published the outcome. This showed that there are considerable differences. For example, at 1,5 degrees of warming part of the coral reefs is preserved, whereas with more warming they almost entirely disappear. A rise below 1,5 degrees also limits sea-level rise and the chance of extreme heat, which can also be dangerous for people.

title: Bomb threats about flights in Europe, Irish broadcaster's building evacuated due to threat
lead: For the third time this week, a series of bomb threats has been made about flights in Europe. Media in Ireland and the United Kingdom have also received threats about explosives. As far as is known, no bomb has been found in any case. It is unclear who is responsible for the threats. The Irish <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> says about the bomb threats to media that it concerns a "coordinated action". A bomb threat was also received about a KLM flight from Prague to Amsterdam. The aircraft landed at Schiphol and was checked. No explosives were found on board, the Royal Military Police tells NOS. In recent days there have been repeated hoax threats, which appear intended to disrupt passenger aviation in Europe. This week such threats were made about several dozen aircraft. There is no overview of how many flights are involved, but at least about ten aircraft are affected. The new threats concern, among others, aircraft in Portugal, Italy, Bulgaria, the Netherlands, Czechia, Denmark, France and Hungary. In this article you can read how pilots and authorities deal with a bomb threat: Fighter jets of the Hungarian air force escorted three civil flights this morning. They concerned aircraft flying from Brussels to Sofia and from Prague to Cyprus and Bucharest. There had been reports of bombs on board. For at least nine flights to and from Prague, threats of improvised explosives on board have been reported, says the Czech <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> on social media. It is the second day in a row that the police at Prague's international airport have had to take action. The same applies to Copenhagen airport. The Danish police report that neither passengers nor people at the airport were in danger. That is also the message from the Bulgarian authorities. In that country, reports of threats on board two aircraft were investigated. Newsrooms evacuated in Ireland In the Irish capital Dublin, the headquarters of public broadcaster RTÉ was evacuated for several hours today due to a bomb threat. Live broadcasts were cancelled. According to the Irish police, media organisations in other European countries have also been threatened. In Dublin, the newsrooms of Mediahaus and Independent News Media were also evacuated as a precaution. Virgin Media also received a threat, but the building was not evacuated there, RTÉ writes. The British news channel Sky has also been affected by a bomb threat. The news organisation has had the situation investigated and has informed the authorities. The top of the news company has not released further details. Hoax bomb threats occur regularly, but rarely so many in such a short period.

title: Belgian king does not accept government's resignation, budget negotiations resume
lead: Belgian King Philippe has refused the resignation of the cabinet of Prime Minister De Wever. On Monday the prime minister offered his resignation after months of coalition negotiations over the budget had failed. At that time the king said he would "take it under consideration". As far as he is concerned, Belgium "cannot afford a prolonged political crisis". After a meeting of about two hours, De Wever was sent off this morning with the request to resume budget negotiations immediately. Cutting costs: Belgium must cut about 10 billion euros over the next three years to remain within the European expenditure standard, but the parties disagree on where those cuts should fall. De Wever's party (N-VA) wants to cut spending on healthcare, while other parties advocate tax increases. The social democratic Vooruit, for example, makes a point of the tax benefits for the rich, such as professional footballers. In recent days King Philippe has spoken with other party leaders in the De Wever government. They have stated that they still want to reach an agreement on the budget, reports the Flemish broadcaster VRT. Had the Belgian king accepted the resignation, early elections would have followed. Giving ground: The largest opposition party, Vlaams Belang, does seem to be pushing for new elections. "As far as we are concerned, it is time to put an end to the endless muddling along. Not the king, but the voter should have the final word", said Barbara Pas, parliamentary group chair of the radical right-wing party. For now, however, it does not seem to come to that. The five party chairs have promised that they will give ground in order to still reach an agreement. The prime minister is expected back with the king in ten days. According to the VRT it is not clear whether that is the final deadline for an agreement. The king has only stated that the prime minister will report back to the head of state again on 16 November.

title: Belgium adopts controversial law on entering the homes of undocumented residents
lead: After an all-night debate lasting hours, the Belgian parliament has approved a bill that has caused much controversy. Under the law, police may enter private homes of people who do not have valid residence papers in order to arrest them. Protests against it were still held this week in dozens of places across the country. The De Wever government wants to find a way to send back people who do not want to return to their country of origin anyway.
