Under this law, officers may raid homes between 05.00 and 21.00 to pick up people and then, for example, place them in a closed reception centre. There are, however, conditions attached to the law. Only people who pose "a danger to public order or national security" may be arrested. This may only happen if a decision has already been made that they may not remain in Belgium and if it is clear that they do not intend to leave the country. An investigating judge must give permission for such a 'home entry'. What happens to the children? Another sensitive point during the handling of the bill was what would happen if children were also living in the home. Children themselves cannot be arrested, but the other people in the home can. The law does state that separating children from their parents must be avoided and that "harm and trauma to children must be prevented as far as possible". The umbrella organisation for NGOs in Belgium, called 11.11.11, believes the conditions are not strict enough. It compared entering homes to the violent arrests carried out by the American immigration service ICE. The Association of Investigating Judges believes the law is not necessary at all, because there are already enough legal options to carry out a house search. The Bar Association considers it troubling that there is no appeal possible against a decision by the investigating judge to carry out a raid. And from the political opposition there are concerns that it has not been made sufficiently clear when someone poses a danger to public order. 'No longer hiding behind the front door' Minister Van Bossuyt of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity> nevertheless speaks of a historic moment. "After years of political opposition and a great deal of disinformation, it can finally come into effect." According to her, the law targets "rapists, drug offenders and hate preachers". "Those people will no longer be able to hide behind a front door." The Belgian coalition has been under pressure for some time due to the failure of the budget talks. This subject was also sensitive, but in the end there were no votes against. Only one member of parliament from the Walloon Christian democrats chose not to vote. There is a good chance the law will be challenged before the Constitutional Court. Several mayors have said earlier that they will oppose the implementation of the law.

title: Parents killed in car during storm on Corsica after picking up daughter from airport
lead: On the French island of Corsica, a couple died last night during a storm when their car was swept away by a flood caused by heavy rainfall, local authorities report. Their daughter could be rescued from the car. She was taken to hospital by helicopter. The car ran into trouble around 01.00 hours between Bonifacio and Porto-Vecchio on the RT10, the main road along the east coast of the island. The occupants were, according to the local medium Corse Matin, on their way home to Porto-Vecchio from Figari airport. Parents picked up daughter The parents had driven to the airport "to pick up their daughter who came to visit them", according to a spokesperson for the mayor of Porto-Vecchio, who also said that the mother had a birthday. After the car was swept away by the water on the way back, rescuers, including a diver, managed to reach the car and free the 40-year-old daughter. Help came too late for her parents. They were found dead in the car. A firefighter involved in the rescue operation had to be taken to hospital with symptoms of hypothermia. The blow to the island is great, said mayor Angelini of Porto-Vecchio. "We are shocked and deeply saddened." Minister Nuñez of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> writes on social media that many emergency operations were carried out yesterday. Daily Le Parisien reports that 43 rescue operations were carried out in the south of Corsica, in which 32 people were rescued. A lot of rain in a short time Corsica has been battered since Wednesday by a so-called Mediterranean rain front. Warm, moist air from the Mediterranean is pushed against the mountains of Corsica. As a result, enormous amounts of rain can fall in a short time, which can lead to flooding. Also in the southern French departments of Hérault and Gard, downpours caused flooded streets and roads.

title: Cabinet wants more with AI, but Netherlands will remain dependent
lead: The Netherlands must become more involved in the world of AI, but we will always remain dependent on other countries. That is what the vision that <entity id="person:willemijn-aerdts">staatssecretaris Aerdts</entity> of Digital Economy and Sovereignty has made public today states. "Full independence" is, according to Aerdts, not the goal, because it is not realistic. "The raw materials, the chips, the software, we cannot do all of that alone as the Netherlands." What the cabinet aims for is enough "knowledge and capacity" to keep being able to use important technology and to "keep making our own choices ourselves". The aim is for the Netherlands not to depend on "one country, one company, one player". Most computing power: American and Chinese companies in particular determine the extremely rapid development of AI. "They have the most money, the largest models and the most computing power." But the cabinet wants the Netherlands and Europe to catch up. The AI vision stresses the importance of doing as much as possible within the EU or with other "trustworthy partners". Aerdts mentions, among others, Singapore, South Korea, Japan and Canada. At the same time, it is clear to the cabinet that cooperation with the United States and China is unavoidable. Therefore it wants the Netherlands and the EU to "work on stable and predictable relations" with those superpowers. What is AI? AI stands for Artificial Intelligence (kunstmatige intelligentie, in other words). It concerns (computer) systems that analyze their environment and can, to a greater or lesser extent, act independently to achieve goals. Not only the reasoning power is important here, but also the ability to learn and to make decisions on their own. To keep up, the Netherlands itself must put even more effort into industry, says the D66 state secretary. She refers among other things to ASML and to other companies in the Eindhoven region that are developing AI-driven robots. Aerdts believes what mainly needs to happen is creating preconditions for companies here to develop AI. That includes, for example, improving the investment climate and clear laws and rules. Data centers The cabinet is barely setting aside money to add strength to all of this. Aerdts writes in her vision about 120 million euros for a European AI project. Hundreds of billions are at stake in AI worldwide. Within the cabinet, thought is still being given to "room for computing power", in other words building data centers. These are needed to make AI, which requires a lot of computing power, possible. But building them is sensitive, because data centers use a lot of water and electricity. And both are not unlimited in the Netherlands. Thinking about this is therefore not finished yet; at the beginning of next year Aerdts wants more clarity about "AI infrastructure". Toothless tiger Volt leader <entity id="person:laurens-antonius-josephus-maria-dassen">leider Dassen</entity>, who is much occupied with the topic in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, is critical that the cabinet is coming only with a vision document for now. "I expect from the cabinet that there are actually plans. This is a toothless tiger." According to him, it is telling that no real money is being set aside. "AI should be a top priority. It isn't if there is no budget," says Dassen. "We need money to ensure that we can keep up in the global struggle that is now underway."

title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison for starving 190 children
lead: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 190 children and one adult. The children were starved on his orders and buried in a forest. Mackenzie is linked to the mass killing of more than 400 people. Also 28 other members of Mackenzie's cult have been convicted. These include guards who enforced his rules and people who helped dig and conceal the mass graves. With one exception, all the convicted have denied the charges. According to them, they did not force anyone to do anything. One convicted person did confess. Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 following a tip from a human rights organisation. In the weeks that followed, the Kenyan <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> discovered mass graves containing 400 bodies. For 101 of the 191 victims examined, the cause of death could not be determined, due to the state of decomposition of their bodies. In most other cases the cause of death was starvation. In some cases it was suffocation, strangulation or traumatic head injury. The investigation into the other victims found in the mass graves is still ongoing. Doomsday movement Mackenzie was the leader of a doomsday movement, a religious current that believes the end of times is near. He persuaded his followers to starve their children "so that they could meet Jesus sooner". Followers who went against his orders were tortured and in some cases strangled. The children died between January 2021 and September 2023 in the Shakahola forest in Kenya. Medical treatment was not permitted, as it would be "an instrument of Satan". Mackenzie did allow himself to be treated, according to the statement of a witness. "He said that they had to starve themselves before the end of the world, and that he would be the last one and would lock the doors." During the trial, another witness stated that a mother was not allowed to breastfeed her newborn child. The baby died twelve days later as a result. 'Cool and calculated' According to the judge, the murders were "cool and calculated". According to her, the perpetrators showed no mercy. Research showed that there was food and water present in the camp. The judge ruled that the children were deliberately starved and rejected the defence that they died voluntarily. Babies, toddlers and young children cannot give consent, and children between the ages of six and ten could not foresee the consequences, the judge said. During the sentencing, Mackenzie often smiled, according to news agency Reuters. He also regularly spoke with his assistant preacher, who was himself sentenced to 160 years in prison. Two other court cases against Mackenzie are still ongoing. In them he is accused of terrorism, child abuse and torture.

title: Podcast De Dag: The game composer's game
lead: This week a new version came out of one of the most popular games ever made: Zelda, Ocarina of Time. And later this month, fans can finally fire up the games console after years of waiting for GTA VI, the biggest game release ever. Music goes hand in hand with those games. Soundtracks, which get more and more attention and appreciation. Next week, the Gamemuziek Top 50 will be heard on broadcaster NPO Klassiek. The music is released as a record and you can increasingly go to concerts where music from games is performed live. Listen here: This episode of De Dag you can listen to via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. In the podcast, game composer Jonathan van den Wijngaarden talks about the power of these soundtracks, what they do to you as a player and why they are not limited to the games themselves. From his studio he shows how you make such music. Respond: mail to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Mattijs van de Wiel Editorial team: IJsbrand Terpstra Final editing: Rosanne Sies

title: Higher sentence for driver who killed two women and two children in Oud Gastel
lead: A driver from Roosendaal who four years ago ran over and killed two children and two mothers has received a heavier sentence on appeal. The 31-year-old Omar E. must serve six years and eight months in prison, according to the Court of Appeal in Den Bosch. At the lower district court he had earlier been sentenced to four years in prison. The fatal accident happened in September 2022 in Oud Gastel, north of Roosendaal. The man was driving a rented Mercedes well over 150 kilometres per hour on a road where the speed limit is 50. He was tailgating, overtook on the right and accelerated when he approached an intersection where the traffic lights were flashing orange. There he struck the side of the stationary Toyota Yaris carrying the two women and three children at 95 kilometres per hour. Only one child survived the accident. E. was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Much grief. The Court of Appeal imposes a higher sentence than the district court because, according to the court, there is a case of "meerdaadse samenloop". Put simply, the court holds the man more accountable because four people died. "He has also caused the surviving occupant and all the next of kin immeasurable grief", the court said. The driver was also given a ten-year driving ban, the maximum period that can be imposed. The court says the man has taken no responsibility for the accident. Omar E. does admit he was driving too fast, but believes the woman should have let him go first because he was on a priority road. The Court of Appeal, and earlier the district court too, did not go along with that and ruled that the accident was caused by the man's dangerous driving. Anyone who sees it differently, according to the court, is dealing with "a fundamental lack of insight or denial against better knowledge". Not the first time. It was not the first time Omar E. had broken traffic rules. In 2020 he lost his driving licence after being caught on the A16 driving 183 kilometres per hour where he was allowed a maximum of 100. Less than a year later he had to pay 1750 euros for a speeding offence.

title: 33 dead in attack by rebel group in eastern Congo, Ebola patients on the run
lead: In an attack by armed militants of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in a village in eastern Congo, at least 33 people have been killed. According to a local civil society organisation, houses were set on fire and looted. "We heard gunfire and houses about 50 metres away were set on fire," says the director of a local hospital. The attack took place in Cantine in the province of North Kivu. Residents of the village have fled to other parts of the province. Among the refugees are also an Ebola patient and around 180 people who may be infected with the virus. They were cared for in the local hospital. Fear of a source of infection. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever is ongoing. The director says that "high-risk cases and other patients who were being monitored" have fled. "Our concern is that when people with possible Ebola infection walk around freely, they can become a source of infection." So far, 5000 people have died in the Ebola outbreak and 10,000 people have been infected with the virus. This week the World Health Organization approved the use of two new vaccines against the deadly Bundibugyo variant. Militant groups The area has also been plagued for years by various militant groups, about 100 of which are active in the region. ADF is a militia originally from Uganda that arose in the 1990s as a resistance movement against President Musenevi. The Allied Democratic Forces have sworn allegiance to the jihadist group Islamic State and regularly carry out attacks in the border region. The largest rebel group in the region is M23, which is allegedly supported by Rwanda. M23 conquered large parts of eastern Congo in 2021 and took the most important cities, Goma and Bukavu, in early 2025. In April the rebel group and <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of Congo concluded an agreement on allowing humanitarian aid.

title: NCTV: governments and companies not keeping pace with online threats
lead: Dutch companies, organisations and governments are taking measures to increase their resilience against online attacks, but not quickly or firmly enough to keep up with the rising pace of all threats, the National Coordinator for Counterterrorism and Security (NCTV) observes. It calls this a "serious risk to national security". According to the NCTV, it increases the chance of "society-disrupting espionage, data theft, sabotage and outages of digital processes". The question is not whether, but when, things will go wrong in the Netherlands. <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> calls on companies and organisations, in response to the NCTV's "worrying" latest report, to use the newest technology to defend their networks effectively. "Some say there needs to be a cyber version of 9/11 to wake us all up," he said after <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity> concluded. "I hope not." Cyber incidents NCTV Marc Kuipers wrote his annual overview of digital threats before the cyberattack on Ahold Delhaize last month. That cost the supermarket group between 200 and 250 million euros in revenue and caused shops to have empty shelves and websites and apps to be unreachable for days. Subsidiary Delhaize was hit by a hack again earlier this week. According to the NCTV, there are now many such "cyber incidents", a whole series of which are included in the report. In March, for example, Russian state hackers broke into WhatsApp and Signal accounts of government employees worldwide. They also gained access to sensitive information of Dutch civil servants. A month later, malicious actors stole the personal data of nearly all residents in a cyberattack on the servers of the <entity id="org:gemeente-epe">gemeente Epe</entity>. In the same period there was a hack at telecom provider Odido, in which the data of more than 6 million (former) customers was taken, one of the largest data thefts in Dutch history. Kuipers notes that even when companies pay ransom in such cases, stolen data is not always deleted by the criminals, even though that was promised. The Counterterrorism Coordinator makes no effort to hide his irritation at the "inadequate resilience" of some Dutch (government) organisations and companies. "Despite years of warnings and concrete cyber incidents, some still do not have the basic measures in order," he states. It also still happens that identified vulnerabilities are patched too late, "despite preventive warnings". The NCTV and the intelligence services had earlier warned that AI is making it increasingly easy to find gaps in computer systems and to organise larger attacks. Attackers use artificial intelligence, among other things, to develop malware, malicious software intended to damage or disrupt systems. AI also makes it easier to adapt and refine the malware during an attack if needed to bypass security. Increasing numbers of countries It has long been known that, alongside criminals, countries such as Russia, China, Iran and North Korea are very active in this area. The NCTV now sees more and more other countries having or working on such programmes. The problem is even bigger at this point than assumed, because only a limited part of the Chinese operations against the Netherlands in particular is noticed and countered. There are various causes for resilience against this still not being at the required level, ranging from a lack of "administrative direction" to a lack of money and manpower. This is a particular challenge for smaller organisations and companies. The NCTV fears that the resulting "uneven growth" relative to the rapidly increasing threat could erode citizens' trust. Or that apathy could even set in.

title: Podcast De Stemming: Cheating, crazy Henkie and a classic Bontenballetje
lead: Negotiations on the tax plan are still stuck fast, and according to the opposition <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is making a mess of it. Criticism is also coming from within the coalition itself, because CDA-<entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">fractieleider Bontenbal</entity> accuses <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of casino politics. According to Bontenbal the cabinet is driving towards a wall, because it is not certain of a majority in the Tweede- and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. That is why Bontenbal and the other two parliamentary group leaders are themselves looking for majorities in both chambers. What consequences does that have for relations within the coalition and the cabinet? De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister. You can also find all previous episodes there. Just like all other well-known podcast channels. About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings (EenVandaag, AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) go through the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Audax, publisher and owner of Bruna stores, in financial trouble
lead: The company behind the Bruna and ReadShop stores has been granted provisional protection from its creditors by the court. Parent company Audax has a cooling-off period until 17 November at the least, during which it can negotiate with creditors about the future. The stores of the group remain open during that period. If no solution is found, the company may go bankrupt. Audax has had money problems for years. The company had a debt of millions to the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> and the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity> due to the coronavirus crisis. Last year it concluded agreements under which part of those debts were forgiven. There are other debts too, for example to suppliers. These problems mean that products are sometimes not delivered to stores on time. Suppliers only want to deliver once they are paid. Dispute in the board. On top of that, there is a dispute within Audax's board. The company's top boss, Paul Sies, was suspended last month over "differences of opinion about how decisions are made". Sies also wanted to sell travel products in Bruna stores, but that plan failed. A spokesperson for Audax says the stores are fundamentally viable, but that the group is struggling with problems from the past. At least one party has requested Bruna's bankruptcy. Audax now has temporary time to reach an agreement with creditors. The company thinks it needs at least two months for that. The court will decide after a hearing on 17 November whether the company gets that time. Old store chain. Almost 800 people work at Audax. The company itself runs 91 Bruna stores. In addition, there are 190 Bruna franchise stores and 136 Readshop franchise stores. The Readshops are less dependent on Audax than Bruna and have so far experienced little impact from the financial problems. It is not known how many people work there in total. Bruna was founded in 1868 and is one of the oldest store chains in the Netherlands.

title: Father of Meghan Markle arrested by FBI for possession of child abuse images
lead: Meghan Markle's father (82) was arrested by the FBI at a nursing home in the United States. That is what the office of the public prosecutor in Florida reports. He has been charged with possessing images of sexual abuse of children. According to the prosecutor, there were also sexually explicit photos of himself with young girls. The material was found in two storage units near Los Angeles that he had rented for almost twenty years. Material on the Philippines Last month, images of child abuse were also found in a house of the 82-year-old Markle by a brother of Meghan Markle. He found on a phone in their father's house in the Philippines a 15-minute video with images of naked young girls. Later he found more shocking material. He filed a report with the Filipino police, who started an investigation and afterwards confirmed the discovery of child pornography. An investigation is also underway in Mexico into Thomas Markle. There, material of sexual abuse of children is said to have been found in a storage unit in his name, the British newspaper Daily Mail reports. Handcuffs Thomas Markle was staying in a nursing home in Florida, where he was recovering from a stroke. According to the Daily Mail, the FBI raided it there and took him away. He was led away in a wheelchair with handcuffs around his wrists. If Markle is convicted, he can receive a prison sentence of up to 20 years. Contact severed Earlier, Meghan Markle, wife of the British Prince Harry, said she was "deeply saddened" by the news that her father would possess child pornography and that her thoughts go out to the victims. Meghan Markle severed contact with her father long ago. In 2018 she was reportedly informed about "disturbing and shocking allegations" about him.

title: Municipalities struggle with refugee reception, in Oss they have a solution
lead: More and more municipalities are turning to the refugee reception in Oss. They want to know what makes the reception there so different. They are also looking into the possibility of following this example. The first seven municipalities are today on a course at the foundation that houses the refugees. Sixteen policy officers from those municipalities are listening attentively to the director of Stichting Thuis in Oss, Angelo Schuurmans. Shared reception They hear that around 500 people are currently being received in Oss: Ukrainians, asylum seekers and status holders live there together. Responsibility for the reception lies largely with the municipality. And it works closely with Stichting Thuis in Oss. Every month there are fixed visiting moments when the door is open here; fifty municipalities have meanwhile visited on working visits. "We were being bombarded with phone calls," says Schuurmans. "We are now in contact with 106 municipalities. Municipalities all have to get to work and want to gain inspiration and know how it works here." Own responsibility The reception has existed for 4.5 years. In 2022 Schuurmans got to work with volunteers. "Residents are at the helm here themselves, they have responsibility for their own living environment. And we don't move them around, so they feel at home here." That also becomes clear during the tour. Volunteer Rian Broeren is leading the municipalities around today. "This place radiates positivity. At first I had doubts myself. I wanted to give language lessons, but also thought - oh, with only men? But it was not scary at all, I was treated with a lot of respect. My prejudices have melted away, I no longer have them." Residents' council Residents feel at ease here, says Dana Kharatin from Ukraine. "This is the best location. It is a safe place for everyone who lives here," she says. "For me it feels like a big family." Sadaqatali Shirzad from Afghanistan has only just moved here with his family. "It feels very normal here to live together with many nationalities. It doesn't matter where you come from, we are all people." After four years the team in Oss consists of thirty staff members and over 200 volunteers. The newcomers also take part themselves, including through their own residents' council. Under supervision The list of municipalities under the supervision of the minister has become longer again on Monday, there are now 74. All the interest in the reception in Oss shows that municipalities are indeed looking for solutions. But talking to the media about it? Preferably not. During the course the policy officers prefer to stay in the background. Many municipalities are afraid of unrest and protests. One municipality explains why they are there today. "We wanted to see whether it could also be done differently. That people here have more say is really very interesting. And how have they got so many volunteers enthusiastic? We would very much like to do that too." Initially there was also resistance to the reception in Oss, says director Schuurmans. "We certainly also have people who are critical, but I am happy to talk with them. I need them too, you can't achieve this alone with half the population of Oss." More own control Municipalities are longing for more calm around the subject of asylum reception. In Oss this form of reception arose on their own initiative, but the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity> welcomes it too. "There are now 18 sustainable municipal reception locations. It is expected that more municipalities will opt for this reception, and certainly for smaller locations it can be a good set-up for a municipality", a spokesperson for the COA writes. "Textbook example" Minister of Asylum Van den Brink sees Oss as an example for other municipalities. "It is a very nice development, the big advantage is that a local organisation is in direct contact with society and then you see that it fits better." The minister has to talk with more and more municipalities that do not yet meet the dispersal act. And that often concerns the form of reception. "It may well be that we ourselves suggested going to Oss", according to the minister. Interest in the other approach only keeps growing, notes director Schuurmans. "We now have a waiting list of municipalities. The second round for this course is already planned for February."

title: Jetten on criticism from Rode Lijn: 'The Netherlands is definitely going out on a limb'
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity>-Jetten is taking no additional measures against Israel. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> are concerned about the situation of the Palestinians and emphasise that the Netherlands is increasing pressure on Israel in all sorts of ways to prevent further escalation. "The Netherlands is definitely going out on a limb", the prime minister said at his weekly press conference in response to the upcoming Rode Lijn demonstration. "But if you really want to exert effective pressure on the Israeli government, it works better with a broad front from Europe and with other international partners." On Sunday afternoon the fourth Rode Lijn demonstration takes place, starting from Museumplein in Amsterdam. The organisation demands that the cabinet-Jetten "increase the maximum political, economic and diplomatic pressure to definitively end the illegal occupation of Palestine". The organisers want a comprehensive arms embargo, in which "all direct and indirect arms trade and military cooperation with Israel" is halted. The cabinet must also recognise that the Israeli government "is committing genocide and ethnic cleansing against Palestinians". Trade ban Furthermore, the trade ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements must be extended to "all trade and investment". In September the Netherlands introduced a national trade ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements. Jetten did not directly address the demands of the Rode Lijn organisation at his press conference. The prime minister's message is mainly that the Netherlands is doing "everything" to prevent escalation in the area and to improve the humanitarian situation. "In bilateral talks with Israel we are increasing pressure to make clear that the situation in Gaza, the West Bank, but also in Jordan and Syria, is not acceptable", says Jetten. Jetten acknowledges that the coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA in principle think differently about Israel policy. But eight months ago, during the coalition negotiations, they agreed on a number of measures on which they could find common ground. "There is common ground and you have to look at where you can find each other", said Jetten. According to the prime minister, the cabinet has in recent months also significantly increased humanitarian aid, including financial and medical assistance. The Netherlands is also helping with the evacuation of sick children to Jordan. But the cabinet is not in favour of further expanding the trade ban, as the Rode Lijn organisation asks. Minister Berendsen of Foreign Affairs says that an expanded trade ban should preferably be introduced at European level and together with other international partners. "You must try to increase pressure on Israel at European level to change its behaviour", said Berendsen. First priority Defence Minister Yesilgöz, who was also asked about the wishes of the Rode Lijn demonstrators, is not at all in favour of stopping arms trade with Israel. "It concerns protective equipment that we cannot obtain from anywhere else", said the minister. "Protecting our own military personnel is my first priority." As D66 leader, Jetten spoke of genocide last year, but as prime minister he no longer wants to use that word. When asked about this he says: "As a cabinet it is our duty to do everything to prevent escalation." Jetten joined a previous Rode Lijn demonstration, but he will not do so now, because he is "in a different role". It does not look like the cabinet will change its course on Israel after the demonstration. Also in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> there is a majority for the current course. Recently, for example, proposals to recognise genocide and to introduce a total trade embargo were rejected in the House.

title: Knot and Hernández de Cos the only ones left in the race for ECB presidency
lead: Klaas Knot, the Dutch candidate for the position of president of the European Central Bank, has only one opponent in the contest for that position. Today the period for registering candidates closed. Only Pablo Hernández de Cos, the former president of the Spanish central bank, is in the race for the position alongside Knot. No other candidates have been nominated for the presidency of the ECB. Mid-December It is expected that a decision will be made in mid-December on who will succeed the current president, Christine Lagarde. That person must in any case win over at least 16 of the 21 EU countries where payments are made in euros. Together these countries must represent at least 65 percent of the population of the eurozone.

title: German parliament votes for five-year prison sentence for administering date rape drugs
lead: In Germany, the penalties for administering so-called date rape drugs, such as GHB, are becoming harsher. A majority of the German Bundestag has voted for a proposal to raise the minimum prison sentences for this from three to five years. The bill concerns administering drugs intended to render someone unconscious and then (sexually) abuse them. Because drugs such as GHB cause memory loss and hardly leave traces, these 'knockout drugs' are used for rape and robbery. If the Bundesrat, on behalf of the sixteen German states, also agrees to the proposal, the law will be introduced. 'Treacherous act' The drugs are often put in a drink. "By doing so, a person is deprived of the opportunity to defend themselves," says Carmen Wegge of the social democratic SPD, writes Tagesschau. CDU parliamentarian Susanne Hierl calls administering this type of drug "a particularly treacherous act". The amendment follows from a ruling of the German Federal Court of Justice. That court ruled that these drugs should be regarded as "dangerous instruments for crimes". That means that anyone who uses them for robbery or rape is treated as if they had used a weapon. 'Symbolic politics' Speaking to the German broadcaster WDR, forensic pathologist Britta Gahr calls the increase in penalties "symbolic politics" when it comes to the abuse of this type of drug for rape. According to her, the law should state that consent to sex is a requirement, and that if it is absent, there is sexual violence. Right now, sex against someone's will is only a crime if the person explicitly refuses, for example by saying 'no'.

title: Suspect confesses to attempted murder of Iranian publicist in Haarlem
lead: One of the six suspects in a failed assassination attempt on an Iranian activist and publicist in Haarlem has confessed that he came to the Netherlands to commit a murder on commission. The trial of five men and one woman started today in the extra-secure courtroom at Schiphol. The six are suspected of involvement in the 2024 attempted murder of Iranian activist Siamak Tahmasbi, who lives in Haarlem. Mehrez A., born in Tunisia, answered "yes" today to the judge's question of whether he intended to kill someone. The other two suspects present invoked their right to remain silent. A. stated that he did not know Tahmasbi: "I did not even know his name. For me it was a matter of money; I needed money to be able to get out of Europe. I was being sought by Europol and Interpol", the news agency ANP wrote down from his mouth. Alarm raised Tahmasbi raised the alarm on 6 June 2024 when he saw two men walking around his home at night. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was quickly on the scene and arrested two suspects. "One of them is also suspected of the failed liquidation attempt on the Spanish politician and Iran critic Alejo Vidal-Quadras", writes the <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity>. The intelligence service suspects that Iran ordered the attempted murder. Tahmasbi regularly expressed critical views online about the Iranian regime. Sledgehammer and firearms The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> sees the six suspects as "international criminals who were prepared to kill the victim for money". Today the case of four suspects was discussed on its merits. The 42-year-old Edwin V.C. from Colombia is suspected, together with the 29-year-old S.S.B., of preparing the assassination. The 29-year-old Colombian Gabriël O.S., B. and A. are suspected of carrying out the failed attempted murder of Tahmasbi. They are said to have gone to his house that night with a sledgehammer and firearms. B.'s case is being heard in absentia, because he is a fugitive. The cases of the other two suspects, a 23-year-old man and a 29-year-old woman, will be discussed on their merits next week. Next week the Openbaar Ministerie will announce its sentencing demands, and on 21 December the judge will deliver a verdict.

title: Amersfoort exhibition on the Jewish community may after all go ahead
lead: After all the criticism of the unexpected cancellation of an exhibition on 300 years of Jewish life in <entity id="org:gemeente-amersfoort">Amersfoort</entity>, Museum Amersfoort will look into how the exhibition can go ahead after all. This intention follows interference by Amersfoort mayor <entity id="person:lucas-bolsius">Lucas Bolsius</entity>. Next year the Amersfoort synagogue on the Drieringensteeg turns 300 years old. That a synagogue has been in use for so long is unique in West European history. Five years ago it was therefore decided to celebrate this anniversary in a big way. The Jewish Community of Amersfoort would make an exhibition together with Museum Amersfoort. Suddenly Museum Amersfoort cancelled the exhibition. According to museum director Paul Baltus, the reason was the heated debate about the war in Gaza and the situation in the Middle East. This would put the exhibition in a different light. "We do not want to expose our volunteers to the growing tension in society", Baltus told RTV <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> on Wednesday. Bewildered, angry and sad The museum received much criticism for the decision. Chairman Alexander van Dijkhuizen of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort told the regional broadcaster that he was "bewildered and also angry". He also asked why the museum thinks the volunteers might be in danger. Mayor Bolsius said in the municipal council on Wednesday that he was "extremely sad" about the decision and promised to talk with the museum soon. The Council of Churches also quickly made its voice heard and, in a critical letter to the museum director, called on him to let the exhibition go ahead after all. An Amersfoort story Last evening the Amersfoort mayor, the alderman for Culture, and the management and supervisory board of the museum discussed the exhibition. "It was a good and intensive conversation", Bolsius said. "Together we have established that we find it important that an exhibition comes that tells the story of 300 years of Jewish culture in Amersfoort. An Amersfoort story that must of course be told and fits the nature of the museum." He promised that the municipality will take extra security measures, in case that proves necessary. Encouraging The chairman of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort is happy with the outcome of the conversation. "The mayor acted very quickly, that is an enormous encouragement."

title: Americans vote against data centers, what does that mean for tech companies?
lead: They are essential to realising the grand ambitions that tech companies have with AI, but following this week's American election results it is in question whether all the planned data centers in the US will actually be built. In states such as Texas, Ohio and Georgia, where many of those centers are on the planning books, voters chose Democratic candidates on Tuesday. They are mostly critical of these centers and want to pause the construction of data centers. For the large tech companies, this means less support for their ambitions. This was also noticeable on the stock market after Tuesday, where the share price of tech stocks fell. This makes the Democrats' win seem like bad news for tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI. Tech companies had just invested massively in accelerating the construction of data centers in recent times. A large share is going to the US, but there is also growing criticism there of the high electricity and water consumption. More difficult from 2028 With the election results, there is an additional setback for the AI companies. In the short term, this will probably make little difference. "Projects that are on the planning for 2027 will not be quickly undone," says Rogier Quaedvlieg, US economist at ABN AMRO. "Construction has often already started, the permits have been granted." In 2028 the situation is different. "It takes some time before the policy of the new administrators and legislators, who take office in January, takes effect," says Quaedvlieg. "From 2028 the application procedure for new projects begins. Tech companies will find it harder to get permission for those than they do now." Referendums on data centers have also been held in several states. Almost everywhere, the population voted for a construction stop or against new centers. That could mean construction becomes more difficult in some states soon. Americans more negative For some voters this will be a relief. Americans think more negatively about the potential impact of data centers on the environment and the economy than at the beginning of the year. A majority finds a data center in their neighbourhood unpleasant. It is unlikely that all those concerns will disappear, thinks Philip Marey, US analyst at Rabobank. "In some states there will indeed be less construction after the change of legislators, but that does not mean that companies suddenly no longer want to build data centers." "Tech companies now have three options," says Quaedvlieg. "Option one: still try to influence public opinion. For example, by contributing to the infrastructure needed for the centers or by drawing up environmental plans." Another option is lobbying to have decisions on data centers made at federal level. "Then it is not the states that decide, but the national government." If none of that works, there is a third alternative: "Moving to other places." Moving elsewhere This has been experimented with for some time. "There are companies investigating whether they can build underwater," says Marey. Outer space is also sometimes mentioned. "Data centers in space look very attractive right now," Elon Musk wrote on X, just after the elections. It is more likely that companies will choose states that are more positive about AI and data centers, thinks Quaedvlieg. "In the extreme case they could even leave the country entirely." Quaedvlieg does not expect companies to move to Europe en masse. "Regions such as the Middle East are much more interesting. There is a lot of energy available there and the rules are often more lenient." Technology race This is a scenario that many American politicians do not want to think about. "The Democrats and Republicans agree that America must maintain its leading position in the technology race with China," says Marey. "That may also mean that in the long run the Democrats are willing to negotiate, to make concessions." According to Marey, this is characteristic of the tug-of-war over the construction of new data centers. "There is growing resistance to the expansion and to Trump's data center optimism. Critical voices are also emerging within the Republican party." At the same time, there is also the realisation that not taking part in the AI race is not an option. "That is comparable to the industrial revolution. You have to take part. The only question is where, how and at what price?"

title: Smoke bombs found at the away section of the FC Dordrecht stadium
lead: Smoke bombs were found this morning at the football stadium of FC Dordrecht, near the section where supporters of the visiting club sit. Staff of the Explosives Disposal Service made them harmless and removed them. The smoke bombs were found in the grass at the back of the away section, reports regional broadcaster Rijnmond. <entity id="org:politie">Politie</entity> and sniffer dogs searched the surroundings, but found nothing else. The stadium was released during the afternoon. It is not known how the smoke bombs ended up at the stadium. No one has been arrested. Center circle removed The find comes on the day FC Dordrecht and NAC meet. According to the regional broadcaster, there is a threatening atmosphere around tonight's match. Security cameras have been placed at the away section on the advice of the police. Since yesterday afternoon there has also been a camera on the Scheffersplein in Dordrecht. It has not been confirmed whether this is related to the disappearance of the center circle. Footage circulating on social media shows some NAC supporters entering the stadium in Dordrecht in the middle of the night and removing the center circle. FC Dordrecht did not want to respond to questions from Rijnmond.

title: White House chief of staff gone, Trump chooses hardliner Stephen Miller as successor
lead: White House chief of staff Susie Wiles is leaving. The important confidante of President Trump will be succeeded by hardliner Stephen Miller. "Susie Wiles has done an excellent job", President Trump writes in the message announcing her departure. "I thank her for her work as chief of staff." He praises Miller (41) as "one of my most trusted advisers". Until now he had been deputy chief of staff under Wiles. In Trump's first term he also served as speechwriter and top adviser to the president. Smoothing out differences The chief of staff is considered a pivotal figure in the White House, someone who smooths over political differences by correcting or placating party members and rivals. They are a spider in the political web who decides who gets to speak to the president or not. Especially with a president who, like Trump, is more focused on the big picture, this person has considerable influence over the fine political nuances. We previously made this portrait of Stephen Miller: Wiles (69) was the first woman to become chief of staff of the White House. She also lasted the longest in that role under Trump; in his first term, Trump went through four. 'Ice queen' Wiles is considered a confidante of the president, in his words an "ice queen" who firmly directed matters behind the scenes and one of the few whose disagreement he appears to tolerate. As campaign manager she had also helped with Trump's re-election. "I am proud of everything we have achieved together, from securing our border and lowering taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America back in first place", Wiles writes in a farewell message. She will still remain active in Trump's political organisation, the president said. In the recent period there had already been speculation that Trump would shake up his team after his major loss in the midterm elections. Wiles had already been named as one of the key figures who might step aside. Other names that came up were those of Defense Secretary Hegseth (as a scapegoat for the Iran war) and Secretary of State Rubio (who may be starting a presidential campaign). Both men deny preparing to leave, but Wiles also dismissed such speculation three weeks ago. More or less MAGA? It remains to be seen how Miller's appointment will be received in Washington. He is known as a hardliner on immigration. He defended the separation of families as a way to deter illegal immigration and he organised the deportation of migrants to a notorious prison in El Salvador. Democrats will argue that their election victory means the US now needs less MAGA and that politicians should focus more on the purchasing power of ordinary citizens. Trump, who shortly after his election defeat still said he wanted to work with the Democrats, appears with this move to be preparing for a hard line instead.

title: At least 150 demonstrators arrested at protest against data center in Amsterdam
lead: At a protest against a Microsoft data center in Amsterdam-West, an estimated 150 to 200 suspects have been arrested. They are suspected of trespassing, the police said. Some of the demonstrators voluntarily left the site. The activist group Fossielvrij demonstrated today at the construction site of the data center, at a designated location. The group opposes the arrival of data centers because some run on gas. The demonstration quickly got out of hand when another group of activists broke through the fences around the site. According to the police, pro-Palestinian demonstrators had an angle grinder and climbing equipment with them. Because they did not hand over the items despite repeated calls, the police intervened. This led to confrontations with the ME. Vandalism and theft Later, demonstrators nevertheless managed to get onto the construction site. There they climbed a crane and the roof of the data center under construction. According to the police, hundreds of pro-Palestinian activists had entered the site. The ME eventually cleared the site. Vandalism is said to have been committed at the construction site. The police found items among the arrested suspects that are believed to have been taken from the site. The suspects have been taken to a detention complex. Tonight it will be decided whether they remain in custody for longer.

title: Agreement in German coalition: Ilse Aigner to become the next federal president
lead: The German government parties are nominating Ilse Aigner (CSU) as the new federal president. The nomination will be officially announced on Monday, but it has leaked through almost all German media. It would be the first time a woman holds the highest office in Germany. Aigner has long been able to count on the support of the CSU and SPD, but Chancellor Merz (CDU) had blocked her nomination until now. He is reportedly now nonetheless backing her. The 61-year-old Aigner is mainly a well-known name in Bavaria, where she has already been parliamentary president for eight years. Earlier she was Minister of Agriculture in two cabinets of Chancellor Merkel. According to Bavarian Premier Söder (CSU), Aigner has proven herself as a unifying and human figure who brings a great deal of political experience. In terms of views, she stands in the centre, between left and right. Aigner has not yet responded to the nomination. The President of Germany is a largely ceremonial function. In recent weeks she had already hinted that she regarded the speculation as a compliment. Striking run-up However suitable someone may be, the choice of a president is mainly about politics. Although the CDU/CSU and SPD together have only a third of the voters behind them, they divide the post among themselves as they always have. The current federal president Steinmeier, who must step down after two terms, is an SPD member. That is why it is now the Christian Democrats' turn. CSU leader Söder was quick off the mark and let Aigner's name drop this spring. Because she was seen as an internal rival of Söder, that initially looked like a calculated move to sideline her. In the Berlin bubble, the political rule is that whoever is named first will not get the job. But it turned out to be serious. Aigner remained for months the only name that was taken seriously and was constantly praised by Söder. Both the East German CDU branches and the SPD and the Greens expressed support for her. Merz reticent Chancellor Merz remained reticent. Again and again he said that the CDU would sooner or later come up with a candidate. A power game may be involved: the smaller CSU must be subordinate to the larger CDU. Arguments as to why Aigner would not be suitable never came. Merz did commit himself to the next federal president being a woman. A noble aim, but also a limiting factor; the CDU is quite a men's party. All sixteen state parliamentary groups are led by a man, as are the most important ministries. With two exceptions, all current and former CDU state premiers are men. Eventually, the name of Ines Claus was floated in the rumour mill through German newspapers. "Ines who?" was the headline of many media outlets. She is the CDU parliamentary group leader in Hesse. She has never held a political office, so she was not taken seriously as a candidate. "That trial balloon did not rise very high," according to the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. CSU takes the lead With Aigner's nomination, Markus Söder's dream of becoming chancellor is over. He had already tried twice without success, and because of the faltering leadership of the unpopular Merz, his name regularly comes up as a possible replacement for the chancellor. Still, it is unthinkable that the two highest positions in the country would fall to the small CSU. With the choice of Aigner, Söder has proven himself to be the shadow chancellor. The CSU leader made the choice and the political centre rallied behind him, while Merz was left out in the cold. The power decline of the faltering chancellor has once again become visible. Symbolic function The power of the federal president is limited and the function is mainly ceremonial. As the first woman in this office, a certain symbolism does come with it. Signing laws and appointing ministers is mainly a formality. The president only intervenes in day-to-day affairs in exceptional situations. That happened recently, incidentally, when current president Steinmeier intervened in the umpteenth conflict between the coalition parties. As president, Aigner will represent Germany internationally at state visits, conferences and commemorations. In addition, the president is regarded as the constitutional conscience of the state. In the discussion about a possible ban on the AfD, she can therefore play a crucial, guiding role. Aigner still has some time to move from Munich to Berlin. In January there will be a vote and in March she will then take office.

title: Judge: ANWB strike may go ahead, but with enough roadside assistance patrols on the road
lead: During a strike by ANWB employees next Monday, a minimum staffing level of 12.5 percent must remain at the road services organisation. That is what the interim relief judge has ruled. The ANWB had started summary proceedings against a strike by, among others, employees of the Wegenwacht and the Alarmcentrale. The strike was organised by the trade unions. The road services organisation feared that stranded motorists could not be helped and that chaos would break out on the roads. For that reason the ANWB asked for a mandatory minimum staffing level. Employees would also have to return to work in emergencies. Car stuck in tunnel According to the judge, the strike is lawful, but a restriction is justified "because this is urgently necessary from a societal point of view". In the event of serious accidents or, for example, a stationary car on the hard shoulder or in a tunnel, the ANWB must take action. In that case, employees who are not taking part in the strike will be deployed first, but striking members must also be able to step in in the event of a very serious accident, the judge ruled. The ANWB employees are striking because the collective labour agreement negotiations have stalled. They want better working conditions and a higher salary.

title: Cabinet wants stricter rules for posting migrant workers from another EU country
lead: The cabinet wants stricter requirements for the deployment of migrant workers from outside the European Union who are posted to the Netherlands via another EU member state. According to <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">minister Vijlbrief</entity> (Social Affairs, D66), this "backdoor route" is being used more and more and is intended to circumvent Dutch rules. Anyone who wants to work in an EU country needs a work and residence permit for that. Compared with other countries, the Netherlands is fairly strict about this, so personnel are brought in to the Netherlands via a different route. For example, a person from Belarus is then deployed by a company from Poland for a job in the Netherlands. In 2021, 18,000 such posted third-country nationals were registered; in 2025, just over 29,000. The actual number is probably much higher. Three months of work The cabinet wants third-country nationals who come to work in the Netherlands via this route to first work for three months in the European country where they entered, in the example above Poland. The Labour Inspectorate will check this. Under the plans, the migrant worker in the country of arrival must also have a residence permit valid for longer than the work in the Netherlands lasts. That way, the person can return once the job in the Netherlands is finished. The rules must take effect on 1 July 2027. The Schoof cabinet made a first attempt last year to limit the backdoor route. Then-minister Van Hijum (Social Affairs) said his successor would probably have to finish the job. Fines rise sharply Employers who disregard the rules will face higher fines from mid next year. From 1 July, fines for violating labour laws will rise by about 22 percent. An employer who pays an employee less than the minimum wage currently faces a maximum fine of 10,000 euros, for example. Under the new rules, that will be about 12,200 euros. More plans Minister Vijlbrief has announced more plans in recent months to tackle abuses involving migrant workers. For example, from 1 July 2028 companies will no longer be allowed to withhold money from employees' minimum wage in exchange for housing. There is also a plan for a ban that year on hiring temporary agency workers in the meat sector. This often concerns migrant workers. The cabinet's plans will be discussed next Thursday in a committee debate with members of the House of Representatives and minister Vijlbrief.

title: Paint producers AkzoNobel and Axalta may merge under conditions
lead: The European Commission has approved the merger between paint producers AkzoNobel and Axalta. There is one condition: AkzoNobel must divest its European division that produces automotive coatings. The Commission believes the combination would become too large in certain coatings. Garages that repair cars could then face high prices. Garages cannot easily switch to another supplier, because they use special equipment for mixing. "European consumers are already dealing with rising prices for mobility and transport. For commuters and families, affordable car repairs are important to keep the car roadworthy throughout its entire lifetime", says responsible European Commissioner Teresa Ribera. The market for coatings is largely in the hands of four producers. The American Axalta is the largest and focuses only on producing coatings. In fourth place is the Dutch AkzoNobel, which produces both paint and coatings. In August, shareholders of both the Dutch and American companies almost unanimously approved the plan to merge. The merger may go ahead, provided a suitable buyer is found for AkzoNobel's coatings division. The Commission must also approve this buyer. "Through the commitments AkzoNobel and Axalta have made regarding their merger, players in the automotive repair market are prevented from pursuing high margins, rising prices or lower quality at the expense of consumers", according to Ribera.

title: Green light for Trump's triumphal arch, but judge halts construction immediately
lead: A US judge has halted construction of the triumphal arch that President Trump wants to build in Washington. This happened an hour after a commission had approved the structure. That commission called it a fitting tribute to American history and the country's veterans. The triumphal arch is to be 76 meters high, taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. The arch is to be placed at Memorial Circle, a few kilometers from the White House. Close to this spot lies the Arlington National Cemetery military cemetery. Eight-hour session Opponents protested yesterday against the arch, also known as 'Arc de Trump'. Meanwhile, the National Capital Planning Commission, a body that oversees urban planning changes in Washington, assessed the proposed building plans in a public hearing lasting more than eight hours. Both supporters and opponents had their say. Opponents argue that the structure obstructs the view of Arlington National Cemetery. Thousands of American military personnel are buried there. Many opponents also consider the project illegal, because the plans have not been approved by Congress. Some of the commission members were appointed by Trump. In the end, the commission gave a green light: eight members voted in favor and four were against. Nevertheless, a federal judge decided an hour later that construction must remain halted for fourteen days. The court will use the next two weeks to examine the arguments of both parties. The White House does not agree. A spokesperson called the court 'activist' in a post on X. "We are confident that we will be fully vindicated in this lawsuit and look forward to the completion of this beautiful arch", according to a statement. Trump wants the arch to be standing in two years, when his second term as president ends. Prestige projects The triumphal arch is one of the prestige projects with which Trump wants to leave his mark on the city of Washington. He is also having a ballroom built at the White House and has designated two rooms in the White House as national monuments. With this, he aims to prevent his successors from undoing the changes he has made to the Oval Office. Trump has, among other things, added gold decorations to his study, and there is also a gilded bronze eagle sculpture.

title: Man arrested at Schiphol for bomb threat on flight to Prague
lead: The Royal Netherlands Marechaussee has arrested a 45-year-old man because he allegedly made a false bomb threat at Schiphol. The threat was made last evening and concerned a departing flight to Prague, a Marechaussee spokesperson confirms. The man, who has Czech nationality, was arrested last evening at a gate at the airport. According to the Marechaussee, he made the bomb threat verbally. He had a ticket for the flight to Prague. The plane departed for the Czech Republic with some delay. The man was released this afternoon. It is not known whether he will be prosecuted. Days of false alarms. A bomb threat was also received today about a KLM flight from Prague to Amsterdam. The plane landed at Schiphol as normal and was checked. No explosives were found on board, the Marechaussee says. In recent days, more false bomb threats have been made about flights in Europe. As far as is known, in none of these cases was a bomb found. The threats appear intended to disrupt passenger aviation.

title: Mats Akkerman wins Slimste Mens, also farewell to Paulien Cornelisse
lead: WNL reporter Mats Akkerman has won the final of the thirtieth season of the knowledge quiz De Slimste Mens. He won in the final against NOS reporter Jeroen Gortworst. Before that, Claudia de Breij had been eliminated, after which Jeroen Gortworst and Mats Akkerman had to battle it out. Akkerman ultimately won with a question about actress Olivia Colman. He was handed the trophy by presenter Herman van der Zandt. Normally the previous winner does that, but WNL presenter Frank van Leeuwen was unable to attend. Ahead of the 2026 final, attention was also paid to the death of jury chair Paulien Cornelisse. The cabaret artist and writer died at the end of September at the age of 50 from the consequences of cancer, but had still been seen in the broadcasts in recent weeks. Personal message Presenter Van der Zandt spoke in a personal message about missing Paulien Cornelisse and said he felt supported by all the reactions that came in after her death. "You, like the candidates and I, have been able to enjoy our fantastic, funny and insightful Paulien Cornelisse over the past period", says Herman. "And tonight is the last time." Looking ahead to the broadcast, he promised that it would nonetheless be a festive evening. "With a winner, with gold confetti, with a trophy being handed over and with a kind jury chair like there was only ever one." At the end of the broadcast, some memorable clips of Paulien Cornelisse from this season were shown.

title: Will Mississippi elect a Democrat as senator or not? Race remains tight
lead: The last Democratic senator from Mississippi was elected in 1947: John C. Stennis, a fierce supporter of racial segregation as a 'Dixiecrat'. Now a Black party colleague has a significant chance of winning in the conservative state. Public prosecutor Scott Colom is currently 2010 votes ahead of sitting Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith; it is 49.1 to 48.8 percent. A light blue corner in the otherwise deep red South of the US. It is a development that many political experts until recently considered impossible. The final result will take a few more days, because mail-in ballots may still arrive up to five days after the election. The dynamics here are slightly different from the other seven states where Trump's Republicans lost a Senate seat. Everywhere they suffered from the unpopular presidential policies, but they also felt the consequences of demographic shifts (Georgia), an awkward candidate (South Carolina) or scandals (Texas). Colom had to overcome the traditional hurdles for Democrats. Voting made difficult Democrats should have it easier in Mississippi; there is no state with a larger Black minority (37 percent), a population group that votes Democratic above average. But voting is not made easy for them: Mississippi is one of three states where you cannot vote early, you must have an excuse for a mail-in vote, and an identification document is mandatory, something poorer residents often do not have. Finding time to vote is often too expensive for them anyway. Voters there also lose their voting rights for some convictions. That is a legacy from the period right after the Civil War, when white power holders wanted to exclude millions of voting-eligible former slaves. For a long time there was racist harassment at polling stations, where Black voters had to 'prove' they were worthy of their vote, with questions about the number of feathers on a chicken or bubbles from a bar of soap. Reaching out to the base. That legacy puts Democrats at a disadvantage. Hyde-Smith previously won by 10 percentage points, and Trump won the state three times with a lead of 20 percentage points. The last time a Black senator won here was in 1875, a former slave. Colom focused on mobilizing his base. Together with the advocacy organization NAACP he helped voters register so they could vote. He also visited his voters everywhere. When Donald Trump campaigned for Hyde-Smith, Colom stood outside welcoming her supporters to "lend my ear". What did not help Hyde-Smith was her unfortunate answer when she was asked about high beef prices: "Can't you just choose other meat?" Colom immediately added a food truck to his campaign caravan where people could get tacos with the meat of their choice, under the motto "better choose a different senator". Radiating confidence. In October Democrats began to believe in Colom's chances. Party heavyweights such as Bill Clinton and Kamala Harris came to campaign. This led to Trump also coming to give Hyde-Smith a boost, contrary to all expectations. He called Colom a "Marxist radical" and "a fraud". Hyde-Smith warned that Colom wants to make children transgender, will raise taxes and grants health insurance to illegal immigrants. Such attacks seemed to affect Colom less in an election where price increases were the main issue. He hammered home that Hyde-Smith had voted against healthcare subsidies and had therefore made life more expensive. While counting the votes, Colom now radiates confidence. "We will make sure every vote is counted, and then we will get this seat." Hyde-Smith also remains fierce. "I assure you, I remain senator", she promised her supporters. "The Democrats worked hard and many turned out, but not enough." Possible recounts. The tension will last until at least November 10. Until then, around 3,600 mail-in ballots can still arrive, provided they were sent on or before election day. In addition, there are provisional votes, whose validity is checked afterwards. How many there are exactly is unclear. Colom estimates around 15,000. Even when all of those have been counted, the process is not over: the candidates can request recounts. Only in Mississippi that is not formally arranged. A candidate must enforce it through a judge, with evidence that something may have gone wrong. Since all of that costs money, both candidates have already called on their supporters to dig deep once again.

title: Alliana new president of Paraguay, Peña officially removed after banking crisis
lead: Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as president of Paraguay. He succeeds Santiago Peña, who shortly before was officially removed by parliament. Peña is held responsible for a banking crisis that has left nearly 3 million of the 6.5 million Paraguayans unable to access their savings. The 52-year-old Alliana was vice president under Peña for years and will remain interim president until the next elections in 2028. Both men are members of the conservative Colorado party. Immunity Peña submitted his resignation earlier this week to get ahead of an impeachment procedure. Parliament rejected that request during a joint session of <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> and the Chamber of Deputies. Then both chambers voted unanimously for his removal. Through his removal Peña loses the legal protection he could have had as a former president. Now he can therefore be prosecuted more easily. His lawyers argued that the impeachment procedure should have stopped after he offered his resignation, but the senators did not agree. Shareholders The Public Prosecution Service of Paraguay has meanwhile issued an arrest warrant against Peña and placed him under house arrest. He will remain so for the time being until the investigation is completed. According to prosecutors, the former president had close ties with the Ueno bank, which was placed under receivership on Thursday by the Paraguayan central bank. This was done because of serious financial problems. Peña was still a shareholder of that bank until last year. Because of the banking crisis Paraguay is in a financial and political crisis. Millions of people have feared for their savings since the problems at Ueno, one of the country's largest banks, which among other things manages government money. The crisis led to large-scale street protests. Paraguay is generally seen as one of the more stable countries in South America. After his swearing-in Alliana gave a short speech in the Senate. In it he promised that affected Paraguayans would be compensated as quickly as possible. The central bank has meanwhile begun gradually paying out funds to account holders. For now this is happening in the form of advances. The removed Peña has not yet taken responsibility for the unrest in the country, but did express regret. "I want to apologise to the people, if at any point I have disappointed them," he said. "It was never my intention to violate the trust they placed in me." Millions of people cannot access their money, which led to large protests in Paraguay:

title: A32 open again after closure due to risk of falling glass panels
lead: The A32 near Grou in Friesland is open again in both directions. The road was closed on Thursday evening due to a dangerous situation at the Aquaduct Mid-Fryslân. The culprits were the glass panels of the lights above the roadway, which could fall down. According to Omrop Fryslân, all light boxes in the aqueduct have now been removed and the roadway has been cleaned. That means there is temporarily no light in the tunnel tub. The work went faster than expected. On Friday evening around 20:00 the road towards Leeuwarden from Heerenveen opened again, and later the other side too. Wear: the 84 light boxes in the aqueduct, 42 per driving direction, had according to <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> been subject to wear due to heavy traffic, the suction effect of lorries and splashing salt water. "We can state that there is material fatigue in the light fittings. These have prematurely reached the end of their technical service life." The road manager will also examine other aqueducts in the North of the Netherlands for wear and damage to the light boxes in the coming period. The A32 runs under the Prinses Margrietkanaal. The 66 kilometre long motorway is an important traffic artery in the North of the Netherlands and connects Leeuwarden, Heerenveen and Meppel. Traffic between Heerenveen and Leeuwarden was diverted during the closure via Drachten, over the A7 and the N31.

title: Suspect arrested near White House with multiple firearms in car
lead: The Secret Service, responsible for protecting President Trump, arrested a man near the White House on Thursday evening local time who had three weapons in his car, including a semi-automatic rifle. The suspect told agents that voices in his head had instructed him to travel to the American capital to kill the president. The man is reportedly a Venezuelan and has been residing illegally in the United States since March 2024. The three weapons were in a vehicle registered as stolen. There were also dozens of rounds of ammunition in the car. It is not known where Trump stayed that evening. Earlier that day he was still in the White House, where among others his wife Melania spoke about the recent ceasefire around the South Ukrainian city of Olesjky. The suspect is charged with criminal offences, including illegally transporting weapons and unlawful possession of weapons, according to the American Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>. He was arrested on Constitution Avenue, south of the White House, after he displayed suspicious behaviour in the vehicle he was sitting in. A core task of the Secret Service is protecting the president and leading American politicians. The White House is heavily guarded and is currently protected by a high fence covering a larger area than before. The suspect has been placed in custody and is under the supervision of the federal police service. The incident is the most recent in a series of arrests and threats directed at President Trump and his family since his return to the White House last year. For example, last May there was an exchange of gunfire near the White House in which a man died. Trump has not yet responded to this incident.

title: Podcast De Dag: the sex lives of older people with dementia
lead: In the new feature film Queen at Sea we see a partner, a daughter and essentially an entire family struggling with the sexual wishes of an older woman with dementia. Who decides that she still wants that, when she can no longer clearly express it herself? Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Don't forget to subscribe. According to care editor Floor Ligtvoet of Nieuwsuur, the film offers a unique view of a taboo that care providers are very eager to get rid of. Experts call for opening the conversation about it, because older people with dementia also have sexual desires and a need for intimacy. They are people like you and me. But how do you break that taboo? The discomfort is noticeable among care staff, says specialist in geriatric medicine at AMSTA Micky Las van Bennekom. In podcast De Dag she explains how that conversation is now being held. And how, within the walls of a nursing home, sexual desires among residents are guided in the right direction. Should the family also know about it, or is it private? Reactions? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editor: Wouter Sloekers Final editor: Rosanne Sies

title: Ambulance dispatch centre East Netherlands 'on black' due to understaffing
lead: The ambulance dispatch centre East Netherlands in Apeldoorn has been struggling with understaffing for months. As a result, the dispatch centre has for several nights been unable to take 112 calls. The largest dispatch centre in the Netherlands is in crisis mode, writes Omroep Gelderland based on internal documents of the dispatch centre East Netherlands. 'On black' At the dispatch centre East Netherlands in Apeldoorn, the ambulance, <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and fire services of five safety regions work together: Gelderland-Zuid, Gelderland-Midden, Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, IJsselland and Twente. For months gaps have appeared in the roster, mainly due to staff shortages at Gelderland-Midden and Gelderland-Zuid. Staff from the dispatch centre in Noord-Nederland then have to step in. On the night of 30 September to 1 October, the dispatch centre Noord-Nederland had to take over all 112 calls: the dispatch centre East Netherlands went 'on black'. A few days later this happened again. Patient safety "This is a matter of life and death," says Patiëntenfederatie Nederland. "Everyone who calls 112 and needs care immediately must be able to get it in time." Whether the waiting time actually increases due to the understaffing, the cooperating ambulance regions do not want to say. It is never certain whether a longer waiting time has consequences for a patient. "We understand that every second can feel long for someone calling 112, especially in an emergency," the regions respond. "Based on the available data, we have no indications that patient safety is at stake." Crisis team To prevent the dispatch centre from going 'on black' more often, a crisis team has taken measures. For example, staff must temporarily stop training and side tasks, supervisors who are normally surplus are scheduled, and the Inspectorate of Health Care and Youth has been informed.
