Even so, opposition leader Lieberman suddenly said on Thursday that he was willing to compromise on national service, if that would allow a coalition to be formed without Netanyahu. It remains to be seen whether the other opposition leaders, and above all Eisenkot himself, will agree. A day later Eisenkot posted a message on X restating his four conditions for cooperation, including military and civilian national service for everyone. Finally, a government of national unity is also on the table, in which Eisenkot and Netanyahu would work together. Netanyahu called for this again last night, but Eisenkot rules out any cooperation with Netanyahu, as do the other opposition leaders. A new war with Iran could possibly change that. The threat of a new attack by America and Israel has been hanging in the air for weeks. If an attack happens, the call for national unity could grow. That could increase the pressure on Eisenkot to cooperate with Netanyahu after all. Breaking election promises Israel's political landscape has thus become entangled in election promises and red lines. In the coming weeks it will become clear which parties are willing to adjust their positions. Eisenkot faces a complicated political puzzle, and it looks like election promises will have to be broken. He has 28 days to reach a coalition, with an extension of 14 days. If Eisenkot does not succeed within that time, the turn may pass to Netanyahu.

title: Two women and a man found dead in house of Krakau shooter, presumably family
lead: In the house of the 24-year-old man who shot six people dead in Krakau on Saturday afternoon, two women and a man were found dead. Polish Prime Minister Tusk announced this at a press conference with the security services in Krakau. The victims are probably the man's immediate family members. According to Polish media, the victims are the perpetrator's father, mother and sister. Tusk said he was convinced that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> would quickly arrest the shooter's "accomplices". The motive is still unclear. The <entity id="pos:minister-van-defensie">minister van Defensie</entity> speaks of "a terrorist act against the residents of Krakau". The minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says the shooter was presumably inspired by far-right ideologies. Firearms and ammunition were found in the man's car. The weapons were registered in the name of his father. It was also announced that one of the six people shot dead in the centre of Krakau holds British nationality. Fifteen people were injured in the attack. Among them are two police officers and five foreigners. After a firefight with the police, the shooter himself was taken to hospital; his condition is said to be critical. In Krakau, an investigation is underway at the spot where the shooter was shot. It is being checked whether the car could explode, and residents have been evacuated. The shooting minute by minute: Minister Kierwinski of Binnenlandse Zaken praised the quick action of the police; according to him, a "much greater bloodbath has been prevented". The man wore military clothing and a bulletproof vest during the attack, and used a military firearm. This fuelled reports that he was a former soldier, but this has been contradicted by the minister of Defensie. 'The square will be ours again' The mayor of Krakau, Lukaz Gibala, has announced that the city will be in mourning until Wednesday. He also promised that Krakau will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy. "The square will be ours again," he said on social media. The Dutch <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> reports that, according to the police in Krakau, there are no Dutch nationals among the victims. The shock in Poland is great. Eyewitness Konrad looks back on the day for the Polish news site Interia. Right after the first shots were fired, shortly after 15.00, he still thought someone was setting off fireworks. Firecrackers, he suspected. But everything he heard afterwards was different, he says. "Rhythmic, cyclical and deep," he says. Something he had never heard before. He was not the only one whose Saturday afternoon turned into a nightmare. "Suddenly I saw a black car drive past, shots were fired from the driver's window. Everyone started running, people fell." He too ran, in a straight line to the police station on the central market square. "I rushed inside and saw countless people lying on the floor. Hiding. Nobody spoke Polish, they were all tourists." 15 million tourists a year While he and the tourists were taking cover, two police officers went outside. "They hesitated for a moment, but went anyway. They got into a police car and drove away." Eventually Konrad also dared to leave the police station. He found chaos on the square, which is known as one of the most beautiful and largest medieval market squares in Europe. It lies in the middle of the historic city centre, which is on the Unesco World Heritage List and partly for that reason attracts around fifteen million tourists a year. Krakau is also an important departure point for people wishing to visit the former Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration and extermination camp. Once outside, Konrad saw victims lying on the ground everywhere. "I walked to a clothing shop and saw them trying to resuscitate a woman. I don't think she survived." Footage shows that the panic is great: people flee into shops, dive under restaurant tables, and screaming can be heard. An eyewitness tells the Polish medium Onet that people took off their shirts to stop victims from bleeding. "It was shocking." The shooter eventually came to a halt in his black Subaru when he crashed into a white car. He then ended up in a firefight with the police. The moment the shooter is shot down, the officer was himself hit by the shooter:

title: Ice rink in Leeuwarden closed again due to ammonia leak
lead: The Elfstedenhal in Leeuwarden has been evacuated again due to an ammonia leak, Omrop Fryslân reports. Earlier this week the ice rink also closed due to an ammonia leak. Ammonia is used in the technical room of the hall to cool the motors. Ammonia also leaked here on Tuesday. "It really was spurting out," said director Klaas Siderius at the time to the Leeuwarder Courant. There were 400 people in the hall, who had to leave immediately. Now, according to Siderius, the ice rink is experiencing the same fault. The Elfstedenhal will in any case remain closed until Monday. Small amount The director emphasises to Omrop Fryslân that no one has been in danger. This time, according to him, only a small amount of ammonia escaped, and the leak was discovered immediately. "When there is a leak, an alarm goes off immediately at the technical service," says Siderius. "They then see a red screen. And according to our protocol, the hall is immediately evacuated when there is an ammonia leak."

title: Building in Zutphen city centre partly collapses, several houses evacuated
lead: In the center of Zutphen, a building partially collapsed on Saturday evening. Several homes in this building were evacuated, the safety region reports. As far as is known, there are no victims. At the end of the evening, an interior wall of the building collapsed. Afterwards, the floor of two homes came down. How this could happen is not clear. The building and surrounding houses were evacuated. According to news agency ANP, ten residents were evacuated. An inspection showed that the building is stable and cannot collapse further. The residents of the houses where the floor collapsed cannot return to their homes. The residents of the surrounding homes may return. After the collapse, a smell of gas was noticed near the building, the safety region writes. Liander came to the scene to shut off the gas.

title: US army says it fired on ship in Gulf of Oman
lead: The United States fired on a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday. The US army reported this on X. The crew of the M/V Huda, sailing under the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis, tried to evade the US naval blockade, the army says. The crew also reportedly ignored warnings from the army. The ship came from an Iranian port. The US has been blocking shipping traffic to and from Iran since April this year. The US army published these images of the attack: An American military aircraft then carried out an attack on the stern of the ship. As a result the ship lost steering. The last confirmed American attack on a ship in the Gulf of Oman was almost a month ago. The US has not disclosed what happened to the crew. The National Guard of the United Arab Emirates does say it rescued 22 people from a burning ship in the Gulf of Oman. It is not clear whether it is the same ship. Explosions: On Saturday evening, according to Iranian state media, there were also explosions on the Iranian island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz and in the port of the Iranian city of Jask. The US army has said nothing about this. The US did earlier announce that it carried out an attack on Qeshm on Friday evening, for the first time since the interim American elections. According to President Trump, that attack was limited in scope.

title: Cabaret performer Herman Finkers named greatest Twentenaar
lead: Cabaret performer Herman Finkers has been named the greatest Twentenaar. He received the title from daily newspaper Tubantia after a public vote and jury assessment. The 71-year-old Finkers was nominated most often and received by far the most votes. The poet and songwriter Willem Wilmink, who died in 2003, came second. Leendert Overduin, who has also died, finished third. During the Second World War he led an organisation providing aid to Jews. Finkers responded to the title in his characteristically dry, deflating manner. "The greatest Twentenaar of all time. Well, my wife thinks differently about that." Finkers spoke of "an honourable mistake". "But I think it's very sweet of all those people who voted for me." Finkers was born in Almelo and grew up there too. Twente regularly features in his work. For example, in 2020 he released the Twente feature film De beentjes van Sint-Hildegard. And last month, partly on Finkers' initiative, a new edition of the Biebel in the Tweantse dialect by Anne van der Meiden was published.

title: Iran executes three men for, among other things, arson at protests
lead: In Iran three men have been executed for their role in anti-regime protests in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. That is what state news agency IRNA reports. The protests came to a boiling point at the beginning of this year. To put a stop to them, Iranian authorities and paramilitaries carried out a massacre among demonstrators. An estimated more than 7,000 protesters were killed , and thousands of activists were also detained. The three executed men, Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh, reportedly used firearms, grenades and Molotov cocktails at demonstrations on 8 and 9 January, according to Iranian authorities. They allegedly set fire to public facilities and damaged an electricity station, which reportedly led to power outages in some areas. The men were also accused of carrying out assignments for Israel and the United States, arch-enemies of Iran. The executions were carried out after the sentences were upheld by the Iranian Supreme Court, which is controlled by the Iranian regime. The belongings of the executed men have been confiscated. Eight other men were sentenced to prison terms of five to ten years. See this explainer on the number of executions rising worldwide: In the recent period Iran has carried out more executions related to the January demonstrations. As with the now executed trio, it regularly concerns people accused of having ties with Israel and the US. According to news broadcaster Iran International, based in London, at least seventy people have been executed between 7 January and 5 October, half of them because of the protests in January. Human rights organisations believe the real numbers are higher. Human Rights Watch wrote in a report in September that in Iran there are hasty procedures, and that confessions are sometimes obtained through torture. Also, people are executed in public, to spread fear and discourage dissidents.

title: Wake-up call 8/11: Rode Lijn protest against Israeli violence • European cyclo-cross championships in the Achterhoek
lead: Good morning! Today there is another 'Rode Lijn' demonstration in Amsterdam, a march against the violence in the Palestinian territories. In the Achterhoek the European cyclo-cross championships for men are being held . First the weather: in the middle of the country the sun is still shining for now, but over the coming hours cloud cover will increase. It is 5 to 9 degrees. Especially in the southwest there will be some rain now and then this evening, and overnight it cools to 2 to 8 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? In the home of the 24-year-old man who shot six people dead in Kraków yesterday afternoon, two women and a man have been found dead . That is what Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reports at a press conference with the security services in Kraków. Most likely these are close family members of the man. Polish media report that they are the shooter's father, mother and sister. Tusk said he was convinced that the police will quickly arrest the shooter's "accomplices". There is still no clarity about a motive, although Minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said the shooter is presumably inspired by far-right ideologies. Other news from the night: And then just this: For the second time this autumn, people were able to skate on the natural ice rink in Winterswijk yesterday morning. Overnight a thin layer of ice was made there so that skates could be used. Hundreds of people were there extra early. Have a nice day!

title: More details known about Krakow attacker, motive of Michal O. still unclear
lead: The motive of the attacker who shot dead six people in the Polish city of Krakow yesterday is still not clear. However, more is gradually becoming known about his background. According to Polish media, the perpetrator is 24-year-old Michal O., a man from the southeast of the country. In the attack in the centre of Krakow, besides the fatal victims, four women and two men, fifteen people were also injured. Among them are some coachmen, two police officers and five foreigners. They are in hospital, a police spokesperson told news agency PAP this morning. One of the officers is in life-threatening condition. The police have called on the Polish public to donate blood for him. The gunman himself is in critical condition in hospital, after a shootout with the police. The perpetrator was wearing camouflage clothing and a bulletproof vest when he opened fire from a car yesterday afternoon. He fired with an AR-15, a semi-automatic weapon that can fire hundreds of shots per minute. He was also armed with a handgun and had more weapons and ammunition in his boot. This is how the attack unfolded moment by moment: Rumours that he was a former soldier were denied by the authorities yesterday. Minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said that O. was probably inspired by far-right ideologies and is an "ultranationalist". According to Polish media, Michal O. and his father both had a firearms permit and he is said to have taken the weapons from the family home. That home is in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town about 140 kilometres northeast of Krakow. That residence was searched last night: two women and a man were found dead there. The police have now confirmed that they are his parents and sister. 'Such a normal boy' Neighbours tell Polish media that they never expected Michal O. to be capable of such an act. "A boy, just a boy. He wore a hood and said hello. I cannot say anything bad about him", a neighbour tells Radio Swietokrzyskie. "He's such a normal boy, cheerful and happy", another neighbour tells the outlet Echo Dnia. "As far as I know, he used to win prizes at school." Information from news website Interia confirms that picture. As a young teenager he took third place in a religious art competition at school in 2013. And during his studies at a vocational school for automotive engineering, he won a competition together with two other classmates, according to Interia. His sister was three years younger than him and was an artist. According to Wirtualna Polska, Michal O. had two firearms registered in his name. He also trained at a shooting club, where his 53-year-old father Janusz was also active. According to the newspaper, the eleven firearms and the car from which the attack was carried out were registered in the father's name. The police investigation into the perpetrator's motive is still in full swing. The outlet Onet says it is likely that the public prosecutor will open a terrorism investigation today. A spokesperson says it will not be possible to question the perpetrator in the coming hours or days, given his condition. Investigators are still working at the scene of the attack. The area remains cordoned off. The city has a period of mourning until and including Wednesday, the mayor announced yesterday. Correction from the editors In an earlier version of the reconstruction video, an incorrect starting point of the attacker's route was marked. The route is now shown correctly.

title: Parachutists die after mid-air collision in California
lead: Two parachutists have died in a mid-air collision in the United States. During the jump their parachutes became entangled, after which both fell to the ground. The victims are women aged 56 and 29. The accident happened on Friday near Los Angeles. According to the company that organised the jump, the jump initially went without problems and both parachutes opened. About 45 metres above the ground things went wrong. The two collided while preparing to land. Because of the collision their parachutes became entangled. Both parachutists sustained serious injuries when they landed and died in hospital. The authorities are investigating the cause of the accident. According to American media, both victims were very experienced parachutists. The 56-year-old woman had been jumping since 2015 and had made more than 1700 jumps. The other was head instructor at a company offering indoor skydiving.

title: Over twenty injured in earthquake in central Japan
lead: An earthquake in central Japan has injured at least 24 people, local media report. Footage shows people fleeing buildings and shop windows having shattered. There is also footage of a bookshop where stacks of books fall from the shelves. Some people were injured when they fell down stairs while trying to flee. In Shizuoka, a woman in her nineties broke her shoulder when she fell out of bed during the earthquake. Local media report the earthquake was felt as far as Osaka, in the west of the country. There, someone had to go to hospital after falling from the second floor of an apartment. Footage of the tremor: According to the Japanese Meteorological Institute, the earthquake had a magnitude of 5.7, although the American meteorological institute reports a magnitude of 5.5. Aftershocks were also recorded. Elsewhere in the country there were also tremors, for example in the Kumamoto region. The quake mainly struck places near Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures. Nearby lie, among others, the coastal cities of Chita and Hamamatsu, the former capitals Kyoto and Nara, and neighbouring Yamanashi prefecture, where Mount Fuji is located. The earthquake disrupted train traffic in some places. Delays and disruptions mainly affect regional routes, but some high-speed trains are also experiencing hindrance. The Japanese meteorological institute had already warned people earlier this week of possible severe earthquakes in these days. "Be aware of mudslides, falling rocks and the possible consequences of rainfall," an official of the institute said. In July a severe earthquake struck the southern Japanese island of Kyushu, killing dozens. Many buildings were destroyed and houses and office buildings suffered major damage. Parts of bridges and factories collapsed. Many thousands of people could not yet return home in the days after the earthquake, and tens of thousands of households were without electricity or water.

title: Migrant boat that drifted for hours off the Belgian coast has sailed to France
lead: A boat carrying around thirty migrants that drifted for hours off the coast of the Belgian town of Nieuwpoort is now in French waters, Belgian media report. Belgian police received a report at around 05.30 of a boat in distress on the North Sea, near the coast. The occupants reportedly called the emergency services themselves, according to VRT. Only men are on board. They refused to leave the boat and to follow instructions, HLN reports. Poor visibility After the report, various means were deployed to trace the boat. A helicopter was among those sent up, a spokesperson for the local police said. Rescue and police boats were also deployed. "Due to poor visibility at sea it was not easy to find the boat," a police spokesperson told VRT. "But shortly before 08.00 the helicopter located it more than three kilometres off the coast of Nieuwpoort." The boat drifted for hours off the coast. "It is not taking on water, but it has clearly lost its way," a spokesperson said of it. At 14.45 the boat crossed the French border. The French authorities have taken over the rescue operation from Belgium. Boat off Zeeland A rubber boat carrying 38 people was pulled from the sea off the Zeeland town of Breskens just over a week ago. That boat had presumably set out from Dutch territory. The occupants were 36 Afghans and two suspected people smugglers from Sudan. The latter have been arrested. Six of the occupants were minors. It is not yet clear what the boat's intended destination was. Below are images of the boat at sea off the Dutch coast eight days ago:

title: Ten years after the Hirak protests in Morocco: the streets are quiet, the discontent remains
lead: The call for hospitals, a university, but above all dignity rang loudly through the streets of Al Hoceima ten years ago. For months thousands of people took to the streets to end the neglect of their region, in the Rif area in northern Morocco. The protest movement, known as the Hirak, grew into one of the largest popular movements in the country in years. In spring 2017 the protests were brought to an end with an iron fist. The main protesters, including Hirak leader Nasser Zefzafi, disappeared into prison. A decade later it turns out that the demands of the Hirak movement are still very much alive. When the Gen Z movement took to the streets last year, the call for more good hospitals and schools rang out too. But the government's approach to these protests also turned out not to have changed: repression followed. The death of Mohsin Fikri. The central square in the city of Al Hoceima, named after the current king Mohammed VI, is the place where the Hirak movement began. Where the square now lies deserted because the tourist season is over, in late October 2016 it was packed with furious Riffians. The death of fish seller Mohsin Fikri was the direct trigger. He died in the press of a garbage truck when he tried to prevent the authorities from destroying his confiscated consignment of 500 kilos of swordfish. His death led to a wave of anger and outrage. Lina, now 24, clearly remembers that the day after Fikri's death she joined the protest on Mohammed VI Square with her classmates. "The day after Mohsin Fikri died we just went to school. Our teacher said: 'What are you doing here? Go outside and demand justice.'" According to Zohra Koubia of the human rights organisation AMDH, Fikri is still regarded as a martyr, certainly in the Rif. As long as the authorities do not account for his death, the pain in the Rif will continue, Koubia says. Release of prisoners. She also calls for the release of six prominent Hirak leaders who are still in prison. "Even if they are released tomorrow, their lives have been completely destroyed," says the activist. The best known of these prisoners is Nasser Zefzafi. He is serving a twenty-year prison sentence. Activist Mohamed Jelloul is another Hirak leader in detention. For his 75-year-old mother Rhimou Saidi the protests are still an open wound. Jelloul had just been released after a five-year prison sentence for activist practices. Barely six months later he was again convicted for his role in the Hirak movement, this time to ten years. "My son Mohamed is a real man," says his mother. "He was no good-for-nothing. He wanted his country to be free. That we would have better facilities here. That we would be just like Europe." Hogra. Because the Hirak prisoners have regularly been transferred in recent years to prisons spread across the country, Jelloul's mother, together with the parents of the other prisoners, has made many exhausting trips from Al Hoceima to visit her son. Given all the hardship, Saidi sums up the situation as 'hogra'. This is the word used for repression and humiliation by the state. "I am mainly tormented by hogra, just like the Rif as a whole. But I always say: God is enough for me and He is the best protector." Meagre progress and faster repression. Zohra Koubia of the human rights organisation AMDH is pessimistic about the progress made in Al Hoceima since the Hirak protests. "Young people are leaving here. We did get a hospital. But only the walls and the machines." According to Koubia, a worrying trend can be seen in the government's response to the waves of protest in Morocco over the past fifteen years. "After the protests in 2011 during the Arab Revolution there was still optimism. The demands of the protest movement were quickly met. The Hirak protests lasted seven months, after which repression followed. And with the Gen Z movement the intervention came much faster. They did not even get the chance to catch their breath."

title: At least 200,000 people at Rode Lijn demonstration in Amsterdam, says organisers
lead: In Amsterdam, according to the organisers, at least 200,000 people demonstrated against the Israel policy of the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. The Rode Lijn demonstration went off without major incidents, says the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Many demonstrators wore red clothing and waved red and Palestinian flags. There were also signs and banners with texts such as "Zionism is racism", "No Dutch support for apartheid" and "Free Palestine". Participants demanded that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> take a harder line against Israel because of the violence against Palestinians. "I still think we are not doing well in the Netherlands. This is already the third time I have walked along," said a woman who was marching. "It probably makes little difference, but it is the only thing you can do." The demonstrators marched around the Vondelpark, starting and ending at the Museumplein. There were some incidents, however. AT5 reported that on the Overtoom officers used batons against demonstrators. That happened when police wanted to arrest a man who was standing at a bus shelter and would not leave. Bystanders were also involved in the incident. The man was eventually arrested. Along the Overtoom a group of people stood with banners that included, among other things, "We support Hamas". The organisation had earlier said it could not completely rule out that Hamas supporters would join, but stressed that the demonstration is mainly about people standing up for human rights. Participants in the march also chanted that they would never be for Hamas, NOS reporters heard. Former politicians Job Cohen and Jozias van Aartsen joined the march, as was already reported yesterday. On the Museumplein a large stage hosted speeches. Among others, former minister Lilianne Ploumen, journalist Amal Helles from Gaza and Palestinian activist Omar Barghouti addressed the demonstrators. It was the fourth Rode Lijn demonstration. This time thirteen organisations took part, including Amnesty International, Oxfam Novib and Save the Children. The organisers demanded that the Jetten cabinet exert "maximum political, economic and diplomatic pressure to definitively end the illegal occupation of Palestine". At the previous protest, in October last year, an estimated 250,000 people joined. In May last year <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> was also there, but he is skipping this edition because he is prime minister. He says he is now "in a different role". As D66 leader, Jetten spoke of genocide in Gaza last year. As prime minister he no longer uses that term. Asked why he does not, he says the cabinet has a duty to do everything to prevent further escalation.

title: Convicted son of Norwegian queen attacked in his own home, police start investigation
lead: Marius Borg Høiby, the son of Norwegian Queen Mette-Marit, was attacked in his home by an unknown man. The incident took place on Friday evening, just before midnight. A man in his thirties entered the Skaugum royal estate of the Norwegian royals. He pounded on the door of 29-year-old Hoiby's home, who opened it. The man then tried to force his way in, but Høiby managed to push him outside. Police were then able to overpower the man. Suspected of assault and trespassing. Norwegian media report that the intruder has psychological problems. Police announced today that they will investigate the case. The man is suspected of assault and trespassing, Norwegian media report. In response to a question from Norwegian newspaper VG as to why police had not immediately started a case, a police spokesperson said that "new information has come to light today". Ankle tag after conviction. Elsewhere on the estate King Haakon and Queen Mette-Marit also live. As far as is known, they have not been endangered. Høiby is Mette-Marit's son from an earlier relationship. He has no official role within the Norwegian royal family. Hoiby has been staying at Skaugum since July wearing an ankle tag. This summer he was sentenced to four years in prison for two rapes and domestic violence against an ex-girlfriend. He has appealed. That case begins in February.

title: Building of Saudi state oil company in heart of Riyadh damaged in missile attack
lead: In Saudi Arabia, a building of state oil company Aramco was damaged by falling debris after a foiled attack. Footage shows windows blown out on several floors. The facade was also damaged. The building is one of the tallest in the financial district of the Saudi capital Riyadh. According to the Ministry of Energy, the damage remained limited. Earlier, the Saudis reported that they had intercepted two missiles fired from Yemen at Riyadh by the Houthis. The Aramco building may have been damaged by debris from the two projectiles. Several loud explosions were also heard in the city. In addition, cruise missiles were intercepted and destroyed in the south of Saudi Arabia. A civil war has raged in Yemen since 2014 between the Houthis, who are supported by Iran, and the Yemeni government army, which is supported by Saudi Arabia. In 2022, a ceasefire was agreed after mediation by the United Nations. That largely ended the fighting between the two parties. Since July this year, the Houthis have resumed their attacks on Saudi targets. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition is carrying out airstrikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. According to the Houthi-led Ministry of Public Health, at least 33 people died in a Saudi attack yesterday. That happened near the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The Saudis say they are investigating the attacks.

title: Staff of Israeli settlement day-care centre charged with serious abuse
lead: Three staff members of a day-care centre in Israel have been charged with abuse and violence against at least seventeen babies and toddlers. The youngest were only six months old. In total, more than four hundred incidents are involved. The day-care centre is located in Ariel, a settlement in the occupied West Bank. According to the prosecutor, the children were, among other things, strangled and tied up by the three female suspects, including the director. Choking They allegedly shook the children and locked them in dark rooms. They also allegedly made sure the children could no longer breathe by stuffing paper or cloths into their mouths. This continued until the children turned completely red and nearly choked. Several children became disoriented and lost their balance as a result. The Israeli news outlet Ynet reports that the abuse came to light after a mother discovered injuries on her child. The suspects appeared in court today. Footage from the courtroom shows parents confronting the three suspects while security personnel lead the women away. Israel has in recent years had more frequent incidents of abuse at day-care centres. For example, last month three women were arrested for throwing children onto the ground and throwing objects at children.

title: Cape Town argues over plan to lock up 'problem baboons'
lead: While the wolf is the topic of debate in the Netherlands, in South Africa it is the baboon. After years of attempts to let humans and baboons live together peacefully, the city of Cape Town wants to catch more than sixty baboons and house them in a fenced area. The plan is leading to protests. It is Bin Day in Simon's Town, at the southern tip of the Cape Peninsula. A baboon tips over a grey rubbish bin and rummages through the waste. It finds half a croissant and a carton of sour milk. Within seconds, the contents of the bin are scattered across the street. The baboons know exactly when to strike: on the day household waste is collected, food lies there for the taking. Some animals have even learned to open doors and windows to steal food from kitchens. The South African Adam Welz, who lives in another coastal town on the peninsula, has experienced this several times. He shows a video of a baboon eating a jar of peanut butter off his kitchen counter. "It looks funny, but he has sharp teeth, bigger than those of a lion. I worry about my young children and my dogs." As the residential areas keep growing further into the mountains, the baboons' living area is shrinking. The animals are therefore increasingly moving into built-up areas in search of calorie-rich food. Encounters between humans and baboons are thus becoming an increasingly frequent source of conflict. Around six hundred baboons live on the Cape Peninsula. The city is trying to drive the baboons back into the mountains with the help of baboon monitors. Armed with paintball guns, the monitors constantly chase the animals. But the baboons are fast and things regularly go wrong. Two troops of more than sixty animals each cause the city a great deal of nuisance. The city and wildlife management agencies therefore want to catch the animals and house them in a fenced area on the Cape Peninsula. The fences have already been put up. The site is roughly the size of seven football fields. There are also wooden platforms where the baboons can rest. "It is not ideal," says Gregg Oelofse, coastal and nature manager at the City of Cape Town. "But we have two choices: euthanise these baboons or lock them up. And we think we can give them a good life." Because a good life is what they do not have now, says Oelofse. "When baboons die, we take X-rays. Almost all of them have pellets in their bodies, because frustrated residents shoot at them. All that rubbish full of calories and sugar they eat is also bad for their health." The proposal, however, is meeting strong opposition. Where Oelofse sees a facility where the baboons can spend their old age in peace, opponents see a death camp. Residents who oppose the plan demonstrate at the fences every weekend. "They are taking them there to die out," says demonstrator Lucinda Bovill. "They are sterilising them so the group eventually disappears. Yet this is their natural habitat. They were here first. We have to adapt and take our responsibility. That way we can secure our bins better." The demonstrators fear that the holding site will set a precedent. "If the first relocations prove successful, the city could lock up more baboons in the future," says demonstrator Lauren Wild, who is standing with a plush baboon toy. "In the end I am afraid that not a single baboon will be left." The City of Cape Town disputes this and says the hundreds of other baboons can simply stay where they are. Adam Welz, who found the baboons in his kitchen, also prefers a different solution. Through his own small nature conservation organisation, the South Peninsula Nature Alliance, he does not argue for fences around the baboons, but for a fence between the residential areas and the mountains. "That way the baboons keep their natural habitat and we have peace in our homes." But according to Oelofse of the City of Cape Town, a hard reset is simply needed. "It is an illusion to think these troops of baboons lead a beautiful and wild life in nature. Locking them up is the only option. I am not happy about that either." The city is still waiting for the final permits for the capture operation but wants to catch the first baboons as soon as possible.

title: Dutch woman (81) dies after accident in which camper van tipped over on motorway in Belgium
lead: In an accident involving a camper van on the E313 motorway in Belgium, an 81-year-old Dutch woman has died. Belgian media report that the vehicle she was in landed on its side in the accident. It is still unclear how the fatal accident happened. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating. The 81-year-old woman was the only occupant of the vehicle. The accident happened at around 10.30 a.m. east of Antwerp. Emergency services have set the camper van upright again. Cars driving on the motorway where the accident happened had to turn around. The E313 was then partly closed for a number of hours. It has since reopened.

title: Seven dead and over a hundred injured in train collision in Egypt
lead: At least seven people have been killed and 112 injured in a train accident in Egypt, the country's authorities report. The accident happened near Al Ayyat in the Giza governorate, about 50 kilometres south of the capital Cairo. Among those who died was the driver of one of the trains, the transport ministry reports. According to the ministry, a train heading towards Fayoum collided with the rear of a train that was travelling from Cairo to Aswan. Several carriages then derailed. These images clearly show the wreckage of the accident: 72 ambulances have been deployed to take 88 injured people to hospitals for treatment. The Red Cross is also present to help victims. Images show carriages lying alongside the track, with people around them. It is unclear whether these are passengers from the trains. President Sisi announces investigation President Sisi says he is closely following developments surrounding the train accident and has instructed the authorities to investigate the incident. "Anyone proven to have been negligent will be held accountable", he writes on X . He also says he sympathises with the families of the victims. "I extend my sincere condolences to the families of the deceased and my sincere wishes for recovery to the injured", Sisi said. Last August, at least three people died and nearly 100 were injured when seven wagons of a train derailed. That also happened near the capital Cairo. The country has an outdated railway network, and poor maintenance of it leads to dangerous situations.

title: Woman hides from police in a wheelie bin, but is arrested anyway
lead: In Kwintsheul, South Holland, a woman was arrested after hiding from police in a waste container. Officers were searching for her following a report of vandalism. The police received a report this morning that a woman may have committed vandalism, Omroep West writes. Once on the scene, the officers did not find her. Neighbours had not seen where she had fled to. The woman was also not visible on camera footage. The officers therefore suspected she could not be far away. Strange noise While the officers were speaking with witnesses, they heard a sound coming from a wheelie bin. The officers went to the waste container and lifted the lid. They promptly found the woman they were looking for. She has been arrested. The police do not disclose what she is alleged to have damaged. "After this unusual find we were at least wide awake immediately", the officers write on Instagram.

title: Action group hoists Palestinian flag at Reichstag building, German Unity flag thrown to the ground
lead: For a brief moment the Palestinian flag flew in front of the Reichstag building in Berlin. A 22-year-old man climbed the flagpole this morning, threw the German Flag of Unity, six by ten meters, to the ground and hoisted the Palestinian flag in its place. The police arrested him, as well as a 20-year-old man who was also involved in the action. A 32-year-old man was detained. The incident took place around 11:30 a.m. The 22-year-old man climbed the nearly thirty-meter-high mast secured with a climbing harness. He was helped by the men aged 20 and 32, who remained standing below. Livestream on TikTok That pair filmed the action and broadcast it live on TikTok, a police spokesperson tells the German newspaper Der Tagesspiegel. Emergency services cordoned off the site of the incident, after which the mast climber came down by himself at 12:30 p.m. At around the same time, the Palestinian flag was removed by the emergency services. After the flag action, only the 22-year-old climber remains in custody. The other two have received an area ban. Action claimed The action was claimed by the action group Peacefully against Genocide. "We must not shirk our responsibility to stop crimes against humanity," the group writes on Instagram alongside photos of the action. Last summer, activists from the action group glued themselves to the entrance of the Berlin factory of arms manufacturer Rheinmetall. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg was also there. Other factories were also blocked in protest against arms deliveries to Israel. 'Shows contempt for our democracy' The mayor of Berlin has condemned the action. "Anyone who takes down the flag in front of the Reichstag building and hoists the Palestinian flag shows their contempt for our democracy," Kai Wegner writes on X. He calls the incident "unacceptable, especially on the eve of 9 November." Nearly 37 years ago, on 9 November 1989, the Berlin Wall fell, which put an end to the division of Berlin and of Germany as a whole. 9 November is also the date of Kristallnacht, the major Nazi pogrom of 1938, and it is the day in 1918 when the republic was proclaimed from the balcony of the Reichstag. Less than a year after the fall of the Wall, on 3 October 1990, the GDR, the communist state in eastern Germany, was dissolved and East Germany merged into the Federal Republic of Germany. On the night of 2 to 3 October, the Flag of Unity (Flagge der Einheit) was raised on the square in front of the Reichstag building (Platz der Republik). At the foot of the mast, "Duitse Eenheid 3 oktober 1990" is written on a bronze plaque. At night the flag is lit by four large spotlights. Only in rare cases is the six-by-ten-meter flag flown at half-mast, such as after the attacks of 11 September 2001.

title: Much creativity and difficult political choices needed, says Israeli formateur Eisenkot
lead: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot wants to form a government that restores unity and connection between the different groups in Israeli society. According to him, this requires a lot of creativity and unconventional political choices. Eisenkot spoke after President Herzog formally gave him the mandate to form a new government. According to Eisenkot, the situation in which Israel finds itself is extremely difficult, partly due to the wars in Iran, Lebanon and Gaza. "Fighting continues on several fronts and the war aims have still not been achieved," he said. "At the same time we are in a deep diplomatic crisis. Even our most loyal friends and allies are reconsidering their relationship with Israel." With that last remark he probably refers to the statement by US Vice President Vance, who cited the American relationship with Israel as an important cause of the Republicans' loss in the midterms last week. Domestically, Eisenkot sees trust in democracy and state institutions declining. "That is why we need new leadership, leadership that deserves our trust and puts our well-being and our security first." Open door: Eisenkot says all parties are welcome to join, including the members of parliament from Likud, the party of rival and prime minister Netanyahu. "My door is open." He does demand that they endorse the four conditions for cooperation that he announced earlier. Netanyahu himself has no place in his government, he has already made clear. In the elections at the end of October Likud came out as the largest party, Eisenkot's Yashar came second. Still, President Herzog gave the formation mandate to Eisenkot because a majority in parliament believes he has the best chance of forming a new coalition. Difficult task: Eisenkot faces an extremely difficult task in any case. Two Arab parties could help him to a majority, but other parties needed for that exclude cooperation with those Arab parties. Eisenkot has at most 42 days to form a government. If that does not succeed, the turn may pass to Netanyahu.

title: Defeat for the ANC in South African cities
lead: The ANC, the party that liberated South Africa from apartheid more than thirty years ago, has been heavily punished in local elections. Especially city dwellers have had enough of the poor governance and corruption of the ANC at every level. For a long time the party of the late president Nelson Mandela was the obvious choice for most South Africans. But according to the official result of the local elections, announced at the beginning of the evening on Sunday, the ANC comes out at about 30.8 percent of the votes. That is still quite a lot, and the ANC remains the largest party nationally, but it is 15 percentage points less than in 2021. Six metropolises. The party is taking a beating especially in the cities. In six of the most important metropolises another party has become the largest. In most cases that is the liberal Democratic Alliance (DA). The eyes were especially on Johannesburg, the economic heart of South Africa. There too most votes went to the DA. The city of millions has become the symbol of the failure of the ANC. Because the engine of the South African economy is poorly maintained. Johannesburg is dealing with power outages, rubbish on the streets, neglected buildings, water shortages and high crime. In contrast, Cape Town is often held up, the touristic seaside city with Table Mountain, which has been governed by the DA for twenty years. There, at least in the better neighbourhoods, everything seems to work better. That city remains in the hands of the DA. Helen Zille. In Johannesburg and a host of other cities they now seem to hope to get some of the better governance of Cape Town. A former DA mayor of Cape Town is therefore the mayoral candidate for that party in Johannesburg. The 75-year-old politician Helen Zille ran a striking campaign with the message that she will simply solve Johannesburg's problems. During her campaign she went snorkelling in a flooded pothole in the road, for example, and rowed a small boat through a flooded street in the Soweto township. Footage of those stunts went viral. It is not yet certain whether she will become mayor. The party did become the largest in Johannesburg, but did not get enough votes to take over the reins directly and must therefore form a coalition. White party. It is nevertheless remarkable that the DA has become the largest in Johannesburg, because it is a city where mainly poorer Black South Africans live, who traditionally mostly vote for the ANC. The DA is still seen by many as a white party, which mainly looks after the interests of the middle class and the wealthier. But many South Africans mainly want better governance. Especially in their own neighbourhoods and cities they see that the ANC is not doing enough. They complain about cronyism in the distribution of jobs, corruption and councillors who simply do their work badly. According to research, only 39 of the 257 municipalities in South Africa have clean accounts. Notably, many of those municipalities lie in the Western Cape province, where many municipalities are governed by the DA. Other parties too. Not only the DA grew, but other parties too. In Durban, for example, many people voted for MK, the party with which former president Jacob Zuma split from the ANC in 2023. Already in the national elections of 2024 a shift could be seen. That year the ANC lost the majority for the first time since the country became democratic and now governs in a unity government with, among others, the DA. And now cooperation with other parties must also take place at the municipal level. Political analysts think that the ANC realises that it must account more for its policy and that it understands it must actually deliver results. Already before the weekend ANC chairperson Fikile Mbalula called that a lesson for his party. President Cyril Ramaphosa said this evening that having a choice is healthy for a democracy. He called for good cooperation between the parties, in the interest of the voters.

title: Square in Krakow reopened after attack, victims commemorated with flowers and candles
lead: The square in the Polish city of Krakow where six people were shot dead yesterday has been reopened. The police have completed the investigation on site, so the central square in the historic centre is accessible to the public again. The square had been closed since yesterday afternoon after a man opened fire from a moving car. Four women and two men lost their lives in the attack and fifteen people were injured, including several coachmen, two police officers and a number of foreigners. The foreign victims come from the United Kingdom, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria. The suspected shooter Michal O. was seriously wounded in a shootout with the police and is in life-threatening condition. Far-right ideologies The masked 24-year-old O. wore camouflage clothing and a bulletproof vest during the shooting. He fired with a semi-automatic weapon capable of firing a hundred shots per minute, an AR-15. Also found in his car were a handgun and other weapons and ammunition. Not much is yet clear about his motive, but according to Polish minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, Michal O. was presumably inspired by far-right ideologies and is an "ultranationalist". The Polish Public Prosecution Service has started an investigation into a "crime with a terrorist character". Michal O. came from Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town about 140 kilometres northeast of Krakow. Neighbours describe him as "a boy, just a boy" and "a normal, cheerful and happy boy". In his early teenage years he reportedly won prizes in art and automotive technology. The family home was searched by the police yesterday evening. There the police found two dead women and a man: the father, the mother and the sister of the suspect. They are presumed to have been shot dead. Polish media report that both the suspected perpetrator and his father held a firearms licence. The weapons found in the car after the attack are registered in the name of father Janusz. The Public Prosecution Service has seized data carriers such as mobile phones and computers, as well as notes from the home. Seven more firearms were also found in the home. 9 ton for police In St Anne's Church, close to the central square of Krakow, people have gathered to commemorate the victims. The mayor of the city was also present there. Flowers are being laid and candles lit on the square itself. The officers who intervened after the shooting and overpowered O. are being praised in Poland for their heroism. One of them was seriously injured, was taken to hospital and had to undergo surgery. A fundraising campaign has been started for the "true heroes", as Polish prime minister Tusk called them yesterday. Thousands of donors have already contributed almost one million euros to the campaign.

title: Police make large-scale response in Copenhagen over costumed Comic Con visitors
lead: In the Danish capital Copenhagen, costumed Comic Con visitors have caused panic. Police responded in force after a report of a suspicious situation at the country's largest shopping centre, but it turned out to be a false alarm. Police were called in after two people, dressed in military clothing and carrying weapons, were seen running in the car park of shopping centre Field's, according to Danish public broadcaster DR. Further on, in the Bella Center, a Comic Con event was held this weekend. "We are currently present with a large unit," police wrote at 15:41. Officers were at Field's, on the edge of the city, not far from the airport. Fatal shooting in 2022 In the same shopping centre, in the summer of 2022, a 22-year-old man opened fire. Three people died as a result. In 2015 there was also a shooting incident. No one died then, but three people were injured. Police asked people this afternoon to remain calm and follow instructions. After some time, police announced that the investigation had been concluded and that people in costumes had been the cause of the commotion. "They did not stop to think that their costumes could cause panic among others," police said. Comic Con Comic Con events are held all over the world, attracting many thousands of visitors, often dressed as their favourite superhero, anime character or comic book character. The fairs focus on films, series, games, cosplay, comics and anime. In Copenhagen, among others, Harry Potter actor Matthew Lewis (who played Marcel Lubbermans) and the American actor Giancarlo Esposito, born in Denmark (Breaking Bad, Better Call Saul), attended.

title: Explosions at homes in Schiedam
lead: In Schiedam, explosions occurred shortly after each other at two homes. The first was around 8:15 p.m., Rijnmond reports, the second just after 9:00 p.m. No one was injured. The homes did sustain damage. They are about one kilometre apart. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> told Rijnmond that the explosions are being investigated as separate incidents. The police could or would not say whether they are connected to the fatal shooting in Schiedam yesterday afternoon. Unknown persons opened fire on three men who were working outside a house. One of them, a 19-year-old, was killed. The other two were injured, but not life-threateningly. The police are searching for three unknown men. A description of them has been circulated.

title: Teletext suffers an outage on television: new pages not always displayed
lead: The Teletext pages on television are experiencing an outage. As a result, the latest news on the Teletext pages of NOS Nieuws and NOS Sport has not always been displaying properly since Sunday at 3:00 p.m. Outages also occurred almost the entire previous month, although those did not last as long. On various pages, old data was shown during outages. The outage affects only Teletext on television. The NPO is working hard on a solution, but it is expected not to be resolved before tomorrow morning. For the most current news, Teletext users can go to the app and to the Teletext shown on NOS.nl. Those do display the latest news.

title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO spy affair, top executive admits affair
lead: Chip giant Nvidia is launching an independent investigation into the intimate relationship of top executive Jensen Huang with a woman who, according to American intelligence services, was recruited by the Chinese secret service for espionage. The company says so in a press release following reports by The New York Times and the British newspaper Financial Times (FT ). This week the newspapers reported that the woman, who is a manager at Megaspeed, a Singaporean customer of the American Nvidia, tried to obtain chip secrets from the Nvidia top executive on behalf of the Chinese secret services. She had reportedly been under the watch of American intelligence services for a year already. The board of directors says in the statement that there is no reason to assume that national security or the company's secrets have been compromised. Spy for China That the woman, named Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, may have been a Chinese spy was shared in a memo with a small group of American officials. This happened just before President Trump traveled to Beijing in May to meet with Chinese leader Xi . Megaspeed is one of Nvidia's largest customers in Southeast Asia. The company bought more than 4.8 billion dollars' worth of chips over the past two years, The New York Times writes . Last year, the US accused Megaspeed of smuggling advanced Nvidia chips to China. An employee of the American Department of Commerce found boxes with Nvidia equipment in a Megaspeed data center in Malaysia. That the items were still packed would suggest they were not being used in that data center, but were to be shipped to China, in violation of American export rules. According to Nvidia there was no evidence of irregularities, but the American Department of Justice is still investigating the case. Trump On top of that, Jensen Huang this year tried to persuade Trump to export advanced chips to China. The US does not want that because it could lead to the Chinese military modernizing faster and developing AI models. To prevent this, the US has imposed export restrictions. Earlier, Nvidia said there was nothing unusual about the relationship. According to the company, its CEO meets thousands of customers every year, and therefore a meeting with the woman would also be unremarkable. Images of the two on various occasions are circulating on social media. For example, they can be seen drinking whisky together and in a restaurant in the Taiwanese capital Taipei. The CEO of the chip giant has acknowledged in a message to the board of directors that he cheated on his wife. He says he takes full responsibility for it. According to a spokesperson, Huang remains in charge of the company and will cooperate with the investigation. "I remain fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn your trust back," the CEO said. With a market value of nearly 5 trillion dollars, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. The chips the company makes are needed for developments in the field of AI.

title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal coast: at least 34 dead
lead: A boat carrying migrants bound for Europe sank off the coast of Senegal. At least 34 people died, the Senegalese news agency APS reports. The boat sank off Kébémer, in northwestern Senegal. According to the Senegalese ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, it was a so-called pirogue, a traditional boat that is also used for fishing. It is still unclear how many people were on board. One survivor has been found. A search for possible missing persons is ongoing. The small boat was sailing the Atlantic route from West Africa to Europe, one of the deadliest migration routes in the world. Thousands of people died on that route in recent years. State of emergency: Yesterday a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro. Since early November, more than 3,300 migrants have arrived there on dozens of boats. As a result, public services on the island have come under pressure. The Spanish minister of Interior visited Senegal this week and called on the country to do more to stop the dangerous crossings.

title: Frans Weekers wants to change VVD course and runs for the Senate
lead: Former state secretary Frans Weekers (VVD) wants to be the VVD lead candidate for the Senate. With his candidacy he is going against the party leadership, which has put former minister Adriaansens forward as lead candidate. Weekers said on the programme Pauw, De Wit en Moggré that Halbe Zijlstra and Johan Remkes, among others, support his candidacy. The former state secretary said he wants to help the party board, but also that he wants to "bring the VVD back to the right course". Weekers wants, among other things, that "no party is excluded" from cooperation. Weekers criticised that during the election campaign the VVD ruled out parties, including Pro, in advance. With his remarks he voices part of the VVD base: mainly the more administratively minded VVD members do not support excluding Pro. According to Weekers, things are not going well for the VVD and many members are leaving. "Some think the VVD is sitting on D66's luggage rack, others think it is PVV-light." That needs to change, Weekers believes. He says he wants to help party leader Yesilgöz make the VVD more liberal again. Concerns about governability of the country: the remarks of Weekers come on the eve of a tense week awaiting the minority cabinet, which still has not found a majority for the tax plan. Weekers says he is very concerned about the governability of the country. This is partly because the coalition is divided internally over which opposition parties it should seek support from. D66 and CDA favour cooperation on the left, while the VVD wants to go to the right. Member of parliament and state secretary Weekers was a member of the Tweede Kamer from 2003 to 2010, and in the Rutte I and II cabinets he was <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity>. If Weekers pursues his candidacy, party members must decide who becomes lead candidate. They can vote digitally between 9 and 15 December. The lead candidate will be announced on 16 December. . Incidentally, Weekers has not called party leader Yesilgöz to inform her of his plans.

title: Trump calls announcement of UFC boss Dana White as White House press secretary a 'joke'
lead: US President Trump announced combat sports boss Dana White as the new White House press secretary on Saturday. This caused a stir, but now Trump is dismissing his announcement as "a joke". On his social media platform Truth Social, Trump wrote on Saturday that he had offered White the role of White House press secretary, with a number of well-known combat sports fighters as his assistants. Trump described White as a "violent fighter and warrior". He said he needs White and his team "to defend us against the left, the deranged extremists". Trump also wrote that White "would become a spokesperson like no other". Trump: 'It was just a joke' The striking announcement came a few days after the midterm elections, which were disastrous for the Republicans. The Democrats won the majority in both <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> and the House of Representatives. As a result, Trump faces a Congress dominated by his political opponents for the next two years. Speaking to journalists on Sunday evening US time, the president dismissed his announcement as a joke. "I can tell you that I was just joking," he said, adding that White himself thought it was "a great idea". "He is a very capable man," said Trump. It is not yet known who will become the new White House press secretary. Combat sports boss and confidant White (57) has been head of the UFC, the largest mixed martial arts (MMA) organisation in the world, for more than twenty years. He is also a close friend and confidant of Trump. White was involved in Trump's 2024 election campaign, for example, and stood on the stage when Trump was re-elected. The close ties between the two became clear in June of this year, when the White House became the setting for a UFC cage fight for the 250th anniversary of the US. MMA fighters then walked into the White House in shorts. The combat sports boss already said on Saturday evening that he would fly to Washington for a meeting with Trump. The US president confirmed that he will receive White tomorrow, but stressed that the conversation will be about "other matters". No press secretary The position of press secretary, one of the president's most important spokespersons, has been vacant since 16 October. Katie Zacharia then left after only five days as White House press secretary. Zacharia's first press conference went particularly poorly. There was also discussion about her past. Zacharia had repeatedly presented herself on social media as a lawyer, while she had not passed the required bar exam. The 41-year-old Zacharia was the successor to Karoline Leavitt (28). Leavitt stepped down in the summer because she wanted to spend more time with her family. She had a communication style similar to Trump's and did not shy away from confrontation with journalists. She was regarded as one of Trump's confidants. Chief of staff replaced After the midterms, which were dramatic for the Republicans, Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles on Friday with hardliner Stephen Miller. The chief of staff is regarded as a pivotal figure in the White House, someone who smooths over political differences by correcting or placating party colleagues and rivals.

title: Yellow warning in parts of Drenthe, Groningen and Overijssel due to dense fog
lead: The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> has issued a yellow warning from 02.00 tonight until 10.00 tomorrow morning for parts of the northeast of the Netherlands due to dense fog. The warning is in effect in parts of Drenthe, Groningen and Overijssel. In the second half of the morning the (dense) fog will gradually lift, according to the KNMI. The fog may arise suddenly tonight and this morning. In case of local fog, visibility is less than 200 metres. The KNMI advises road users, among other things, to drive more slowly, keep greater distances from other road users, and switch on their fog lights at the front (when visibility is less than 200 metres) and at the rear (when visibility is less than 50 metres). Road users must also take into account delays and dangerous situations on the road. First regional code Since this month, weather codes are no longer issued for entire provinces, but warnings are given more targeted. For example, when it was slippery in the south of Limburg, the KNMI issued a weather warning for the whole province. Now such a warning is given locally. On Saturday a regional warning was issued for the first time.

title: Nearly 400,000 Russian deaths in war with Ukraine, hacked data shows
lead: Nearly 400,000 Russians have died as a result of the war since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. That is what hacked data from the Russian statistics bureau Rosstat shows, which news agency Bloomberg has viewed and analysed. The Belarusian hacker group Cyberpartisans and the Ukrainian hacker organisation Silent Crow obtained the data from Rosstat, the Russian counterpart of the Dutch <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS). It is said to involve a dataset of more than 11 million Russian death records, including information on age, place of residence and place of death. Nearly 400,000 Russians dead. The data show that between February 2022 and late August 2026, 392,700 death records contain an explicit reference to the war with Ukraine. This happens through codes or descriptions such as "military operation", "bombing" or "drones". According to Bloomberg, the actual death toll is "almost certainly" higher. Some soldiers are missing, bodies have not been identified, and others may have died later from wounds without this being registered as war-related. Hacker group Silent Crow estimates the number of dead at around 450,000. Bloomberg could not definitively prove the database is authentic, but found no evidence of forgery during its investigation. The data largely matched previously published official Russian mortality figures. Hack. The hackers reported on 1 November that they had hacked Rosstat's systems. A few days later the statistics bureau confirmed that it had been the target of targeted cyberattacks, although Rosstat denied that confidential data had been stolen. Russia does not disclose the number of soldiers killed in the war with Ukraine. No official figures have been published on this since the first months after the invasion in February 2022. Rosstat has also increasingly stopped publishing mortality statistics since then.

title: Teen who made plans for a terrorist attack in Australia will not go to prison
lead: A 16-year-old boy who made plans for a terrorist attack in Sydney does not have to go to prison, reports Australian public broadcaster ABC . The boy was arrested more than two years ago at the age of 14 in Sydney, after he had searched online for how to make a bomb with a pressure cooker. He also tried to make contact with one of the perpetrators of the attack on the Boston Marathon in 2013 . The boy examined several potential targets, including the finish line of the Sydney Marathon at the Sydney Opera House. According to the judge, however, his preparations were not very concrete. For example, the teen had not gathered materials to make a bomb and had not chosen a date for an attack. Extremist videos on TikTok The boy said he had come into contact with extremist videos via TikTok. He said he found that "interesting". Then he watched increasingly violent material from, among others, terrorist groups Al Qaida and Islamic State (IS). The judge assessed that behavior as "a great degree of naivety". Since his arrest, the boy has, according to the judge, distanced himself from Islamic extremism and convincingly shown remorse. Also taken into account was that the boy repeatedly evaded or brushed off questions from people he chatted with who asked him whether he would carry out an attack. The judge considers his chances of successfully returning to society high. The boy's identity has not been disclosed.

title: Pianist falls off cruise ship and is rescued after floating for 9 hours in the Pacific Ocean
lead: A pianist from a cruise ship has been rescued in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, nearly 30 kilometers off the Californian coast. He was presumably floating for about nine hours after he was knocked overboard during the night. It is not yet clear how the man fell from the fourteen-deck cruise ship. The 37-year-old man was rescued by two fishermen from Newport Beach, who were on their way back from a fishing trip. According to the US Coast Guard, the man was then taken to hospital. He is expected to survive the incident. The fishermen saw the man in the water and pulled him on board. Once he had recovered, he said that he was the pianist on the cruise ship Ovation of the Seas of Royal Caribbean, which was on its way from Long Beach to Ensenada in Mexico. "The only thing he said to me was: 'Thank you. I thought I was going to die'", said Sean Norton, one of the fishermen, to CBS News . El Niño According to Norton, the relatively high temperature of the ocean played a part. He points to the weather phenomenon El Niño for this. "The water was 24 degrees. In another year he would never have survived." A spokesperson for cruise company Royal Caribbean confirmed the incident to CBS News. "We are offering our crew member support and help during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we cannot share any further details." Earlier, Nieuwsuur made this item about the strongest El Niño ever measured:

title: Extra breakdowns on top of breakdowns today: roadside assistance strikes
lead: Motorists who break down on the road today will have to be patient. ANWB employees - including roadside assistance - are laying down their work for 12 hours, from 09.00 in the morning until 21.00 in the evening. The trade unions are taking action because negotiations on a new collective labour agreement have stalled. Among other things, they consider the workload at the ANWB too high and see problems with the rosters. The unions must, by court order, ensure minimum staffing. As a result, emergencies, such as a stalled car in a tunnel, can still be resolved.

title: Wake-up call 9/11: Roadside assistance strikes • UN climate summit kicks off
lead: Good morning! Today ANWB employees are laying down their work and the National Crystal Commemoration takes place in the Portuguese Synagogue in Amsterdam. First the weather: this morning it is foggy in some places. As the day goes on it becomes increasingly sunny. It will be 9 to 11 degrees and there is little wind. Are you going out today? Here you can find an overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? Since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, nearly 400,000 Russians have died in the war. This is according to hacked data from the Russian statistics bureau Rosstat, which was viewed and examined by news agency Bloomberg . Bloomberg could not definitively prove the authenticity of the database, but found no indications of falsification in its research. According to Bloomberg, the true death toll is "almost certainly" higher. Some soldiers are missing, bodies have not been identified, and others may have died later of injuries without this being recorded as war-related. The number of dead is estimated at around 450,000. Russia does not disclose the number of soldiers killed in the war with Ukraine. Other news from the night: And then also this: Central Japan was struck yesterday by an earthquake of magnitude 5.7. At least 24 people were injured. There was also material damage, such as shattered shop windows among other things. The moment of the quake was captured by several cameras: Have a nice day!

title: Krakow shooter dies in hospital
lead: The attacker who shot six people dead in the Polish city of Krakow on Saturday has died in hospital. Polish police reported this on X. "We want to inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died in hospital early this morning," the police wrote in the statement. The perpetrator is 24-year-old Michal O , Polish media reported. He was shot by officers after opening fire on passers-by from a car.

title: Cabinet designates five more locations where homes must be built faster
lead: The cabinet designates five more locations where homes must be built faster. These concern locations in Assen, Best, <entity id="org:gemeente-roosendaal">Roosendaal</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-zuidplas">Zuidplas</entity> and the area around Middelburg and <entity id="org:gemeente-vlissingen">Vlissingen</entity>. In total, around 25,000 homes must be ready by 2040, sooner than planned. The municipalities have had plans to build homes here ready for some time. But bringing those plans to a successful conclusion often proves difficult in practice. This is partly due to time-consuming objection procedures by local residents and the nitrogen problem. The cabinet therefore already designated several locations where the national government will help municipalities, for example with those permit applications. There are now 31 of them, across all provinces. In total, it concerns just over 400,000 homes that must be built faster than planned. Which locations have now been precisely designated? In Assen, around 5,000 to 6,000 homes will be built in Kloosterveen, Stadskwartier and Zuidoost. In Best, it concerns 3,500 homes, mainly around the station. On the Zeeland island of Walcheren, around 5,000 homes will be built in and around Middelburg, Vlissingen and Veere. In Roosendaal, 5,000 to 6,000 homes will be built in the railway zone. In Cortelande in the South Holland Zuidplas, an entirely new village with around 6,000 homes will be created. That village is controversial, because it lies at the lowest point in the Netherlands. Extra money for infrastructure will not be provided at these five locations. According to <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan</entity>, this is also not necessary, because these places are already well accessible. On part of the sites where the homes are to be built, businesses are currently located. These may therefore need to relocate. Boekholt-O'Sullivan wants to make "careful agreements" about this, she writes in a letter to Parliament.

title: Polder talks about a new social accord, but why exactly?
lead: It is time for a new 'social accord', which is why talks on this are starting in 'the polder'. Among others, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and ministers Vijlbrief of Social Affairs are meeting with trade unions and employers today. But what exactly is a social accord, who decides on it, and why are they negotiating precisely now? That there will be talks about a social accord is quite remarkable: so far, six such national accords have been concluded. The first was in the early 1970s, and the latest accord dates back to 2013, although one could also argue that the 2019 pension accord falls under it. A social accord (sometimes also called a central accord) is an agreement between employees, employers and the government. These parties, who together are called 'the polder', make agreements on, for example, wage developments, benefits and working conditions. These frameworks must still be translated into legislation and, for example, sector collective labour agreements (cao's). Cabinet collapse. So a direction is agreed on in which the country is to move. And because so many stakeholders are involved, the agreements have broad support, is the idea. As a result, the plans hold up, even if, for example, a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> falls. A social accord has broad support because many parties sit at the table. On behalf of the employers, the employers' organisation VNO-NCW, the entrepreneurs' association MKB-Nederland and the agricultural organisation LTO are taking part. Together, they represent, by their own account, around 500,000 businesses. On behalf of the employees, the trade unions FNV, CNV and VCP are participating. Taken together, they have more than a million members. What makes the support a bit broader is that a number of political parties have long felt connected to one of the negotiating partners. For example, Pro has close ties with the FNV, CDA feels connected to the trade union CNV and the farmers' organisation LTO, and VVD has a lot in common with the business clubs VNO-NCW and MKB-Nederland. A social accord is not concluded at fixed moments. Trade unions, employers and the cabinet decide at some point, when things are brewing, that it is time for new agreements. In 1982, for example, the 'Wassenaar Accord' was concluded. The core then was that, under pressure from rising unemployment, wage increases were limited. Employees received in return that they would not have to work as much. The agenda of this accord This time, incapacity for work is an important theme, especially the WIA. WIA stands for Work and Income according to Labour Capacity Act and regulates a benefit for people who cannot work because they are ill.
