Bertulazzi took off his ankle monitor, tampered with it so that the authorities would not become suspicious, and went to the balcony on the fifth floor of the apartment in central Buenos Aires. He then lowered himself down on a rope with a climbing harness and climbed over a metal fence, writes the Argentine newspaper La Nación. Images from a surveillance camera show how he falls onto the pavement and lies still for a moment. 'Interpol was already ready' Since then, every trace of the man, who was arrested in Argentina in August 2024, has been missing. A few hours before the escape, his last appeal to stop his extradition was rejected, writes the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera. "Interpol was already ready to arrest him and bring him to Italy," the newspaper says. Argentine media speak of a cinematic escape. The Italian, who was sentenced in absentia, wore an ankle monitor but managed to remove it without arousing suspicion. He managed to fool the device so that the ankle monitor could still measure a body temperature. Only when it was noticed that the ankle monitor registered no movement at all was a check carried out. Officers did find an ankle monitor in the apartment, but the septuagenarian was nowhere to be seen. Red Brigades The 74-year-old Bertulazzi was a member of the Red Brigades, an Italian Marxist terrorist group that was active in the 1970s and 1980s and was behind several kidnappings and assassination attempts on prominent figures. The best-known example is the kidnapping and murder of former Italian prime minister Aldo Moro in 1978. Moro was abducted while he was on his way to parliament by car. Several of his bodyguards were killed by the Red Brigades. The prime minister was held for well over fifty days in an apartment and was then killed. His body was found in the trunk of a Renault parked in central Rome. A year earlier, in 1977, the Genoa branch of the Red Brigades kidnapped marine engineer Pietro Costa, who came from a wealthy family. Costa was released after months, once well over 1.6 million lire in ransom had been paid. The money was used for the apartment where Prime Minister Moro was held a year later. Status withdrawn Bertulazzi was sentenced in absentia in 1977 to a prison sentence of 27 years for involvement in the kidnapping of Costra and participation in a criminal organisation. The Italian arrived in Argentina at the beginning of this century. In 2004 he was granted refugee status, which meant he could not be extradited to Italy. In 2024 this changed, not long after Javier Milei, who is known for his tough migration policy, took office as president. Bertulazzi's refugee status was withdrawn and he was arrested . The Argentine government is offering a reward of about 12,000 euros for the tip that leads to the arrest of the fugitive septuagenarian.

title: Man sentenced to twelve years in prison and TBS for killing ex-wife with knife
lead: A 52-year-old man from Lent in Gelderland has been sentenced to twelve years in prison and TBS with compulsory care for manslaughter of his ex-wife. The 45-year-old victim was killed with dozens of stab wounds last October. The woman was attacked in front of her home on the evening of 2 October by suspect Danny C. He stabbed the victim in her chest, stomach and back, among other places. The victim was seriously wounded and died later in hospital. Suspect C. was arrested shortly afterwards. The investigation showed that the victim had ended the relationship with C. a few days before the attack. The man had previously been given a home and contact ban after he was found guilty of abusing the woman and threatening their eldest son, Omroep Gelderland writes. According to the court, the incidents were part of years of tension within the family "which were partly caused by the man's use of alcohol and drugs". The latest incidents were the reason the woman finally decided to end the relationship. No memories At the trial, the man stated that he could not remember anything about the incident. He wanted to talk with the victim that evening, after which things "went black" for him. He also said he was under the influence of alcohol and drugs at the time. According to experts, it is unlikely that the suspect has no memories at all of the stabbing incident. No medical or neurological indications of such total memory loss were found. According to Omroep Gelderland, the judges also openly doubted the suspect's statements, in which he repeatedly said he could not remember anything. No premeditation The court speaks of a "deliberate" and "brutal" act and rules that C. is guilty of manslaughter. According to the judges, this is partly due to witness statements suggesting that the man wanted to talk with the victim that evening. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> wanted C. to be convicted of murder. But the court does not follow this and finds there is too little evidence of premeditation. For example, there are no concrete indications that he planned in advance or that he had decided to kill the woman before the stabbing. The fact that the man was carrying a knife that evening is also insufficient evidence of acting with premeditation, the court states. Disorder The investigation shows that the man has a mild intellectual disability and a personality disorder. C. also struggles with serious addictions. According to the experts, these problems influenced the suspect's behaviour during the stabbing. The court has taken this into account in the sentencing, so the sentence imposed is slightly lower than the fifteen years in prison the OM had demanded. In addition to the prison sentence and TBS, C. must pay the victim's next of kin more than 100,000 euros in damages.

title: Future of minority cabinet hanging by a thread as VVD openly doubts
lead: The mood in the coalition of D66, VVD and CDA has sunk to rock bottom. VVD leader Yesilgöz wants her coalition partners to withdraw the deal they struck with the left-wing opposition. If they do not, Yesilgöz doubts whether she still wants to continue. But D66 and CDA have no intention of doing so. Despite the threatening words of the VVD leader, they are sticking to the agreement on adjusting the tax plan. They said so yesterday evening. "We will not renegotiate." The amendments that D66, CDA, Pro and Volt want to make to the tax plan are "bad for the Netherlands, bad for stability and moreover they go against the coalition agreement", Yesilgöz said earlier in the evening, at the bottom of the steps of her stately <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">ministerie van Defensie</entity>. "We have been ambushed. This is not the way we should work together", she said, visibly angry. That her coalition partners were talking with Pro and Volt was known. "We kept asking how things were going, but we were only informed a quarter of an hour before Klaver's press conference that there was a deal." VVD leader Yesilgöz reacted on the steps of the Ministry of Defence to the deal her coalition partners have struck with opposition parties Pro and Volt: D66 and CDA do not recognise that picture. They say they did keep their coalition partner fully informed of the progress of the negotiations. They instead put the ball in the VVD's court, which they say refused to take part in the negotiations. The votes on the tax plan and the proposed amendments are scheduled for tomorrow afternoon. If D66 and CDA stick to their deal with Pro and Volt, Yesilgöz wants a "fundamental reset" of the coalition. She did not explain exactly what she means by that, but it is clear that trust is far to seek. "It is of course possible that D66 and CDA would prefer a coalition with Pro. But say so!", said the VVD leader. It was certainly not the reaction D66 and CDA had hoped for, after negotiating with Pro and Volt until deep into the night. The agreement they reached shifts about 1 billion euros from taxes on labour to taxes on capital. It is a watered-down version of the opposition parties' original plan. Workers and small savers would then, according to the four parties, be better off, while more is demanded of the wealthy. Paternotte (D66) and Bontenbal said earlier today that they had good hopes that the VVD would agree to it, or at least would not oppose it. The major advantage of such a deal with the left is that there is then also likely to be a majority for the tax plan in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. But Yesilgöz sees the amendment as a breach of the coalition agreement, in which the parties agreed that they would ensure a stable tax and investment climate for entrepreneurs. Parliamentary debate live on NOS. The parliamentary debate on the tax plan begins at 10.15 a.m. and can be followed live via the NOS app, NOS.nl, <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> 1 and NPO Politiek en Nieuws. Updates can regularly be heard on NPO Radio 1. Behind the scenes it can be heard that D66 and CDA cannot judge well what Yesilgöz will exactly do if they vote for the agreements with the left-wing opposition. She does not say in so many words that she will then pull the plug on the coalition. And so D66 and CDA are for now gambling on it. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> has let it be known via the <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> that he will not respond further to Yesilgöz's remarks this evening. Tomorrow he is expected in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, where the tax plan will again be debated. It could lead to the fall of his minority cabinet, which took office less than nine months ago. It followed <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Schoof, which also collapsed long before the four-year term was over. Yesterday the House of Representatives adopted a motion from the ChristenUnie to first look at an attempt to patch things up or a new formation if the cabinet falls prematurely, rather than immediately calling new elections.

title: Minister: goal of zero homeless people in 2030 not achievable, 'it is incredibly tough'
lead: The ambition to ensure that the Netherlands has zero homeless people in 2030 is not achievable. <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Minister Sterk</entity> says she wants "to tell the honest story". In 2022, the fourth <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>-Rutte promised in the National Action Plan on Homelessness that the counter would be at zero in 2030. That is not going to happen, the current minister of Long-Term Care made clear during a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The cabinet will continue to do its best to significantly reduce the number of homeless people. "We will keep working on it. But it is incredibly tough." The minister had already reported the abandonment of the zero-homelessness goal in a letter to the Tweede Kamer last Friday evening, to the surprise of some members of parliament. "I had expected some urgency from this cabinet, but what I see is disinterest," said SP member of parliament Beckerman. Members of parliament from Pro and the ChristenUnie, for example, fear that by abandoning the ambition it will also become unclear what results the cabinet actually wants to achieve. Coalition party D66 and CDA also have questions about Minister Sterk's decision. 33,000 people Minister Sterk assured the Tweede Kamer that the cabinet will continue with various existing action plans to arrange, among other things, suitable housing and to prevent people from ending up on the street. Currently about 33,000 people between the ages of 18 and 65 in the Netherlands have no permanent place to live. This number may in reality be higher, because it is not known how many people stay with family or friends. Most of this group stays in the big cities, where it is relatively easy to earn money. Lack of money Today's debate prompted the mayors of the four largest cities to write an urgent letter to the Tweede Kamer on behalf of 40 other large municipalities. Their main message is: provide 100 million euros in extra national funds for social shelter, ensure more emergency shelter for homeless families, and make medicinal treatment available for crack and cocaine addiction. Because of the large housing shortage, the waiting lists in mental health care and the increase in homeless migrant workers, "no dignified shelter" is possible anymore, and that leads to tent camps and nuisance. Alderman Arjen Dubbelaar of <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, responsible for social shelter, says the city faces a shortfall of 14 million euros in providing good shelter for homeless people. "That shortfall keeps growing. We do not want people sleeping in parks, but at the same time our shelter locations are bursting at the seams," the alderman adds. But the extra financial amount will not come for now, Minister Sterk said. The Kamer first wants insight into how the financial resources currently provided to municipalities will be used. That is not clear at the moment.

title: Man fires shot in Tilburg hotel, no injuries
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested a 53-year-old man from Oisterwijk after a shooting incident in the restaurant of a hotel in Tilburg. No one was injured. The police suspect the man fired blank cartridges. The police received a report at 6:35 PM of a shooting incident in the restaurant of an Ibis hotel on Dr. Hub van Doorneweg, a street named after DAF founder Hub van Doorne. The hotel is on the edge of Tilburg. After the shooting, the suspect fled. When asked by NOS, the police said that it is a "subject of investigation" whether the man was, for example, eating in the restaurant himself or had walked in. 'Sat at a table as a guest' Omroep Brabant reports that the man was sitting at a table as a guest, drew his weapon and fired a shot. The regional broadcaster writes that the man then reportedly pointed his weapon at hotel staff. Several people were in the restaurant at the time of the shooting. A police spokesperson cannot give a specific number. The police quickly identified the suspect and then launched a manhunt. Around 9:00 PM he was arrested on the Ringbaan-Zuid in Tilburg.

title: Wildlands tries to get harmful beetle out of tropical greenhouse: 'Still quite a jungle'
lead: No visitors, but researchers are peering through binoculars at the plants in the large tropical greenhouse of Wildlands Adventure Zoo in Emmen. The animal park, together with the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> (NVWA), is looking for an unwelcome guest: the bark beetle. The so-called Euwallacea fornicatus was discovered in the greenhouse two years ago. The beetle species, which originally comes from Asia, poses a threat to the trees and plants in the greenhouse. They bore tunnels into the plants and can also transmit disease-causing fungi, causing branches or even entire trees to be lost. The bark beetle species has moreover been placed on the control list by the European Union and is regarded as an invasive alien species. Wildlands is therefore trying to prevent further spread of the beetle and to eradicate the insects. To do that well, Wildlands together with the NVWA has set up research to find out exactly where the bark beetles are in the greenhouse and how many there are. Then the best way to control them can be examined and new planting can be taken into account. The search for the bark beetle turns out to be quite a challenge. The research in the Wildlands greenhouse is special, because the little insect often does not occur in the Netherlands. "This beetle has a fairly hidden way of life," says insect expert Bas van de Meulengraaf of the NVWA to RTV Drenthe. "The female flies around and looks for a suitable plant to bore a hole in. They carry a fungus with them that they plant in a weakened tree. If that fungus takes hold, they can go on, because that is their food. They are basically gardeners." The search for the beetle turns out to be quite a challenge. The little creature is about 3 millimetres big and also hides in the trees and branches. Moreover, the greenhouse is 23 metres high and the building has a surface area of 16,000 square metres. To do structured and thorough research, all trees and plants in the greenhouse have been mapped. The greenhouse was then divided into sections and teams go through the trees and plants one by one with aerial work platforms, binoculars and torches. When inventorying the greenery, the animal park assumed around 200 to 300 different tree and plant species, says animal and park management manager Jan-Minze Zomer. "But we have double that: we have 700 trees in the greenhouse, apart from all the palms and banana plants. So it is still quite a jungle." Valuable research Trees or plants affected by the bark beetle are marked with a ribbon. That does not necessarily mean they are doomed, says Van de Meulengraaf. Sometimes the damage remains limited. "It may be that only pruning is needed. That only a branch or the top part is removed and the rest can stay standing," he says. The research is not only valuable for the NVWA and the park, but possibly also for others. "If we have the knowledge, we can also share it with other gardens and parks also within Europe," says Zomer. "So it is very exciting that we can contribute here." The 'field research' continues until 13 November. After that, the data still needs to be analysed before conclusions can be drawn from it.

title: Iconic ship that carried famous Americans is to become a popular diving attraction
lead: An iconic American passenger ship has been sunk in the Gulf of Mexico, off the coast of Florida. For years there was debate about what should happen to the ship, which was taken out of service as early as 1969. Eventually it was decided that the ship should become the largest artificial reef in the world. Around 20:40 Dutch time, flooding of the 'S.S. United States' began. The sinking took several hours. Supporters of the plan hope the vessel will offer shelter to underwater life. The ship is to become a popular attraction for divers on the seabed. This is how the iconic ship slowly disappeared beneath the waves: Opponents felt the ship should be preserved as a historic monument. But their objections were rejected in court. The vessel was bought in 2024 by a party that wanted to convert the ship into a floating museum, but the group did not succeed. Since March 2025 the ship has been moored in the American city of Mobile, in the state of Alabama. Before the ship was sunk, loose objects and harmful substances and materials were removed from it. Once the ship is in place, its upper deck will lie about eighteen metres below the water surface. John F. Kennedy and the Mona Lisa The ship crossed the Atlantic Ocean more than 800 times in the decades it was part of the American fleet. The rich and famous of the time sailed from the United States to Europe and back; on board were politicians, kings and artists, among others. Former US president John F. Kennedy once set foot on the deck, as did celebrities Coco Chanel, Sean Connery, Marilyn Monroe, Salvador Dalí and Walt Disney, according to the ship's website, which functions as a digital museum and archive. Not only world stars sailed on board. In 1963 the Mona Lisa was shipped to the United States for exhibitions in Washington D.C. and New York. Speed record The ship also holds a speed record. During its first trans-Atlantic crossing in 1952 it crossed the ocean in record time. The journey from New York to Southampton in England took three days, ten hours and forty minutes. No other passenger ship has broken that record since. The ship received the informal honour of the Blue Pennant for this. The S.S. United States had a top speed of around 70 kilometres per hour. By comparison, the passenger ship Titanic could reach a maximum of 44 kilometres per hour. Fireproof piano That the ship could reach that speed was because more aluminium was used than in other shipbuilding projects. Aluminium is a light metal, which benefited the speed. The ship was designed by the American naval architect William Francis Gibbs. The vessel was 301.8 metres long, more than thirty metres longer than the Titanic. Gibbs required the ship to be fireproof, so absolutely no wood was to be used. There was one exception: the wings on board were made of fireproof mahogany. One of the pianos was doused with petrol beforehand, after which a test was done trying to set the instrument on fire by holding a match to it. The instrument did not burn. On board the ship there was no lack of any luxury. Besides being able to play the piano, there was sufficient food available. For the first voyage of the S.S. United States, 7935 litres of ice cream and 227 kilograms of caviar were stocked.

title: Historic result in Mississippi as well, Democrat wins Senate seat in deep-red state
lead: In the very conservative American state of Mississippi, the Democrats have achieved a historic victory. A week after the midterm elections, news agency AP reports that Black Democrat Scott Colom has been elected to <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Colom (43) defeated Republican candidate Cindy Hyde-Smith (67) by several thousand votes. Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video on social media. "Although this is not the outcome we worked toward or hoped for, I respect the decision of the voters of Mississippi," she said. With the victory in Mississippi, the Democrats will have a majority of at least 55 of the 100 seats in the Senate from January, when all elected members take their seats. The Republicans stand at 44 seats. In the state of Alaska the result is not yet known. There, the Democrats' candidate currently has a slight lead in the vote count. Deep-red Mississippi was for decades a Republican stronghold. Donald Trump, for example, won the southern state by 22 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Nearly 40 percent of residents are Black, the highest percentage of all US states. But for the Senate, white politicians were consistently chosen: the last Black senator from Mississippi left Washington D.C. in 1881. Correspondent Sjoerd den Daas was in Mississippi this week, where discriminatory rules long kept Black voters away from polling stations: Leader Chuck Schumer of the Democrats in the Senate praised Colom's election campaign. "Together with his staff and volunteers, he ran the campaign of his life and gave a new definition to what is possible for Democrats in the South". Senate and House The Democrats have achieved a series of important victories in the midterm elections. The party has taken control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. That means, among other things, that it will be much harder for Republican President Trump to carry out his plans in the last two years of his term.

title: Veterans call Minister Hegseth to account: 'He is a war criminal'
lead: A first attempt to start impeachment proceedings against US Minister Hegseth failed in the House of Representatives. But a growing group of veterans is unhappy with him. "I am extremely disappointed that he will not be removed for now," says Alice Mascitti. She served 26 years in the medical corps of the US Army. Now she stands with an American flag and a protest sign in front of the Capitol in Washington D.C. She believes Hegseth should be held responsible for the war against Iran and the capture of Venezuelan president Maduro. According to the failed impeachment proposal, Hegseth violated the constitution by launching these military actions without the approval of Congress. "As a veteran, I took an oath to the constitution," says Mascitti. "I am shocked by the way the government ignores our constitution." Veterans Day On Veterans Day a group of veterans gathered at the Capitol in Washington, D.C. During this national holiday all living and deceased veterans are honoured for their service in the US armed forces. According to the organisation there are around two hundred people from all over the country. "I have already spoken with people from California, Florida, Louisiana, Alabama and Texas," says one veteran. "That shows how much this means to us." It is a sea of protest signs with texts such as 'Loyal to the constitution, not to the president' and 'Impeach Hegseth, bring the troops home.' They call Hegseth a war criminal. Attack on the military Hegseth called the impeachment proposals not only an attack on him, but on all the military who serve the country. According to him, his political opponents suggest that their military service is a crime. "None of that is true," says veteran Mascitti. She in fact thinks his actions are disrespectful and, like many of those present, hopes the war against Iran ends soon. "The war was started for economic and political gain. I do not want our country to wage war unnecessarily and expose soldiers to danger." At the military cemetery in Arlington, Virginia, a mix of booing and loud applause can be heard for Pete Hegseth. During the annual ceremony President Trump praises his defence minister. "He cares about you and protects you. That is what he stands for." Trump kept supporting Hegseth during the attempt to remove him. In his speech he emphasises how good the government now is for veterans. "Never has our armed forces been so strong and powerful. More people want to join the army." He also expressed his appreciation for the American soldiers in the Middle East. Triumphal arch To honour all veterans, Trump points to his plan for a monumental triumphal arch, just outside the cemetery. "Soon we will unveil an impressive triumphal arch," he says. "It is in honour of our great veterans and our armed forces. They have been waiting here for 200 years." At the protest in the capital they are less enthusiastic. "I hate the triumphal arch," says veteran Mascitti. "The arch is disrespectful to our fallen comrades." Further along, a veteran stands with a sign reading 'Stop the arch'. He wears a cap and pins from the navy ships on which he served for eight years. He carries a photo of his deceased cousin, who is buried in Arlington. "I find the triumphal arch appalling, because it blocks the view of the Lincoln Memorial." Shadow Besides the blocked view, there is criticism of the shadow Trump's triumphal arch would cast over the graves at the military cemetery. Nine relatives of the Kennedys also oppose the construction. They have joined a lawsuit to stop the project. According to the family, the arch would cast a shadow over the grave of former president John F. Kennedy. Construction of the project has been halted for at least another week and a half, after a judge imposed a temporary construction stop. The veterans' hope rests on Congress, which convenes in January with new members and a Democratic majority in both the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. They hope the new representatives will commit more to veterans and try again to hold Hegseth to account.

title: Frisian coin from the Eighty Years' War fetches record sum at auction
lead: A gold coin from <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity> has sold for a record price. The rare half Philip daalder from 1580 was auctioned in <entity id="org:gemeente-ijsselstein">IJsselstein</entity> for 369,000 euros, making it the most expensive Dutch provincial coin ever. The coin shows Philip II, the King of Spain and ruler of the Spanish Netherlands at the start of the Eighty Years' War. He regularly appeared on Dutch coins in the first years of the revolt. Very rare In Friesland few of these coins were minted, and to date only two silver half Philip daalders from this province are known. The coin was last exhibited in 1877 in <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity>, when it was owned by former mayor Rengers. Who bought the gold half Philip daalder has not been disclosed by Heritage Auctions Europe. The auction house regularly sees special collectibles change hands.

title: European negotiator for Ukraine wanted: 'Otherwise we risk becoming irrelevant'
lead: Who on earth should speak on behalf of Europe about an end to the war in Ukraine? That question is becoming increasingly pressing now that the continent is trying to secure a seat at the negotiating table alongside the Americans, Ukrainians and Russians. Ukrainian president Zelensky is also pressing: it must become clear this month who will represent Europe. The matter is back on the agenda at a summit in Dublin. Besides many European leaders, Ukrainian president Zelensky and NATO chief <entity id="person:mark-rutte">Mark Rutte</entity> are also in the Irish capital today. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> is skipping it; he has to resolve a coalition crisis at home. Europe stands on the sidelines. The other leaders are being briefed on the talks of the past few days in Abu Dhabi. Later today US negotiators Witkoff and Kushner come to Ireland. They first travel to Moscow to speak with Putin. Afterwards they will report back to Zelensky. The role of the Europeans remains unclear. "The future of Ukraine is also about our future," European leaders stress time and again, and therefore we must be involved. They fear the Americans and Russians will make disadvantageous agreements over their heads, without European input. Recently we set out the interests of the American and Russian negotiators in this piece: In recent days several European countries and EU and NATO representatives stood on the sidelines in Abu Dhabi. They did speak separately with Ukraine and America, but were not allowed to join the 'real' talks with Russia because that country refused to receive the Europeans. Not giving an inch Moscow does not appear to give an inch in the talks. During the talks in the United Arab Emirates Russia kept attacking Ukraine, among other things energy infrastructure was hit, leaving Ukrainians without electricity. The Europeans do not believe Moscow is negotiating seriously, yet they want to be directly involved. But they simply cannot agree on who should speak on their behalf or what the strategy should be. The differences are large, as became clear recently when Finnish president Stubb and Norwegian prime minister Store called Russian president Putin for an hour and a half in an attempt to engage with neighbouring Russia themselves. 'Do not keep the dictator as a friend' Their initiative was coordinated with Ukraine, but still led to mixed European reactions. Danish prime minister Frederiksen was critical. "I think we must keep Europe united rather than each acting alone," she said. According to her Swedish colleague, peace must be reached through 'strength' rather than 'appeasement politics'. The Estonian prime minister goes even harder: Europe should not mediate at all, he says in an interview with Politico. "You should not try to keep the dictator as a friend". Several countries, including the Netherlands, are more positive and appreciate the Finnish-Norwegian effort to end the war in Ukraine. Irrelevant In May the discussion about a European negotiator also flared up, but it did not lead to results. Half a year later the countries have not come closer together. To the annoyance of, among others, Italian prime minister Meloni. She put the topic on the agenda for the European summit in Dublin. Now too many European initiatives are running alongside each other, says Meloni, who fears it undermines European credibility. And so someone must be appointed. "Otherwise we run the risk of Europe becoming irrelevant in the negotiation process." The lack of a clear European position and a European negotiator serves, according to the Italian prime minister, mainly the interests of those who want to keep this war going. Raising pressure Meloni refers here to the Russians, who are only too happy to stress that Europe is divided. And the Americans also see their image of Europe confirmed in the stumbling search for a European negotiator. "It would be a greater achievement if Europe could name one person who speaks on their behalf than to convince the Russians to involve them in the negotiations," mocked Trump's son-in-law Kushner. He says he will discuss possible European participation in the talks with Putin today and hopes for the Russian president's 'blessing'. But even if that were to come, nobody in Dublin expects a major breakthrough in the talks on an end to the war in Ukraine. According to Zelensky, that will depend on the extent to which the Americans step up pressure on Russia. European leaders are not optimistic about that.

title: 'Nvidia makes quick decision on dismissal of top executive Huang after news of second affair'
lead: The board of chipmaker Nvidia will decide on a very short timeline whether the embattled top executive Jensen Huang will be dismissed or not. This is reported by news agencies Bloomberg and Reuters, among others, following reporting by The Wall Street Journal. The reason is a new affair that has come to light. According to American media, this time it concerns an employee of Nvidia. Earlier it emerged that Huang had an affair with a woman who, according to American intelligence services, spied for China. She reportedly tried to obtain chip secrets and has since returned to Beijing, writes Bloomberg. Nvidia previously announced an independent investigation into possible espionage. The board of the American chipmaker then said it had no indications that sensitive company secrets had been stolen. We previously wrote this profile of top executive Jensen Huang and Nvidia: The United States is concerned about the possibility that advanced chips could end up in Chinese hands, allowing China to modernise its military faster and better develop AI models. AI data centres The company in California is one of the most important players in the field of artificial intelligence and makes, among other things, chips used for AI data centres. In recent years these are being built out at a rapid pace, and this is leading to large profits for companies such as Nvidia. After the scandal became public, Nvidia's share price took heavy hits on the American tech exchange Nasdaq.

title: Never before so many shoulder injuries among Dutch sports people
lead: The number of shoulder injuries among Dutch sports people is rising sharply. Figures from VeiligheidNL, the knowledge centre for injury prevention, show that there were 530,000 shoulder injuries in 2025. Never before has that number been so high. Last year, 4.7 million Dutch people together suffered 5.7 million sports injuries. The knee was the most affected, followed by the ankle. In third place is the shoulder. In many sports, such as the popular hyrox and padel, the shoulder is heavily loaded. "People find their new sport so much fun that they go at it fanatically and overload their shoulder in the process", says sports doctor and assistant professor at Erasmus MC Femke Claessen. Build up slowly. It happens that people, out of enthusiasm, start sporting several times a week out of nowhere, says Claessen. She sees this with padel, for example. Claessen works as the KNLTB padel medical officer, the umbrella body for tennis and padel clubs in the Netherlands. "You may be fit yourself, but your shoulder is not trained to be loaded so often." A good warm-up, building up slowly, and exercises to strengthen the shoulder can prevent you as a sportsperson from getting a shoulder injury. This applies to all overhand sports, says Claessen, such as handball, javelin, baseball, volleyball, shot put and tennis. Injury risk. That the number of shoulder injuries is rising does not mean that the risk of such an injury has increased. "We have, proportionally, taken up sport more as a whole", says Ellen Kemler, researcher in sports injury prevention at VeiligheidNL. "The injury risk is expressed as the number of injuries per 1,000 hours of sport. Because the number of sporting hours has increased proportionally more than the number of injuries, the risk has not increased." The annual report from VeiligheidNL further shows that half of the injuries required medical treatment. Many sports injuries also involve overloading of muscles and tendons. That can result in a hamstring injury, Achilles tendon injury or tennis elbow. According to Kemler, it is necessary to devote more attention to preventing these rather than to recovering from the injury. "By gradually building up the load, you can considerably reduce the risk of an injury."

title: Wake-up call 12/11: Make or break for cabinet • Appeal against Erasmus shooter
lead: Good morning! The future of the minority cabinet hangs by a thread, and in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> a vote on the tax plan takes place today. In <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> the appeal against Erasmus shooter Fouad L. begins. First, the weather: the day starts with quite a lot of cloud and a few showers. In the afternoon sun and clouds alternate and it is mostly dry. With a moderate to fairly strong northwesterly wind, it will be 8 to 11 degrees. The forecast for the coming days and more weather news can be found here in NOS Weather. Are you heading out today? Here you can find an overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? In the highly conservative American state of Mississippi, the Democrats have achieved a historic victory. One week after the midterm elections, news agency AP reports that Black Democrat Scott Colom has been elected to <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Colom (43) defeated Republican candidate Cindy Hyde-Smith (67) by a few thousand votes. That is remarkable, because Mississippi was for decades a Republican stronghold. Other news from the night: And one more thing: in Brabant and Limburg, carnival season kicked off yesterday. In <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity> there was long discussion about young people at the Elfde van de Elfde. The municipality wanted free access for minors, because carnival is a party for everyone. But the hospitality sector wanted to be able to refuse minors at certain times. As a result, the party risked not going ahead. After several talks, the municipality, hospitality sector and carnival foundation agreed that anyone who causes nuisance or is noticeably under the influence of alcohol or drugs can be refused. The number of NIX18 teams has also been increased; they speak to minors who are drinking alcohol. And so-called buddies walk around the festival grounds to support security. Even so, the party was able to start again at the Elfde van de Elfde. Have a great day!

title: Building collapses in New York: eight dead and at least seventeen injured
lead: In the Brooklyn neighbourhood of New York at least eight people have died and seventeen have been injured after a building collapsed. Four of the injured are in critical condition. Authorities warn that the number of victims is likely to rise. Rescue workers do not know how many people are still missing. Construction workers were digging on the adjacent plot when the three-storey building collapsed, local authorities said at a press conference. The collapse, shortly after 4 p.m. local time, tore away the wall of an adjoining building, leaving a staircase, a bed and cupboards exposed in the open air. Footage shows firefighters searching for survivors: According to the fire brigade, people are still trapped at the site of the collapse. Dozens of firefighters are removing the rubble stone by stone in search of victims. The search could last days. "Everything collapsed and everyone was screaming", says a woman to The New York Times. She saw the building collapse when she had dropped off her daughter at a nearby hairdresser's. "The whole building started shaking and then it just collapsed." It is not clear how many people were in the building when it collapsed. Possibly there were more people at home than on an ordinary Wednesday. Because of Veterans Day, schools and some businesses were closed. The collapsed building dates from 1930 and was used as a residential building and for shops, The New York Times reports, based on city archives.

title: Six dead in Israeli attack on hospital in southern Gaza
lead: Six people, including a surgeon, were killed early this morning in an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser hospital in Khan Younis in southern Gaza. Twenty people were also injured, Gaza's rescue service reports. The Israeli army stated after the attack that it was aimed at a senior Hamas member and other members of the movement's armed wing. According to the army, they were in the hospital. In a statement, Israel accused Hamas of using the hospital complex as a command centre for military operations. According to the army, weapons were stored there, command rooms were set up, and hospital facilities were used as observation posts and hideouts for fighters. It provided no evidence for this, and the accusations could not be independently verified. Ceasefire violated: Since October last year a ceasefire has been in force between Israel and Hamas, but in practice Israel violates the ceasefire almost daily. Israel says Hamas is trying to regroup and wants to rebuild its arsenal. According to health authorities in Gaza, more than 1600 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire took effect. Israel reports that four Israeli soldiers have been killed in the same period.

title: Grave mooring too shallow for Sinterklaas steamboat, Defence comes to the rescue
lead: In Grave they could already picture it: the steamboat mooring in the fortified town during the national Sinterklaas arrival. But the mooring place at the Loswal is too shallow for the large boat. The solution: a floating gangway. That way Sinterklaas can still set foot ashore there the day after tomorrow. At <entity id="org:gemeente-land-van-cuijk">gemeente Land van Cuijk</entity>, of which Grave is part, the problem was, according to a spokesperson, "known for some time". The help of the Ministry of Defence was called in to fix it in time. Soldiers from the Engineer Regiment, who are responsible for construction and technical tasks within the armed forces, came to Grave to place the pontoon. "We are laying a little bridge for Sint and the pieten", says Jan Möllers to Omroep Brabant. "That way the Sint can still moor here to celebrate." Dry summer. At first the drought of last summer was seen as the main possible spoiler for the steamboat arrival. This summer exceptionally little water flowed through the Dutch rivers. That is no longer a problem, according to <entity id="person:mario-jacobs">Mario Jacobs</entity>, dike reeve. The water level in the Meuse is high enough to moor in the Brabant town. However, <entity id="org:waterschap-aa-en-maas">Waterschap Aa en Maas</entity> has checked whether the dikes are safe enough. "Because of the drought a dike can tear and crack", says the dike reeve. During the arrival many people will be standing on and around the dikes. "If there are deep cracks it can become less sturdy and slide away." But there is no question of that. "The dikes of Grave are in order." Yvonne and Henk. The arrival will be broadcast on Saturday from the home of Yvonne and Henk Nuijen. The large windows of the house offer a perfect view of the quay where Sinterklaas will moor on Saturday. In July they were approached by the broadcaster NTR with the question of whether that part of the house could be converted into a studio. And that is allowed, on one condition. "If our own grandchildren can't look through the window, it won't go ahead", says Yvonne. "They come before everything."

title: German police intercept van full of illegal fireworks on way to the Netherlands
lead: German customs have intercepted a van carrying 1,260 kilos of heavy fireworks during a checkpoint on the motorway near Dresden, not far from the Czech border. The driver was a 44-year-old Czech who was on his way to the Netherlands to sell the fireworks. He has been detained on suspicion of transporting explosive substances and reportedly made a partial confession. The load contained 85 boxes with, among other things, heavy bangers and mortar shells, which are banned in Germany and also in the Netherlands. The fireworks contained 760 kilos of explosive charge. No licence. The man reportedly loaded the fireworks in the Czech Republic on 4 November and drove to Germany in the evening in a van to continue from there to the Netherlands. The man had no licence for the fireworks. The fireworks have been seized and removed by experts.

title: Australian boy (17) survives six days in the bush on crisps and water
lead: In Australia a 17-year-old boy who went missing has survived six days in the wilderness on little more than a bag of crisps and water. Not far from the spot where he had wanted to camp, he got lost and became stuck last week. The teenager from the town of Morwell was reportedly camping with a friend in a nature reserve in the state of Victoria last weekend. When the boy went to fetch the last of his belongings from the place where his mother had dropped him off, he went missing and his friend raised the alarm. A large search was then launched, in which many volunteers also combed the remote area with dense vegetation looking for William. In the end it was rescue workers who, during a flight over the area, spotted a fish-box about 2 kilometres from the campsite: The teenager was sunburnt from the fierce sun: Near that box William was found lying by a stream. After getting lost around the campsite on Friday, he overlooked an opening in a rock face after a night alone in the wilderness, according to the first accounts. He fell down and could no longer move properly. The boy then stayed in that area until he was found. He used towels he had with him, brought for camping, to stay warm at night and drank water from a nearby stream. For food he had only a bag of crisps with him. After William was found, rescuers lifted him out by helicopter and took him to the command post, the police report in a statement. Footage of the emotional reunion there with his mother has been shared by the emergency services of the state of Victoria. Life house arrest. "I never gave up hope," said mother Elizabeth Barkley to the Sydney Morning Herald. "Deep down I knew he was still alive. I prayed to God for a miracle, and a miracle happened. So as soon as that helicopter landed and they brought him out, I gave him the biggest hug." According to Barkley her son is in "good health" and is in good spirits. Physically, he is said to have come out of his week in the wilderness with only a few scratches and a sunburnt body; when he got lost he was wearing only shorts and shoes. She joked that she is now giving her son life house arrest.

title: Russian serviceman killed by explosive under car in Saint Petersburg
lead: A Russian serviceman has been killed by an explosive that went off under his car. The explosion happened early this morning on a road in the south of Saint Petersburg. The explosive was placed under the vehicle and detonated remotely, writes the Russian news site Fontanka. The man was driving away from his home at the time. The identity of the serviceman has not been released. Fontanka reports that he is a colonel. A bus with around forty passengers that was driving on the road was also hit. According to Fontanka, the windows of the vehicle were damaged. No one was injured. The Russian authorities have launched an investigation into the explosion. A series of attacks. Since the start of the war in Ukraine several Russian servicemen have been killed in attacks. Russia points to Ukraine as responsible for the attacks. Ukraine has not yet responded to today's attack. At the end of August a Russian serviceman was also killed in Saint Petersburg by a bomb placed under his car. This reportedly was a lieutenant colonel of the air force. His wife, who was also in the vehicle, was seriously injured. Two weeks before that, an officer of the Russian army was killed by a bomb explosion in Crimea. At the beginning of August a Russian drone manufacturer was seriously injured when his car exploded in Yekaterinburg.

title: DNB: more expensive mortgage for almost a million households
lead: Around 950,000 homeowners can expect considerably higher mortgage costs in the coming years. This applies to people with a variable interest rate or a mortgage whose fixed-rate period is due to expire soon. De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) calculated this on the basis of customer data from the major banks. Interest rates have risen considerably in recent years. Five years ago the average mortgage interest rate was 1.6 per cent, and now it is around 4 per cent. People who have fixed the interest rate on their mortgage for ten or twenty years are not losing sleep over it. Their monthly payments remain the same. A fifth of the total mortgage debt. In the Netherlands it is relatively uncommon for people to have a short fixed-rate period. Only 3 per cent of new mortgages have such a variable interest rate. That means the rate can change monthly based on the market rate. Besides that group, the fixed-rate period of 16 per cent of all mortgages ends before the end of 2028. Taken together, the interest rate on almost a fifth of the total mortgage debt in the Netherlands can therefore change before 2029. Because interest rates have been rising for years, these two groups can soon expect considerably higher monthly costs, the central bank concludes. In the rest of Europe a variable interest rate is much more popular among homeowners. There, 16 per cent of new mortgages have such a variable rate. In that sense the impact will be limited for homeowners in the Netherlands. More money to spend too. For an average household that falls into one of these groups, this amounts to 150 euros in extra interest costs per month. That is gross; because of mortgage interest tax relief the actual increase in costs will be lower, how much depends on the personal situation. Other affected households can count on at least 300 euros extra gross monthly costs per month. In other cases the increase in costs will be around 50 euros gross. DNB does not expect people to get into serious trouble en masse because of the rising mortgage costs. This is mainly because many people have recently had more money to spend.

title: Iran: two oil tankers 'disabled' in Strait of Hormuz
lead: Iran says it attacked two large oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. According to the country, the ships did not keep to the route set by Iran through the narrow waterway. According to Iranian state media, the ships were warned several times. The attacks have not yet been independently confirmed. It is unclear under which flag the two ships sail. According to Iran, the ships together carried around 4 million barrels of crude oil. A fire is said to have broken out after the explosion. What has happened to those on board is not known. Both the US and Iran have, since the beginning of this year, introduced their own shipping rules in the Strait of Hormuz, after the US together with Israel attacked Iran. Expensive oil: Since then Iran has been held responsible for dozens of attacks on commercial ships and tankers. The US has also attacked several ships that did not comply with the rules set by America. The Strait of Hormuz is important for world trade because of its strategic location. Countries such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and also Iran use the strait to export their commodities. Before the war broke out, around 20 per cent of all oil was transported through the narrow sea route. But liquefied gas, diesel and raw materials for the chemical industry also pass through the strait. As a result of the conflict between Israel, the US and Iran, energy prices have risen sharply worldwide.

title: Belgium places fugitive brothers from Weert on European wanted list
lead: The Belgian federal police have added two Dutch brothers to the national and European wanted list. They are Samir M. and Youssef M. from the Limburg town of Weert. The brothers were convicted in Belgium of a very violent home invasion of an elderly couple in the town of Bocholt, just across the border with the Netherlands. At the beginning of last year, the Antwerp court of appeal sentenced both brothers to eight years in prison in absentia. They are fugitives and were not present at their trial. The robbery for which they were convicted took place in February 2017. The brothers acted very violently, the Belgian federal police report. The elderly couple was tied up, gagged and threatened. The man was severely beaten and stabbed in the leg with a knife. He died a few months later. The loot they took was very limited: about 200 euros and some jewellery. Europol campaign The addition of the brothers to the Belgian and European wanted list is part of a new Europol campaign. It draws attention to fugitives who have been convicted of serious crimes against vulnerable victims, such as the elderly and minors. In total, nineteen internationally wanted people are on the new so-called Europe's Most Wanted list. The Belgian authorities hope that international attention will bring new information about the brothers' whereabouts. People who know where they are staying are asked to contact the Belgian police. Tips can also be passed on anonymously.

title: Four schoolchildren in Uganda possibly die from poisoning, another still in hospital
lead: In Uganda, four pupils from a primary school in the capital Kampala have died, possibly from poisoning. How this could have happened has not yet been clarified. It could involve chemicals or food poisoning. The exact cause of death has yet to be established. Three children died at home and a fourth in hospital, where she had been taken with symptoms of illness. They are four girls aged 9 to 11. One pupil is still in hospital. The headteacher has been taken to the police station to answer questions. Several parents of the children who died accuse the school of not having given clear information. Oranges According to the school, eight children had eaten oranges that another pupil had handed out. Five children became nauseous and had to vomit, including the four girls who died. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is also investigating in the village where the oranges came from. Longer-standing concerns There have been longer-standing concerns about health and safety at schools in Uganda. UN children's organisation Unicef, among others, says that the target of one toilet per forty children is not always met. Drinking water is also often kept in jerrycans or buckets instead of sealed water containers. It has happened before that children became ill from food poisoning or exposure to harmful substances. A few children have been admitted to hospital in recent years with symptoms such as stomach cramps, vomiting and breathing problems. Aid organisations and human rights organisations are urging the authorities to better monitor the school food programme, promote hygiene and create more safety for the pupils.

title: Ukraine reports restrictions with Starlink again
lead: Ukrainian President Zelensky reports further delays in the connection of the Starlink satellite network. The problems have been occurring for several days along the entire front line and in the Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine, Zelensky says on X. Zelensky speaks of "systematic speed restrictions" as a result of which Russian drones cannot be intercepted in time. Defence drones, among others, cannot fly faster than 161 kilometres per hour. As a result, several Russian attacks have already taken place in Ukraine, Zelensky says. 'Terms of use breached' Ukraine uses Starshield, the military version of Starlink. The network is essential for the defence of its own airspace. Starlink owner Elon Musk also restricted the network speed last month because, according to him, the Ukrainian army had breached the terms of use. According to Musk, the satellite system was not allowed to be used for offensive drone attacks. After more than a week, on 24 October, Ukraine reported that the connection with Starshield was stable again. Abu Dhabi The new disruptions come a day after negotiations in Abu Dhabi. It was the first time since February that Russia spoke directly with Ukraine about ending the war. The United States mediated the talks. No major breakthrough appears to have been reached after the two-day discussions. Expectations had not been very high beforehand. Russia and Ukraine only agreed to exchange prisoners. According to a Ukrainian official, the disruptions did not come up in Abu Dhabi.

title: Criticism of Guust's new blunder turns into praise
lead: From outrage and lawsuits to compliments and admiration. The Canadian cartoonist Delaf followed in the footsteps of André Franquin two years ago with a new Guust Flater book. Franquin is seen as the absolute grand master of the humorous comic strip. Matching him seemed impossible. But Delaf's Guust became such a success that the anti-hero simply blunders on with a new book. With the continuation of Guust, publisher Dupuis played a high-stakes game. The company owned the rights, but Isabelle Franquin argued in court that her father had not given permission to continue the strip. In the end the daughter could not prevent the publication, but the court did give her the right to assess the new Guust for quality. Remarkably, Flater slaat weer toe appeared without any hitch, and today the successor Knallende flaters appears without a murmur. In French alone, that came in a first print run of one million copies. Hopeless Many comic fans place Franquin's swinging drawing style and slapstick humour on a lonely height. Although series such as Robbedoes, Ton en Tineke and the Marsupilami were taken over by other authors, nobody dared to risk their hand at Guust. An attempt to match not only the drawings but also the jokes of the bumbling office clerk seemed hopeless beforehand. Delaf's Guust has now been embraced even by the biggest critics. How do you step into the body and mind of someone who is seen in the comic world as being on the level of Rembrandt or Van Gogh? "Franquin is a genius", Delaf says in conversation with the NOS. In Flater slaat weer toe, Guust swapped the extremely bad comics of a friend with those of Franquin in a few jokes, after which they ended up in the weekly Robbedoes. "That drawing friend? Yes, that's me indeed", laughs Delaf. For his second Guust, Delaf got help from the Frenchman Lewis Trondheim with making the jokes. "Even Hergé, the artist of Kuifje, thought Franquin was a better artist", he begins. "That says something." Not Franquin, but Guust To avoid making a blunder himself, Delaf mainly did not look at Franquin, he explains his method: "It is impossible to imitate him. Readers don't expect Franquin either, but Guust. It is about portraying Guust as well as possible." Trondheim says the same about making the jokes: "I have read Guust since I was young. So it's a bit in your DNA. You have to enjoy it. When I started, I thought about the bad drawings of Guust's friend from the previous book. That will surely have produced a lot of reader mail. So the first joke I came up with was Guust making a mini-golf course in the editorial office out of all that mail." Brussels Franquin drew much of his inspiration from Brussels, from the busy streets to the parking meters. "Publisher Charles Dupuis asked at the time for a setting that looks a bit like Paris and Brussels. But everyone mainly recognises Brussels in it", Delaf says. "So I look a lot at photos of Brussels from the seventies, because Guust keeps being set in that period. What did a beer tap look like? That sort of thing." Even so, Guust's world is relatively small, Trondheim admits: "But at the same time there are so many characters you can take in different directions. How do you put De Mesmaeker with his contracts in a new situation? What can the seagull do?" What is good stays good, Trondheim sums it up. And that applies especially to Guust, Delaf adds: "Someone who doesn't listen to orders, is a bit lazy, loves nature and basically goes his own way, that is an anti-hero we can still recognise ourselves in and that we also need a little."

title: 128,000 email addresses from De Vrienden van Amstel exposed in data breach
lead: A data leak has exposed 128,000 email addresses of De Vrienden van Amstel Live and Amstel Live in de Kroeg. These are personal details of people who were approached for visitor research. Parent company Heineken warns of phishing emails or other suspicious messages. The leak originated at hosting company Cloudbear, a supplier of research agency Abbi Insights, which carried out visitor research for the companies. It concerns email addresses, names, telephone numbers, postcodes, gender and dates of birth, among other things. "We deeply regret this", a Heineken spokesperson says. Those affected were informed by email last night. In it they are warned to be extra alert to suspicious messages. They are also urged to be wary of suspicious text or WhatsApp messages and phone calls. "Never just share passwords, verification codes or other sensitive information", Heineken says. Investigation started: It is still unclear to what extent the data has been viewed, copied or misused. Heineken says it has launched an investigation together with Abbi Insights and Cloudbear. "Protecting personal data is a very high priority for us and we are looking at which additional measures are needed to limit the consequences and prevent a repeat", the spokesperson said. Heineken has reported the matter to the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity>.

title: Belgium also has indications that Iran is behind the cyberattack on cooling systems
lead: Following France, Belgium also has indications that Iran was involved in the recent cyberattacks on cooling systems in several European countries. Dozens of Belgian shops had to throw away large quantities of food as a result earlier this month. According to Minister Quintin of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> en Veiligheid, Belgian security services have indications that Iran-linked hacker groups were involved in the cyberattacks, the Flemish broadcaster VRT reports. Justice is now conducting further investigation into these indications. "There is no reason for panic, but we remain particularly vigilant", says Quintin. The minister says the Belgian government takes the attacks very seriously and that it "is deploying all necessary means to map out the threat". He referred in this regard to the role of the military intelligence service and the "considerable resources" Belgium is investing in <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>. Shortly after Quintin's remarks, minister Prévot of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> hastened to say that Belgium is not charging Iran. The services are on top of this matter, he stated, "but the data we currently have are not sufficient to officially hold Iran responsible". With that, Prévot is correcting his fellow minister, the VRT concludes. French investigation: France also has strong indications that Iran was involved in the large-scale sabotage. On Monday it became known that French justice has started an investigation that, according to news channel BFM, is targeting the head of the hacker group Shahid Kaveh. That group has ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the elite force of the Iranian state. The investigation into the cyberattacks revealed a "characteristic modus operandi" of the Iranian group, according to a statement from the French Public Prosecution Service. For example, it is said to have communicated in Persian and the IP addresses used could be linked to Iran. Last month's cyberattack hit around 700 French supermarkets, including large chains such as Intermarché and E.Leclerc. Shops with outdated software saw temperatures in fridges and freezers rise to as high as 50 degrees and had to throw away their stock. Last week, cooling systems at French blood banks were also attacked. New attacks: In Luxembourg, Sweden and the Netherlands too, shops were hit by attacks on their cooling systems earlier this month. At at least seventeen businesses, the temperature of cooling and freezing systems was adjusted remotely. Large supermarkets escaped unscathed, while small businesses such as butchers and neighbourhood shops were the victims. This butcher in the Belgian town of Hove has suffered damage running into tens of thousands of euros after the cyberattack earlier this month:

title: 12 years' prison and TBS sought for online abuse of 245 girls
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has demanded 12 years' imprisonment and a TBS treatment order against a man for online abuse of at least 245 girls. The 41-year-old Bas P. from Herten in Limburg came to the attention of the investigative services last year following a tip from America. According to the OM, P. has for years shared abuse images of minor girls on a forum on the dark web, a closed part of the internet. He met the girls on an online platform where young people can start a webcam conversation with random strangers. Coercion The suspect played a so-called highscore game with the girls there. While the girls sat in front of a webcam, they had to carry out tasks. That began innocently, but over time the tasks became more explicit. The girls did not know that Bas P. filmed everything and would later also share it. In addition, according to the OM, P. extorted girls with the footage by forcing them to perform even more extreme sexual acts for their webcam. 255 videos of girls were found on P.'s computer from September 2017 to October 2025. He had sorted the videos into folders by the victims' age. One folder was called BM, which according to the OM probably refers to blackmail, extortion. In the videos in that folder, the girls, often crying, are forced to perform even more extreme sexual acts on themselves than they had already done. 'Fantasy world' P. denies that he blackmailed the girls. He says he received the folder with coerced footage. The OM does not accept this because the method in those images matches the videos of the girls who were not forced. Yesterday P. gave a statement on the first day of the hearing. In it he said, among other things, that he is "taking responsibility" for what he has done. He also said he believes he deserves punishment. He said that he fled into a "fantasy world" with the abuse, in which he had lost sight of the fact that "on the other side there was a real person". The OM believes P. has made 245 victims in total. Only some have been identified. Justice knows there are at least twelve Dutch and eight Belgian victims. The OM also says P. made victims in America, Australia and Germany. The youngest girl was 8 years old.

title: After years of protests, proposals and lawsuits, Enschede gets a new mosque
lead: After years of political wrangling, a new mosque is finally being built in Enschede. The place of worship replaces the two current, considerably outdated mosques in the city. "How happy can you be? We are going to celebrate this in a big way", says Gökhan Çelik, chair of the board of the new mosque. The new mosque, which will be called the Turkish Cultural Centre, will soon accommodate 625 people. During Islamic holidays the capacity may grow to around 1,500 people. On the mosque grounds there will also be a shop and a catering outlet for visitors to the place of worship. Construction starts on 18 December and the building is intended to be finished within two years. When the place of worship can actually open after that is not yet known. Trouble The approval for the construction of the new mosque did not come without a fight. The first plans date from 2009, reports RTV Oost. The municipal council did not vote in favour at the time, because residents nearby had concerns about the call to prayer. The council only wanted to grant permission for the mosque to be built if good agreements were made with the residents. That happened, and in 2016 the municipal council voted in favour. The executive produced a zoning plan, but it was struck down by the Council of State, to which nearby residents had turned. According to the residents, the municipality had not adequately justified how the traffic situation around the mosque would be, and the council agreed with them. The highest administrative court in the country also did not give the green light to a revised proposal. Protest In 2020 the third version of the zoning plan was ready, but at that point it was the municipal council itself that scrapped it. A majority felt the executive should better map out the traffic and parking pressure. Meanwhile there was also protest against the arrival of the prayer centre. The far-right group Pegida, for example, smeared the site of the planned mosque, reportedly with pig's blood. Action groups also organised demonstrations. In 2022 a majority of the <entity id="org:gemeenteraad-enschede">gemeenteraad van Enschede</entity> voted for the start of construction. And a year later the Council of State also gave the green light. The new proposal included an extra junction to relieve the traffic pressure. Three generations "We have had to wait seventeen years, but now it is finally happening", says Çelik of the mosque board. "Three generations are happy. This project has lived in the dreams of our grandfathers, our fathers took action and now we are allowed to make it happen." How much the construction of the new mosque will cost depends on which contractor carries it out, he says. The new mosque is needed, says Çelik. "The two current mosques are very old buildings, a lot of parking fees have to be paid and the neighbourhood suffers from traffic congestion." At the start of construction next month, mayor <entity id="person:roelof-bleker">Roelof Bleker</entity> will be present.

title: Parties blame each other in debate on tax plan
lead: Which coalition party bears most of the blame for the crisis over the tax plan? Opinions differ on this in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, as became clear at the start of the debate on that plan. Left-wing parties such as Denk and the Party for the Animals believe the VVD is behaving irresponsibly by openly doubting the future of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. Right-wing parties such as the PVV, JA21 and Forum for Democracy are aiming their arrows at D66 and CDA, which in their view show themselves to be unreliable by making a deal without the VVD with opposition parties Pro and Volt. "You have handed the keys of the Torentje to Pro. They are now the boss and you have deliberately crossed the VVD's pain threshold", PVV-<entity id="person:geert-wilders">leider Wilders</entity> accused D66-<entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity>. "You have made them so angry that they are now considering leaving the cabinet." Paternotte called that "nonsense". According to him, the adjustments he is proposing together with CDA, Pro and Volt only really affect people who make 60.000 euro profit a year on their wealth. "That is about 68.000 people. At the same time, all people with an average income, including Henk and Ingrid, will pay about 100 euro less tax." Majority for the plan not yet certain: D66, CDA, Pro and Volt presented their plan yesterday as a way out of the impasse, because it could at least gain a majority in both the Senate and the House. They counted on the support of the ChristianUnion and 50Plus. But today it turns out those parties are quite critical of the agreements. The ChristianUnion has great difficulty with the fact that part of the funding has not yet been filled in, so a financial gap may arise. 50Plus leader Struijs mainly sees problems for people who receive only the state pension (AOW). According to him, a calculation shows that this group does not benefit under the plan. D66 and CDA hope that the ChristianUnion and 50Plus will ultimately vote in favour. Otherwise they have put the survival of the cabinet at stake with a plan that ultimately does not even have a majority. Paternotte again denied that he ambushed the VVD yesterday with the deal. "We have actually been very transparent." VVD leader Yesilgöz said yesterday that she was only informed about the content of the agreement when Pro and Volt gave an explanation to the press. Paternotte acknowledged that in recent times things in the coalition have not always gone smoothly. "All of the Netherlands has been able to see that." Yesilgöz suggested yesterday "a fundamental reset" of the coalition, and Paternotte also sees something in that. He sees it as "a logical call that I take very seriously". "I can well imagine that there are many reasons to ensure that we do things differently, and I want to work on that with my coalition partners", said the D66 parliamentary leader. Compromise: Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> also defended the agreement he reached yesterday with part of the coalition. He stressed that it is a compromise, and that his party has also given up a lot. He also does not understand why the VVD and other right-wing parties are so up in arms against his plan. "As if asking the wealthy for an extra contribution is the very, very, very worst thing that could happen. It has zero effect on the lives of these people." For workers, on the other hand, even a small tax cut makes, according to Klaver, "a real difference". Today's debate officially concerns the tax plan, which regulates government revenue for next year. So far it has mainly been about the confidence crisis in the minority cabinet. The intention is for a vote on the tax plan and the amendments submitted by the various parties to take place later today. It is still unclear how the vote will eventually go and whether the tax plan will get a majority.

title: Temporary disruption to Eurostar due to bomb threat at Calais station
lead: Due to a bomb threat at Calais-Fréthun railway station in France, which has since been lifted, delays have arisen on Eurostar's international trains. Rail traffic at the station was halted at 09.40 this morning for security checks. This was reported by local authorities on X. This led not only to delays for French trains, but also for international rail traffic such as Eurostar, which crosses between Calais in France and Folkestone in the United Kingdom via the Eurotunnel. At 11.18 rail traffic could resume. "The situation has been checked and resolved", the authorities wrote.

title: British woman missing from cruise ship, possibly thrown overboard
lead: A British woman who was on board a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean has vanished without trace. The 72-year-old was last seen on Monday, travel organisation TUI reports. It is believed she may have gone overboard. The ship, the Marella Voyager, is on its way to the Caribbean and has covered almost 900 kilometres since Monday. It is not clear exactly when the woman disappeared. Staff found out on Tuesday evening that her bed had not been slept in and immediately raised the alarm. The ship was searched and the passengers on board were counted. They had to gather urgently at designated spots, line up in rows of four and show their ticket to confirm their identity. Search Ships in the area were asked to keep a lookout for the woman. The US Coast Guard told the captain of the cruise ship that he had better carry on sailing rather than return to search for the woman. Footage from video cameras on board is being reviewed for possible clues. The ship had previously run into a storm, leaving passengers seasick or anxious, but it is not assumed that the woman's disappearance is related to this, British media report. The Marella Voyager has around 2,000 passengers and 800 crew members on board. The ship departed from the Spanish port city of Málaga on 4 November for a voyage to Antigua, where it is expected tomorrow. It then sails on to Dominica, arriving at its final destination of Barbados on Sunday. Last Monday it became known that a pianist from a cruise ship had fallen about 30 kilometres off the coast of California. The man was rescued by fishermen after he had been in the water for around nine hours.

title: Sleeping in rush hour lands self-driving car driver with a fine
lead: A woman who was caught asleep behind the wheel of her self-driving car during the morning rush hour has been fined by Canadian police. The car was on Highway 417, which runs right through the capital Ottawa, among slow-moving traffic. A police officer noticed the woman and drove close to her car to record on a bodycam that she was in the driver's seat with her eyes closed and hands off the steering wheel. The siren stayed off. The woman probably woke up when her car warned her of approaching traffic. The driver can expect a fine for careless driving, the Ottawa police write in a report about the incident. The penalty costs 490 Canadian dollars, a good 300 euros. The woman also receives 6 penalty points on her driving licence, which is enough on its own for a warning letter from her province. Children in the back seat The police are using the incident to remind motorists that they must keep their attention on the traffic at all times. "Even if a vehicle has an autonomous driving function, drivers remain obliged to give the necessary care and attention to the traffic when they are behind the wheel", the police write on social media. Officer Michael Fathi tells CBC News that, as far as he knows, this is the first time Ottawa police have caught someone asleep behind the wheel of a self-driving car. In the western province of British Columbia, several motorists also recently dozed off. According to a witness, two children were sitting in the back seat in one car. Sunglasses In theory, the car's system should warn the person in the driver's seat if the steering wheel has not been touched for a while, or if a camera in the rear-view mirror registers that someone's eyes have been closed for a while. But that system is not foolproof. If the driver wears sunglasses, for example, eye movements are difficult to detect. Fathi points out that automatic steering is indeed 'a very interesting option' to have in your car, but that 'you still have to keep control of your vehicle'. The technology is not infallible, he stresses, and has led to traffic accidents, some of them fatal. In the Netherlands too, the driver of a self-driving car is always responsible.

title: Chipmaker Nvidia's chief Huang leaves with immediate effect over affairs
lead: The curtain has fallen for Jensen Huang as chief executive of chipmaker Nvidia. The CFO, current finance chief Colette Kress, is temporarily taking over the role. The company has also started a search for a successor, looking inside and outside the company. Huang was one of the founders of Nvidia in 1993, which is one of the most valuable companies in the world by market capitalisation. He played a key role in the company's success. With his departure the company enters a period of great uncertainty, and this is reflected on the stock market in America. The share stood 13 per cent down when trading opened on Wall Street.
