After almost an hour and a half of trading, investors have recovered from the worst shock and the share stands at minus 5 per cent. Yesterday The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with a direct employee at Nvidia. That is against the company's internal code of conduct. It is said to involve Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at the group. The newspaper bases its report on anonymous sources within the company. Powell has not yet confirmed the report. The revelation came a few days after the news that Huang had an affair with a woman who is suspected of spying for China. President Trump, with whom Huang had built a close bond, says in a reaction on his platform Truth Social that Huang has done a 'fantastic' job. According to Trump, there is only one person who can succeed him: Tim Cook, who until recently was CEO of Apple. 'A legend must replace a legend.' Cook still works for Apple in the role of chairman, comparable to a supervisory board chairman in the Netherlands, and plays an important role in the lobbying of the tech company. We previously wrote this profile of Jensen Huang and Nvidia: Earlier it was assumed that Huang could survive the espionage affair. He was said to be too big to fire for Nvidia, too important to dismiss. But the accumulation of revelations has made it impossible for him to stay on. Huang ran Nvidia rather single-handedly. He had dozens of managers reporting directly to him. That is far more than at comparable companies, where management responsibility is usually spread over a broader layer. The new interim CEO, Colette Kress, is part of the small circle of top people around Huang. She has worked for the company for thirteen years, and before that held senior positions at Cisco and Microsoft. Her baptism of fire in this new interim role is very likely next week, when Nvidia presents its quarterly figures after the close of trading in the US. Analysts will probably have many questions. The now former chief executive does not speak for himself in the press release. Huang is only briefly thanked by the board for his 'immense contribution'. Chairman With Huang's departure, Nvidia is also announcing the appointment of a so-called board chairman. This is a board member who chairs meetings and is at a distance from day-to-day affairs. The chairman has a supervisory task, somewhat comparable to a supervisory board chairman in the Netherlands. Huang did not see the need for such an official at Nvidia. But now he is coming after all. Musk Elon Musk earlier let it be known that he finds it 'an honour to hire Huang'. Nvidia is an important supplier of graphics processors to Musk's car company Tesla. It is not known whether Huang is open to that. Last Sunday, when it was still only about the affair with the possibly Chinese spy, there was quite a lot of support for Huang from Silicon Valley. Through the rise of artificial intelligence, Nvidia grew into one of the most valuable listed companies in the world. There is a fear that through Huang's relationship with the alleged spy, company secrets have fallen into Chinese hands. It is not known whether that has really happened.

title: Prison sentences of up to 20 years demanded for attempted murder of Iranian activist in Haarlem
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has demanded prison sentences of up to 20 years in a case concerning the failed assassination of an Iranian publicist and activist in the Netherlands. In total, six suspects have been identified: five men and one woman. According to the OM, the six formed an international murder squad that planned, in the night of 5 to 6 June 2024, to kill Siamak Tahmasbi in his flat in Haarlem. But their plan failed. The intended victim saw the silhouettes of two men on his balcony and was able to alert the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in time using an emergency button. They arrived within a minute and arrested the Tunisian Mehrez A. (40) and the Colombian Gabriel O. (29). They had a loaded firearm and a hammer with them. According to the OM, they had been hired by the Spanish-Moroccan Sami Bekal Bounouare. He is said to have coordinated the attack and therefore, according to the OM, deserves the highest sentence, 20 years. However, he is being tried in absentia: he is the only one of the group still at large and is on the National Search List. For the money The Tunisian Mehrez A. admitted guilt last week at the start of the trial. He stated then that he had accepted the assignment for the money: by his own account, he did not know who the victim was. The OM has demanded more than fifteen years' imprisonment for him because he was arrested with the firearm. For the Colombian man with the hammer, the sentence demanded is slightly lower, just over thirteen years. The three other suspects helped with the preparations, according to the OM. They face demands of between seven and ten years in prison. 'Order from Tehran' The victim had feared for his life for some time. Siamak Tahmasbi is a publicist and activist who stands up against the fundamentalist regime of his homeland, Iran. He reaches many people with this: he has more than 68,000 followers on Instagram. Before the incident in Haarlem, he had already survived an attempt on his life when he was shot at in Mijdrecht. He narrowly escaped by ducking. At the hearing, the public prosecutor said the case concerns not only an attempted murder but also "the right to freedom of expression". "The fact that the victim is a journalist and activist, without any ties to the criminal milieu, further adds to the seriousness." In the trial, which is being held in the extra-secure courtroom at Schiphol, it is unlikely to become clear who gave the order for the attempted murder. But according to intelligence service <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity>, it is likely that the order came directly from the regime in Tehran. Nieuwsuur previously broadcast a report on the role of the Iranian regime in attempted murders of Iranians in Europe.

title: Podcast De Dag: the VVD in (cabinet) crisis
lead: At just before eight on Wednesday evening, VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz leaves the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">ministerie van Defensie</entity>. In front of a group of journalists with cameras running, she says she was blindsided by the agreement that coalition partners D66 and CDA reached earlier that day with opposition parties PRO and Volt. Yesilgöz believes a fundamental reset is needed if the rest of the coalition agrees to this. Listen here: you can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps . Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. The VVD has been struggling with its role in the coalition for some time, explains political commentator Nynke de Zoeten. D66 and CDA had already assumed that deals with the left would be needed in this minority arrangement, but the VVD had not. But the VVD's role is also drawing criticism. The solo actions of <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> and his rigid attitude in negotiations have angered D66 and CDA. But the tension is now rising over shifts in taxes of 1 billion on a total of 480 billion euros. According to Nynke de Zoeten, that is a very deliberate choice and strategy by the VVD. Where will that lead? For the party? And for the durability of this <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>? Reactions: email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial team: Rosanne Sies Final editing: Rosanne Sies

title: After the 'blue wave' in the US, migrant caravans from Central America are on the move again
lead: A column of around 1,500 migrants, mostly from Central America, set off on Wednesday from the far south of Mexico towards the United States. An important reason for their departure is the outcome of the midterm elections in the US, in which the Democrats won major victories, including in border states. In migrant communities, partly encouraged by people smugglers, rumours are circulating that American asylum policy will change as a result of that outcome. The group left San Pedro Sula, a Honduran city, in October, mainly fleeing violence in their country and the lack of economic prospects. Along the way, migrants from countries such as El Salvador and Guatemala also joined. Photos show that young children and babies are also part of the caravan. In southern Mexico, people from South America and Africa, among others, have joined. After arriving in Mexico, the caravan left the city of Tapachula, in the state of Chiapas on the border with Guatemala, after a few days. Tapachula has in recent years grown into a place where Central American migrants heading for the US have become stranded, and where, conversely, Mexicans and people from other countries are sent back by American authorities. The phenomenon of migrant caravans is not new in Central America and Mexico. In attempts to reach the US, migrants often travel in large groups, to be less vulnerable to criminal organisations that try to rob, kidnap or recruit them along the way. Particularly between 2021 and 2024, several migrant caravans set off each year towards the US. With the return of Donald Trump to the White House in 2025, asylum policy in the US became much stricter. Asylum applications were hardly processed at all, and both Mexican authorities and the American border patrol made illegal crossings almost impossible. Migration flows towards the US therefore came to a standstill. The illegal migration industry, mainly people smugglers who made large sums of money by bringing migrants to the US, also dried up. A former coyote, as people smugglers are called in Mexico, tells NOS that after the midterm elections in the US, migrants are being approached more actively by criminals to try crossing the border again. That the migration policy of the American government remains unchanged and strict despite the Democratic Party's victory is not mentioned by these recruiters. Migrants who try to cross the border still run a sky-high chance of being arrested and deported, either before or after. As for the large sums, often thousands of dollars, that they paid to people smugglers, they can forget about getting it back. What is Mexico doing? For the migrant caravan that set off this Wednesday, however, the American border is still far away. Initially they hope to reach Mexico City, more than a thousand kilometres from Tapachula. There the migrants hope that federal authorities can accompany them during the final stretch towards the US. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum emphasised on Wednesday that her government is trying to convince the migrants that asylum policy in the US has not changed. She has also said that the group will be offered humanitarian aid and temporary residence permits. Nevertheless, it is striking that the current caravan has been left alone by the Mexican authorities. Partly under pressure from the Trump administration, Mexican police officers have often intervened in Chiapas in recent years when large groups of migrants formed that wanted to travel to the US together. Another group of more than a hundred migrants from Central America was stopped on Tuesday at the border with Guatemala and Mexico. Mexico appears to understand that if more migrant caravans form in the coming period and head for the US, relations with its northern neighbour will come under further pressure, while the humanitarian challenges for Mexico will increase. Trump has meanwhile made himself heard via social media, warning Mexico that it may expect additional tariffs if the caravan moves further towards the border.

title: One dead, four injured in shooting in Washington D.C.
lead: In Washington D.C., at least five people have been shot in a shooting about one and a half kilometres from the White House. At least one person was killed. Three others were injured but are out of danger. One person is in critical condition. All four injured have been taken to hospital. The alleged gunman has since died, various American media report. He is a man who barricaded himself in a building for several hours after the shooting. The shooting took place near a gym, in the Logan Circle neighbourhood. One person was shot dead inside the gym. The man then fired several shots outside. Shortly after 8.00 a.m. local time, the first shots were heard. Barricaded in building: several streets around the area have been cordoned off. The police also called on people on X to stay away from the neighbourhood. The police have surrounded a building where the gunman was believed to have fled. The police tried to clear the premises when more shots were fired from the seventh floor of the building. This revealed that the suspect had barricaded himself on that floor. Negotiators then had telephone contact with the gunman for at least an hour, when the police heard another shot. The contact was then broken off, after which an arrest team stormed in. There they found the gunman with a "self-inflicted gunshot wound", a police spokesperson reports. Some time later the man died, American media report. It has not been made public whether the man died from that same gunshot wound. Gym: the person in the gym was dead on the spot, according to an eyewitness. "Within seconds a man fell to the ground, and a pool of blood appeared," the eyewitness tells news agency AP. "A member of the gym rushed over to help him. He was dead on the spot. He had been shot in the neck," the man said. Little is yet clear about the gunman's motive. The police do report that the matter is probably a conflict involving the apartment complex. Alongside the shooting, a fire was also set, which has been extinguished. The emergency services had turned out in large numbers.

title: Over 1,800 Italian schools alarmed again by bomb threats
lead: For the second day in a row, bomb threats have been sent to Italian schools. More than 1,800 schools across the country are affected. The police have found no explosives. The Ministry of Education says no evidence has been found that the schools are in danger. Schools are advised to restart their lesson programmes. If a school thinks there is nonetheless a threat, they can provide additional evidence to local authorities for a new risk assessment. If necessary, the municipalities can still decide to evacuate the buildings. 'Bloodbath' Some schools say the emails arrived at 10.49 and threatened to carry out a "bloodbath", ANSA news agency reports. The educational institutions were then evacuated and the police investigated every report. According to the Public Prosecution Service, the emails come from foreign servers and are signed "Mikhail Andropov", ANSA writes. This is the same sender who also sent threatening emails to Italian schools yesterday. It is still unknown who is behind the emails. The investigation is being coordinated by a special counter-terrorism unit of the Public Prosecution Service. Three schools in France were also evacuated after a bomb threat. The French Ministry of Education, however, rules out a large-scale wave of threatening emails like in Italy, Le Parisien reports. Second day This is the second day in a row that European educational institutions in several countries have received threatening emails. Yesterday schools in Italy, Northern Ireland and Scotland were evacuated. According to the Italian Ministry of Education, at least 6,000 Italian schools received a threat yesterday. More than 300 schools were evacuated, and many emails had ended up in the spam folder. No explosives were found yesterday either. The false reports appear designed to cause fear, Prime Minister Meloni said on social media yesterday. The threatening email also claimed that a bomb had been placed in the prime minister's car. Meloni called on people to keep a cool head.

title: Indonesia's vice president resigns after diploma scandal and rising tensions
lead: Indonesia's vice president has resigned. The 39-year-old Gibran Rakabuming Raka is embroiled in a scandal over the authenticity of his secondary school diploma. It is the first time in 28 years that the country's vice president has stepped down. President Prabowo Subianto said he had accepted Gibran's resignation "with a heavy heart". They embraced each other, and Prabowo praised the work Gibran had done in his two years as vice president. Within sixty days parliament must vote on a successor. Gibran faced impeachment proceedings. A court had ruled that the vice president had not submitted a valid secondary school diploma. The 39-year-old maintains that his diploma was in order. The decision to step down has nothing to do with the affair, Gibran told journalists. He said it was a personal consideration and intended to give the government ample room to continue governing. Wiretapping scandal The uproar over Gibran's diploma is only one of the issues that have raised tensions in Indonesia considerably. President Prabowo, a former general, is unpopular and under fire for his authoritarian style of government. The economy is doing badly, and there is also dissatisfaction with the handling of the many forest fires in the archipelago, for example. Several senior officials are accused of having wiretapped President Prabowo and have been arrested. There is sufficient evidence to prosecute them and a number of politicians, activists and journalists for treason in the wiretapping scandal, the police announced today. Army deployed Last week thousands of soldiers were mobilised in and around the capital. Behind the scenes there appears to be a power struggle. One of the main suspects in the wiretapping scandal is a confidant of former president Joko Widodo. Widodo is still popular among Indonesians, and is also the father of Gibran, who has stepped down as vice president today. The former president spoke conciliatory words about his successor. "We will continue to support the government of President Prabowo", Widodo told journalists outside his home, according to news agency Reuters.

title: Market visitors on the political crisis: 'It's the same old song every time'
lead: "It's like little children squabbling", says a woman at the market in Rotterdam Hoogvliet. About the political crisis in The Hague she has no kind words. As far as she is concerned, there should be new elections. "Just get rid of the lot of them. Put together a different team in The Hague." She is not the only one. Whether you walk around the market in Hoogvliet, or the ones in Veendam or Oisterwijk, disappointment with national politics prevails everywhere. Many visitors say they are losing faith in The Hague more and more. Our reporters asked people on the street for tips for politics: In Veendam, a market visitor followed developments on television. "It's the same old song every time. They're picking holes in each other. They say they want to work together, but you don't see it." It's a shame, he thinks. "We have a really beautiful country, but this is no way to move forward. It's a constant repeat of moves: back to the ballot box and then the same thing comes again." According to him, responsibility does not lie with politicians alone. "I blame the voter first and foremost, we shouldn't vote so fickle." Others place the blame entirely on politics. At the market in Hoogvliet, a man points to the attitude of the parties. "They're all stuck in their own point of view. And at some point the relationships are so disrupted that working together is no longer possible. I'm not pointing at one culprit, because they've all had a hand in it." No home: Important problems remain unsolved, according to many market visitors. The housing market is often mentioned in particular. A young Rotterdammer fears that for the time being he won't be able to find his own home. "I think that within now and three years I still won't have a home to buy or rent." His faith in politics has collapsed. At the previous elections he still cast his vote, but next time he will probably stay at home. "It doesn't really matter which party wins. title: Tax plan triggers serious coalition crisis: four questions and answers
lead: The annual tax plan is leading to a serious coalition crisis this autumn. For a long time, political The Hague was mainly concerned with how wealth in box 3 should be taxed. Now the question is how much tax should be paid and, above all: by whom? 1. What is this plan, and why does it need to be renewed? In the tax plan the government sets out the revenue for next year. In total that amounts to around 500 billion euros. The tax plan sets out which changes <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> wants to make to taxes. It is announced every year on Prinsjesdag, after which it is discussed and voted on in both chambers. 2. Why is there a political crisis now? The political crisis concerns a small part of the plan, an amendment by Pro and Volt, which coalition parties D66 and CDA have agreed to. If that amendment goes ahead, wealthy people would pay a billion more. Money that would then be used to reduce a tax increase for workers. Not only the content but also the way the amendment came about is causing division. Because according to coalition partner VVD, the plan came about without their consent. That party says it was caught off guard by how things went and calls the increased burden on wealthy people and entrepreneurs harmful to the economy and to the investment and business location climate. That is the extent to which a country, region or city is attractive and predictable for businesses to settle, invest and also remain. 3. How much money is involved? This plan shifts 1 billion euros from income tax to wealth tax. There would be two tax rates instead of one for income earned from wealth, such as profit from shares, real estate and crypto. Anyone who earns more than 60,000 euros this way in a year would have to pay 38.5 percent on it instead of 36 percent. This is to yield 221 million. In practice, someone with a wealth of 1 million and a return of 80,000 euros now pays 28,800 euros in tax on it. Under the newly proposed rates they would pay 29,000 euros: 200 euros extra tax per year. Paper gifts, so to speak an advance on an inheritance, are also being tackled. Restricting this option is to yield 274 million. In addition, this plan is meant to ensure that more entrepreneurs move into the higher bracket of box 2, which covers the tax they pay on income from companies in which they hold a large stake. That is to yield 93 million. Finally, the bulk (412 million) is to be raised by cutting various existing tax benefits for wealthy people. 4. What does business say? The VVD says this plan is bad for the Dutch business climate. But according to Barbara Baarsma, chief economist at PwC, numerous matters are relevant here, she says on radio programme Spraakmakers. "The business climate is much broader than that. By narrowing it down to tax measures you do violence to reality," says Baarsma. PwC monitors the quality and development of the Dutch business climate. According to Baarsma, the unpredictability of government policy is high on the list of irritations. A cabinet that falls would in that respect be bad news. In response to the political crisis, business organisations VNO-NCW and MKB-Nederland also write that entrepreneurs urgently need stability. Chief economist at ING Marieke Blom states that the millions in taxes are therefore unworthy of a political crisis. She calls it not a small matter but a trifling one. "It is more symbolic than that I think the economic future of the Netherlands will be determined by this."

title: US Supreme Court: construction of a border wall through Texas nature park may proceed
lead: The US Supreme Court has allowed the resumption of construction of the border wall desired by President Donald Trump in Big Bend National Park in West Texas, a nature area. The court brushed aside environmental objections.

title: More than 350 sports clubs report data breach after cyberattack at AllUnited on Monday evening
lead: More than 350 sports clubs indicated on Wednesday that member data has been stolen following a cyberattack at AllUnited. The cyberattack took place on Monday evening, but only now has it become clear that a data breach has also occurred in the online system with which affiliated associations keep their membership administration.

lead: FC Twente is still without a loss of points in the Conference League after three matchdays. The team of coach John van den Brom came back from a deficit after half-time against Cypriot club Pafos FC and won 3-1 at the Grolsch Veste.

lead: Johan and Ine Smeets have just under a month left behind the counter of snack bar De Smulhoek on the Tilburg Leenherenstraat. Joys and sorrows have been shared, but on 1 December they step away from the fryer after more than 42 years.

lead: Feyenoord suffered its first defeat of the season in Friesland. The Rotterdam side seemed to have the points secured when it was 0-2, but Heerenveen fought back. First to 3-2 and later to 4-3. In the final seconds the home side also scored a fifth goal: 5-3.

lead: Pensions in the care, construction and metal and technology sectors will rise slightly next year, but will lag behind inflation. In these sectors, pensions will rise by about 0,8 percent.

lead: Paraguayans hold president Santiago Peña partly responsible for the major financial problems at Ueno. The digital bank, of which about 60 percent of adult Paraguayans are customers, has too little equity.

lead: Players of the online computer game Fortnite are obsessed with a very rare prize in the game. If you manage to find a special coin, you can claim items from the online shop that normally cost money. The chance of finding that coin? About 1 in 137,500. The latter is in Dublin today for a European summit. One of the items on the agenda is Europe's role in the negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. And that is striking, because until now Europe has not been admitted to the negotiating table.

lead: Pump prices for fuel fell faster over the past month than the price of crude oil. Remarkable, because usually it is the other way around. How is that possible, and above all, will prices keep falling?

Because his identity is unknown, he is also called Lucky, Chris the Canadian, Lee, Louis and Sonny. But who he really is remains a mystery even after three years of investigation.

The 24-year-old skater for Team Essent seemed on course for a medal until then, but ultimately finished fifth.

lead: Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton visited the Egyptian border crossing at Rafah on Tuesday and met aid workers there who are providing aid to the Gaza Strip, which has been devastated by war. This is according to a statement from the Egyptian government, reports news agency AFP.

title: AP: Tax Administration progress is slow
lead: The Tax Administration still does not comply with privacy legislation in many important areas. The improvement is also too slow. At the same time, the intensified supervision by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) is bearing fruit: the Tax Administration is visibly working to solve the problems. This is shown by the first edition of the 'State of data protection at the Tax Administration', which the AP publishes today.

title: Uncertainty again in the municipality of Moerdijk: must the village go, partly go, or stay? 'We are back to square one'

But since <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> came up with an alternative scenario, the surrounding villages fear that they will bear the brunt of it.

The institute is to stimulate technological innovation of defence equipment and improve domestic production capacity. According to the cabinet, this is necessary to counter less predictable threats.

title: US House votes by Wednesday on impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth
lead: The United States House of Representatives will vote by Wednesday on removing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth from office. Republican congressman Thomas Massie had previously announced that he would start impeachment proceedings. Hegseth has been under heavy pressure since the Republican defeat in the midterms.

title: Romano has autism and calls for more calm in hotels at the breakfast buffet
lead: A hotel stay should offer relaxation, but for people with autism it is precisely the breakfast that can cause overstimulation. The <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> will now handle a case on this. Someone with autism asked in advance for an alternative to the regular breakfast buffet. The hotel offered a quieter time, but that too proved insufficient.

title: A year after the heist, the Louvre crown jewels are still missing: 'Recovery could take 40 years'
lead: A year after the spectacular break-in at the Louvre, the stolen crown jewels are still missing. On 19 October 2025 the thieves stole nine jewels with an estimated value of around 88 million euros. Ten days after the robbery, four main suspects were arrested. But where the loot has gone remains a mystery for the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>.

title: Major setback for Xavi: captain Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey withdraw from Oranje
lead: Captain Virgil van Dijk and striker Brian Brobbey will miss the Netherlands national team's last group matches against Greece and Germany in the Nations League. They are insufficiently fit and not available, the KNVB reports.

title: Report: global warming can be stopped at 1.7 degrees with strong intervention
Prospects for young people
lead: The latest figures on young people on welfare are worrying. There are now 44,000 of them: over 27 percent more than at the end of 2022. In the past year alone, about 2,400 young people were added: a growth of 5.7 percent. By comparison, among 27- to 45-year-olds the growth was 0.8 percent and among those over 45 it was 0.2 percent. Of the 4,100 additional welfare recipients in total, nearly 60 percent are therefore under 27 years old.

title: Police release names and photos of five suspects in the notorious Maastricht art heist
lead: Four men and a woman have been added to the national investigation list for a violent jewelry theft during the TEFAF art fair in Maastricht in 2022. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has offered a reward of 20,000 euros for the golden tip.

title: Psychological fatigue among employees grows; mainly an increase among young people and women
Massively carpooling again to solve traffic jams? 'It needs to become financially attractive'
lead: Traffic jams are increasing enormously again due to the thick fog, but those who drive on the motorway are spectators of a 'parade of empty seats.' The number of 'single' motorists has been rising for years, causing traffic jams to increase. That is why we should fall back on a classic: carpooling. 'If you start carpooling tomorrow, the traffic jam will not be a metre shorter tomorrow,' says traffic psychologist Gerard Tertoolen on Spraakmakers.

title: These doctors rushed to help immediately in Kraków: 'Injured officer the great hero'
lead: Six people were killed in a shooting on Saturday in the Polish city of Kraków. The gunman fired from a car. These two surgeons were in the centre of Kraków on Saturday and rushed to help after the shooting.

title: Jetten waters down plan for the royal house after pressure from coalition

Behind the scenes, the idea of a 'broad exploration of a future-proof royal house' has been discussed, sources tell the political desk of RTL Nieuws. Financing would also be examined.

title: Coach Jesus regrets Ronaldo's departure: wanted him to stay
lead: LISBON (ANP/DPA) - National team coach Jorge Jesus of Portugal regrets that Cristiano Ronaldo will no longer play for the national team. "It's his decision and I have to accept that, but I would have liked to keep him. I also asked him to remain available, but there is no way back", Jesus told the Portuguese broadcaster Canal 11.

title: I pictured a headline: 'Zeist cannot reach footballer, trainee fired'
How Black women and a burger advert gave Scott Colom victory in Mississippi
lead: Something remarkable happened in one of the most conservative states in the United States. Democrat Scott Colom won the Senate seat for Mississippi by a narrow margin over his Republican challenger Cindy Hyde-Smith. Black women and an election advert about protein helped the lawyer to victory.

title: Anti-European sentiment in the United States transcends party political lines
lead: Anti-Europeanism is deeply rooted in American politics. Even the new generation of Democrats sees a more independent Europe as a necessity, while the American gaze shifts elsewhere.

title: Cabinet prepares possible restriction of Woo despite ongoing evaluation

This is happening while the official evaluation of the act is still ongoing. During the cabinet formation, various options were already mentioned to restrict access to government information, including excluding internal emails and civil servants' advice.

title: Council of State approves construction of wind farm in Zutphen
lead: Three wind turbines may now definitively be built in Zutphen next to an industrial estate along the Twente Canal. The <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">provincie Gelderland</entity> has sufficiently substantiated that the emission of chemicals and plastic particles from wear of the blades is acceptable, the Council of State ruled.

title: Ministry insufficiently protects animal welfare in the meat sector: 'Money is the focus'
lead: Animal welfare often loses out to financial interests in the meat sector. Companies want to produce as efficiently as possible, while the ministry intervenes insufficiently. As a result, animals are sometimes treated badly, even when companies comply with the rules.

title: Let the old, polluting industry die out? That doesn't work, the whole Jenga tower will collapse
lead: The chemical industry in the Netherlands is highly integrated: hundreds of companies work together, sometimes literally attached to one another. What has always been a strength threatens to become a weakness now that more and more factories are closing. "When do we realise: oh, that was one Jenga block too many?"

title: Italian chef fired over Hawaiian pizza: 'Do you want to kill me?'
lead: An Italian chef in Australia has been fired for refusing to make a Hawaiian pizza. Because while we have no problem putting pineapple on pizza or cream in pasta, Italians are strongly opposed to it.

title: Autism can make motherhood harder but also provide support
lead: Autism is often only discovered later in women, and motherhood can be a turning point. The many changes, unpredictability and stimuli can cause mothers to get stuck. Yet there is little attention for the impact of autism on motherhood.

title: Lisa (13) probably chosen at random, suspect previously on the radar of prosecutors
lead: The 13-year-old Lisa from Berlin, who was found dead yesterday after being missing for almost a week, was probably a random victim. Initial investigation shows no indications that the suspect and the victim knew each other, according to German prosecutors.

title: Hengelo pays 2000 euros a day to keep Ukrainian 'drug brothers' out of the shelter

title: Water boards: 'Not all infrastructure is sufficiently future-proof'

But what if that infrastructure is just as aged as the roads and bridges, are we still safe? 'We live in a vulnerable part of Europe', says <entity id="person:vincent-lokin">Vincent Lokin</entity> of the Unie van Waterschappen.

lead: However the vote turns out on the cabinet plan for tax on savings and investments, the hassle will continue for now. What awaits savers and investors?

title: Rens Kroes gives birth to a baby boy: 'Born on the same day as your big sister'
lead: Rens Kroes has given birth to her second child. The cookbook author and entrepreneur says the little boy is named Loïc. "You could choose any day, but now you share your birthday with your big sister," she writes.

title: RDI warning: digital infrastructure not always available as a matter of course
lead: In the Netherlands we are used to critical infrastructure working. Availability and accessibility are normally almost 100 percent (>99.98%). But due to the strong increase in hybrid threats, the RDI doubts whether this will also be the case in the future, as described in the annual trend radar.

title: Rachel Hazes sells rights to music by her husband André after forty years
lead: Rachel Hazes has sold the rights to the music of her late husband André Hazes after almost forty years. Since Monday the rights have been in the hands of Pythagoras Music Fund, the Dutch investment fund of, among others, composer John Ewbank.

title: Cabinet gives Zelensky 'winter support package' during visit to Netherlands: drones and air defence for Ukraine
lead: With Ukraine being bombarded almost every day by Russian drones and missiles, the Netherlands is coming to its aid with additional drones and air defence weapons. During a surprise visit to The Hague, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday that the support helps with 'saving lives'. "We need it to get through this winter."

title: Part of tunnel in A28 rises again
lead: For the second time in almost three years, parts of the Vollenhoven tunnel on the A28 near Zeist are moving. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> is placing weights on the central reservation.

title: Over twenty injured by a strong earthquake in central Japan
lead: An earthquake with a magnitude of 5.7 in central Japan injured at least 24 people on Sunday, local media report. The quake caused damage to buildings and disruption to train traffic. No deaths have been reported.

title: Mike Hammer actor Stacy Keach (85) has died
lead: American actor Stacy Keach has died at the age of 85, his wife told The Hollywood Reporter . He died at home in the Polish town of Magdalenka as a result of heart failure.

Dutch government knew that underpayment of temp workers clashed with European rules

lead: You have a desire to have a child, but you cannot become pregnant yourself. Then you can choose a surrogate. But how does that work in the Netherlands?

title: Ukraine peace talks fail again, parties fight on
Trump: 'largely true' that the war on Iran is to blame for the Republican losses
lead: The Democrats score a huge victory over the Republicans, both in the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. It is a rebuke for Trump's Republican Party. Several states that normally colour 'deep red' are blue this time. Read back the liveblog about the midterms here.

lead: Singer Bob Dylan was at the Vatican this week for a conversation with Pope Leo XIV. The photos were compared to Star Wars, Spanish Baroque painting and Kermit the Frog. But the contrast between the two giants is less great than it seems.

title: KLM takes drastic action, but is cutting jobs enough to survive?
Weghorst: happy with converted penalty and a well-deserved point
lead: Wout Weghorst played a leading role in FC Twente's home match against his former club Ajax (2-2). "I am happy that I was able to earn us a very well-deserved point", he said.

title: Messi first player to be MLS top scorer for a second year in a row
lead: Lionel Messi has become the first footballer ever to be top scorer in the American football league MLS for a second year in a row. The Argentine received the American version of the Golden Boot for it. The 39-year-old star scored 26 goals in 34 matches for Inter Miami. He finished ahead of Petar Musa of FC Dallas, who scored 22 times.

title: 'Stop the match': why Joey Kooij interrupted a mega chance for FC Twente against Ajax on the advice of the VAR
lead: 'Stop the match. Stop the match.' The moment of the weekend was the whistle with which Joey Kooij interrupted a mega chance for FC Twente on the advice of the VAR, and then did not award an alleged penalty to Ajax. What exactly happened? A reconstruction of a crazy minute in the intense and tumultuous top match.

title: State Secretary Eric van der Burg to the Windward Islands for Statia Day and Kingdom Summit
A lot had changed in the relationship between young women and men
Another coach sacked at Manchester United: crisis costs Michael Carrick his job
lead: Manchester United sacked coach Michael Carrick on Thursday. The former midfielder is held responsible for the poor results at the fallen giants and is thus the latest coach who has had to leave Manchester prematurely.

title: Parliamentary majority wants ban on generative AI for primary school pupils
lead: The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> wants children at primary school not to use generative AI. A motion from Volt and CDA received a broad majority on Thursday. The parties want <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to arrange such a ban.

title: Bill Gates did not come to Leeuwarden, where three judges considered the charge that 'the global elite' wanted to commit genocide with Covid-19
lead: A case about conspiracy theories surrounding Covid-19 is being heard in Leeuwarden. Seven citizens are suing, among others, Bill Gates, <entity id="person:mark-rutte">Mark Rutte</entity> and <entity id="person:hugo-de-jonge">Hugo de Jonge</entity> over alleged vaccine damage and 'genocide'. title: German government wants ice hockey World Championship without Russia
lead: The German government has taken a clear position on the men's ice hockey World Championship in May 2027. That tournament can go ahead as planned in Germany, but without Russia.

title: Have your say: care is more important than speed when you want to change tax rules
lead: The cabinet's plan to change the tax on wealth is shaky in the eyes of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. According to the cabinet adviser, there is no point in rushing the plan for box 3, partly because the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> cannot cope with the change. In De Kwestie we put a statement to our readers on this. Respond below as well.

title: Backpay scheme for Indies and Moluccan widows to be applied for from February

lead: Young people again dream of a revolution and want to set it in motion

title: We are becoming more productive, but we are working fewer hours
lead: Labour productivity in our country has risen by almost 5 percent since the beginning of 2024. This is the largest increase in ten years. That is remarkable, given that we have started working fewer hours.

title: Grinwis warns cabinet about new box 3 system: 'Get it right in one go'
lead: ChristenUnie MP Pieter Grinwis has serious doubts about the new box 3 system the cabinet wants to introduce. According to him, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> is given insufficient time to assess the legislation carefully, while <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, the Dutch Banking Association and the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> all have strong criticism. lead: KLM flight 461 from Amsterdam, which was targeted by a bomb threat on Thursday, cannot continue to Tel Aviv after an intermediate landing in the Romanian capital Bucharest due to a technical fault. A KLM spokesperson said so.

title: Privacy watchdog: Tax Administration does not comply with privacy rules, citizens' fundamental rights at stake
Council of State: salt mining in Groningen may continue
lead: Salt may be extracted until 2045 in the villages of Borgercompagnie and Tripscompagnie in the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>. That was decided by the <entity id="org:afdeling-bestuursrechtspraak-raad-van-state">Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak van de Raad van State</entity>. The plan for the extraction of magnesium salt remains in place.

title: Dozens of migrants drowned again off the coast of Senegal during a deadly crossing to the Canary Islands
lead: The 'Atlantic route' is one of the most dangerous migration routes in the world. This weekend again showed this; at least 34 people lost their lives in a shipwreck. Meanwhile, the local government of the Canary Islands warns that the region cannot cope with the number of migrants who have arrived.

title: Giovanni van Bronckhorst criticises Feyenoord's organisation after a drubbing in Friesland: 'We think we are very good'
lead: The puzzle at Feyenoord seemed solved, but the weak performance at Heerenveen shows that everything is open again for the Rotterdam club. Giovanni van Bronckhorst openly said he doubts the organisation. 'We think we are very good.'

lead: Zeven inbrekers zijn zaterdag aangehouden op het dak van een bedrijf in Groningen. Brandweerlieden gebruikten een hoogwerker om hen naar beneden te halen, meldden lokale media.

title: Arokodare feels confident heading into Twente after scoring twice
lead: Tolu Arokodare feels confident after two goals and a comfortable Ajax win over Midtjylland in the Conference League (1-6) heading into Sunday's top match against FC Twente in the Eredivisie. The Nigerian striker, who has scored in the last four matches in a row, said this in Herning to Ziggo Sport.

Biden gives update on cancer treatment: 'One day is better than the other'

title: Bomb threats on planes: how do you tell whether a threat is real or fake?
lead: This week there have already been eight bomb threats on European flights, but so far zero explosives have been found. How is it weighed whether a threat is serious? "The number of bomb threats this week is phenomenal."

lead: US intelligence services have informed the government in Washington that a woman who had built a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang worked for a Chinese intelligence service. According to The New York Times , which first reported this, she had been recruited to gather information about him.

title: Mark Rutte said: do not waste time on drones that 'now and then drift into our territory'
lead: It had been a while, but Mark Rutte was once again on Dutch television. In a one-hour bilateral meeting with Jeroen Pauw, the NATO chief said we had to look through the mist.

title: Cruise ship pianist falls overboard and is found in the middle of the sea nine hours later by fishermen
lead: A crew member of a cruise ship was found in the middle of the Pacific Ocean on Friday by two fishermen. The duo rescued the man, who turned out to work as a pianist on board a Royal Caribbean cruise.

title: Essay: the myth of the overcrowded neighbourhood
lead: It's busy in the neighbourhood, people often say. More and more experts from more and more organisations are active to support residents. Isn't it too busy? Researchers Neeltje Spit and Arno Kierkels studied the supposed busyness and find that care workers themselves do not feel that too many people are concerned with the fate of a neighbourhood. Collaboration between professionals often comes about naturally, they write in their essay.

title: Wesley builds a supersonic oliebollen bistro with underfloor heating and spotlights: 'The baking oven costs more than my car'
lead: Underfloor heating in the floor and counter, a baking oven that costs more than his car and a dark blue ceiling full of mood spotlights. The familiar Dutch doughnut stall has made way for a supersonic 'oliebollen bistro' at oliebollen baker Wesley Smit. "You don't really see a matte blue ceiling like that anywhere."

title: Man sentenced to five years in prison for running over a boy (4) in Maastricht
lead: Janus K. was sentenced by the court in Roermond on Wednesday to a prison term of five years for running over and killing a four-year-old boy in Maastricht. In addition, the thirty-year-old man will receive a five-year driving ban.

lead: International train travellers are experiencing delays as a result of a bomb threat at a station in northern France. Trains may therefore not run through Calais-Fréthun station, which is causing delays on Eurostar, the international train operator reports.

title: What do you want to know about the political crisis that has arisen in The Hague?
lead: Tensions in The Hague have risen sharply. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is wobbling after the agreement on the tax plans between D66 and CDA with PRO and Volt. lead: The leadership of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> and the coalition, after months of disagreement, are in agreement on the approach to box 3 and next year's tax plan, Hague sources say. lead: It seems only a matter of time before the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has all the suspects in the murder of Tico (19) from Schiedam behind bars. One of them is already in custody, and the names of the others are circulating. Meanwhile the authorities are on alert for revenge attacks. Also because the victim is said to have been connected to a notorious youth gang.

title: Board of AI giant Nvidia investigates affair of top executive with alleged Chinese spy
lead: The board of US AI chip company Nvidia is launching an investigation into whether top executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign espionage operation. The announcement of the investigation followed a confession by Huang to his employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife.

title: Code yellow in parts of the country due to locally dense fog
lead: In parts of the Netherlands a code yellow applies Sunday morning due to locally dense fog. The warning applies to the west and centre and later also to the north, reports the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> .

lead: The cabinet wants to set aside 350 million euros for tax relief. In addition, the introduction of the new box 3 plans will be postponed by one year. At the earliest the introduction will take place in 2028, and at the latest in 2029. Insiders told RTL Nieuws this.

title: Dave De K. found guilty of kidnapping and killing Dean (4) in Zeeland
lead: A special court in Belgium found Dave De K. guilty on Friday of manslaughter and kidnapping Dean (4) in 2022. De K.'s ex-girlfriend, the Dutch national Romy W., was acquitted of attempted kidnapping. The sentence will be announced on Monday.

Municipalities and housing corporations: more flexible homes for status holders
lead: Municipalities, housing corporations and national government will make an attempt to give more status holders suitable housing. Within the next three years, the backlogs for this group of asylum seekers must be fully eliminated, including by building extra flexible homes, encouraging shared housing and converting old offices.

lead: The cabinet's top has agreed on adjustments to the tax plan for next year. Tomorrow it will be sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> after it has first been discussed once more by an extra <entity id="org:ministerraad">ministerraad</entity>. Whether the adjustments can also count on a majority in parliament remains uncertain.

title: King couple visits Qatar on first state visit to the Middle East
lead: <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima will make a state visit to Qatar at the beginning of December. It is Willem-Alexander's first state visit as king to a country in the Middle East.

title: Dutch people must be able to survive at least 72 hours, but the disaster broadcaster does not manage that
lead: To prepare for 72 hours without electricity and water, the government advises people in the Netherlands to get an emergency radio at home and tune it in advance to the regional disaster broadcaster. But there is a good chance that the radio will go silent at some point in an emergency: the emergency broadcasters cannot themselves broadcast for 72 hours non-stop.

title: Strike in regional transport called off, talks on collective labour agreement resume
lead: The planned strike in regional transport tomorrow is called off. Trade unions and employers are resuming talks on a new collective labour agreement. FNV hopes to reach an agreement with the employers and suspends the actions for two weeks.

title: State Secretary Erkens wants a ban on keeping dolphins
lead: State Secretary Silvio Erkens (Animal Welfare) is working on a breeding ban for dolphins. Dolphins must also disappear from the Dolfinarium in Harderwijk in the coming years.

title: Court of Audit: central government must take the lead in protecting peat areas
lead: Things are going badly for the peat areas in the Netherlands. According to the National Audit Office, this is because many parties are involved in nature policy, and they sometimes have conflicting interests. The different layers of government must weigh those interests, but this does not always succeed. Central government, which spent well over 6 billion euros on nature management and restoration from 2014 to 2023, must therefore take the lead, the Audit Office believes.

title: Eelco Heinen already has the cheese slicer in hand
In South Korea, more strollers for pets are now sold than for babies

lead: Robotisation offers opportunities for the Dutch manufacturing industry, but without sufficient technically trained people, those opportunities will remain unused.

lead: Nederland heeft geen duidelijke afspraken over hoe de goudreserves in tijden van crisis zouden kunnen worden gebruikt.

title: Gelderland derby cancelled as De Graafschap supporters block their own club's players' bus
lead: Some De Graafschap supporters are angry because they were not welcome in the area outside the Gelredome. Last year, disturbances took place during Vitesse vs De Graafschap.

title: At least eight dead after New York building collapse, seventeen injured
lead: A three-storey building has collapsed in New York. At least eight people lost their lives and seventeen others were injured. Four of the injured are in critical condition. Among the victims are also children, although it is not known whether they were injured or killed. The fire brigade is searching the rubble with hundreds of rescue workers.

title: Volumia! band members wage bitter battle in court: 'Just as much my baby'

title: Woman drives brommobiel onto A15 near Rotterdam and overturns
lead: A woman drove onto the A15 near Rotterdam with a brommobiel on Tuesday afternoon. At the Vaanplein junction, the vehicle overturned.

title: Cookbook author and influencer Emma de Thouars (37): 'It seems logical to me that you speak out against terrible things, such as a genocide'
Newborn baby found in garbage bag in Belgian field
lead: The body of a deceased newborn baby was found in a field in the Belgian province of Liège. The body was discovered on Sunday afternoon in a garbage bag by the son of a farmer.

title: This factory is set to make Europe independent of Starlink
lead: Europe is going to build its own satellite network at a cost of billions of euros. Think of it as a European alternative to the American Starlink. It will be built entirely by European parties. The most important component, the satellites, comes from our southern neighbours. We were given an exclusive look..

title: Senior police officials do not want measurable goals
lead: In 2027 almost 10 billion euros of tax money will go to the police. By law, the police must spend this budget efficiently. But in June the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Algemene Rekenkamer</entity> concluded that the police have little insight into what happens to the money. A working group within the police wants to make the work even harder to monitor.

lead: Het kabinet hervat deze week de gesprekken met zeven oppositiepartijen terwijl het probeert de stemmen te verkrijgen die het nodig heeft...

New potato varieties are developed in the lab and research is done into sustainable cultivation. We spoke with several experts about how things really stand with the potato. In her book 'De magie van de achterkamertjes', political coach Kiki Bakker uses seventeen interviews with (former) politicians to describe how things go in the council and parliament, and explains how to develop political savvy. 'Self-reflection is the most important quality of the politician.'

And Donald Trump has declared the Oval Office, the presidential workroom in the White House, a national monument. He thus wants to prevent successors from being able to undo the changes he made to the office. Follow all developments in the United States via our liveblog.

title: Residents protest against electricity substation right in front of their door on Veerstraat: 'Surely nobody is waiting for that?'
National government wants to reduce digital dependencies through procurement
lead: The national government wants to use its purchasing power more emphatically for digital autonomy and the continuity of public services. Joint ICT procurement, more room for European providers and better exit arrangements should reduce dependence on a limited number of technology companies. At the same time, the procurement organisation must work more simply and cheaply.

title: 'I no longer believe in Jetten. It's all taking far too long'

lead: Former Groningen mayor Koen Schuiling is appealing to the Supreme Court. In March 2024 he was fined for masturbating in his car based on the testimony of a single witness. Earlier NRC reporting showed that the criminal file was incomplete and influenced by assumptions about Schuiling's homosexuality.

title: I traded in my 1995 Toyota Corolla. I dare not say what I drive now
lead: After 16 years of loyal service, Japke-d. Bouma traded her old, dirty, faded red 1995 Toyota Corolla for a newer car. Since then she has stomach ache, feels like a traitor and is inconsolably nostalgic. "I dare not say which car I drive now."

title: Confused man runs at King Willem-Alexander during working visit, security guards have to intervene
lead: A man ran at King Willem-Alexander on Friday afternoon during his visit to the North Holland village of Ursem. He was then calmed down by the king.

title: Rob Jetten and his partner are expecting a baby: the rules on surrogacy in the Netherlands
lead: The Netherlands is getting a 'first baby': Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his fiancé Nicolás Keenan are expecting a child next year. The couple had already expressed their wish to have children, but finding a surrogate is complicated because of the rules in our country.

title: Choice for maintenance is right, but not at the expense of our water plan
lead: The state of many Dutch waterways and bridges is nothing to be proud of. It is right that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is freeing up money for the large backlog of maintenance. But that this comes at the expense of plans to protect us against drought is asking for new problems, writes political reporter Hans van Soest in this commentary.

More and more seniors with psychological complaints after the rise in the AOW age
lead: The number of employees suffering from psychological complaints has risen sharply over the past ten years. title: Tax plan appears headed for debate in House of Representatives without a majority
lead: There is a real chance that the minority cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA will have to submit the Tax Plan for 2027 to the House of Representatives without a secured majority.

title: Code yellow again due to dense fog, warning applies to almost the entire country
lead: In a large part of the Netherlands, code yellow applies until Tuesday 12.00 hours due to locally dense fog. The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> reports in the night from Monday to Tuesday that the chance of fog is spreading to more places. Visibility may be less than 200 metres.

title: Wave of inheritances brings risks of fraud and inequality
lead: The Netherlands will have many heirs in the coming decades who will receive large sums in their accounts. They run a greater risk of becoming victims of fraud, warns <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">Autoriteit Financiële Markten</entity> (AFM). The shift in wealth also causes more inequality on the housing market.

title: Zeeland looks to English coastal town: learning from Folkestone
lead: 'From Zeeland it is actually only a short drive: two and a half hours to the Channel Tunnel, at the end of the tunnel turn left, and you are there.' Last September, Zeeland deputy Johan Aalberts took a seat on a bus heading for the English coastal town of Folkestone, not far from the famous White Cliffs of Dover. Besides the King's Commissioner <entity id="person:hugo-de-jonge">Hugo de Jonge</entity>, a group from Zeeland's education and business sectors was also on the bus with him.

lead: Sepp van den Berg has been added to the Dutch national team squad. The 24-year-old defender from Brentford has been called up for Oranje for the first time. He reports Tuesday evening in Zeist to the squad of head coach Xavi Hernández.

title: Xavi calls leaving out Taylor the hardest choice: 'Last time that was Memphis'
lead: Head coach Xavi Hernández found leaving out Kenneth Taylor the hardest choice with his Oranje squad. The Spaniard had less difficulty passing over the unfit Memphis Depay.

title: Maite and Adinda both thought they were straight: 'Then I decided to seize my chance'
lead: For years they were attracted to men, and neither had ever imagined being together with a woman. Until musicians Maite Hontelé and Adinda Meertins kissed each other one evening on a bench in a Colombian park. Ten years and two children later they are still madly in love. Now they are also releasing an album together. "I could not be with someone who does not understand what I hear in music."

title: Skaters head to Beijing for the first World Cup: the full programme and all Dutch participants
lead: The first long-track speed skating World Cup of the season takes place in Beijing from Friday to Sunday. Which Dutch skaters are travelling to China and what does the programme look like? An overview.

title: Water board tax up again by tens of euros
lead: The water board tax will again rise by a few tens of euros next year for households with an owner-occupied home. For tenants, the tax also rises by an average of 7 percent, and for farmers and nature managers by 7.5 percent. The Association of Water Boards expects this based on the proposals on the table in the 21 water boards. They are setting their rates for 2027 in these weeks.

title: Is there hope for the cabinet? There are reasons why the tax plan may still pass
lead: Once again the cabinet is reworking its tax plans, hoping to still win support from opposition parties. They are grumbling, but note that they are not closing the door completely either. Three reasons why the cabinet could still succeed.

title: Videoland may take over streamer Viaplay, including Formula 1 and darts
lead: Streaming service Viaplay will become property of DPG Media, and will be merged with Videoland. The <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">Autoriteit Consument en Markt</entity> (ACM) has approved this.

lead: Paintings by Vincent van Gogh have flooded the world on coffee mugs, mouse mats and fridge magnets. Now Museum Kröller-Müller is showing all 88 Van Goghs from its own collection. Curator Renske Cohen Tervaert shows how to look at them as if you had never seen them before.

title: Queen Máxima was set to listen to a pro-Palestinian band on 7 October, and then the visit was called off
lead: A working visit by <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima is rarely cancelled at the last minute. Yet it happened earlier this month: Máxima was due to visit Poppodium 013 on, of all days, 7 October, with the pro-Palestinian band Droom Dit on the programme. Behind the scenes it is now said that this date was not a good choice for the visit.

title: School bus crashes into tree in France, two dead and several injured
lead: Two people have died in an accident involving a school bus in eastern France. They are a child and a young adult. Sixteen people were injured, three of them seriously.

title: Imam used WhatsApp not to call for riots, yet police came to his door
lead: Imam Azzedine Karrat had police at his door because he allegedly called for riots. That was based on a misunderstanding. According to the imam, it feels to people with a certain background and religion as if they are "under a magnifying glass". Police Rotterdam says it "deeply regrets" the incident.
